Balance 1,500 Deficiency $ 250 (f) As used in sec. 3271, the term "rebate" means so much of an abatement, credit, refund, or other repayment as is made on the ground that the tax imposed by the Act is less than the excess of (1) the amount shown as the tax by the taxpayer upon his return increased by the amount previously assessed (or collected without assessment) as a deficiency over (2) the amount of rebates previously made. For example, assume that the amount of the tax shown by the taxpayer upon his return for the taxable year is $600 and the amount claimed as a credit under sec. 3035 for tax withheld on wages is $900. If the Secretary determines that the tax imposed by the Act is $600 and makes a refund of $300, no part of such refund constitutes a "rebate" since the refund is not 41

T.§ 3271-1 

Ch. 253

made on the ground that the tax imposed by the Act is less than the tax shown on the return. If, however, the Secretary determines that the tax imposed by the Act is $500 and refunds $400, the amount of $100 of such refund would constitute a rebate since it is made on the ground that the tax imposed by the Act ($500) is less than the tax shown on the return ($600). The amount of such rebate ($100) would be taken into account in arriving at the amount of any deficiency subsequently determined. § 3272. Procedure in general 

[Text of Act, see 13 L.P.R.A. § 3272.] § 3272-1. Assessment of a deficiency 

(a) If the Secretary determines that there is a deficiency in respect of the income tax imposed by this Act, the Secretary is authorized to notify the taxpayer of the deficiency by registered mail. Within 30 days after notice of the deficiency is mailed, or within any extension of such period granted by the Secretary, the taxpayer may file a written request with the Secretary for reconsideration of such deficiency and an administrative hearing on the same. No particular form is prescribed for the written request but it should cover all items which the taxpayer questions and may be accompanied by a statement of any additional facts upon which the taxpayer intends to rely or by a brief if the taxpayer desires to file one. In case the taxpayer desires an administrative hearing, a statement to that effect should be included in the written request. In determining such 30-day period, Saturday, Sunday, or a legal holiday in Puerto Rico is not to be counted as the 30th day. Should the taxpayer fail to request reconsideration within the 30 day period, or having requested reconsideration and the proposed deficiency is thereafter confirmed in whole or in part, the Secretary in either case, is authorized to notify the taxpayer by registered mail of his final determination of a deficiency and to indicate the amount of bond that the taxpayer must file should he desire to appeal to the Superior Court from such determination of deficiency. Within 30 days after notice of final determination of a deficiency is mailed, the taxpayer may file a complaint in the form provided by law, with the Superior Court for a redetermination of the deficiency, provided he previously files with the Secretary a bond in his favor and subject to his approval, in the amount stated in the notice of final determination of a deficiency. Should the 42

Supp. L

DEFICIENCIES 

T.13 § 3271-1 taxpayer agree to a part of the deficiency, he may pay that part of the tax to which he agrees and litigate the remainder, in which event, the required bond shall not exceed the amount of tax which is being litigated plus interest. See sec. 3272(a) for other provisions pertaining to the jurisdiction of the Superior Court in the matter of the bonding of the tax in controversy, including interest and penalties. Except as stated in paragraphs (b), (c), (d), (e), and (f) of this section, no assessment of a deficiency in respect of a tax imposed by this Act shall be made until such notice of final determination of a deficiency has been mailed to the taxpayer, nor until the expiration of such 30-day period, nor, if a complaint has been filed with the Superior Court, until the judgment of the Superior Court has become final. (b) If a taxpayer is notified of an additional amount of tax due on account of a mathematical error appearing upon the face of the return, such notice is not to be considered as a notice of deficiency, and the taxpayer has no right to file a complaint with the Superior Court upon the basis of such notice, nor is the assessment of such additional tax prohibited by the provisions of sec. 3272(a). (c) If the Secretary believes that the assessment or collection of a deficiency will be jeopardized by delay, such deficiency shall be assessed immediately, as provided in secs. 3273 and 3273-1. (d) Upon the adjudication of bankruptcy of any taxpayer or the appointment of a receiver for any taxpayer in any receivership proceeding, any deficiency determined by the Secretary in respect of the tax shall be assessed immediately, irrespective of the provisions of sec. 3272(a), if such deficiency has not been assessed in accordance with law prior to the adjudication of bankruptcy or the appointment of a receiver. See secs. 3274, 3274-1, 3274-2 and 3298. (e) (1) If the Superior Court renders a judgment and determines that there is a deficiency, and, if the taxpayer desires to file an appeal for review of the judgment by the Supreme Court, the deficiency determined by the Superior Court must be paid in full, within the period provided by law for appeal to the Supreme 

Court. However, see secs. 3272 (b) (3) and 3272 (b) (4) providing for cases wherein the taxpayer is unable to pay the deficiency or is able to pay only a part of it. (2) If the Secretary appeals from the judgment of the

Superior Court declaring the nonexistence of a deficiency in whole, or in part, or if the taxpayer having appealed has failed to pay 43

T.§ 3271-1 

Ch. 253

the total amount of the tax, and should the decision of the Supreme Court be favorable to the Secretary, the deficiency determined on appeal or the unpaid balance of the same, will be immediately assessed. (f) The taxpayer may at any time by a signed notice in writing filed with the Secretary waive the restrictions on the assessment of the whole or any part of the deficiency. The notice must in all cases be filed with the Secretary. The filing of such notice with the Superior Court does not constitute filing with the Secretary within the meaning of the Income Tax Act. After such waiver has been acted upon by the Secretary and the assessment has been made in accordance with its terms, the waiver cannot be withdrawn. (g) If a complaint is filed with the Superior Court, the taxpayer should notify the Secretary that the complaint has been filed, in order to prevent an assessment by the Secretary of the amount determined to be the deficiency. If no complaint is filed with the 

Superior Court within the period prescribed, the Secretary shall assess the amount determined by him as the deficiency and of which he has notified the taxpayer by registered mail. In such case the Secretary will not be precluded from determining a further deficiency and notifying the taxpayer thereof by registered mail. 

Where a complaint is filed with the Superior Court, the entire amount redetermined as the deficiency by the judgment of the Superior Court which has become final shall be assessed by the 

Secretary. If the Secretary mails to the taxpayer notice of a deficiency, and the taxpayer files a complaint with the Superior Court within the prescribed period, the Secretary is barred from determining any additional deficiency for the same taxable year except in the case of fraud. § 3272-2. Collection of a deficiency 

Where a deficiency as redetermined by a judgment of the Superior Court which has become final is assessed, or where the taxpayer has not filed a complaint and the deficiency as determined by the Secretary has been assessed, the unpaid portion of the amount so assessed shall be paid upon notice and demand from the 

Secretary. As to interest on deficiencies, see sec. 3292. § 3272-3. Extension of time for payment of a deficiency (a) If it is shown to the satisfaction of the Secretary that the payment of a deficiency upon the date or dates prescribed for the 44

Supp. L

DEFICIENCIES 

payment thereof will result in undue hardship to the taxpayer, the Secretary may grant an extension of time for the payment of the deficiency or any part thereof for a period not in excess of 18 months, and in exceptional cases for a further period not in excess of 12 months. The extension will not be granted upon a general statement of hardship. The term "undue hardship" means more than an inconvenience to the taxpayer. It must appear that substantial financial loss, for example, due to the sale of property at a sacrifice price, will result to the taxpayer from making payment of the deficiency at the due date. If a market exists, the sale of property at the current market price is not ordinarily considered as resulting in an undue hardship. Sec. 3272 (h) provides that no extension will be granted where the deficiency is due to negligence or intentional disregard of rules and regulations or to fraud with intent to evade tax. (b) An application for an extension of time for the payment of a deficiency should be made and must be accompanied or supported by evidence showing the undue hardship that would result to the taxpayer if the extension were refused. The application must be verified by a written declaration that it is made under the penalties of perjury. A statement of assets and liabilities of the taxpayer and an itemized statement showing all receipts and disbursements for each of the three months immediately preceding the month in which falls the date prescribed for the payment of the deficiency are required and should accompany the application. The application with the evidence, must be filed with the Secretary. An application for an extension of time for the payment of a deficiency will not be considered unless request therefor is made on or before the date prescribed for payment thereof, as shown by the notice and demand, or on or before the date or dates prescribed for payment in any prior extension granted. (c) As a condition to the granting of such an extension, the Secretary will usually require the taxpayer to furnish a bond in an amount not exceeding double the amount of the deficiency or to furnish other security satisfactory to the Secretary for the payment of the liability on or before the date or dates prescribed for payment in the extension, so that the risk of loss to the Government will not be greater at the end of the extension period than it was at the beginning of the period. If a bond is required, it shall be conditioned upon the payment of the deficiency, interest, and additional amounts assessed in connection therewith in accordance 45

T.§ 3272-3 

Ch. 253

with the terms of the extension granted, and shall be executed by a surety company, and shall be subject to the approval of the Secretary. In lieu of such a bond, the taxpayer may file a bond secured by deposit of bonds or notes of the United States. The amount of the deficiency and additions thereto shall be paid on or before the expiration of the period of the extension without the necessity of notice and demand from the Secretary. Payment of the deficiency and additions thereto before the expiration of the extension will not relieve the taxpayer from paying the entire amount of interest provided for in the extension. See sec. 3296. § 3273. Jeopardy assessments 

[Text of Act, see 13 L.P.R.A. § 3273.] 

§ 3273-1. Jeopardy assessments (a) If the Secretary believes that the assessment or collection of a deficiency will be jeopardized by delay, he is required to assess such deficiency immediately, together with the interest and other additional amounts provided by law. If a deficiency is assessed on account of jeopardy after the rendition of a judgment by the Superior Court on the merits of such deficiency, the jeopardy assessment may be made only with respect to the deficiency determined by the Superior Court. (b) If notice of a deficiency was mailed to the taxpayer (see sec. 3272(a)) before it was discovered that delay would jeopardize the assessment or collection of the tax, a jeopardy assessment may be made in an amount greater or less than that included in the deficiency notice. On the other hand if the assessment on account of jeopardy was made without mailing the notice required by sec. 

3272 (a), the Secretary must within 30 days after the making of the assessment send the taxpayer notice of the deficiency by registered mail. The taxpayer may file a complaint with the 

Superior Court for a redetermination of the amount of the deficiency within 30 days after such notice is mailed, not counting Saturday, Sunday, or a legal holiday in Puerto Rico as the 30th day. The Secretary may, at any time before the decision of the 

Superior Court is rendered, abate such assessment, or any unpaid portion thereof, to the extent that he believes the assessment to be excessive in amount. If the complaint of the taxpayer is filed with the Superior Court, either before or after the making of the jeopardy assessment, the Secretary is required to notify the 46

Supp. L

DEFICIENCIES 

T.13 § 3273-1 

Superior Court of such assessment or abatement, and the Superior Court has jurisdiction to redetermine the amount of the deficiency together with all other amounts assessed at the same time in connection therewith. (c) After a jeopardy assessment has been made, the Secretary is required to send notice and demand to the taxpayer for the amount of the jeopardy assessment. Regardless of whether the taxpayer has filed a complaint with the Superior Court, he is required to make payment of the amount of such assessment (to the extent that it has not been abated) within 10 days after the sending of notice and demand, unless before the expiration of such 10-day period he files with the Secretary a bond of the character hereinafter prescribed. The bond must be in such amount, not exceeding the amount for which the stay is desired, as the Secretary deems necessary and must be executed by sureties satisfactory to the Secretary. It must be conditioned upon the payment of so much of the amount included therein as is not abated by a final determination of the Secretary or a decision of the Superior Court which has become final, together with the interest on such amount provided for in sec. 3297. If the bond is given before the taxpayer has filed his complaint with the Superior Court, it must contain a further condition that if a complaint is not filed before the expiration of the 30-day period provided for the filing of such complaint, the amount stayed by the bond will be paid upon notice and demand at any time after the expiration of such period, together with interest thereon at the rate of 6 percent per annum from the date of the jeopardy notice and demand to the date of the notice and demand made after the expiration of the 30-day period. If a complaint is not filed with the Superior 

Court within the 30-day period, and, if collection of the deficiency has been stayed by the filing of a bond within 10 days after the date of jeopardy notice and demand, the Secretary will give notice and make demand for payment of the amount assessed plus interest. Any bond filed after the expiration of 10 days from the date of the jeopardy notice and demand is not such a bond as is contemplated by sec. 3273 (d), and, while the Secretary may in his discretion accept the bond and stay collection of the deficiency, the taxpayer will not be relieved from payment of interest on the amount of the deficiency at the rate of 6 percent per annum from the date of the jeopardy notice and demand to the date of payment. 47

Ch. 253

(d) Upon the filing of a bond of the character described within 10 days after the date of notice and demand for payment of the amount assessed, the collection of so much thereof as is covered by the bond will be stayed. The taxpayer may at any time waive the stay of collection of the whole or any part of the amount covered by the bond. If as a result of such waiver any part of the amount covered by the bond is paid, or if any portion of the jeopardy assessment is abated by the Secretary before the decision of the Superior Court is rendered, then the bond shall at the request of the taxpayer be proportionately reduced. If the Superior Court determines that the amount assessed is greater than the correct amount of the tax, the bond will also be proportionately reduced at the request of the taxpayer after the Superior Court renders its decision. (e) After the Superior Court has rendered its decision and such decision has become final, the Secretary will then send notice and demand for the unpaid portion of the amount determined by the Superior Court, the collection of which has been stayed by the bond. The Secretary is required to include in the notice and demand for the unpaid portion, interest at the rate of 6 percent per annum from the date of the jeopardy notice and demand to the date of the notice and demand referred to in this paragraph. If the amount of the jeopardy assessment is less than the amount determined by the Superior Court, the difference, together with interest as provided in sec. 3292, will be assessed, and collected as part of the tax upon notice and demand from the Secretary. If the amount included in the notice and demand made after the decision of the Superior Court is not paid within 10 days after such notice and demand, there shall be collected as part of the tax, interest as provided in sec. 3294 (b). If the amount of the jeopardy assessment is in excess of the amount determined by the Superior Court, the unpaid portion of such excess will be abated. If any part of the excess amount has been paid, it will be credited or refunded to the taxpayer as provided in sec. 3322. § 3274-1. Bankruptcy and receivership proceedings (a) During a bankruptcy proceeding, or a receivership proceeding, the assets of the taxpayer are in general under the control of the court in which such proceeding is pending, and the collection of taxes cannot be made by distraining upon such assets. However, any assets which under applicable provisions of law are not under the control of the court may be subject to distraint. (b) As used in this section and sec. 3274-2, the term "bankruptcy proceeding" includes proceedings under Chapters I to VII of the Bankruptcy Act [11 U.S.C., cc. I-VII], or under sec. 75 or 

77, or Chapters X-XIII of such act; and the term "adjudication of bankruptcy" includes, in addition to an adjudication in a proceeding under Chapters I to VII, the approval of a petition as properly filed under sec. 77 or Chapter X by a court of competent jurisdiction or the filing of a petition under sec. 75 or Chapters 

XI to XIII with a court of competent jurisdiction. (c) A trustee in bankruptcy (including a trustee, receiver, debtor in possession, or other person designated as in control of the assets of a debtor in any bankruptcy proceeding by order of the court in which such proceeding is pending) or a receiver in any receivership proceeding is required to give notice in writing to the 

Secretary of the adjudication of bankruptcy or the appointment of a receiver. 

(e) Under sec. 64 of the Bankruptcy Act [11 U.S.C. § 104], taxes are entitled to the priority over other claims therein stated and the trustee, receiver, debtor in possession, or other person designated as in control of the assets of the debtor by the court in which the bankruptcy or receivership proceeding is pending, may be held personally liable for failure on his part to protect the priority of the Government respecting taxes of which he has notice. Bankruptcy courts have jurisdiction under the Bankruptcy 

Act to determine all disputes regarding the amount and validity of taxes of a bankruptcy or of a debtor in a proceeding under the Bankruptcy Act. A bankruptcy or receivership proceeding does not discharge any portion of a claim of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico for taxes except in the case of a proceeding under Chapter X of the Bankruptcy Act, and except to the extent which may be. provided in a plan or arrangement duly effectuated in a bankruptcy proceeding. Any portion of a claim of Puerto Rico for taxes which has been allowed by the court in which the bankruptcy or receivership proceeding is pending and which remains unsatisfied after the 49

T.S 3274-1 

Ch. 253

termination of the bankruptcy or receivership proceeding shall be collected with interest as provided in sec. 3298. 

Codification. Section contains no subsection (d). § 3274-2. Immediate assessments in bankruptcy and receivership cases (a) If the Secretary has determined that a deficiency is due in respect of income tax and the taxpayer has filed a complaint with the Superior Court prior to the adjudication of bankruptcy or the appointment of a receiver, the trustee, receiver, debtor in possession, or other person designated as in control of the assets of the debtor by the court in which the bankruptcy or receivership proceeding is pending, may prosecute the taxpayer's appeal before the Superior Court as to that particular determination. No complaint shall be filed with the Superior Court for a redetermination of the deficiency after the adjudication of bankruptcy or the appointment of a receiver. (b) Claim for the amount of a deficiency, even though pending before the Superior Court for consideration, may be filed with the court in which the bankruptcy or receivership proceeding is pending without awaiting final decision of the Superior Court. In case of final decision of the Superior Court before the termination of the bankruptcy or receivership proceeding, a copy of the Superior Court's decision may be filed by the Secretary with the court in which such proceeding is pending. (c) While the Secretary is required by sec. 3274 to make immediate assessment of any deficiency, such assessment is not made as a jeopardy assessment within the meaning of sec. 3273, and consequently the provisions of that section do not apply to any assessment made under sec. 3274. Therefore, the notice of the deficiency provided for in sec. 3273 (b) will not be mailed. Although such notice will not be issued, nevertheless a letter will be sent to the taxpayer, or to the trustee, receiver, debtor in possession, or other person designated by the court in which the bankruptcy or receivership proceeding is pending as in control of the assets of the debtor, notifying him in detail how the deficiency was computed, that he may furnish evidence showing wherein the deficiency is incorrect, and that upon request he will be granted a hearing with respect to such deficiency. If after such evidence is submitted and hearing held any adjustment appears necessary in the deficiency, appropriate action will be taken.

[Text of Act, see 13 L.P.R.A. § 3275.] 

§ 3275-1. Period of limitation upon assessment of tax

The amount of income tax imposed by this Act must be assessed within four years after the return was filed. For the purposes of subsections (a), (b), (c), and (e) of sec. 3275, a return filed before the last day prescribed by law for the filing thereof shall be considered as filed on such last day. Exceptions to the period of limitation stated in this section (other than those provided for elsewhere in the Act) are as follows: (a) In the case of income received during the lifetime of a decedent or by his estate during the period of administration, or by a corporation or partnership contemplating dissolution, the tax shall be assessed within 18 months after written request therefor by the fiduciary or legal representative of the estate of the decedent or by the corporation or partnership, but not after the expiration of four years after the return was filed. The effect of this provision is to limit the period in which the Secretary may assess the tax in such cases to a period of 18 months from the date the request is filed, even though more than 18 months still remain of the regular 4-year period in which the assessment may under ordinary circumstances be made. The request, in order to be effective, must be made after the return is filed and must be in such language as to make it clear to the Secretary that it is desired to take advantage of the provisions of sec. 3275(b). In 51

T.§ 3275-1 

Ch. 253

the case of a corporation or partnership the 18-month period of limitation shall not apply unless (1) The written request notifies the Secretary that the corporation or partnership contemplates dissolution at or before the expiration of such period, (2) The dissolution is in good faith begun before the expiration of such period, and (3) The dissolution so begun is completed either before or after the expiration of such 18-month period. 

Such a request does not have the effect of extending the regular period of limitation even though the request is made less than 18 months before the expiration of the regular period of limitation. (b) If a corporation or partnership makes no income tax return under the Income Tax Act, but each of the shareholders or partners includes in his personal return his distributive share of the net income of the corporation or partnership, the tax of the corporation or partnership shall be assessed within five years after the last date on which any such shareholder's or partner's return was filed. (c) In the case of a false or fraudulent return with intent to evade tax, the tax may be assessed at any time after such false or fraudulent return is filed. 

(d) If there is omitted from the gross income stated in the return an amount properly includible therein which is in excess of 25 percent of the gross income so stated, the tax may be assessed at any time within six years after the return was filed. (e) In the event the taxpayer fails to file a return, the amount of tax due may be assessed at any time after the date prescribed for filing the return. But see paragraph (b) of this section. (f) If the taxpayer omits from gross income an amount properly includible therein under secs. 3115 (c) or 3186 as an amount distributed in liquidation of a corporation or partnership, the tax may be assessed at any time within five years after the return was filed. (g) If before the expiration of the time prescribed in sec. 3275 for the assessment of the tax the Secretary and the taxpayer have consented in writing to the assessment of the tax after such time, the tax may be assessed at any time prior to the expiration of the period agreed upon. The period agreed upon may be extended by subsequent agreements in writing made before the expiration of the period previously agreed upon. 52

3291. Failure to file return 

[Text of Act, see 13 L.P.R.A. § 3291.] 

§ 3291-1. Addition to the tax in case of failure to file return (a) In case of failure to make and file a return required by the Act within the prescribed time, a certain percent of the amount of the tax is added to the tax unless failure to file the return within the prescribed time is shown to the satisfaction of the Secretary to be due to reasonable cause and not to willful neglect. The amount to be added to the tax is 5 percent if the failure is for not more than 30 days, with an additional 5 percent for each additional 30 days or fraction thereof during which failure continues, not to exceed 

25 percent in the aggregate. (b) A taxpayer who wishes to avoid the addition to the tax for delinquency must make an affirmative showing of all facts alleged as a reasonable cause for failure to file the return on time in the form of a written statement containing a declaration that it is made under penalties of perjury, which should be filed with the Secretary, and, if the Secretary determines that the delinquency was due to a reasonable cause, and not to willful neglect, the addition to the tax will not be assessed. If the taxpayer exercised ordinary business care and prudence and was nevertheless unable 55

T.133291 

Ch. 253

to file the return within the prescribed time, then the delay is due to a reasonable cause. (c) If the addition to the tax for delinquency in filing the return has been added, the amount so added shall be collected in the same manner as the tax. (d) For addition to the tax in case of a deficiency due to fraud with intent to evade tax, see sec. 3293. As to the making of returns for taxpayers by the Secretary in the case of delinquency in filing a return, see sec. 3416. § 3294. Additions to the tax in case of nonpayment 

[Text of Act, see 13 L.P.R.A. § 3294.] § 3294-1. Additions to the tax 

(a) In general. Sec. 3294 (d) provides for certain additions to the tax in the case of (1) Failure to file timely a declaration of estimated tax; (2) Failure to pay within the time prescribed any installment of declared estimated tax; and (3) Substantial underestimate of the estimated tax. 

These additions to the tax are in addition to any applicable criminal penalties. (b) Additions for specific failures on the part of the taxpayer with respect to the estimated tax. (1) Failure to file declaration. (i) Sec. 3294(d)(1)(A) provides for an addition to the tax in the case of a failure to make and file a declaration of estimated tax within the time prescribed unless such failure is shown to the satisfaction of the Secretary to be due to reasonable cause and not due to willful neglect. Such addition to the tax shall be in an amount equal to 5 percent of the unpaid amount of each installment and in addition 1 percent of the unpaid amount of the installment for each month (except the first) or fraction thereof during which such amount remains unpaid. Such addition. to the tax with respect to any installment due but unpaid shall not exceed 10 percent of the unpaid portion of such installment. 

For the purposes of sec. 3294(d) (1) (A), the amount and due date of each installment shall be the same as if a declaration had been filed within the time prescribed showing an estimated tax equal to the correct tax reduced by the credits for tax withheld at source. (1 56

(ii) The addition to the tax for substantial underestimate of the estimated tax shall not apply to the taxable year in which the taxpayer makes a timely payment of estimated tax within or before each quarter of such year in an amount at least as great as though such estimated tax were computed on the basis of the taxpayer's status with respect to the personal exemption and credit for dependents on the date of filing the declaration, and on the basis of the tax withheld, and reasonably expected on the date of the filing of the declaration to be withheld, on wages received during the calendar year ending with or within the taxable year, but otherwise as though such estimated tax were computed on the basis of the net income shown on the taxpayer's return for the preceding taxable year. The net income shown on the taxpayer's return for the preceding taxable year shall be considered to be zero for the purposes of this section if for such year the taxpayer did not file a return and was not required to file a return. In the case of farmers exercising an election under sec. 3060 (a), such addition to the tax shall not apply to the taxable year in which the taxpayer makes a timely payment of estimated tax within the last quarter of such year in an amount at least as great as though computed on the basis of the taxpayer's status with respect to the personal exemption and credit for dependents on the date of filing the declaration, but otherwise 59

Example (2). A, a professional man made a return on January 10, 1955, for the calendar year 1954. A was entitled to the exemption of a married person for 1954. However, for 1955 he was entitled to only the exemption of a single person as he was not the head of a household. On April 15, 1955, A filed a declaration of estimated tax on which estimated tax for 1955 was shown in the amount of $11,000. He made payment of the estimated tax in four installments of $2,750 each on April 15, June 15, and September 15, 1955, and January 15, 1956. As a result of a transaction occurring in December 

1955, A received taxable income in an amount which made him subject to a tax for the calendar year 1955 in the amount of $15,000. A's tax at 1955 rates on 1954 income amounts to $10,940. 

Since the installments of $2,750 each were timely paid for each quarter and each was at least as great as one-fourth of $10,940, A is not subject to the penalty for underestimating the tax for 1955.

(a) The amount for which a transferee of the property of a taxpayer is liable, at law or in equity, and the amount of the personal liability of a fiduciary under sec. 3142 (d) in respect of any income tax imposed by the Act, whether shown on the return of the taxpayer or determined as a deficiency in the tax, shall be assessed against such transferee or such fiduciary, as the case may be, and collected and paid in the same manner and subject to the same provisions and limitations as in the case of a deficiency in the tax imposed by the Act, except as hereinafter provided. The period so agreed upon may be extended by subsequent agreements in writing made before the expiration of the period previously agreed upon. § 3312. Notice of Fiduciary relationship [Text of Act, see 13 L.P.R.A. § 3312.] § 3312-1. Fiduciaries 

(a) As soon as the Secretary receives notice that a person is acting in a fiduciary capacity, such fiduciary must, except as otherwise specifically provided, assume the powers, rights, duties, and privileges of the taxpayer with respect to income tax imposed by the Act. If the person is acting as a fiduciary for a transferee or other person subject to the liability specified in sec. 3311, such fiduciary is required to assume the powers, rights, duties, and privileges of the transferee or other person under that section. 

The amount of the tax or liability is ordinarily not collectible from the personal estate of the fiduciary but is collectible from the estate of the taxpayer or from the estate of the transferee or other person subject to the liability specified in sec. 3311. The "notice to the 

Secretary" provided for in sec. 3312 shall be a written notice signed by the fiduciary and filed with the Secretary. The notice must state the name and address of the person for whom the fiduciary is acting, and the nature of the liability of such person; that is, whether it is a liability for tax, and, if so, the year or years involved, or a liability at law or in equity of a transferee of property of a taxpayer, or a liability of a fiduciary under sec. 3142(d), in respect of the payment of any tax from the estate of the taxpayer. Unless there is already on file with the Secretary satisfactory evidence of the authority of the fiduciary to act for such person in a fiduciary capacity, such evidence must be filed with and made a part of the notice. If the fiduciary capacity exists by order of court, a certified copy of the order may be regarded as such satisfactory evidence. 

When the fiduciary capacity has terminated, the fiduciary in order to be relieved of any further duty or liability as such, must file with the Secretary written notice that the fiduciary capacity has terminated as to him, accompanied by satisfactory evidence of the termination of the fiduciary capacity. The notice of termination should state the name and address of the person, if any, who has been substituted as fiduciary. 63

T.§ 3312-1 

Ch. 253

(b) If the notice of the fiduciary capacity described in paragraph (a) of this section is not filed with the Secretary before the sending of notice of a deficiency by registered mail to the last known address of the taxpayer (see sec. 3272(a)), or the last known address of the transferee or other person subject to liability (see sec. 3311), no notice of the deficiency will be sent to the fiduciary. In such a case the sending of the notice to the last known address of the taxpayer, transferee, or other person, as the case may be, will be a sufficient compliance with the requirements of the Income Tax Act, even though such taxpayer, transferee, or other person is deceased, or is under a legal disability, or, in the case of a corporation or partnership, has terminated its existence. 

Under such circumstances if no complaint is filed with the Superior Court within 60 days after the mailing of the notice to the taxpayer, transferee, or other person, the tax, or liability under sec. 

3311, will be assessed immediately upon the expiration of such 60-day period, and demand for payment will be made by the Secretary. (c) The term "fiduciary" is defined in sec. 3411 (a) (6) to mean a guardian, trustee, executor, administrator, receiver, conservator, or any person acting in any fiduciary capacity for any person. (d) This section, relating to the provisions of sec. 3312, shall not be taken to abridge in any way the powers and duties of fiduciaries provided for in other sections of the Income Tax Act.

§ 3322-1. Authority for abatement, credit, and refund of tax

Authority for the credit and refund of any overpayment of any income tax imposed by the Income Tax Act of 1954 is contained in sec. 3322. Sec. 3273 (i) prohibits the filing of claims for abatement by taxpayers with respect to assessments of income tax imposed by the Act. 

§ 3322-2. Credit and refund adjustments 

Credits or refunds of overpayments may not be allowed or made after the expiration of the statutory period of limitation properly applicable unless, before the expiration of such period, a claim therefor has been filed by the taxpayer. The claim, together with appropriate supporting evidence, must be filed with the Secretary through the office of the collector of internal revenue or Bureau of Income Tax in which the tax was paid. Where an amount of tax in excess of that properly due has been paid by a withholding agent, the credit or refund of such excess amount shall be made to the withholding agent unless the amount of such tax was actually withheld by the withholding agent. See sec. 3143 (e). As to interest in case of credits or refunds, see sec. 3324. § 3322-3. Claims for refund by taxpayers (a) Claims by the taxpayer for the refunding of taxes, interest, penalties, and additions to tax erroneously or illegally collected shall be made on Form 452.0 or on Form 480.0 or 480.0A, or an amended return, and should be filed with the collection of internal revenue or Bureau of Income Tax. A separate claim shall be made for each taxable year or period. (b) No refund or credit will be allowed after the expiration of the statutory period of limitation applicable to the filing of a claim therefor except upon one or more of the grounds set forth in a claim filed before the expiration of such period. The claim must set forth in detail each ground upon which a refund is claimed, and facts sufficient to apprise the Secretary of the exact basis thereof. 

The statements of the grounds and facts must be verified by a written declaration that they are made under the penalties of perjury. A properly executed return on Form 480.0 shall, at the election of the taxpayer, constitute a claim for refund or credit within the meaning of sec. 3322 for the amount of the overpayment disclosed by such return. For the purposes of sec. 3322, such claim shall be considered as filed on the date on which such return is 65

T.§ 3322-3 

Ch. 253

considered as filed. An election to treat the return as a claim for refund or credit shall be evidenced by a statement on the return setting forth the amount determined as an overpayment and advising whether such amount shall be refunded to the taxpayer or shall be applied as a credit against the taxpayer's estimated tax for the taxable year immediately succeeding the taxable year for which such return is filed. If the taxpayer elects to have all or part of the overpayment shown by his return applied to his estimated tax for his succeeding taxable year, no interest shall be allowed on such portion of the overpayment credited and such amount shall be applied as a payment on account of the estimated tax for such year or the installments thereof. The filing of a properly executed return on Form 480.0A shall constitute an election by the taxpayer to have the return treated as a claim for refund and such return shall constitute a claim for refund within the meaning of sec. 3322 for the amount of the overpayment shown by the Secretary's computation of the tax on the basis of the return. For the purposes of sec. 3322, such claim shall be considered as filed on the date on which such return is considered as filed. In any case in which a taxpayer elects to have an overpayment refunded to him he may not thereafter change his election to have the overpayment applied as a payment on account of his estimated tax. A claim which does not comply with this paragraph will not be considered for any purpose as a claim for refund. With respect to limitations upon the refunding or crediting of taxes, see secs. 3322-7 to 3322-11, inclusive. (c) If a return is filed by an individual and, after his death, a refund claim is filed by his legal representative, certified copies of the letters testamentary, letters of administration, or other similar evidence must be annexed to the claim, to show the authority of the legal representative to file the claim. If an executor, administrator, guardian, trustee, receiver, or other fiduciary files a return and thereafter a refund claim is filed by the same fiduciary, documentary evidence to establish the legal authority of the fiduciary need not accompany the claim, provided a statement is made in the claim showing that the return was filed by the fiduciary and that the latter is still acting. In such cases, if a refund is to be paid, letters testamentary, letters of administration, or other evidence may be required, but should be submitted only upon the receipt of a specific request therefor. If a claim is filed by a fiduciary other than the one by whom the 66

return was filed, the necessary documentary evidence should accompany the claim. (d) A claim may be executed by an agent of the person assessed, but in such case a power of attorney must accompany the claim. (e) Checks in payment of claims allowed will be drawn in the names of the persons entitled to the money and may be sent to such persons in care of an attorney or agent who has filed a power of attorney specifically authorizing him to receive such checks. 

The Secretary may, however, send any such check direct to the claimant. (f) The Secretary has no authority to refund on equitable grounds penalties or other amounts legally collected. Claim for payment of judgment obtained against Secretary (a) A claim for the amount of a judgment against the Secretary of the Treasury for the recovery of taxes, penalties, or other sums should be made on a properly executed Form 452.0, and filed directly with the Secretary. The claim must be verified by a written declaration that it is made under the penalties of perjury. 

Two certified copies of the final judgment should be attached to the claim. If the judgment specifically provides for the recovery of court costs, an itemized bill of the court costs paid, receipted by the clerk of the court, should also accompany the claim. If the case was appealed, two certified copies of the mandate of the Supreme Court should also be attached to the claim. A judgment will not be paid until the period for appeal has expired unless a stipulation, signed by both parties to the suit, waiving the right to appeal, has been filed with the clerk of the court, and two certified copies of such waiver are furnished to the Secretary. § 3322-7. Limitations upon crediting and refunding of taxes paid; general rule (a) Unless a claim for credit or refund of an overpayment is filed within four years from the time the return was filed by the taxpayer or within three years from the time the tax was paid, the Secretary is prohibited from allowing or making a credit or refund of income tax imposed by the Act for such year after both periods have expired. If no return is filed by the taxpayer, the 

Secretary is prohibited from allowing or making a credit or refund 67

T.S 3322-7 

Ch. 253

of such tax after three years from the time the tax was paid unless, before the expiration of such 3-year period, a claim therefor is filed. 

The amount of the credit or refund in any case shall not exceed the portion of the tax paid (1) If a return was filed by the taxpayer, and the claim was filed within four years from the time the return was filed, during the four years immediately preceding the filing of the claim. (2) If a claim was filed, and (i) no return was filed, or (ii) if the claim was not filed within four years from the time the return was filed by the taxpayer, during the three years immediately preceding the filing of the claim. (3) If no claim was filed and the allowance of credit or refund is made within four years from the time the return was filed by the taxpayer, during the four years immediately preceding the allowance of the credit or refund. 

(4) If no claim was filed, and (i) no return was filed or (ii) the allowance of the credit or refund is not made within four years from the time the return was filed by the taxpayer, during the three years immediately preceding the allowance of the credit or refund. (b) For the purposes of this section and secs. 3322-8 to 3322–11, inclusive, a return filed before the last day prescribed by law for the filing thereof, or an advance payment of any portion of the tax made before such date, shall be considered as filed or made on the last day prescribed by law for the filing of such return or the payment of such tax. If the taxpayer elected to pay the tax in installments, such an advance payment shall be considered as made on the last day prescribed for the payment of the first installment, but in all cases the last day prescribed by law for filing the return or paying the tax shall be determined without regard to any extension of time granted the taxpayer for filing the return or paying the tax. The provisions of this article are subject to the exceptions provided in secs. 3322-8 to 3322-11, inclusive.

In any such case, the decision of the Superior Court as to whether the statutory period upon collection of the tax expired before notice of the deficiency was mailed shall, when the decision becomes final, be conclusive. § 3322-11. § 3361-1. Taxation of registered investment companies (a) If for any taxable year beginning after December 31, 1953, a registered investment company has during its entire taxable year fulfilled all of the requirements and conditions provided in any Act of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico relative to investment companies it shall be taxed as a domestic corporation, except that: (1) The provisions of sec. 3102 providing for additional surtax on corporations improperly accumulating surplus is not applicable; (2) There must be included in gross income all dividends and profit distributions received from corporations and partnerships which are themselves exempt from income tax under Act No. 184, approved May 13, 1948 [13 L.P.R.A. §§ 221 to 238] as amended or supplemented by any other tax exemption Act of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico; (3) The gains or losses from the sale or other disposition of capital assets shall be disregarded; 75

T.§ 3361-1 C 

Ch. 253 (4) The net operating loss deduction provided in sec. 3023 (s) shall be disregarded; and (5) The provisions of sec. 3047 (c) providing that the net income for a short period on account of a change in the accounting period is to be placed on an annual basis, shall be disregarded. (b) If a registered investment company distributes during the taxable year to its shareholders as taxable dividends or as dividends from industrial development income (see sec. 3361-2), an amount not less than 90 percent of its net income for the taxable year computed as provided in paragraph (a) of this section, there shall be allowed to such company as a credit against net income for the purposes of both, the normal tax and the surtax, the amount of said dividends paid during the taxable year. (c) In determining whether a registered investment company distributes during the taxable year to its shareholders as taxable dividends or as dividends from industrial development income an amount not less than 90 percent of its net income for the taxable year, any taxable dividend or dividend from industrial development income declared by the company after the close of such taxable year and before the time prescribed by law for the filing of its return for such taxable year (including the period of any extension of time granted for filing such return) shall, to the extent the company so elects in such return, be treated as having been paid during such taxable year. This rule is applicable only if distribution of the entire amount of such dividend is actually made to shareholders in the four-month period following the close of such taxable year and not later than the date of the first regular dividend payment made after such declaration. (d) The election referred to in the preceding paragraph must be made in the return filed by the company for the taxable year. 

The election shall be made by the taxpayer by treating the dividend to which such election applies as a dividend paid credit for the taxable year in computing its net income subject to tax. The election provided in sec. 3361(a)(3) may be made only to the extent that the earnings and profits of the taxable year exceed the total amount of distributions out of such earnings and profits actually made during the taxable year (not including distributions with respect to which a prior election has been made under sec. 

3361(a)(3)). The dividend with respect to which the registered investment company has made a valid election under sec. 3361 (a) (3), shall be considered as paid out of earnings and profits of the 76

After the expiration of the time for filing the return for the taxable year for which an election is made under sec. 3361 (a) (3), such election shall be irrevocable with respect to the dividend to which it applies. (e) A taxable dividend or a dividend from industrial development income is not distributed to its shareholders during the taxable year within the meaning of sec. 3361 (a), unless the dividend is received by the shareholders during the taxable year of the company. Meaning of terms used in sec. 3361 (a) Exempt dividends. The term "exempt dividend" is defined in sec. 3361 (c) (1) to mean any dividend or portion thereof which is designated as such by a registered investment company in a written notice mailed to its shareholders within 60 days after the close of its taxable year. Such dividend must be paid out of current or accumulated earnings and profits attributable to income exempt from tax under sec. 3022 (b). If the aggregate amount so designated with respect to a taxable year of the company is greater than its current or accumulated earnings and profits attributable to income exempt from tax under sec. 3022 (b), then the portion of each distribution which shall be considered an exempt dividend shall be only that proportion of the amount so designated by the investment company which such current or accumulated earnings and profits attributable to income exempt from tax bear to the aggregate amount of dividends so designated. (b) Dividends from industrial development income The term "dividend from industrial development income" as defined in sec. 3361 (c) (2) means any dividend or portion thereof which is designated as such by a registered investment company in a written notice mailed to shareholders within 60 days after the close of its taxable year. Such dividend must be paid out of current 77

to 238], as amended or supplemented by any other tax exemption. 

Act of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, made by such corporations or partnerships from the income derived from the operations covered by the exemption. If the aggregate amount designated by a registered investment company as "dividends from industrial development income" is greater than its current or accumulated earnings and profits attributable to dividends or distributions from corporations and partnerships holding grants of tax exemption under any Commonwealth law, then the portion of each distribution which shall be considered a dividend from industrial development income shall be only that proportion of the amount so designated by the investment company which such current or accumulated industrial development earnings and profits bear to the aggregate amount of dividends so designated. (c) Capital gain dividends. The term "capital gain dividend" is defined in sec. 3361 (c) (3) to mean any dividend or portion thereof distributed by a registered investment company out of its current or accumulated earnings and profits attributable to gains from the sale or other disposition of property. (d) Taxable dividends. The term "taxable dividend" means any dividend distribution or portion thereof made by a registered investment company out of its current or accumulated earnings and profits which does not qualify either as (1) an exempt dividend, (2) a dividend from industrial development income, or (3) a capital gain dividend, as such dividends are defined in sec. 3361 (c). § 3361-3. 3403-1. Taxpayers to whom Supplement T is inapplicable § 3400. Imposition of tax 

[Text of Act, see 13 L.P.R.A. § 3400.] § 3400-1. Scope and application of Supplement T 

(a) (1) In lieu of the taxes imposed by secs. 3011, 3012 and 3406, an individual may elect to pay the tax imposed by sec. 3400 if his adjusted gross income is less than $5,000, regardless of the sources from which such income is derived and regardless of whether such income is computed on the cash basis or on the accrual basis. (2) The application of subparagraph (1) of this paragraph may be illustrated by the following example:

Example. A is employed at a salary of $4,600 for the calendar year 1954. 

In the course of such employment, he incurred travel expenses of $750 for which he was reimbursed during the year. Such items constitute his sole income for 1954. In such case the gross income is $5,350 but the amount of $750 is deducted from gross income in the determination of adjusted gross income and thus A's adjusted gross income for 1954 is $4,600. Hence, the adjusted gross income being less than $5,000, he may elect to pay his tax for 1954 under Supplement T. Similarly, in the case of an individual engaged in trade or business (excluding from the term "engaged in trade or business" the performance of personal services as an employee), there may be deducted from gross income in ascertaining adjusted gross income those expenses directly relating to the carrying on of such trade or business. (b) (1) For the purposes of determining whether a taxpayer may elect to pay the tax under Supplement T, the amount of the adjusted gross income is controlling, without reference to the credits for personal exemption and dependents to which the taxpayer may be entitled. (2) The application of subparagraph (1) of this paragraph may be illustrated by the following example:

Example. If X has, as his only income for 1954, a salary of $5,800 and his spouse has no gross income and derives her entire support from X, then X's adjusted gross income is $5,800 (not $5,800 minus $2,000 or $3,800) and he is not, for such year, entitled to pay his tax under Supplement T. If, however, X has for 1954 a salary of $6,000 and incident to his employment he incurs 82

Supp. T T.13 § 3401-1 

INCOME LESS THAN $5,000 

expenses in the amount of $1,200 for travel, meals, and lodging while away from home, the adjusted gross income is $6,000 minus $1,200, or $4,800. In such case his adjusted gross income being less than $5,000, X may elect to pay the tax under Supplement T. If, however, X's wife has adjusted gross income of $200, thus bringing the aggregate adjusted gross income to $5,000, the taxpayer cannot elect to pay the tax under Supplement T. (c) To determine the amount of the tax, the individual ascertains the amount of his adjusted gross income, refers to the table set forth in sec. 3400, ascertains the income bracket into which such income falls, and finds the tax in the vertical column having at the top thereof a subheading descriptive of his marital status (whether single, married, or head of family) and a number corresponding to the number of dependents to which the taxpayer is entitled. Thus, if for 1954 A has adjusted gross income of $4,715, and he is married living with his wife with one dependent minor child, his tax is $232. (d) In the case of an individual entitled to either or both of the deductions provided by subsecs. 3023 (bb) and (cc), sec. 3400 provides that there be subtracted from his adjusted gross income the amount to which he is entitled on account of such deductions plus an amount equal to 10 percent of such amount, and the remainder shall be the amount of income subject to tax under Supplement T. The adjusted gross income must be less than $5,000 prior to the subtraction of the deductions provided by subsecs. 

3023 (bb) and/or (cc) for an individual to be entitled to elect to pay the tax under Supplement T. (e) The fact that the taxable year is a period of less than 12 months resulting by reason of the death of the taxpayer does not prevent the application of Supplement T in the determination of the tax for such period. § 3401. Rules for application of sec. 3400 

[Text of Act, see 13 L.P.R.A. § 3401.] 

§ 3401-1. Rules for application of table in sec. 3400 (a) For taxable years beginning after December 31, 1953, the determination of whether a taxpayer is a single person, a married person, or the head of a family, or whether he has a dependent, is to be made as of the close of such taxpayer's taxable year or, in the event of the death of his spouse during the taxable year, upon the date of such death. A married person not a head of a family and not living with husband or wife is treated as a single person. For definitions of the terms "dependent" and "head of a 83

T.§ 3401-1 

Ch. 253 family" see secs. 3025(d), 3025-2 and 3025-4. After the marital status and number of dependents, if any, as of the close of the taxable year is ascertained, the tax under Supplement T for the taxable year is determined by reference to the table contained in sec. 3400 and by reference to the column of such table appropriate to the status of the taxpayer (whether single, married or head of a family) and to the number of his dependents. The tax is the amount in such column shown on the line appropriate to the taxpayer's adjusted gross income. (b) The application of this section may be illustrated by the following examples:

Example (1). For the calendar year 1954 A, an unmarried person, has a gross income of $2,832, derived from salary and interest. He is not entitled to any of the business deductions specified in sec. 3022(n), thus his gross income of $2,832 constitutes adjusted gross income. A's status on December 31, 1954, is that of a single person. To determine the tax imposed upon him for the calendar year 1954 under sec. 3400, A refers to the column of the table applicable to a single person who has no dependents (in this instance column one), and finds that the tax imposed upon a single individual whose adjusted gross income falls within the bracket running from $2,825 to $2,850 is $221. 

Since $2,832 is within this bracket, A's tax is $221. 

Example (2). B, a married man whose duties as an employee require traveling away from his home, has as his sole gross income a salary of $5,600 for the calendar year 1954. His traveling expenses, including cost of meals and lodging, amount in such year to $750, and, hence, his adjusted gross income is $4,850. His wife, C, has as her sole income dividends of $85, and thus the aggregate adjusted gross income of B and C is $4,935. B has two dependent children neither of whom has any income. B and C file a joint return for 1954 on Form 480.0, electing not to use the optional return Form 480.0A. 

The adjusted gross income falls within the tax bracket $4,925-$4,950. By referring to such tax bracket in the table and to the column headed "Or; (2) Taxpayer is married and has —", in this case, "Two Dependents", the tax is found to be $207.

Example (3). For the calendar year 1954, D has a gross income of $2,965, derived wholly from wages. His wife had died during 1953 and on December 

31, 1954, D is supporting and maintaining a home for two dependent children both of whom are under the age of 21. Neither dependent has a gross income of as much as $400. Since D would not occupy the status of head of a family except for the fact that he maintains a home for such children, the credit in respect of one of such dependents is disallowed by sec. 3025 (b) (2). However, provision is made for this limitation in the table contained in sec. 3400. To determine his tax for the calendar year 1954, D refers to column 5 of the table (applicable to head of family with two dependents) and finds that the tax in the case of a taxpayer whose adjusted gross income falls in the bracket running from $2,950 to $2,975 is $34. Since $2,965 the gross income and adjusted gross income of D is within this bracket, his tax is $34. (c) Payments to a wife in the nature of, or in lieu of, alimony which are includible in her gross income under secs. 3022 (k) and 

3171 may not be considered as a payment by her husband for the support of any dependent (for definition of husband and wife for purposes of this sentence, see sec. 3411(a) (14)). 84

§ 3411. Definitions [Text of Act, see 13 L.P.R.A. § 3411.] § 3411-1. Classification of taxables 

For the purpose of taxation the Income Tax Act makes its own 86

Ch. 254

T.13 S 3411-3 

MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS 

classification and prescribes its own standards of classification. 

Thus, a trust may be classed as a trust or as an association (and, therefore, as a corporation), depending upon its nature or its activities. See sec. 3411-3. The term "partnership" is not limited to the common meaning of partnership, but is broader in its scope and includes groups not commonly called partnerships. See sec. 

3411-4. The term "corporation" is not limited to the artificial entity usually known as a corporation, but includes also an association, a trust classed as an association because of its nature or its activities, a joint-stock company, an insurance company, and certain kinds of partnerships. See secs. 3411-2 and 3411-4. The definitions, terms, and classifications, as set forth in sec. 3411, shall have the same respective meaning and scope in these regulations. 

§ 3411-2. Association 

The term "association" is not used in the Income Tax Act in any narrow or technical sense. It includes any organization, created for the transaction of designated affairs, or the attainment of some object, which, like a corporation, continues notwithstanding that its members or participants change, and the affairs of which, like corporate affairs, are conducted by a single individual, a committee, a board, or some other group, acting in a representative capacity. 

It is immaterial whether such organization is created by an agreement, a declaration of trust, a statute, or otherwise. It includes a voluntary association, a joint-stock association or company, a "business" trust, a "Massachusetts" trust, a "common law" trust, an interinsurance exchange operating through an attorney in fact, a partnership association, and any other type of organization (by whatever name known) which is not, within the meaning of the Act, a trust or an estate, or a partnership. An "investment" trust of the type commonly known as a management trust is an association, and a trust of the type commonly known as a fixed investment trust is an association if there is power under the trust agreement to vary the investment of the certificate holders. If the conduct of the affairs of a corporation continues after the expiration of its charter, or the termination of its existence, it becomes an association. 

§ 3411-3. Association distinguished from trust 

(a) The term "trust", as used in the Income Tax Act, refers to an ordinary trust, namely, one created by will or by declaration of 87

T.3411-3 

Ch. 254 the trustees or the grantor, the trustees of which take title to the property for the purpose of protecting or conserving it. The beneficiaries of such a trust generally do no more than accept the benefits thereof and are not the voluntary planners or creators of the trust arrangement. Even though the beneficiaries do create such a trust, it is ordinarily done to conserve the trust property without undertaking any activity not strictly necessary to the attainment of that object. (b) As distinguished from the ordinary trust described in the preceding paragraph there is an arrangement whereby the legal title to the property is conveyed to trustees (or a trustee) who, under a declaration or agreement of trust, hold and manage the property with a view to income or profit for the benefit of beneficiaries. Such an arrangement is designed (whether expressly or otherwise) to afford a medium whereby an income or profit-seeking activity may be carried on through a substitute for an organization such as a voluntary association or a joint-stock company or a corporation, thus obtaining the advantages of those forms of organization without their disadvantages. The nature and purpose. of a cooperative undertaking will differentiate it from an ordinary trust. The purpose will not be considered narrower than that which is formally set forth in the instrument under which the activities of the trust are conducted. (c) If a trust is an undertaking or arrangement conducted for income or profit, the capital or property of the trust being supplied by the beneficiaries, and if the trustees or other designated persons are, in effect, the managers of the undertaking or arrangement, whether the beneficiaries do or do not appoint or control them, the beneficiaries are to be treated as voluntarily joining or cooperating with each other in the trust, just as do members of an association, and the undertaking or arrangement is deemed to be an association classified by the Income Tax Act as a corporation. 

However, the fact that the capital or property of the trust is not supplied by the beneficiaries is not sufficient reason in itself for classifying the arrangement as an ordinary trust rather than as an association. (d) By means of such a trust the disadvantages of an ordinary partnership are avoided, and the trust form affords the advantages of unity of management and continuity of existence which are characteristic of both associations and corporations. This trust form also affords the advantages of capacity, as a unit, to acquire, 88

Ch. T.13 § 3411-4 

MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS 

hold, and dispose of property and the ability to sue and be sued by strangers or members, which are characteristic of a corporation; and also frequently affords the limitation of liability and other advantages characteristic of a corporation. These advantages which the trust form provides are frequently referred to as resemblance to the general form, mode of procedure, or effectiveness in action, of an association or a corporation, or as "quasicorporate form". The effectiveness in action in the case of a trust or of a corporation does not depend upon technical arrangements or devices such as the appointment or election of a president, secretary, treasurer, or other "officer", the use of a "seal", the issuance of certificates to the beneficiaries, the holding of meetings by managers or beneficiaries, the use of a "charter" or "by laws", the existence of "control" by the beneficiaries over the affairs of the organization, or upon other minor elements. They serve to emphasize the fact that an organization possessing them should be treated as a corporation, but they are not essential to such classification, for the fundamental benefits enjoyed by a corporation, as outlined above, are attained, in the case of a trust, by the use of the trust form itself. The Income Tax Act disregards the technical distinction between a trust agreement (or declaration) and ordinary articles of association or a corporate charter, and all other differences of detail. It treats such a trust according to its essential nature, namely, as an association. This is true whether the beneficiaries form the trust or, by purchase or otherwise, acquire an interest in an existing trust. (e) The mere size or amount of capital invested in the trust is of no importance. Sometimes the activity of the trust is a small venture or enterprise, such as the division and sale of a parcel of land, the erection of a building, or the care and rental of an office building or apartment house; sometimes the activity is a trade or business on a much larger scale. The distinction is that between the activity or purpose for which an ordinary strict trust of the traditional type would be created and the activity or purpose for which a corporation for profit might have been formed. 

§ 3411-4. Partnerships 

For the purpose of income taxation, partnerships are, in general, treated in the same manner and are subject to the same provisions as corporations. In other words, a partnership is required to make a return of its income as an entity, and the normal tax and surtax 89

T.§ 3411-4 

Ch. 254

is paid upon the net income, subject to tax, or the partnership. 

Included within the term "corporation" as used in the Act are limited partnerships, joint stock companies, limited liability joint stock companies, private corporations and insurance companies, and any other associations receiving income or making profits taxable under the Act. The term "partnership" is defined to include not only civil, business, industrial, agricultural, or professional partnerships, but also all other partnerships, and it includes two or more persons engaged in a joint venture for profit. 

§ 3411-7. Insurance company 

(a) Insurance companies include both stock and mutual companies, as well as mutual benefit insurance companies. A voluntary unincorporated association of employees formed for the purpose of relieving sick and aged members and the dependents of deceased members is an insurance company, whether the fund for such purpose is created wholly by membership dues or partly by contributions from the employer. A corporation which merely sets. aside a fund for the insurance of its employees is not required to file a separate return for such fund, but the income therefrom shall be included in the return of the corporation. (b) Though its name, charter powers, and subjection to local or State insurance laws are significant in determining the business. which a corporation is authorized and intends to carry on, the character of the business actually done in the taxable year determines whether it is taxable as an insurance company under the Income Tax Act. For example, during the year 1954 the M 

Corporation, incorporated under the insurance laws of the State of R, carried on the business of lending money in addition to guaranteeing the payment of principal and interest of mortgage loans. Of its total income for the year, one-third was derived from its insurance business of guaranteeing the payment of principal and interest of mortgage loans and two-thirds was derived from its noninsurance business of lending money. The 

M Corporation is not an insurance company for the year 1954 within the meaning of the Act and these regulations. 

Codification. Regulation contains no secs. 3411-5 or 3411-6. § 3411-8. Domestic, foreign, resident, and nonresident persons 

A domestic corporation or partnership is one organized or created in Puerto Rico under the law of the Commonwealth of Puerto 90

Ch. 254

MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS T.13 § 3413 

Rico, and a foreign corporation or partnership is one which is not domestic. A domestic corporation is a resident corporation even though it does no business and owns no property in Puerto Rico. 

A foreign corporation engaged in trade or business within Puerto Rico is referred to in these regulations as a resident foreign corporation, and a foreign corporation not engaged in trade or business within Puerto Rico, as a nonresident foreign corporation. 

A partnership engaged in trade or business within Puerto Rico is referred to in these regulations as a resident partnership, and a partnership not engaged in trade or business within Puerto Rico, as a nonresident partnership. Whether a partnership is to be regarded as resident or nonresident is not determined by the nationality or residence of its members or by the place in which it was created or organized. The term "nonresident alien", as used in these regulations includes a nonresident alien individual and a nonresident fiduciary. 

§ 3411-9. Fiduciary 

"Fiduciary" is a term which applies to persons who occupy positions of peculiar confidence toward others, such as trustees, executors, and administrators. A fiduciary for income tax purposes is a person who holds in trust an estate to which another has the beneficial title or in which another has a beneficial interest, or receives and controls income of another, as in the case of receivers. 

A committee or guardian of the property of an incompetent person is a fiduciary. § 3411-10. Fiduciary distinguished from agent

There may be a fiduciary relationship between an agent and a principal, but the word "agent" does not denote a fiduciary. An agent having entire charge of property, with authority to effect and execute leases with tenants entirely on his own responsibility and without consulting his principal merely turning over the net profits from the property periodically to his principal by virtue of authority conferred upon him by a power of attorney, is not a fiduciary within the meaning of the Income Tax Act. In cases where no legal trust has been created in the estate controlled by the agent and attorney, the liability to make a return rests with the principal.

The Bureau of Income Tax and collectors of internal revenue may accept uncertified checks in payment of income taxes, provided such checks are collectible at par, that is, for their full amount, without any deduction for exchange or other charges. The internal revenue stamps affixed on the boxes, containers or packs of cigarettes shall be cancelled by stamping on their surface. the name and address of the manufacturer or importer and the cancellation date. 

§ 4010-7. How cigarettes shall be packaged in Puerto Rico 

Cigarettes for consumption in Puerto Rico shall be packaged in containers or packs of 2, 4, 5, 10, 15, 16, 20, 50 or 100 cigarettes each and in no other quantities. Cigarettes shall not exceed 4 inches in length, or be of the usual length common to cigarettes. § 4010-8. Sales outside Puerto Rico to be tax free

Each and every local manufacturer selling cigarettes outside of Puerto Rico may do so without being subject to these taxes by keeping on file, duly organized by date, for a period of not less than 4 years from the export date, the following documents: (1) Commercial invoice of sale; (2) Bill of lading; (3) Shipper's export declaration; and (4) Landing certificate from the country of destination. § 4010-9. § 4011-11. General definitions 

In construing this division the terms of general use below expressed shall have the following meanings: (1) "Manager or assistant manager" shall be the person in charge of the administration or management of an establishment or place where shows affected by the Act are held, or who represents the impresario at such shows. § 4011-21. Taxes on certain transactions [Text of Act, see 13 L.P.R.A. § 4011.] 

§ 4011-22. Basis, assessment and computation of tax (a) Every impresario is under obligation to collect a tax which shall be computed on the basis of 20 per cent of the price of each admission ticket whose price, without the tax, exceeds 20 cents. (b) In determining the tax, no element integrating the admission fee other than the mere tax on the show provided by the Act shall be deductible from the gross admission price. (c) In the case of a show where, in addition to the performance of artists in person, movies or other shows taxed by the Act are exhibited, the admission fee to such show as a whole shall be subject to payment of the tax. The fact that the impresario breaks down the admission fee shall not alter the situation. (d) In the case of establishments which, in addition to holding shows, also operate hotels, boarding houses, or summer houses, the impresario shall, when the guests or boarders participate in said shows, be under obligation to collect therefrom the taxes in the same form and on the same basis as he collects them from the general public, even though they be not directly charged in their accounts for their right to enjoy the show. (e) In the case of moving-picture shows outdoors (drive-in theaters), the tax shall be computed as follows: (1) On the admission fee charged for each vehicle entering the grounds or within bounds of such establishments, regardless of the number of occupants therein. (2) When persons who are not occupants of the vehicles entering the grounds or within bounds of such establishment are allowed to enter, on the admission fee charged to each such person.

Establishment or premise where various shows are held simultaneously When more than one public show is held simultaneously in an establishment or premise, the impresario in charge of the whole show, or the various impresarios or co-impresarios, shall collect the tax from the attendant crowd in accordance with the admission fee charged for watching each one of the various shows. So, for instance, there shall be subject to the tax the admission fee charged for entering the premise where a fair is being held, and at the same time and independently from these, the admission fees charged for watching other shows held within such premise. $ 4011-28. Establishments where more than one admission fee is charged in certain cases (a) When a spectator who has gained access to a given seat, whether by payment of the admission fee charged for such seat, or because the impresario has granted him a free or courtesy ticket, gains access, while the show is being held, to a higher price seat he is not entitled to, the impresario shall collect from such spectator the unpaid portion of the tax resulting from the difference between the admission fee charged for either seat. (b) Whenever a spectator, having gained access to a given seat, pays the impresario a sum in addition to the admission fee charged for such seat for the purpose of getting more personal comfort or for any other concession, it shall be the duty of the impresario to collect from such spectator, as a portion of the admission fee to the seat, the tax on the additional amount charged. § 4011-29. § 4011-30. Impresario responsible for collection of tax (a) Every impresario shall be responsible for the collection and custody of the taxes on the taxable shows held by him, until his return and full payment thereof to the Secretary. (b) In any case where the person liable for the collection of the tax should for any reason fail to collect it, such person shall be 1962 Vol. 1, No. 3 96.4
