bound to report and pay it to the Secretary in the form prescribed, as though he had collected same. (c) The impresario, once he has collected the tax, becomes the withholding agent of the Secretary and a custodian of public funds. 

As such, he shall be obliged to submit a return in the official form to be prescribed by the Secretary, stating the sums collected, with clear details of the first and last numbers of each series of tickets of different denominations sold in relation to the show or shows held. The impresario in charge of a regular show shall keep an invoice book for making payment of the taxes on the shows held by him. 

§ 4011-31. Bonding of impresarios 

Every impresario shall, in the judgment of the Secretary, give a bond in behalf of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico to answer for the remittal to the Secretary of the taxes collected from spectators, as well as for the payment of such penalties as may be imposed upon him for his failure to comply with the provisions of the Act or this Division.

§ 4011-51. Tickets or other media of collating entrances 

Every impresario of shows taxed by the Act shall equip himself with: (1) tickets or admission cards evidencing all admissions subject to the tax; or (2) recording machines or mechanical devices for recording or marking down the number of persons entering the premise where the show is being held; or (3) any other method, previously approved by the Secretary, 1962 96.5 

Vol. 1, No. 3

T.§ 4011-51 

Ch. 352

EXCISE ACT 

for computing or determining the number of persons having access to the show. § 4011-52. Tickets; their specifications (a) The minimum information which shall appear on the ticket is the following: (1) Name of the establishment where the show is to be held. (2) Price and tax, separately. (3) Serial number in two of the opposite ends, when printed in rolls or in book form. (b) Admission tickets for regular shows shall be numbered consecutively beginning with number 1. No number shall be repeated between the beginning and end of the series, which may reach up to 1,000,000 and recommence with A-1, continue with A-2, A-3, and so on, always with the prefix A, up to A-1,000,000; and this numbering system may be continued up to Z-1,000,000. 

Tickets of consecutive numeration shall be juxtaposed and strung in rolls, with such perforation or incision as will allow their being torn out or let loose; following the progressive numeration as they are distributed to the public. As the impresarios order new tickets for each establishment they shall continue the initial series. There shall be a different and separate series for each established price. (c) In no place where admission tickets are sold shall there be at the same time two or more rolls or series of tickets of the same established price. Serialized loose tickets shall be issued correlatively according to serial number and letter of the alphabet, if any. (d) No impresario shall issue to the public admission tickets bearing an admission fee other than the price he actually charges at the time the show taxed by the Act is held. In the case of tickets becoming obsolete due to changes in the admission fee, the impresario may use them for shows on which the admission price is not subject to tax. (e) In the case of shows requiring an extraordinary promotion and the sale of tickets outside the regular box office, there shall be permitted the use of loose tickets or book tickets if numbered correlatively; but it shall be the duty of the impresario to present, for countersigning, the complete issue of said tickets at the Excise 

District Office. 

§ 4011-53. Printing of tickets; notice to be given

Any person who prints, manufactures, or sells to any impresario tickets or admission cards for any show taxed by the Act, shall, 1962 Vol. 1, No. 3 96.6

Ch. 352

T.13 S 4011-57 

before delivering the tickets, report in writing to the Bureau of General Excise Taxes the following information: (1) name and address of the person to whom the tickets are issued; and (2) the number of tickets issued, with a detail of the serial numbers thereon. 

§ 4011-54. Mechanical devices 

Whenever, instead of cards or admission tickets, any other kind of mechanical device is used for controlling attendance, such devices shall be located at the entrance or at any point along the way to the interior of the premise where the show is to be held, so that every person admitted may be registered. 

The control mechanism of the register or meter of the mechanical device shall not be interfered with until it reaches its total recording capacity, except in cases of sudden impairment, when the impresario shall notify the Bureau of General Excises. § 4011-55. Box office

Every show impresario shall provide himself with the necessary box offices for the selling of tickets. 

§ 4011-56. Poster 

For every show taxed by the Act, there shall be fixed at the box office, in a conspicuous place to the public, a poster not less than 10″ × 8″ in clear, legible characters, announcing the price of each ticket without the tax, the tax, and the gross price of the ticket.

§ 4011-58. Countersigns 

In premises or places where shows are being held and the public is occasionally allowed to leave and come back before the end of the show, the impresario shall provide each outgoing person with a duly identified countersign. The countersign shall be recovered from the spectator upon his return to the show. The use as a countersign of the half ticket originally given the spectator shall not be allowed. 

§ 4011-59. Liquidation 

(a) The tickets sold for each show, as well as the taxes on complimentary or free tickets, shall be liquidated forthwith at the end of the show, or shortly before. (b) Should a fiscal officer who has identified himself as such be present at the show, the liquidation shall not be made by the impresario or his representative without first notifying the fiscal officer designated to cover the show. (c) In the case of shows which are suspended or not even started, if the impresario decides that the gross admission fee be withheld, the liquidation shall be made just as though the show had taken place. The credit owing to the person attending the show which is suspended or not started shall be recognized by the Bureau of Excises for gaining access to such show as the impresario may designate. (d) Should no substitute event be held during the 30 days following the day on which the show was suspended or not started, the withheld taxes shall be paid to the Secretary in accordance with the original liquidation. There may be deducted only such taxes as may have been refunded by the impresario to the persons attending the show, but the impresario shall then turn in the half ticket recovered when he refunded the admission fee to such persons. 1962 Vol. 1, No. 3 96.8

 § 4011-60. Liquidation sheet 

The original of the liquidation sheet (a form to be furnished free by the Secretary) shall be filed with the office of the internalrevenue collector of the municipality where the show is held, not later than 10:00 a.m. of the day following the day the regular show was held. Such liquidation sheet shall contain the information required therein. § 4011-61. Nonregular shows; obligation to notify 

Every impresario of a nonregular show shall be under obligation to notify the Excise District Office, at least 72 hours in advance, of the hour set therefor and the place where it is to be held. 

SECTIONS § 4011-62. Clandestine entrances 

Access to a show shall not be permitted except through the gates officially designated for such purpose. Every gate, opening, or approach, permitting access in any other way, shall constitute a clandestine entrance.

§ 4011-81. Public shows [Text of Act, see 13 L.P.R.A. § 4041 (c) (d).] § 4011-82. Total or partial exemption in certain circumstances 

The release from, and/or the reduction of, the tax mentioned in 13 L.P.R.A. § 4041(d), quoted above, shall be governed by the following rules: (1) The impresario is under obligation to give a 48-hour written notice of his intention and purpose to grant free or complimentary tickets or lower the admission fee, as the case may be, to the Excise District Office or to the office of the internal-revenue collector of the municipality where the show is to be held. (2) The impresario shall be allowed total tax-exemption on the admission fee if he grants free admission tickets to groups of persons as stated below: 

(A) Pupils of the public schools of Puerto Rico. 

(B) Students from colleges duly authorized by the Department of Education. 1962 

Vol. 1 No. 3 

96.9

(C) Students of the University of Puerto Rico and other university-level institutions. (D) Groups of inmates of public or private nonprofit institutions. (E) Children or ladies, collectively. (3) The impresario shall be permitted to collect and pay the tax on the basis of the reduced and actually charged admission fee, in the case of civic or sports promotion groups, provided such groups, in the opinion of the Secretary, fulfill the purpose of the partial exemption granted by the Act. (4) Persons or groups favored by total tax-exemption or partial rebate shall be duly identified by means of uniforms, distinctive marks, or identification cards issued by the institutions where they belong, except when the free admission or rebate in the admission fee is granted by the impresario to children or ladies, collectively. 

There shall be considered as "children" all minors under 12. (5) If the impresario announces and in fact grants rebates in price for one or more shows, the tax shall be computed on the basis of the reduced price actually collected by him, and not on the original price of the seats subscribed for.

Whenever an impresario bound to collect the tax fails to pay same to the Secretary within the time and as prescribed in the Act and in this Division, he shall, as a penalty, in addition thereto and as a part thereof, pay 5 per cent of the outstanding amount, when payment is made after 30 days from the date on which the tax should have been paid, but not exceeding 60 days; or 10 per cent of the amount of the tax when payment is made after 60 days from the date on which the tax should have been paid. He shall, also, pay interest on the amount of the tax computed at the rate of 9 per cent per annum from the date on which the tax should have been paid.

§ 4012-1. Scope and short title 

This subchapter deals with the levying and collection of the license tax on certain occupations, and establishes a uniform system for the authorization and issuing of the licenses called for in chapter II, sec. 12, of the Excise Act of Puerto Rico [13 L.P.R.A. 

§ 4012] and shall be known by the short title "License Regulation". 

The provisions of the Excise Act of Puerto Rico herein quoted are literally from the text.

This subchapter is promulgated in accordance with the authority granted to the Secretary of the Treasury in section 78 of the 

Excise Act of Puerto Rico [13 L.P.R.A. § 4078].

Codification. The regulation carried into this subchapter originally contained the text of those provisions of the Excise Tax Act of Puerto Rico which it construes. They have been omitted from this publication and a reference to the appropriate title and section of L.P.R.A. inserted in their stead.

Separability. Art. 32 of the Regulation set out in this subchapter provided: "If any part of this Regulation is declared null by a court, the remaining provisions shall continue in force." or

Repeals. Art. 33 of the Regulation set out in this subchapter provided: "Every regulation, circular letter decision in conflict with the provisions of this Regulation is hereby repealed but the same shall remain in force as regards the imposition, assessment and collection of all taxes hereby levied, and of all interest, penalties and surcharges heretofore or hereafter earned, imposed or accrued in relation with the acts repealed by Act No. 2, approved Jan uary 20, 1956 [13 L.P.R.A. § 4102]." § 4012-2. General definitions 

In construing this subchapter, the terms of general use below expressed shall have the following meanings: (1) "Certificate" shall mean License Certificate. 1962 Vol. 1, No. 3 96.14

Ch. 352

T.13 § 4012-5 LICENSE REGULATIONS 

(2) "Taxpayer" shall be the person engaged in the occupation subject to license. (3) "Retailer or retail dealer" shall mean any dealer who sells for individual use or consumption. (4) "Act" shall be Act No. 2, approved January 20, 1956, as amended [13 L.P.R.A. §§ 4001 to 4103]. 

(5) "Wholesaler or wholesale dealer" shall mean any person who sells to a dealer and who keeps any stock of articles on his business premises or in relation therewith. (6) "Municipality" shall mean all the municipal governments including the Government of the Capital and the municipality of Culebra. (7) "Person" includes an individual, a syndicate, a trust, an estate, a partnership, a company, a corporation, an association or organization of any type. (8) "Secretary" means the Secretary of the Treasury. (9) "Dealer" shall mean any person who either: (A) engages, in any place whatsoever whether fixed or movable, in the business of selling or exchanging articles; (B) exhibits articles to the public in windows or counters unless the articles (in such numbers as strictly indispensable) fulfill no other conceivable purpose than that of enhancing the exhibition of other items; (C) acquires articles in commercial quantities in excess of his normal consumption requirements. A manufacturer who sells or disposes of his products at wholesale in and from his own manufacturing plant, or who exhibits articles therein without selling or disposing of them at retail, shall not be treated as a "dealer". § 4012-3. § 4012-4. Persons to whom the tax applies 

Every person engaged in any of the occupations enumerated in sec. 4012-45, which is a part of this subchapter, is subject to the payment of a license tax at the rates therein prescribed, except as provided in sec. 4012-21. § 4012-5. Tax applied separately 

The license tax shall apply separately to each occupation so 97

engaged in and to each establishment maintained with respect to that occupation. 

§ 4012-6. Vehicles treated as establishments 

(a) For the purposes of the levying and collection of license. taxes, each vehicle used in the sale or distribution by itinerant dealers shall be treated as a separate establishment. (b) This provision shall not apply to those vehicles owned or used by manufacturers and wholesalers to deliver merchandise previously ordered. It shall be the duty of said manufacturers and wholesalers to provide the drivers of the vehicles with waybills evidencing that the merchandise has been ordered. § 4012-7. Occupations taxed; categories 

[Text of Act, see 13 L.P.R.A. § 4045 (a), fourth sentence.] § 4012-8. Classification 

The director of the Bureau of General Excise Taxes (or the officer to whom he may delegate), shall determine the category in which each establishment subject to the payment of these taxes falls, on the basis of the volume of sales made during the twelve (12) months preceding the quarter for which the license is requested. 

§ 4012-9. Initial classification 

In the case of the initial classification of an establishment or business, or, in default of an accounting system, or of invoices or authentic notes, the classification shall be made taking into consideration the commercial establishment or business to which it bears the closest similarity. This similarity shall be determined by the stock, location, and layout of the establishments. 

§ 4012-10. Duration of initial classification 

When the initial classification of an establishment or business has been determined on the basis of the provisions of sec. 4012-9 above, the category in which the establishment or business has been classified shall last until the end of the fourth quarter. § 4012-11. Period of time utilized in revising license categories 

To determine the volume of sales of the twelve (12) months preceding the quarter, in case of reclassification of license categories, the period of time indicated below shall be used: 98

(1) For the classification corresponding to the July-September quarter, the volume of sales made during the period comprised between May 16 of the preceding year and May 15 of the following year, both dates inclusive. (2) For the classification corresponding to the October- December quarter, the volume of sales made during the period comprised between August 16 of the preceding year and August 15 of the following year, both dates inclusive. (3) For the classification corresponding to the January-March quarter, the volume of sales made during the period comprised between November 16 of the preceding year and November 15 of the following year, both dates inclusive. § 4012-13. Special rules regarding itinerant dealers 

The following rules shall be observed in the granting of licenses to itinerant dealers: (1) If any itinerant dealer maintains a stock of goods in any place other than the place where he uses to store, during periods of inactivity, his stock of the articles he deals in, he is obliged to obtain a fixed-place license for each place in which he keeps such stock, besides his license as itinerant dealer. (2) If any itinerant dealer in jewelry articles sells articles retailed to the consumer at a price per unit higher than those prices indicated below, he is obliged to obtain a license of a higher category, according to the price at which he sold the article to the consumer: $50.00 if a second-category license $25.00 if a third-category license $15.00 if a fourth-category license $5.00 if a fifth-category license

Any itinerant dealer dealing in jewelry articles whose cost at factory is higher than $35.00 per unit, is obliged to secure a first- 99

Ch. 352 category itinerant-dealer license. When the dealer acquires the merchandise from a local wholesaler, it shall be the duty of such dealer to ask the wholesaler and this shall be obliged to indicate in the commercial invoice issued by him the date and number of the internal revenue invoice by which he paid the taxes. § 4012-14. Dealer in jewelry

Every person who sells gold or silver to persons other than professionals legally authorized to practice dental surgery or practical dentistry; or who sells religious articles or other symbols. for personal use if imbedded or adorned with diamonds, precious stones or pearls, shall be considered as a dealer in jewelry. 

§ 4012-15. Payment of taxes [Text of Act, see 13 L.P.R.A. §§ 4063 (a), 4063(b), 4063(d).] 

§ 4012-16. Form of payment; working hours; holidays 

License taxes shall be paid by check or legal tender at the internal revenue collectors' offices.

If the day on which the payment of a tax is due is a holiday, payment shall be made on the first working day thereafter. The same rule shall apply where payment is due on a Saturday. § 4012-17. Periods for which payable; time of payment 

[Text of Act, see 13 L.P.R.A. §§ 4045 (b), 4062 (b), 4062 (c).] 

§ 4012-18. Periods for which payable; quarters

The license tax shall be payable for full quarters, regardless of the time elapsed of the quarter in which the license is requested. 

In cases of license renewal, the taxes shall be paid not later than the sixteenth day of the month on which the quarter commences. 

Quarters shall commence on the first day of January, April, July, and October, and shall expire on the last day of March, June, September and December, respectively. § 4012-19. Optional annual payment; refunds 

Any person may, prior to July 16 of any fiscal year, pay the license tax for the entire fiscal year commencing July 1. In such case, a discount of 10% on the value of the license shall be accorded. 

If after July 16 any person undertakes an occupation or activity subject to license tax, and wishes to avail himself of this system 100

Ch. 352

T.134012-25 

LICENSE REGULATIONS 

of payment, the additional taxes for the unexpired quarters shall be collected without granting any discount. When a person covered by this system of payment ceases to engage in certain given activities, appropriate adjustments shall be made and the Secretary shall reimburse the proportionate part corresponding to the unexpired full months of the quarter. 

§ 4012-20. Tax exemptions [Text of Act, see 13 L.P.R.A. § 4045 (d).] 

§ 4012-21. License tax exemption in certain cases (a) No person shall be bound to secure a license as dealer in articles of jewelry merely because he deals in one or two of the articles listed below, if he holds any other license under the Act: (1) Pocket watches whose retail price does not exceed $5.00. (2) Alarm clocks whose retail price does not exceed $8.00. (3) Clocks designed for automobiles. (4) Compacts and vanity cases whose retail price is less than $3.00. (b) Likewise he shall not be bound to secure a license as dealer in automotive parts and accessories, tires and tubes if he holds any other license, merely because he deals in: (1) Lights for any vehicle, and (2) Articles which in the judgment of the Secretary have a substantial use other than as automotive parts and accessories. § 4012-22. Powers of administration; investigations; inventories; revocation of licenses [Text of Act, see 13 L.P.R.A. § 4077, subsecs. (a), (c), and (e).] 

§ 4012-23. Revocation of licenses 

Before revoking any license issued under the provisions of the Act, the Secretary shall grant the holder thereof an administrative hearing, so that he may set forth the reasons wherefor said license should not be revoked. § 4012-24. General supervisory powers; delegation of authority

§ 4012-27. Obtaining and display of certificates (a) No person shall engage in any of the occupations or transactions subject to the payment of license taxes without first securing the corresponding license certificate. (b) Once the certificate is obtained, it shall be the duty of the taxpayer to post same in a conspicuous place in his commercial establishment, so that it can be readily examined. (c) Itinerant dealers shall carry with them the certificate when engaged in the selling of the articles for which the license was acquired. § 4012-28. Information to be supplied in applying for a license to sell from a vehicle

Any person wishing to obtain a license certificate to engage in selling from a vehicle shall, upon filing his application, indicate the make, model and license number of the vehicle, in addition to the other information he must normally furnish for obtaining any other certificate. § 4012-29. the maximum volume of his classification, the dealer shall be obliged to apply for a higher-category license, in keeping with such volume. § 4012-30. Revision of license classification to a lower category 

No request for revision of the classification of a license to a lower category shall be considered unless the dealer shall make it in writing 30 days in advance of the expiration of the quarter. § 4012-31. Request for transfer, removal or discontinuance of licenses (a) Every request for the transfer, removal, or discontinuance of a license shall be in writing to the agent in charge of the Internal Revenue District where the business is located. (b) No transfer shall be authorized unless the dealer shall pay the property tax for the semester of the year in which he requests the transfer, as well as any other delinquent tax due. (c) No removal shall be authorized unless the dealer shall show the use permit issued for the new premises. (d) No license discontinuance shall be granted unless the dealer shall so request not later than the day of expiration of the quarter for which the certificate was obtained. § 4012-32. § 4012-33. Use permit required (a) No licenses for establishments in the urban zone shall be authorized unless the applicant presents the Use Permit issued by the Permit Officer of the Puerto Rico Planning Board. 

(b) Neither shall licenses be authorized for establishments located in the rural communities established by the Social Programs Administration of the Land Authority, unless the applicant presents an authorization issued by the Secretary of Agriculture and Commerce.

Every person applying for a license certificate to engage in the sale of articles of jewelry or perfumery shall accompany his application by a copy of the inventory of the stock with which 103

he plans to start his business, describing the articles by their commercial names and their cost per unit. At the expiration of his fiscal year if he keeps accounting records, or at the expiration of his calendar year if he keeps no such records, every dealer shall be obliged to submit to the Bureau of General Excises, Department of the Treasury, San Juan, a report on the total volume of sales of articles subject to payment of license taxes, made during the 12 months of his last fiscal or calendar year, as the case may be. If the dealer is engaged in the sale of more than one item subject to payment of license, his report on the volume of annual sales shall specify the total sales for each item. 

§ 4012-36. Sending of copy of inventory 

Every dealer subject to payment of license taxes on articles of jewelry or perfumery shall transmit to the Secretary a copy of the inventory of his stock at the expiration of each calendar year, if he does not keep an accounting system, or at the expiration of his accounting year, if he does, itemizing the articles by their commercial names, indicating serial numbers, if any, cost per unit, and estimated selling price of each. 

§ 4012-37. Issuance of sales invoice 

(a) Every dealer subject to payment of license taxes who engages in the sale of articles of jewelry or perfumery shall issue an invoice or sales voucher to each client at the time of making a sale. When the sale is on credit, or to another dealer, the following data shall be recorded: (1) Date of sale (2) Name and address of buyer (3) Quantity and description of the articles (4) Selling price, etc. 104

§ 4012-42. Specific administrative fines

Administrative fines for specific violations of the provisions of this subchapter are as follows: (1) For not displaying the certificate in a conspicuous place in the commercial establishment, or, in the case of itinerant dealers, for not carrying it with them while engaged in the business, a minimum of $2.00. 105

T.4012-42 

Ch. 352

EXCISE ACT 

(2) In the case of itinerant dealers in articles of jewelry who sell articles at a higher price per unit than the limit established for the category of the license held by them, the penalty shall be 25 percent of the difference between the cost of the license they are obliged to secure and the cost of the license they hold. (3) For not applying for, at the time of renewal or at any other time later, a license of a higher category when, during the preceding 12 months, the dealer has made sales in excess of the limit of the category of the license held by him, 25 percent of the difference between the cost of the license which he is obliged to secure and the cost of the license he holds. (4) For not submitting an inventory within the term prescribed by this subchapter, a minimum of $5.00. (5) For not rendering a report on the volume of sales at the time of renewal of the license, a minimum of $5.00. § 4017-1. Scope of regulation 

(a) This division deals with the time and manner of tax payments on jewelry articles and regulates the provisions of the 

Excise Tax [13 L.P.R.A. § 4001 et seq.] relative to these articles. 

(b) This division is approved by the authority conferred upon the Secretary of the Treasury by art. 78 of Excise Act No. 2, approved January 20, 1956, as amended [13 L.P.R.A. § 4078]. The portions enclosed in quotation marks are cited from the abovementioned Act.

Repeals. Section 25 of Regulation File No. 1072 set out in this division provided: “Any regulation, circular or decision in conflict with the provisions of this Regulation [this division] is hereby repealed, except as regards the levying, assessment and collection of all taxes, interest, penalties and surcharges accruing in relation with legislation in force up to but not including July 1, 1966."

Separability. Section 24 of Regulation File No. 1072 set out in this division provided: "Should any part of this Regulation [this division] be declared null and void by a court of law, the remaining provisions shall remain in force." 

§ 4017-2. Definitions 

The terms listed below shall be defined as follows for the purposes of this division: (1) "Factory price" means the prevailing price for jewelry articles at their point of origin or at the place where they are acquired, whether by sale, transfer, gift or in any other manner, at the time the sender dispatches them to the consignee, bank or other intermediary in Puerto Rico as this price shall be determined from adequate and authentic invoices originally accompanying the shipment of such articles listing said articles. (2) "Retailer or retail dealer" means any dealer selling goods solely for individual use or consumption. (3) "Manufacturer", for the effects of the jewelry tax, means any natural or juridical person engaged in the manufacture of any of the articles taxed in conformity with lines 3, 3A and 3B of art. 10(b) [13 L.P.R.A. § 4010] and listed in art. 17 [13 L.P.R.A. 

§ 4017] of the Excise Tax Act; assemblers of jewelry articles; distributors of articles of jewelry manufactured by others or modified by them from the form in which they were originally received; and the persons who further process partially processed jewelry articles. 

(4) "Imitation precious metals". "Imitation precious metals" are: (A) Base metals gilded, silverplated, platinized or coated with any precious metal; 

Feb. 28, 1967

Vol. 6, No. 2 

114.2

Ch. T.13 4017-2 

(B) Alloys or mixtures, in any proportion, of precious metals with base metals; (C) Any other metal or alloy of metals used in the manufacture of an article which is sold to consumers in Puerto Rico at a price equal to or higher than that of a similar or analogous article which is gilded or otherwise alloyed, in any proportion, with precious metals. In the case of subparagraphs (B) and (C), however, if the article does not contain any gold, silver of platinum, it shall not be taxed unless it is a cosmetic compact, or serves an essentially decorative function, or is an article which, in the Secretary's judgment, is commonly or commercially considered to be jewelry. (5) "Wholesaler or wholesale dealer" shall signify any person selling jewelry articles to a dealer who keeps his stock at his place of business or in related places and who buys said articles to resell them. (6) "Precious metals" are gold, silver, sterling silver, platinum, rhodium and palladium, in any state of purity. (7) "Person" includes an individual, a syndicate, trustee, estate, company, partnership, corporation or association of any kind. (8) "Taxable price in Puerto Rico, as regards jewelry articles introduced in Puerto Rico by a dealer" shall mean, in the case of purchases made directly from the manufacturer or through a middleman, the price quoted by the manufacturer to the dealer in 

Puerto Rico plus 32 percent of said price. "In the case of purchases from distributors, agents, or any person other than the manufacturer," it shall mean the price quoted by such distributor, agent or person other than the manufacturer, to the dealer in Puerto Rico plus 32 percent of said price; and, "as regards jewelry articles sold in Puerto Rico by local manufacturers", it shall mean the cost of raw materials, the direct labor costs, the overall manufacturing costs, the cost of packages or boxes, plus 20 percent of the sum total of such costs. (9) "Purchase price, as regards jewelry articles introduced in Puerto Rico by any person who is not a dealer," shall mean the prevailing price of such article at the time and place it was acquired by the taxpayer, as determined from the authentic invoice including such article. (10) "Sales price, as regards retailed jewelry articles," shall mean the unit price at which each such article is sold to the consumer, not including tax. 

Feb. 28, 1967 

Vol. 6, No. 2 114.3

T.§ 4017-2 

Ch. 353

EXCISE ACT 

(11) "Records and documents" shall signify any account book, register or report; import or export documents, commercial invoices, bills of sale, vouchers, customs declarations, credit and debit notes, sales orders, price lists, or any other document relating to the business of manufacturing, importing or selling jewelry. (12) "Secretary" shall signify the Secretary of the Treasury of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico. (13) "Dealer" means any person who (A) is engaged in the business of selling or transferring goods, whether carrying on his business from a set place or as a traveling salesman; (B) exhibits commodities publicly in shop windows or counters, unless said goods (in quantities not exceeding what is strictly necessary for this purpose) cannot have any conceivable purpose save that of enhancing the exhibition of other commodities; or (C) shall acquire goods in commercial quantities, i.e., in quantities exceeding his personal consumption needs. A manufacturer who sells or otherwise disposes of his products wholesale, from his own factory, or who exhibits commodities on his premises without selling or otherwise disposing of them retail shall not be considered a dealer.

§ 4017-3. Tax rates 

The Excise Act establishes the following rates for taxes on jewelry articles, including cases for such, introduced, or manufactured or sold in Puerto Rico: 

(1) "Introduction"-The act of introducing jewelry articles in 

Puerto Rico, whether by a bona fide dealer or a nondealer. (2) "Sales"-The act of selling or transferring articles manufactured in Puerto Rico for the local market. (3) "Retail sale"-The act of selling articles at retail, when carried out by retailers. (4) "Use, Consumption"-Applicable to such jewelry articles as are intended for personal use or consumption. (5) "Transfer"-The act of alienating jewelry articles in any form or manner other than by sale when carried out by a manufacturer, a retail dealer or any other person liable to the payment of this tax. 

Feb. 28, 1967 

Vol. 6, No. 2 114.4

Ch. T.13 § 4017-4 

(6) "Acquisition"-The act of obtaining jewelry articles in any form or manner by a person liable to the payment of this tax. 

§ 4017-4. Computation of taxes 

Taxes on articles of jewelry shall be computed, in the same order as listed in sec. 4017-3 of this title, as follows: (1) In the case of jewelry articles introduced by a bona fide dealer: TIM (A) The factory price or price at the place or origin of the sender's or agent's invoice shall be verified. (B) Thirty-two percent of the cost thus determined shall be added to the price. The resulting total shall be the "taxable price in 

Puerto Rico". (C) The tax to be paid shall be 2 percent of the "taxable price in Puerto Rico". (2) In the case of jewelry introduced in Puerto Rico by a nondealer: (A) The "purchase price" shall be verified from the sender's or salesman's invoice or, if there is no invoice, from the pertinent catalogue or other trustworthy source. (B) The tax to be paid shall be 10 percent of the "purchase price". (See definition of "purchase price" in par. (9) of sec. 4017-2 of this title.) (3) In the case of jewelry manufactured in Puerto Rico: (A) The cost of raw materials, delivered at the manufacturer's warehouse, the direct labor costs, the overall manufacturing costs, and the cost of packages and cases shall be verified from production records. (B) To the sum of the costs specified in par. (A) shall be added 20 percent to establish the tax base which shall be the "taxable price in Puerto Rico". (C) The tax to be paid shall be 2 percent of the "taxable price in Puerto Rico". (See definition of "taxable price in Puerto Rico", as regards jewelry articles sold in Puerto Rico by local manufacturers, in par. (8) of sec. 4017-2 of this title.) (4) In the case of retailed jewelery: (A) The tax base shall be the retail "sales price" of the article, exclusive of the 5 percent tax to which it is subject. (See definition of "sales price" of articles retailed in par. (10) of sec. 4017-2 of this title.) 

April 30, 1968 

Vol. 7, No. 4 114.5

T.§ 4017-4 

EXCISE ACT 

Ch. 353 (B) The tax to be paid shall be 5 percent of the "sales price" thus determined. (5) In the case of jewelry where the documents submitted by the taxpayer do not, in the Secretary's judgment, constitute material proof of the value or price of the taxable articles, or if they are insufficient or inadequate, or in the absence of any document, the price and value of the articles in question shall be determined by the Secretary by whatever method should be most suitable for the purpose, in accordance with the norms of the Excise Act. § 4017-5. Who shall be subject to this tax 

Any dealer introducing jewelry into Puerto Rico, any nondealer introducing jewelry into Puerto Rico, any jewelry manufacturer who sells, uses or transfers jewelry in Puerto Rico, every person buying jewelry at retail in Puerto Rico, and every person possessing articles of jewelry on which no taxes have been paid, regardless of whether he himself introduced such articles in Puerto Rico, received them, as a gift or in any other way, in Puerto Rico from tax-exempt persons, or acquired them by any other means, shall be subject to payment of the pertinent tax or taxes at the applicable rate or rates.

at the moment of purchase, whether for cash or on credit, the 5 percent tax levied on each item. § 4017-8. Obligation of retailer to collect tax from purchaser at the moment of selling jewelry, whether for cash or on credit The Law imposes on each and every retail dealer of jewelry, the obligation of collecting from a purchaser at the moment of making a sale, whether for cash or on credit, the 5 percent per unit tax levied on each item. § 4017-9. Retailer to act as tax collector

Under sec. 60 (c) of the Excise Act [13 L.P.R.A. § 4060], the jewelry retailer shall act as collection agent for the Secretary and shall remit to the Secretary every month, not later than the 10th day of the month, the total amount of taxes collected from the first through the last day of the preceding month. § 4017-10. Obligation of manufacturers or wholesalers to write in their sale invoices the internal revenue license number of the dealer making the purchase

Jewelry manufacturers and wholesalers shall be obligated, before carrying out a sale, to require the purchaser to present the current internal revenue license accrediting him as an authorized jewelry dealer. The certificate number of the purchaser's license shall be included by the manufacturer or salesman in the invoice. 

§ 4017-11. Issuing invoices 

Every wholesale or retail dealer of jewelry shall issue a prenumbered invoice or sales slip to each customer at the moment of making a sale, whether for cash or on credit. Wholesalers shall submit, at the Secretary's request, the invoices covering each and every one of their local sales, whether for cash or on credit, including the following information: (1) date of sale, (2) name and address of purchaser, if it is a cash sale, provided the buyer is a duly licensed dealer duly possessed of the pertinent internal revenue license, (3) identification number of items included in the invoice, (4) quantity and description of articles, (5) retailer's price, excluding the 5 percent tax to which the article sold is subject.

§ 4017-12. Stamping or labeling 

The retailer shall affix upon each article to be sold a stamp or label indicating separately, among other things, the sales price and the amount of tax upon the article. § 4017-13. Obligation of dealer to submit copy of sales order 

Each and every dealer purchasing jewelry from commission agents, factory agents, or any other intermediary, shall submit, together with the invoice and other shipping documents, a copy of the sales order covering the articles introduced in Puerto Rico. § 4017-14. Obligation of commission agents and other persons to submit to secretary copy of sales order Each and every commission agent, factory agent, or any other person acting as an intermediary between seller and buyer of jewelry, shall submit to the Secretary, immediately upon receiving it from the dealer, a copy of the sales order covering the articles ordered to be introduced in Puerto Rico, as well as the pertinent invoices. § 4017-15. Examination of books, records and other documents by fiscal officers

Wholesale and retail dealers, as well as manufacturers, shall, under the provisions of sec. 77 of the Excise Law [13 L.P.R.A. § 4077], allow fiscal officers of the Tax Bureau, freely to examine and classify their stock, wherever it may be stored, as well as the freedom to examine their account books, invoices and any other records, declarations, financial reports, accounts and any other documents whatsoever relating to the introduction, manufacture, purchase and sale of jewelry. § 4017-16. Obligation of dealer to notify jewelry articles in stock 

Dealers, having in their possession and at their disposition jewelry articles, shall be bound to submit, within the following 30 days of the effectiveness of the Law, an inventory duly identified by lines; and to permit fiscal officers freely to examine said stocks. 

§ 4017-17. Jewelry articles for religious purposes 

Dealers or nondealers, introducing items of jewelry for exclusively religious purposes, shall not be subject to tax or license payments as dealers in such items. Among the items not subject to the jewelry tax as "religious items" shall be medals, crosses, crucifixes, and rosaries unless these shall be introduced with chains, brooches 

Feb. 28, 1967 114.8 

Vol. 6, No. 2

Ch. 

T.13 § 4017-21 or any other jewelry item made of or ornamented with precious stones or metals in which case the chains or brooches made of precious metals or imitations of such are per se taxable. § 4017-18. Obligation of introducer to report parcel-post consignments of jewelry

Each and every person whether bonded or not, introducing jewelry items, shall appear at the Internal Revenue Office, or at one of the Offices of the Collector of Internal Revenue, with the parcel (s) received and a copy of the pertinent invoice (s). § 4017-19. Keeping account books and records, documents and reports relating to the introduction, purchase, sale and exportation of jewelry 

Every wholesaler, retailer, or manufacturer shall keep, for a period of not less than 4 years, in conformity with the provisions of sec. 81 of the Excise Act [13 L.P.R.A. § 4081], all of his account books and records, documents, declarations, financial and account reports relating to his activities of introducing, buying, selling, manufacturing or exportation of jewelry. § 4017-20. Submitting stock inventories

Each and every wholesaler or retailer subject to tax payments on jewelry shall submit to the Secretary a copy of his stock inventory on initiating his operations, at the end of every natural year, and at the end of every one of his accounting years, listing the articles with their commercial names, indicating their serial numbers, if any, their unit cost, estimated sales price, information on Internal Revenue Invoices and when and where the pertinent taxes were paid, and featuring the license number of the wholesaler or retailer, as the case may be, as well as the taxpayer's number.

§ 4017-22. Repeated and persistent violation

Repeated and persistent violation by a dealer or retailer of the rules stated in this division shall constitute sufficient cause for a revocation of said dealer or retailer's license by the Secretary, in addition to the application of the standard penalties, in conformity with par. (e) of sec. 77 of the Excise Act [13 L.P.R.A. § 4077], and said dealer's or retailer's operations as jewelry dealer thereby suspended. 

§ 4017-23. Obtaining tax exemption by false representation 

Each and every person who shall knowingly obtain or attempt to obtain exemption from the jewelry tax by means of false representation regarding the true classification or use of jewelry articles acquired in or introduced into Puerto Rico, or who, to this end, submits false or misleading evidence, shall incur the penalties of sec. 88 of the Excise Act [13 L.P.R.A. § 4088].

§ 4034-1. Legal basis and purpose 

This division is promulgated pursuant to the authority granted by section 78 of the Excise Act of Puerto Rico [13 L.P.R.A. § 4078] 

for the implementation of the aims established in Act No.

80, approved June 25, 1969 [13 L.P.R.A. § 4034], amendatory act of the aforesaid Excise Act of Puerto Rico, which requires that certain information be affixed to all motor vehicles to which the Act applies, for the benefit of the purchasers of said vehicles.

§ 4034-2. Definitions 

Unless otherwise stated, or the context clearly so indicates, the definition of the terms used in this division, except those which follow, shall have the same meaning as in the Excise Act of Puerto

"Administration." The Consumers Service Administration.

"Bureau." The Bureau of General Excises of the Department of the Treasury. "Dealer." Includes all distributor-dealers, and means any person who engages in the business of selling vehicles exclusively for individual use. 1970

Ch. 353 "Motor vehicle." Includes, either used or new, automobiles, truck tractors, trucks and buses. § 4034-3. Duties of dealers and/or dealer-importers

It shall be the duty of every dealer and/or dealer-importer, whichever is the case, who is required to pay a license tax under the pro visions of section 12 of the Excise Act of Puerto Rico [13 L.P.R.A. 

§ 4012], and who introduces and has for sale motor vehicles, to affix on the windshield of every vehicle, or in any other visible place of the said vehicle, a sticker or form with the information prescribed in sec. 4034-4 of this title at the time the vehicle is available for sale. 

§ 4034-4. Sticker or form 

The Secretary of the Treasury and the Administrator of the Consumer Services Administration, jointly, shall prescribe a form or sticker which shall contain the information set forth below, which may be made available to any dealer, or dealer-importer. On the form or sticker the following information will be required: (1) New vehicles. (A) Dealer's name. (i) Post-office address. (ii) Business address. (B) Dealer-importer's name. (i) Business address and/or post-office address. 

(ii) Date of introduction of the vehicle. 

If the dealer-importer and the dealer are the same person it will suffice if such fact is stated under (B) (i). 

(C) Description of vehicle. 

(i) Make. (ii) Model. (iii) Motor serial number. (iv) Body or chassis serial number. 

(v) Number of Internal Revenue invoice. 

(D) Cost. (i) Cost at factory of the vehicle including accessories and equipment installed outside Puerto Rico. (ii) Transportation cost. (iii) Amount of taxes. (iv) Taxable price in Puerto Rico. (v) Selling price. 1970

(A) (i) Dealer's and/or dealer-importer's name. (ii) Post-office address. (iii) Business address.

The Secretary, the Administrator, and their duly authorized agents and employees shall have the power to carry out periodically, or at any time it is necessary, investigations to ascertain the truthfulness of the information contained on the forms or stickers affixed to the vehicles. 

§ 4034-7. Complaints 

The Administration shall carry out the investigations of the facts alleged in the complaints submitted by consumers of possible violations of the law, through the inspection of books, contracts, records, files and any other documents or information necessary or relevant to conduct the same. Complaints received in the Department of the Treasury will be transferred to the Administration for investigation. 

§ 4034-8. Records in the General Excise Tax Bureau 

The Secretary of the Treasury shall place at the disposition of the Administration all the information, records, and files of the General Excise Tax Bureau, necessary for the officers, employees or inspectors of the Administration to carry out their investigations or inspections and for the verification of the correctness and certainty of the information set forth on the form or sticker affixed to the motor vehicles. 2 01 vi cas div ca by sec of f recc Gen of t son befo the (b not s istrap 1970 1970

§ 4034-9. Violation and penalties 

Any person, dealer or dealer-importer, whichever the case, who removes the information affixed to any vehicle before the same is sold to a buyer for his personal use or of his business shall be subject to an administrative fine of not less than 10 dollars nor more than 50 dollars for the first violation and not less than 25 dollars nor more than 100 dollars for the second and subsequent violations. 

§ 4034-10. Other penalties 

Any person, dealer, or dealer-importer who fails to affix or who conceals, in whole or in part, or in any manner alters the information required with the intention or purpose of concealing, damaging or altering it with incorrect or false details or who publishes false information in connection therewith, shall be subject to an administrative fine of not less than 25 dollars nor more than 100 dollars for the first violation and not less than 50 dollars nor more than 200 dollars for the second and subsequent violations. The amount of the fine shall be determined in accord with the extent of the violation. § 4034-11. Repeated and persistent violations

The repeated and persistent violations of the provisions of this division by a dealer or dealer-importer shall constitute sufficient cause for the revocation of said dealer's or dealer-importer's license by the Secretary of the Treasury, pursuant to paragraph (e) of sec. 77 of the Excise Act of Puerto Rico [13 L.P.R.A. § 4077(e)]. 

§ 4034-12. Administrative fines; procedure (a) The administrative fines will be imposed by the Secretary of the Treasury. The Administrator or his agents shall initiate and recommend the administrative fines against the violators to the General Excise Tax Bureau, who shall proceed to notify the violators of the violations and of the fine imposed against them. If the person is satisfied with the fine imposed he shall pay the same on or before the 10th day following such notification by the Secretary of the Treasury. (b) If the person to whom the administrative fine is imposed is not satisfied with the same he may request in writing an administrative hearing within 10 days following the date of notification. 1970

Ch. 353 (c) If the administrative fine is confirmed, the same shall be paid within the next 10 days following the date of notification of its confirmation. § 4034-13. Administrative hearing procedure 

The procedure established by the General Excise Tax Bureau of the Department of the Treasury for the holding of administrative hearings shall apply to the hearings prescribed in this division. 

§ 4034-14. Recourse to judicial enforcement 

(a) The Secretary of the Treasury may choose to file a criminal action before a competent court against the person who commits an offense instead of following the administrative procedure. (b) All persons violating the provisions of Act No. 80, approved 

June 25, 1969 [13 L.P.R.A. § 4034], or of this division, if found guilty by a competent court, shall be fined not less than 100 dollars nor more than 2,000 dollars or to confinement in jail for not less than 30 days, nor more than 1 year. For each subsequent offense, both penalties, fine and imprisonment, shall be imposed. 

§ 4034-15. Effectiveness 

This division shall take effect 30 days after its filing in the Department of State of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, in accordance with the provisions of the Regulations Act of 1958 [3 L.P.R.A. §§ 

1041 to 1059], as amended, unless its immediate effectiveness is ordered by the Honorable Governor of Puerto Rico.

The Authority shall hold public bids for these concessions whenever in its judgment the Authority deems it necessary. 

§ 4051-33. Bidders, requirements-Residence 

In order to participate in the bid it is an indispensable requirement that no less than 51 percent of the ownership interest in the entities requesting to operate the concessions be owned by persons residing in Puerto Rico for the period of time prior to the bid that the Authority determines. The bidders shall submit sufficient evidence regarding the requirements asked for in this section, which evidence will be subject to the approval of the Board of Awards of the Authority. 1971 

Vol. 10, No. 6 114.12

Ch. T.13 § 4051-40 

§ 4051-34. -Experience and ability

The bidders shall demonstrate to the satisfaction of the Authority their experience and ability in the operation of commercial stores. § 4051-35. 

Financial condition

The Authority will require from the bidders any documents it deems necessary relating to their financial condition. The Authority, at its discretion, will consider financial statements of parent corporations or corporations affiliated with the bidder only when these corporations submit written evidence duly certified by their Board of Directors stating that they will be responsible for the financial acts and obligations of the bidder in connection with the operation of the concession. § 4051-36. -Cash funds

The bidders shall submit written evidence showing the cash funds available to begin the concession operations. § 4051-37. -Minimum rent

The Authority shall establish a minimum rent for each concession and the bidders shall submit as proposal the percent of the gross revenue they are willing to pay as rent; it being understood that they shall pay whichever of the 2 sums is greater. § 4051-38. Disqualification

The submission of false or fraudulent data, noncompliance with the requirements herein mentioned and those contained in the bid documents shall constitute sufficient cause to disqualify any bidder. § 4051-39. Information

The bidders shall submit written information evidencing that they have procured and obtained from the corresponding government agencies information relative to the requirements asked for by said agencies to operate the concession. 

§ 4051-40. Licenses 

The successful bidders shall submit the corresponding licenses provided by Act No. 2 of January 20, 1956, known as the Excise

Act of Puerto Rico, as amended [13 L.P.R.A. §§ 4001 to 4103], and/or Act No. 6 of June 30, 1936, known as Spirits and Alcoholic

Beverages Act, as amended [13 L.P.R.A. §§ 1471 to 1827], to oper ate the types of businesses to which the concessions refer.

Ch. 353

EXCISE ACT § 4051-41. Bonds 

The concessionaires shall submit such bonds, deposits or insurance policies which in the discretion of the Authority are necessary to operate the concessions. § 4051-42. Exclusive use

The concessionaires shall use the facilities exclusively for the purposes defined in sec. 4051-31 (b) of this title; it being understood that every article for sale in any of the concessions will be subject to the approval of the Executive Director of the Authority or his authorized representative. Any article not having said approval shall be immediately removed from the concession upon request of the Authority. 

§ 4051-43. Exhibition counters 

The concessionaires shall install, at their own cost, the counters that the Authority determines in each concession with the sole purpose of displaying for exhibition samples of all the articles that have been authorized by the Authority for sale in the concession. 

The quality and design of these counters will be subject to the approval of the Executive Director of the Authority of his authorized representative. 

§ 4051-44. Supply of merchandise 

After reaching an agreement on the sale transactions at the counter, the concessionaires shall supply the sold merchandise from the bonded warehouses and they shall make the pertinent arrangements to deliver the article or articles aboard the ship or airplane which the customer indicates, as the case may be. 

§ 4051-45. Delivery 

The concessionaires shall deliver the purchased merchandise in due time aboard the ship or airplane to avoid inconveniences to the operators of these transportation means. 

§ 4051-46. Regulations 

The concessionaires shall comply with all the Federal or Commonwealth regulations applicable to receiving the merchandise and shipment procedures at the bonded warehouses. 

§ 4051-47. Excluded activities 

The concessionaires shall permit no activities or activities ad- 1971 

Vol. 10, No. 6 114.14

Ch. T.13 § 4051-53 

vertisements in the concessions other than those defined in sec. 

4051-31(b) of this title or those agreed in the concession contract. 

§ 4051-48. Responsibility 

The concessionaires shall be the only ones responsible for any damages caused as the result of the operation of the concession. 

§ 4051-49. Accounting system 

The concessionaires shall establish an accounting system within the municipality in which the concessions are located, separated from every other business of the concessionaires. Said accounting systems shall reflect the revenues of the concessions and shall be subject to the approval of the Authority before the concessionaires put them into execution. § 4051-50. Cash register

The concessionaires shall install in their businesses a cash register to record every daily revenue. The concessionaires shall retain the tapes on which the revenues are recorded for inspection by the Authority. § 4051-51. Audit and examination

The Authority may audit the books of account of the concessionaires whenever it deems convenient. Besides, the Authority shall have the right to examine at any time the spaces of the concessions to determine if the concessionaires are complying with their contractual obligations and with the provisions of this division. 

§ 4051-52. Concessionaires 

Under no circumstances may it be construed that the concessionaires constitute Authority's agents, representatives, or employees for any purposes whatsoever. § 4051-53. Transfer prohibited 

The concessionaires may not, without the written consent of the Authority, sublet areas within the concession, transfer to a third party the rights granted by a concession contract nor sell in whole or in part their ownership interests in the concession. This prohibition will not be applicable whenever the transfer is made to the estate of a deceased, or if it is an assignment by bequest or heritage. 1971 

Vol. 10, No. 6 114.15

T.§ 4051-54 § 4051-54. Natural persons 

If the concessionaires were natural persons, these persons may not form associations or corporations for the operation of the concessions without the prior authorization of the Authority. 

EXCISE ACT § 4051-55. Discrimination prohibited 

In the operation of the concessions, the concessionaires shall refrain from discriminating against any person or class of persons by reason of race, sex, national origin, creed or political affiliation. 

Besides, the concessionaires shall not discriminate against any employee or applicant for employment by reason of race, religion, color or national origin. The provisions of this section shall include, but not be limited to, the following aspects: employment, upgrading, demotion or transfer, recruitment or recruitment advertising, layoff or termination, rates or any other forms of compensation, and selection of personnel for training including apprenticeship. 

The concessionaires shall post in conspicuous places, available for employees and applicants for employment, notices to be provided by the Authority setting forth the provisions of this section. 

Ch. 353 $4051-56. Report of deficiencies

The concessionaires agree to inform the Ports Authority in writing of any failure or deficiency of the facilities, the correction of which is the responsibility of the Authority. § 4051-57. List of prices

The concessionaires shall post in conspicuous places available to the public a list of their prices, which prices must be reasonable in the judgment of the Executive Director of the Authority. The concessionaires shall agree to submit in writing to the Authority the list of the prices fixed and any change which occurs in them during the term of the concession. 4051-58. Administrator 

The concessionaires shall designate an administrator in charge of each one of the concessions who may be the owner himself and who shall be responsible at all times for the appropriate functioning of the concession under his administration. 

§ 4051-59. Cancellation 

Noncompliance by the concessionaires with any provision of this division shall constitute sufficient cause for cancellation of the concession contracts.

§ 4060-1. Scope of regulation; short title 

This division deals with the time and form of payment of the taxes on articles introduced in Puerto Rico, in accordance with 

Chapter IV, Part B of the Excise Act of Puerto Rico [13 L.P.R.A. 

§§ 4060 to 4063], and shall be known by the short title "Regulation on Introduction of Taxable Articles." 

The provisions of the Excise Act of Puerto Rico herein quoted are literally from the text. 115

Codification. The regulation carried into this subchapter originally contained the text of those provisions of the Excise Act of Puerto Rico which it construes. They have been omitted from this publication and a reference to the appropriate title and section of L.P.R.A. inserted in their stead. 

Separability. Sec. 21 of the Regulation set out in this division provided: "If any part of this Regulation is declared null by a court, the remaining provisions shall continue in force."

Repeals. Sec. 22 of the Regulation set out in this division provided: "All regulations, circular letters or decisions in conflict with the provisions of this Regulation are hereby repealed, but the same shall remain in force for the imposition, assessment and collection of all taxes, interest, penalties and surcharges heretofore or hereafter levied, accrued or imposed in relation to the laws repealed by Act No. 2, approved January 20, 1956 [13 L.P.R.A. § 4102]." § 4060-2. General definitions 

In construing this division, the terms of general use hereinbelow set forth shall have the following meanings: (1) "Maritime warehouse" shall be any public or private establishment devoted in whole or in part by its owner to storing merchandise introduced into Puerto Rico by consignees, shippers, or any other person. (2) "Shipping order." By this term shall be understood any form or document used by a carrier to protect, describe or identify merchandise introduced into Puerto Rico by a sender, shipper or any other person. (3) "Taxpayer" shall be - (A) In the case of articles introduced into Puerto Rico in any manner: (i) If the article is consigned directly to consignee the consignee; 

(ii) If the article is shipped to the order of shipper or to an intermediary, or if the consignee is indefinite the person claiming the article. If the article is not taken possession of within 30 days from the date of introduction, the taxpayer shall be the sender; 116

Ch. 354

T.134060-2 

ADMINISTRATIVE PROVISIONS 

(iii) If the article is introduced by a person arriving in Puerto Rico from abroad the traveler or crew member introducing the article. (B) In the case of articles acquired from tax-exempt persons, the taxpayer shall be the person acquiring the article. (4) "Bonded taxpayer" includes every person who avails himself, by furnishing a bond in behalf of the Secretary, of the extension plan for the payment of the taxes after removing the merchandise, according to the provisions of sec. 60 (d), paragraph 

(1) of the Act [13 L.P.R.A. § 4060 (d) (1)]. 

(5) "Commercial invoice" shall be understood to be every authentic document which the manufacturer or the seller abroad transmits to the introducer or consignee, describing the merchandise shipped and giving its cost. (6) "Date of introduction" shall mean the day of arrival of the vessel in port or of the landing of the plane in the airport, regardless of the actual time of unloading. However, in cases of taxable merchandise introduced from outside of Puerto Rico, where, by reason of customs, military or sanitary rules, or of strike at the piers and other terminals, or for some other reason of force majeure, the taxpayer or the person liable for the payment of the taxes levied by this Act is prevented from taking possession of the merchandise within the term of 30 days after its arrival in the Island, then the date of introduction shall be considered to be the date on which the customs office or the pertinent authority allows the taxpayer or the person liable for the payment of the tax to take possession of the merchandise introduced, or on which the termination of the strike has been officially announced by the Secretary of Labor, or the date on which, in the judgment of the Secretary of the Treasury, the circumstances of force majeure have ceased to exist. (7) "Fiscal officials" shall include every Internal Revenue Agent, Accountant or Collector of Internal Revenues or any other person designated by the Secretary to conduct investigations in relation with the payment of taxes on the introduction, sale, use, transfer or consumption of taxable articles. (8) "Introduction" shall mean the arrival at the piers, airports or other terminals in Puerto Rico of: (A) articles consigned to the Island which are actually unloaded at the piers, airports or other terminals; 117

T.134060 

EXCISE ACT 

Ch. 354 (B) articles brought to said terminals by the passengers or crews of ships or airplanes. (9) "Introducer" shall mean any person who acquires an article from outside of Puerto Rico, either as consignee of the article or through a bank, shipping agent, or other intermediary. (10) "Act" shall be Act No. 2 approved January 20, 1956, as subsequently amended [13 L.P.R.A. §§ 4001 to 4103]. 

(11) "Municipality" shall mean all the municipal governments including the Government of the Capital and the municipality of Culebra. (12) "Person" includes an individual, a syndicate, a trust, an estate, a partnership, a company, a corporation, an association or organization of any type. (13) "Tax-exempt person" shall mean any person who by reason of his exempt status as determined in the Act and this division is lawfully authorized to acquire taxable articles without need of paying the taxes. (14) "Carrier" refers to any person engaged in the business of bringing freight to Puerto Rico for the account of senders or shippers from abroad, for delivery to persons or consignees in Puerto Rico, or for the account of any other person, regardless of the means of conveyance used. This definition does not include the 

United States Mail. (15) "Secretary" shall mean the Secretary of the Treasury. § 4060-3. Direct introduction; time of payment; postponement in case bond filed 

[Text of Act, see 13 L.P.R.A. §§ 4060 (a) (2) and 4060 (d) (1).] § 4060-4. Determination of bond 

Every taxpayer to whom the Secretary shall grant an extension of time for the payment of the taxes under this section shall furnish a bond as security for the payment of the taxes plus the corresponding surcharges, interest and fines. The bond may be for an amount equivalent to twice the average amount of taxes the taxpayer would have to pay in a normal month of introductions. 

The bond may be in legal tender or through underwriting by a surety company legally authorized to do business and holding attachable property in Puerto Rico; or through a mortgage on unalienated real property. 118

§ 4060-6. Time of payment for motor vehicle dealers duly bonded (a) For the purpose of computing the 10-day period, the date of sale shall be the day on which the dealer makes physical delivery of the vehicle to the vendee. Such physical delivery shall be evidenced, for which purpose the dealer shall use a form to be known as "Vendee's Order." This Vendee's Order shall bear the same date on which the vendee receives the vehicle. (b) The vehicle disposed of by a dealer for use in the official business of the corporation shall pay the net taxes, without penalties if payment is made as if it were a sale. If he disposes of several vehicles for hire, rent or other like purpose and have not paid the taxes before taking possession of the vehicles devoted to such purposes, he shall be under obligation to pay the taxes, surcharges and interest determined by the Act. § 4060-7. § 4060-9. Ordinary payments (1) At the time of paying the tax the taxpayer shall present the bill of lading and the commercial invoice descriptive of the merchandise lifted, as well as the internal revenue invoice duly executed. Said commercial invoice shall contain the following information: same (A) Number and date of the purchase order (B) Weight of the merchandise (C) Number of bundles, cartons or boxes, which must coincide with the number appearing on the face of the bill of lading (D) Total number of units or articles sent and description of (E) Cost per unit and total cost (F) Description of discount, if any. (2) When the consignee has received merchandise in Puerto Rico through brokers, shipping agents or other intermediaries 119

performing like functions, he shall be obligated to present, in addition to the bill of lading, for the purpose of the paying of the tax, authentic invoices from the broker, shipping agent, forwarder or intermediary, said invoices to be supported by the authentic commercial invoices from the persons from whom or the firm where said agent or intermediary acquired the merchandise at the point of origin, and the internal revenue invoice duly executed. (3) When the introducer of the taxable merchandise is himself the consignee, he shall present, in addition to the bill of lading, authentic invoices from the person from whom or the firm where he purchased or acquired the merchandise at the point of origin, and the internal revenue invoice duly executed. (4) When the introducer is a shipping agent, commission agent, broker or forwarder who has consigned the merchandise to himself, he shall furnish, in addition to the bill of lading, authentic commercial invoices from the person from whom or the firm where he acquired the merchandise at the point of origin, and the internal revenue invoice duly executed. (5) When the introducer is a subsidiary in Puerto Rico that receives the merchandise directly from the principal firm, which firm does not manufacture the articles sent, said subsidiary shall, as introducer, be obligated to present, in addition to the bill of lading, authentic invoices from the person from whom or the firm where the said principal firm acquired the merchandise at the point of origin, and the internal revenue invoice duly executed. (6) When the introducer is a representative, or a subsidiary that receives the taxable merchandise from the principal firm, which firm manufactures said merchandise, said introducer shall present, in addition to the bill of lading, the cost invoices. Said introducer shall also be under obligation to maintain in Puerto Rico such records or documents as may be necessary analytically to reflect the cost of the taxable product at the point of origin, and the internal revenue invoice duly executed. (7) When the introducer is a principal firm (home firm) that receives taxable merchandise from its subsidiary abroad which subsidiary does not manufacture the articles sent, said home firm shall, as introducer, be obligated to present, in addition to the bill of lading, authentic invoices from the person from whom or the firm where said subsidiary purchased the merchandise at the point. of origin, and the internal revenue invoice duly executed. § 4060-11. Surcharges and interest on deficiencies in provisional payment

On any deficiency determined in these cases, when the taxpayer has paid less than 80% of the tax finally determined, he shall pay, in addition to the deficiency, and as a part thereof, surcharges and interest as prescribed in sec. 4060-29 of this title. § 4060-12. Payments under bond

Taxpayers duly bonded shall, at the time of paying the taxes, submit the internal revenue invoice duly executed, accompanied by the commercial invoices corresponding to each shipment declared. § 4060-13. Introduction of merchandise for exempt entities (a) In the case of merchandise introduced for exempt entities on an order previously issued by a local representative or distributor, the person responsible for lifting the merchandise from the consignee's circuit and delivering it directly to the exempt entity's establishment, shall present the following documentary evidence: (1) Bill of lading to the order of the shipper or directly to the exempt entity, with which he intends to lift the merchandise and which must show the number of the previous order and the initials of the exempt entity. (2) The corresponding commercial invoices. (3) The internal revenue invoice duly executed. (b) In the case of building materials consigned to the order of shipper to be lifted by a contractor or subcontractor who is to incorporate same into construction works for an exempt entity, the person responsible for the lifting of said materials shall present the following documents: (1) Bill of lading to the order of shipper and which must show the number of the awarded contract and the initials of the exempt entity. 121

[Text of Act, see 13 L.P.R.A. § 4071, first two paragraphs.] § 4060-17. Duties of carriers 

A carrier or any other person engaged in the business of bringing freight to Puerto Rico: (1) Shall not deliver to any consignee or his representative, nor to a person in charge of the lifting of the merchandise or articles he has received from the shippers or persons abroad for consignees in Puerto Rico and which merchandise is subject to commonwealth tax on its introduction into the Island under the Excise Act of Puerto Rico, without first receiving from said consignee, representative, or person in charge of lifting said merchandise or articles, a certificate from the Secretary or his authorized fiscal 122

official accrediting that the consignee has complied with the provisions of the Act. (2) Whenever said carrier shall direct a maritime warehouse to deliver to a consignee a certain merchandise, he shall do so in writing and stating that the consignee has complied with the Excise Act of Puerto Rico. The carrier shall be liable for the payment of taxable merchandise lifted by the consignee under such circumstances. Nothing provided in this section shall be construed to mean that the owner of a maritime warehouse is released from the duties imposed upon him by the Act in the event the corresponding taxes on the merchandise so delivered had not been paid. Duties of owners of maritime warehouses 

Every owner of a maritime warehouse or any warehouseman totally or partially engaged in the storage of freight or merchandise for the account of consignees in Puerto Rico shall comply with the following rules: (1) Shall not deliver to any person merchandise or freight received from a carrier for its temporary storage, unless the person claiming the taxable freight or merchandise presents a certificate from the Secretary or fiscal official stating that the consignee has complied with the provisions of the Act. (2) Shall keep a register in which he shall daily enter at least the following data: (A) merchandise received from the carriers (B) number of bill of lading (C) number of bundles (D) numeration or identification of the bundles (E) name and address of the consignee (F) data on which merchandise is removed from the warehouse (G) identification of the payment document issued by the Secretary authorizing the lifting of the merchandise (H) In case of sale at auction of the merchandise, he shall give the name and address of the acquirer. 123

(3) Shall pay the taxes on such taxable merchandise as he may for any reason have to sell at public auction. (4) The taxes on the merchandise so sold shall be paid on the next working day following the day of the sale. § 4060-19. Duties of consignees 

Any person who in his capacity as a consignee or otherwise introduces or receives taxable merchandise through any kind of transportation service, shall observe the following rules: (1) Shall declare, except in the cases of bonded merchandise, or merchandise received by mail, before taking possession of the merchandise, in the form prescribed by the Secretary, the quantity of articles introduced. For this purpose the internal revenue invoice duly executed shall be considered as the declaration herein required. (2) Shall not lift or take possession of taxable merchandise from carriers or their agents or from owners of maritime warehouses or their agents, without first obtaining the authorization to lift from the Secretary. (3) Shall permit fiscal officials to examine the merchandise received, when they may deem it necessary. (4) Shall permit said officials to strike a physical inventory of the merchandise, if circumstances so demand, as well as to audit his records in the establishment or premises where the taxable merchandise is stored. (5) When in the judgment of the fiscal officials it becomes necessary to verify the declaration of articles introduced, he shall permit the former to examine the luggage and/or the articles. introduced within the circuit of the establishments of the carrier. § 4060-20. § 4060-21. Keeping and furnishing of documents by carriers 

Every carrier or any other person engaged in the business of bringing freight to Puerto Rico, (1) Shall furnish to the Secretary a copy of the bills of lading covering merchandise or taxable articles, as determined by the fiscal officials. (2) Shall maintain his records relating to the delivery in Puerto Rico of taxable merchandise for at least four years reckoning from the individual date of each record or document. (3) Shall permit the fiscal officials to examine the records and documents in relation to the introduction in Puerto Rico of any kind of merchandise, with a view to determining whether or not the same is taxable and who is the person liable for the payment of the tax. § 4060-22. Keeping and furnishing of documents by owners of maritime warehouses Every owner of a maritime warehouse or any warehouseman totally or partially engaged in the storing of freight or merchandise for the account of consignees in Puerto Rico: (1) Shall maintain all his records relating to the delivery of taxable merchandise for a minimum period of four years reckoning from the individual date of each document. (2) Shall permit the fiscal officials to enter his establishments to examine his records, or physically examine the merchandise, for the purpose of determining the taxable status thereof or clarifying any discrepancy between the quantity of articles stored and the quantity specified in the bill of lading. § 4060-23. Keeping and furnishing of documents by consignees 

Every person who in his capacity as consignee or otherwise introduces or receives taxable merchandise through any kind of transportation service: (1) Shall maintain for a minimum period of four years reckoning from the individual date of each document, his records relating to the introduction of articles taxable or otherwise affected by the Act. (2) Shall permit the fiscal officials to retain in their possession, for the purpose of official investigation, any document relating to the introduction of taxable articles. Said documents may be exchanged for certified copies. 125
