Ch. 354 § 4060-24. Keeping and furnishing of documents by intermediaries 

Every person who in his capacity as representative, agent, commission agent, broker, or as any other intermediary, receives orders for the account of or for his representatives, or intervenes directly or indirectly in the lifting of merchandise taxable under the Act: 

(1) Shall maintain for a minimum period of four years reckoning from the individual date of each document, copies of the orders received from his customers, copies of the commercial invoices, liquidation sheets of the supplying firm and all correspondence relating to his transactions on taxable merchandise. (2) Shall permit the fiscal officials to retain, for the purpose of official investigation, any of the documents above mentioned. Said documents may be exchanged for certified copies. (3) Representatives, agents, commission agents, brokers, or any other intermediaries not residents of Puerto Rico and coming from abroad to take orders for articles taxable under the Act shall, before leaving the Island, furnish to the Bureau of General Excises a copy of each order received, or in lieu thereof, an itemized list of said orders, specifying name and address of each customer, amount and description of articles ordered, and cost per unit thereof. § 4060-25. Keeping and furnishing of documents by financing enterprises Any person operating an enterprise of banking, financial, insurance or credit character: (1) Shall maintain for a minimum period of four years reckoning from the individual date of each document, copies of the drafts, policies, invoices, or other documents referring to his transactions relating to articles taxed under the Act. (2) Shall permit the fiscal officials to examine the documents mentioned above, and shall, on request of the Secretary, furnish copies of the same for purposes of investigation. § 4060-26. Keeping and furnishing of documents 

Any enumeration made in this division with respect to the keeping and furnishing of documents and to the persons who must keep and furnish same, shall not imply a limitation or constitute a limitative enumeration. 126

Surcharges and interest (a) When a taxpayer does not declare or pay the corresponding tax within the time fixed and in the form prescribed in the Act and this division, besides being guilty of a misdemeanor, he shall pay, in addition to said tax and as a part thereof, as a penalty, 5 percent of the amount of the tax when payment is made after 30 days from the date on which the tax should have been paid, but not exceeding 60 days; or 10 percent of the amount of the tax when payment is made after 60 days from the date on which the tax should have been paid. He shall, in addition, pay interest on the amount of the tax at the rate of three-fourths (34) of one percent per month (0.0075) computed from the date on which said taxes should have been paid. (b) In the case of provisional payments where the taxpayer has paid 80 percent or more of the tax finally determined, he shall pay interest on the difference determined, at the rate of three-fourths (34) of one percent per month (0.0075), computed from the date on which said taxes should have been paid. 127

§ 4078-2. General definitions 

In construing this division, the terms of general use herein below set forth shall have the following meanings: (1) "Private Bonded Warehouse" means a store where, through the furnishing of bond satisfactory to the Secretary, are deposited taxable articles introduced or locally manufactured, for sale exclusively to persons leaving Puerto Rico. (2) "Articles for Use and Consumption" any taxable article under Act No. 2, approved January 20, 1956, as amended. (3) "Authorization" means the written recognition granted by the Secretary to an owner or a concessionaire of a store established at an air or maritime terminal in order to sell in said place taxable articles tax free to persons leaving Puerto Rico. (4) "Purchaser" means any person who before leaving Puerto Rico buys taxable articles in stores located at air or maritime terminals and is delivered said articles, tax free, aboard the plane or ship.

(6) "Requirements" means any conditions imposed by the Secretary to an owner or a concessionaire of a store established, and authorized to make commercial transactions of introduction, purchase and sale of articles for use and consumption, at any air or maritime terminal in Puerto Rico, and who is authorized to sell articles for use and consumption to persons leaving Puerto Rico. (7) "Secretary" means the Secretary of the Treasury. (8) "Store" means any commercial establishment used for the storage and sale of articles for use and consumption to persons leaving Puerto Rico and which has been established upon recommendation of the Department of Tourism and with the approval of the Secretary to operate as a private bonded warehouse at air or maritime terminals in Puerto Rico.

§ 4078-4. Secretary's authorization for establishment of stores at air or maritime terminals

Subject to the conditions prescribed in §§ 4078-5 to 4017-15 of this division, the Secretary shall, upon recommendation of the De partment of Tourism of the Economic Development Administration of Puerto Rico, authorize the establishment of bonded stores located at air or maritime terminals in Puerto Rico, which stores shall operate as private bonded warehouses and shall be used exclusively to deposit and store taxable articles for sale, tax free, to persons leaving Puerto Rico. The articles that may be sold in said stores are: (a) Articles introduced by the owner himself or the concessionaire of the store for sale in said store, tax free, to persons leaving Puerto Rico. (b) Articles acquired from local manufacturers by the owner himself or the concessionaire of the store for sale in said store, tax free, to persons leaving Puerto Rico. § 4078-5. Application

§ 4078-6. Requirements 

Stores established in the aerial or maritime zones in Puerto Rico in compliance with the purposes sought by the Excise Act, as amended, shall meet the following requirements: (a) Shall be provided with receptacles, cases, railings, and shelves of adequate size that will permit the orderly and systematic segregation of the articles stored. (b) Shall meet reasonable safety requirements, in the judgment of the Secretary of the Treasury. § 4078-7. Authorization to establish store as bonded warehouse

The Secretary shall, upon the furnishing by the interested person of a bond in the amount said official may deem it necessary to require, issue an authorization for said person to operate such store as a private bonded warehouse, for the sale of taxable articles, tax free, to persons leaving Puerto Rico. 

§ 4078-8. Internal revenue license 

The internal revenue license required for the sale of articles tax free in stores established at air or maritime terminals to persons leaving Puerto Rico shall be posted or placed conspicuously in the store.

The store owner or concessionaire may not store the articles introduced and/or acquired from local manufacturers in other places or premises outside of the store for which the internal revenue license has been obtained. § 4078-12. Articles sold not to be delivered to purchaser until he is aboard plane or ship taking him outside of Puerto Rico In no case of a sale made to purchasers leaving Puerto Rico shall the merchandise sold be delivered immediately to the purchaser. 

Said merchandise shall be duly packed and delivered by the vendor to the person in charge or the representative of the company operating the aircraft or ship, who, after accepting the package and signing the bill of lading or invoice which the vendor shall submit to him, shall see to it that the package containing the articles be deposited in the plane or ship, as the case may be, for delivery directly to the purchaser by the person authorized therefor, after the plane is airborne or the ship has weighed anchor.

The person operating a store at air or maritime terminals shall issue to the purchaser a commercial sale invoice containing, among other things, the following information: (1) Name and address of purchaser.

§ 4078-14. Keeping documents 

The store owner or concessionaire shall keep in his files, chronologically and for a period of at least 4 years counting from the date on which the transaction was made, and separately from any other business, the commercial sale invoices, the import or purchase from local manufacturers invoices, and any other merchandise-delivery document. Likewise, he shall keep, for the same period of time, his accounting books, records, reports, internal revenue returns, and any other document reflecting transactions involving articles for use and consumption, which documents he shall furnish to the fiscal officers of the Bureau of Excise Taxes upon their request. $ 4078-15. Filing inventories

Any person authorized by the Secretary to sell taxable articles in a store established at air or maritime terminals to persons leaving Puerto Rico, shall be under obligation to render, within the 10 days following the close of his annual operations, an inventory containing the description of all articles in his possession, showing the quantity and type of each article, serial or identification number, and cost. 

§ 4078-16. Periodic inspections by fiscal officers 

The fiscal officers of the Bureau of Excise Taxes are hereby authorized to conduct periodic investigations and inspections to verify compliance with the provisions of the law and this division. § 4078-17. Ceasing operations in store

Any store owner or concessionaire who ceases in his activities, or sells or transfers his stock to another person, shall notify in writing the Secretary informing him about the articles sold or transferred or in his possession on the date of ceasing operations. 

The store owner or concessionaire shall be bound to pay the taxes, with penalties, on any articles for use and consumption in his possession upon ceasing operations. Said taxes shall be computed on

§ 4078-18. General provisions 

The provisions of the Regulations promulgated under the Excise Act of Puerto Rico shall be applicable, in addition to this division, insofar as such provisions are not in conflict with Act No. 65, approved June 17, 1966 [13 L.P.R.A. §§ 4012 and 4051]. 

§ 4078-19. Penalties 

Any person authorized to operate a store at air or maritime terminals who fails to comply with the provisions of the Excise Act of Puerto Rico and of this division, shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and upon conviction punished by a fine not exceeding $200 for each case, provided the offense committed does not involve fraud, deceit, systematic evasion, or when the commission of the act herein prohibited seriously endangers the efficacy of the law of this division, in which latter case the fine may be greater than $200 but never more than $2,000. § 4078-20. Codification. The Regulation carried into this division originally contained the text of those provisions of the Excise Act of Puerto Rico which it construes. They have been omitted from this publication and a reference to the appropriate title and section of L.P.R.A. inserted instead. 

Separability. Section 19 of the Regulation set out in this division provided: "If any part of this Regulation [division] is declared null by a court, its other provisions shall remain in force."

§ 4078-102. Definitions 

In construing the Excise Act of Puerto Rico and this division, the terms of general use herein below set forth shall have the following meanings: (1) "Manufacturer" means any person who, through the use of raw material, produces gasoline and gas oil or diesel oil, or substitutes of said products. (2) "Date of introduction" means the day of arrival of the vessel in port or of the landing of the plane in the airport, regardless of the actual time of unloading. However, in cases of taxable merchandise introduced from outside of Puerto Rico, where, by reason of customs, military or sanitary rules, or of strike at the piers and other terminals, or for some other reason of force majeure, the taxpayer or the person liable for the payment of the taxes levied by law is prevented from taking possession of the merchandise within the term of 30 days after its arrival in the Island, then the date of introduction shall be considered to be the date on which the customs office or the pertinent authority allows the taxpayer or the person liable for the payment of the tax to take possession of the 

Jan. 31, 1967 

Vol. 6, No. 1 128.9

T.134078 

Ch. 354

EXCISE ACT 

merchandise introduced, or the date on which the termination of the strike has been officially announced by the Secretary of Labor, or the date on which, in the judgment of the Secretary of the Treasury, the circumstances of force majeure have ceased to exist. (3) "Introduction" means the arrival at the piers, airports or other terminals in Puerto Rico of: (a) articles consigned to the Island which are actually unloaded at the piers, airports or other terminals; (b) articles brought to said terminals by the passengers or crew of ships or airplanes. (4) "Introducer" means any person who acquires an article from outside of Puerto Rico, either as the consignee of the article or through a bank, shipping agent, or other intermediary. (5) "Municipality" means all the municipal governments of 

Puerto Rico. (6) "Person" includes an individual, a syndicate, a trust, an estate, a partnership, a company, a corporation, an association or organization of any type. (7) "Tax-exempt person" means any person who by reason of his exempt status as determined herein is lawfully authorized to acquire taxable articles without need of paying the taxes. (8) "Secretary" means the Secretary of the Treasury. (9) Raw material, any raw material introduced into or produced or acquired in Puerto Rico to be used as such in Puerto Rico within the year immediately following its introduction or acquisition in the manufacture of finished products. "Raw material" includes: (a) any product derived in its natural estate from agriculture or the extractive industries; and (b) any subproduct, by-product, semimanufactured product or finished product.

§ 4078-106. Sales, transfers, deliveries, etc., tax exempt

The tax exemption on gasoline and gas oil or diesel oil established by the Excise Act is applicable both to said products when introduced into Puerto Rico as well as to those manufactured in Puerto 

Rico. The exemptions are as follows: 

(1) With respect to gasoline (secs. 30 and 47(a) of the Excise

Act [13 L.P.R.A. §§ 4030 and 4070(a)]): 

(a) Sales or transfers to the United States of America, its agencies and instrumentalities, and the National Guard of Puerto Rico. (b) Individual deliveries of 5,000 or more gallons to the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico or any of its instrumentalities or political subdivisions. (c) Such as shall have become contaminated with water or other products before or upon being pumped from a ship or from refineries to tanks or installations in Puerto Rico and thereby rendered not commercially salable or usable. (d) Such as has been used in sea and air voyages between Puerto Rico and other places or in air voyages within the territorial limits of Puerto Rico. (In these cases the exemption is of a partial character, it being restricted to 9 cents out of the 11 cents paid on each gallon or fraction thereof.) (e) Such as is exported outside of Puerto Rico under the pro visions of sec. 47(a) of the Excise Act [13 L.P.R.A. § 4047 (a)]. 

(2) With respect to gas oil or diesel oil (secs. 37 and 47 (a) of the Excise Act [13 L.P.R.A. §§ 4037 and 4047 (a)]): 

(a) Sales or transfers to the United States of America, its agencies and instrumentalities, and the National Guard of Puerto Rico. (b) Individual deliveries of 5,000 or more gallons to the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico or any of its instrumentalities or political subdivisions. (c) Such as has been distributed outside of Puerto Rico, including that supplied to ships for use by them in their sea voyages between Puerto Rico and other places. (d) Such as shall have been contaminated with water or other products before or upon being pumped from or to a ship or from refineries to tanks or installations in Puerto Rico and thereby rendered not commercially salable or usable. (e) Such as is exported outside of Puerto Rico under the pro visions of sec. 47 (a) of the Excise Act [13 L.P.R.A. § 4047].

§ 4078-107. Sales to exempt entities 

The exemptions on sales to exempt entities shall be substantiated by commercial invoices, bills of lading, exemption certificates, cargo and landing reports or documents, etc., accompanied by a letter explaining the transaction, addressed to the Secretary of the Treasury.

Refunds or credits by reason of exemptions shall be made or allowed to the person or entity that shows to the satisfaction of the Secretary that he or it has borne the financial burden of the tax, even though such person or entity be other than the one that paid the tax to the treasury.

With request to deliveries of gasoline and/or gas oil or diesel oil made to agencies, dependencies, instrumentalities or political subdivisions of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, the exemption shall be supported by a previous order or contract issued and paid for a quantity of 5,000 or more gallons.

Delivery of petroleum products sold to distributors by refineries The delivery of gasoline and gas oil or diesel oil sold by refineries to local distributors shall be subject to surveillance by the fiscal officers of the Bureau of Excise Taxes. § 4078-114. Examination of documents and records 

Whenever necessary and to the extent the Secretary may deem pertinent, the fiscal officials of the Bureau of Excise Taxes shall examine documents, records, books, inventories, or any other papers related with the introduction, manufacture, sale and transfer of taxable petroleum products in Puerto Rico. § 4078-115. The consignee of the ship shall, either personally or through his agents or employees, deliver to an official of the Bureau of Excise Taxes a copy of the ship's manifest before starting the pumping into tanks or other receptacles. 

§ 4078-117. Use of steel tapelines 

Importers or manufacturers or their agents or employees shall provide themselves with steel tapelines in good working order and approved by the Weights and Measures Division of the Economic Stabilization Administration of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, and shall give to the Government official all necessary cooperation so as to take an exact measurement of the content existing in the tanks where gasoline and gas oil or diesel oil introduced or manufactured in Puerto Rico is to be deposited. § 4078-118. Use of admission and blowoff valves

Importers, distributors or manufacturers shall provide the tanks or reservoirs where petroleum products are to be deposited, with admission and blowoff valves in good working order, in such manner that padlocks and straps may be placed, so that the Department of the Treasury may, during the operation of the pumping of the products, have absolute control of the intakes and outlets. Said padlocks and straps shall not be removed or changed without the presence or authorization of a fiscal official of the Bureau of Excise Taxes.

§ 4078-119. Documents of the importer or manufacturer shall accompany upon making payment of tax 

Every importer or manufacturer of taxable petroleum products shall be bound to present, together with the internal revenue invoice by which he is going to make payment of the taxes on the taxable products imported or manufactured, the following document, as the case may be: outturn [sic] report, report of cargo, certificate of cargo, or any other document setting forth the following information: name of ship or manufacturer, date of unloading, delivery or transfer, tank or tanks where the said petroleum product or products was or were deposited, and quantity received at observed temperature. § 4078-120. Petroleum products dispensed at refineries to bonded distributors not owning storage tanks In the case of bonded distributors not owning storage tanks, said distributors shall obtain the gasoline and diesel oil or gas oil under the following conditions: (1) Dispensing at the refinery shall be made through the use of certified metering equipment in the refinery's filler. (2) The distributor shall provide himself with truck-tanks duly gauged by the Weights and Measures Division of the Economic. 

Stabilization Administration of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico. 

(3) The certificates issued by the Weights and Measures Division with relation to the gauging of the distributor's truck-tanks shall have been previously filed in the Bureau of General Excise Taxes. (4) The internal revenue invoice supporting payment of the tax, which payment shall be made within 10 days after delivery of the product, shall be accompanied by at least the following documents: (a) Delivery or receiving tickets of the refinery which dispensed the product. (b) Certificate of the refinery indicating the number of gallons dispensed daily. § 4078-121. § 4078-123. Procedure for commingled tanks system to deposit, under bond, taxable petroleum products, tax free, for use of exempt entities (a) If the product is introduced into Puerto Rico, it shall be introduced in quantities of 5,000 or more gallons and shall be consigned to the entity exempt in the ship's manifest. (b) Deliveries in tanks of the distributor, of stock deriving from refineries, shall be made in quantities of 5,000 or more gallons and shall be consigned directly to the exempt entity. (c) Gasoline distributing companies shall send to the Bureau of Excise Taxes, not later than the 25th of each month, a detailed statement of all gasoline and/or gas oil or diesel oil imported and/or served from commingled tanks during the previous month and delivered for use of the exempt entity. Said statement, as well as the certifications of the exempt entity, shall be signed by an authorized official of the exempt entity, and such signature shall have been previously registered in the Bureau of Excise Taxes. § 4078-124. DIVISION 3. RULES TO GOVERN THE PROCESSING OR MANUFACTURE OF TAXABLE ARTICLES IN PUERTO RICO AND THE COMPUTATION AND PAYMENT OF THE TAX; 

ON THE POLISHING OF PRECIOUS AND SEMI-PRECIOUS STONES IN PUERTO RICO, AND ON THE TAX EXEMPTION OF MACHINERY AND EQUIPMENT ESSENTIAL TO THE ESTABLISHMENT AND OPERATION OF MANUFACTURING PLANTS PART ONE SUBDIVISION 1. INTRODUCTION SECTIONS 4078-201. Scope of Regulation § 4078-201. Scope of Regulation 

(a) This division deals with the processing or manufacture in Puerto Rico of taxable articles, the computation and payment of the tax thereon, the plants engaged in the polishing of precious or semi-precious stones, the tax exemption on the machinery and equipment essential to the establishment and operation of manufacturing plants; and the tax-exempted raw material as well as with the articles manufactured for exportation, all pursuant to the provisions of the Excise Act of Puerto Rico, Act No. 2, ap proved January 20, 1956 [13 L.P.R.A. §§ 4001 to 4103], as sub sequently amended. (b) This division is promulgated in conformity with the authority conferred upon the Secretary of the Treasury by Section 

78 of the said Act [13 L.P.R.A. § 4078], and shall be known by the short title of "Manufacturers' Regulation".

SUBDIVISION 2. DEFINITIONS 

4078-211. General definitions 

§ 4078-211. General definitions 

In construing this Regulation, the terms of general use hereinbelow set forth shall have the following meanings: 

(1) Taxable article: Any object taxed by the Excise Act of Puerto Rico [13 L.P.R.A. §§ 4001 to 4103]. 

(2) Taxpayer: In the case of articles manufactured in Puerto 

Rico, the taxpayer shall be the manufacturer. (3) Manufacturer: Means any person engaged in the manufacture of any article in Puerto Rico, including: (A) assemblers or integrators of articles; (B) persons who re-process partially processed articles; and (C) persons engaged in the polishing and/or cutting of precious or semi-precious stones. (4) Commercial invoice: Any authentic document which the manufacturer or seller abroad may submit to the manufacturer in Puerto Rico, or which the manufacturer in Puerto Rico may issue to the purchaser of the articles by him manufactured, stating the kind and price of the merchandise. (5) Date of introduction: Means the day of arrival of the ship in port, or of the landing of the plane on the airport, regardless of the actual time of unloading. However, in cases of taxable merchandise introduced from outside Puerto Rico, where, by reason of customs, military or sanitary rules, or of strike at the piers and other terminals, or for some other reason of force majeure, the taxpayer or the person liable for the payment of the taxes levied by law is prevented from taking possession of the merchandise 

May 31, 1968 128.19 

Vol. 7, No. 5

T.§ 4078-211 

EXCISE ACT 

Ch. 354 within the term of 30 days after its arrival in the Island, then the date of introduction shall be considered to be the date on which the customs office or the pertinent authority allows the taxpayer or the person liable for the payment of the tax to take possession of the merchandise introduced, or the date on which the termination of the strike has been officially announced by the Secretary of Labor, or the date on which, in the judgment of the Secretary of the Treasury, the circumstances of force majeure have ceased to exist. (6) Fiscal official: Means any internal-revenue agent, accountant, fiscal aid, internal-revenue collector, or any other person whom the Secretary of the Treasury may designate for conducting investigations with respect to the introduction, manufacture, sale, conveyance, consumption, or acquisition of taxable articles in 

Puerto Rico. 

(7) Introduction: Shall mean the receiving by any person of an article from abroad, whether as consignee, or through a bank, shipping agent, or any other intermediary. 

(8) Act: Is Act No. 2, approved January 20, 1956, as subse quently amended, known as the "Excise Act of Puerto Rico" [13 

L.P.R.A. §§ 4001 to 4103]. 

(9) Raw material: Any raw material (except hydraulic cement) introduced into or produced or acquired in Puerto Rico to be used in Puerto Rico within the year immediately following its introduction or acquisition in the manufacture of finished products. "Raw material” includes: (A) any product derived in its natural state from agriculture or the extractive industries; and (B) any sub-product, by-product, semi-manufactured product, or finished product. (10) Municipality: Means all the municipal governments, including the municipal government of San Juan and Culebra. (11) Person: Includes an individual, a syndicate, a trust, an estate, a partnership, a company, a corporation, an association of any type. (12) Tax-exempt person: Means any person who, by reason of his exempt status, as determined by law, is lawfully authorized to acquire taxable articles without need of paying the taxes. (13) Manufacturing plant: Shall mean the following:

May 31, 1968 

Vol. 7, No. 5 128.20

Ch. 354

T.13 § 4078-221 

ADMINISTRATIVE PROVISIONS 

(A) A plant devoted to the assemblage or integration of tax able articles to which section 4 of the Act [13 L.P.R.A. § 4004] 

refers; or (B) A plant devoted to the conversion of raw material into finished products different from its original condition, as well as a plant that produces a product in relation to which substantial industrial operations are performed in Puerto Rico which, in the judgment of the Secretary of the Treasury, merit treatment as a manufacturing plant because of its nature, extension, investment, magnitude, technology involved, number of jobs provided, and any other contribution the operation has made or will make to the welfare of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, or any one or more of such factors; or (C) A manufacturing plant exempt under the Industrial In centive Act of 1954 [13 L.P.R.A. §§ 241 to 251], the Industrial Tax Exemption Act of 1948 [13 L.P.R.A. §§ 221 to 238], and any other exemption act subsequently approved for the same purposes. 

Definition of "manufacturing plant." "Manufacturing plant" does not include: (i) service plants, including laundry, lumber yards, pasteurizing plants; (ii) commercial establishments in which a manufacturing process of a relatively minor economic importance is carried on as a collateral activity. (14) Stone polisher: Includes all persons engaged in the polishing or cutting of precious or semi-precious stones in Puerto Rico. 

(15) Secretary: Means the Secretary of the Treasury. 

SECTIONS SUBDIVISION 3. SCOPE OF TAX DETERMINATION AND TIME OF PAYMENT

Determination of prices and costs

§ 4078-221. Scope of tax 

The Tax shall apply both to all articles sold by the manufacturer in Puerto Rico as well as to such as he may consume, use, or 

May 31, 1968

128.21

T.4078-221 

EXCISE ACT 

Ch. 354 otherwise dispose of in Puerto Rico, except when only for the sole and exclusive purpose of being exhibited, demonstrated, or used in beneficent, charitable, cultural, educational, scientific, or pedagogical activities, or for purpose of experiment, or of industrial or commercial propaganda, or under any other similar circumstances. 

It shall also apply to such articles as to which, in the judgment of the Secretary, he cannot satisfactorily account for his final disposition thereof. 

§ 4078-222. Determination of prices and costs [Text of Act, see 13 L.P.R.A. § 4055 (a), (b).] § 4078-223. Cost in Puerto Rico to the manufacturer 

Shall be the total cost at his factory of the raw material, plus the cost of direct labor, and general manufacturing expenses, including the cost of containers. 

§ 4078-224. Special rule for certain repairs 

(a) In the case of articles which are unavailable in the Puerto Rican market, and which, under circumstances of an emergency nature, are either repaired or specially manufactured in Puerto Rico, the "cost in Puerto Rico", determined in accordance with the rule established in the Act for manufacturers, may be reduced, in the judgment of the Secretary, by up to 40 percent thereof to offset the extraordinary cost arising from the emergency and the special treatment of the order. The "taxable price in Puerto Rico" shall be the "cost in Puerto Rico" so reduced, plus 20 percent. (b) This reduction shall be considered only in those cases where the manufacturer alleges, and the Secretary can ascertain, that the actual costs of the articles so manufactured or repaired differ from the normal costs thereof. § 4078-225. Determination of "taxable price" of leased articles

In the case of articles which are customarily leased rather than sold by the manufacturer, the "taxable price in Puerto Rico" shall be 50 percent of the bona fide rentals which under the leasecontract would accumulate in 5 successive years of the lease, plus 20 percent of such amount. Notwithstanding the restriction con tained in Section 10 of the Act [13 L.P.R.A. § 4010], to the effect that the tax shall be paid only once, any successive lease or any other transfer after a lease shall be considered as a new taxable event.

Vol. 7, No. 5 128.22

ADMINISTRATIVE PROVISIONS 

§ 4078-226. Determination of "taxable price in Puerto Rico" by the Secretary

In case the information appearing in the documents and/or accounting books in the possession of the manufacturer is not authentic or sufficient for determining the "cost in Puerto Rico" of any article; or, in the opinion of the Secretary, considerably differs from that registered in documents and/or accounting books of other manufacturers of similar products, the Secretary shall then determine the "taxable price in Puerto Rico" in accordance with such method as, in his judgment, is the most appropriate. 

§ 4078-227. Articles taxable under section 10 [Text of Act, see 13 L.P.R.A. § 4060 (b).] § 4078-228. Application of tax 

(a) The tax is due when the article sold is delivered to the purchaser or his representative. If the article is used, consumed, donated, or otherwise disposed of by the manufacturer, the tax is due as soon as the corresponding taxable event falls. (b) Whenever a manufacturer consigns articles to his agent or distributor, but retains the property title to such articles, the tax is due as soon as such agent or distributor sells or otherwise disposes of the articles in Puerto Rico.

The manufacturer shall furnish the Secretary the required information in the monthly statement of articles sold, or any such other information relating to the manufacture and sale of his product as may be necessary in the opinion of the Secretary. 

May 31, 1968 

Vol. 7, No. 5 128.23

T.§ 4078-233 

Ch. 354

EXCISE ACT § 4078-233. Provisional payment 

When a taxpayer shows to the satisfaction of the Secretary that he has been unable to obtain, at the moment the tax becomes due, sufficient or adequate information definitively to determine the "cost in Puerto Rico" of the manufactured articles, he may make a provisional payment based on approximate costs according to similar articles recently manufactured, or according to some other reasonable criterion, in the judgment of the Secretary. The taxpayer, shall be under obligation to make the supplementary payment plus the penalties provided in Section 87 (a) of the Excise Act [13 L.P.R.A. § 4087(a)], within a period of 90 days counting from the date the provisional payment has been made. The taxpayer shall not be bound to the payment of surcharge when the amount of the provisional payment made equals or exceeds 80 percent of the tax finally determined. When the payment is in excess of this amount the Secretary shall reimburse the excess so paid according to the act.

Puerto Rico to tax exempt persons

The tax shall not be applicable to such articles manufactured in Puerto Rico that are exported or sold to exempt persons. The manufacturer shall include in his monthly statement of articles sold, such articles as were directly exported by him, or transferred by him to shipping agents for exportation, or sold to exempt persons. Articles exported and/or sold to exempt persons shall be listed in the monthly statement separately from those sold to local dealers and for which the tax is being paid. With regard to articles exported and/or sold to exempt persons, the manufacturer shall keep in his files a copy of the documents evincing such transactions. 

§ 4078-243. Articles purchased in Puerto Rico by a manufacturer from another manufacturer who processes them, where such purchase is necessary to perform a contract with a person abroad Whenever for any reason a manufacturer needs to acquire, from the production of another manufacturer, articles which are similar to those he manufactures, in order to comply with the terms of a contract with a person abroad, such articles shall be tax exempt. 

The manufacturer who processed same shall include in his monthly statement of articles sold the pertinent information regarding such sale, and shall keep in his files the document evincing same. 

§ 4078-244. Articles manufactured in Puerto Rico for sale to manufacturing plants (a) To obtain tax exemption on articles produced in Puerto Rico and sold to manufacturing plants, under the provisions of Section 

46(b) of the Excise Act [13 L.P.R.A. § 4046 (b)], the manufacturer performing the sale shall, before delivering the articles, make sure that the purchaser is a bona fide manufacturer; otherwise, he shall be liable for the payment of the taxes plus the corresponding penalties in case of delayed payment. (b) Not later than the tenth day of the month following that in which the sale was made, the manufacturer making the sale shall file with the bureau of General Excises of the Department of the Treasury the official Declaration of Articles Sold, wherein shall be indicated the name and address of the manufacturer who

(c) The purchaser shall be liable for the payment of the tax and the pertinent penalties, in case it is found that the acquired articles are not being used for purposes comprised in the exemption. 

§ 4078-245. Returned articles. 

[Text of Act, 13 L.P.R.A. § 4048(a), (b), (c), (d).] § 4078-246. Articles returned to manufacturer

The tax shall not be applicable to articles sold by the manufacturer and returned to him by the purchaser within 60 days from the date of sale, if the latter did not commercially exhibit or use them. The manufacturer shall notify the Secretary of the reasons for the return. If in the opinion of the Secretary the exemption is in order, the amount of the tax paid shall be reimbursed or credited to the manufacturer. § 4078-247. Articles for exhibition or use in certain activities (a) The tax shall not be applicable to articles intended by the manufacturer for the sole and exclusive purpose of being exhibited, demonstrated, or used in beneficent, charitable, cultural, educational, scientific, or pedagogical activities, or for purposes of experiment, or of industrial or commercial propaganda, or under any other similar circumstances, provided property title thereto is not transferred to another person. (b) Before using any article in any of the above-mentioned activities, the manufacturer shall notify his intention to the Secretary, and identify the articles set aside for such activity by name, serial number, if any, and give such other details as may render their identification easier. The said notification shall contain, also, the name of the firm, partnership, association, organization, etc., sponsoring the activity, as well as the name of the place where the articles are to be used and the duration of such activity. 

§ 4078-248. Damaged articles 

If, after payment of tax, any article sold by a manufacturer reaches the purchaser in a condition such as to make it useless, and the purchaser returns it to the manufacturer within 60 days 

May 31, 1968 

Vol. 7, No. 5 128.26

Ch. 354

ADMINISTRATIVE PROVISIONS 

T.13 § 4078-252 from selling date, the manufacturer shall be entitled to reimbursement, provided he shows the following evidence to the Secretary: credit note or return receipt signed by the purchaser, copy of sales invoices, number and date of the Statement of Articles Sold, and date on which the tax was paid. 

§ 4078-249. Intrinsic defects 

(a) When article sold by a manufacturer is returned by the purchaser because it is faulty, the manufacturer shall be entitled to reimbursement, if within the term of 120 days from selling date he shows the Secretary the following evidence: credit note or return receipt signed by the purchaser, copy of the sales invoice, number and date of the Statement of Articles Sold and date on which tax was paid, and a certification of his final disposal of the article. (b) The reimbursement, in this case, shall not exceed 80 percent of the tax collected. § 4078-250. Merchandise returned from abroad to be reprocessed 

The Secretary shall grant exemption on articles manufactured in Puerto Rico which, after subsequent exportation to markets abroad are then rejected or returned to their manufacturer or his distributor in Puerto Rico, for reprocessing, reconditioning, or repacking. This exemption shall be granted if the manufacturer, upon previous notice to the Secretary, reships the articles repaired, reconditioned or repacked, or destroys or uses the same as raw material, all within a period of time which shall not go beyond the last day of the third month following the month of introduction. In such cases the manufacturer shall produce evidence showing his final disposal of the articles, as well as of correspondence exchanged between the purchaser abroad and the manufacturer, such as may serve as a basis to support his right to the exemption. 

§ 4078-251. Articles used in manufacturing processes [Text of Act, see 13 L.P.R.A. § 4046(a).] § 4078-252. Raw material 

Any taxable article used as raw material (except hydraulic cement), shall be exempt from payment of tax, provided it is used May 31, 1968 128.27 

Vol. 7, No. 5

T.§ 4078-252 

EXCISE ACT 

Ch. 354 within the term of one year from the date of its introduction or acquisition, in the manufacture of finished products. Should the manufacturer, for any reason, find himself unable to meet this requirement, he shall so notify the Secretary in writing before the expiration of such period, setting forth the reasons which prevented him from processing the raw material, and requesting an extension of time for processing same. The Secretary shall grant the extension when in his opinion the reasons adduced by the manufacturer so justify.

SECTIONS PART THREE SUBDIVISION 6. POLISHERS OF PRECIOUS OR SEMI-PRECIOUS STONES 

4078-261. 

Unpolished stones 

4078-262. Requirements to be fulfilled by polishers 

4078-263. Loss of stones during polishing or cutting process or after finished for sale or exportation § 4078-261. Unpolished stones

Precious or semi-precious stones in rough form, which have not been cut or polished, shall be deemed raw material. § 4078-262. Requirements to be fulfilled by polishers

In addition to each and every one of the requirements set forth in this division to be met by manufacturers in general, polishers of precious or semi-precious stones must fulfill the following: (1) Receipt of raw material-Upon receipt of precious or semiprecious stones for polishing or cutting, they shall immediately write down on their records the receipt date of each shipment, name of remitter, quantity of stones received, and the gross weight, carats, and value of each. The commercial invoices and other documents relating to the importation of such articles shall be kept for a term of 4 years from date of each document. (2) Deposit of the stones-All stones shall be deposited in a place which meets the necessary safety requirements within the premises of the polishing company itself, and shall be available for inspection of the fiscal officials of the Bureau of General Excises. (3) Exportation of finished stones-The polisher shall keep, for a period of not less than 4 years, the shipping documents of all stones exported-bills of lading, post-office receipts, air waybills, as well as like documents or any other documents-proving 

May 31, 1968

Vol. 7, No. 5 

128.28

Ch. 354

ADMINISTRATIVE PROVISIONS T.13 § 4078-271 

that the stones have arrived at their destination. He shall make a note on his records of the data relating to the quantity, carats, and value of the exported stones, as against shipments received. § 4078-263. Loss of stones during polishing or cutting process or after finished for sale or exportation (a) The tax shall not be applicable to precious or semi-precious stones lost before the same are finished and ready for sale in the local market, or for exportation, provided the polisher meets the following requirements: (1) Not later than the fifth day after noticing the loss of a stone during the polishing or cutting process, the polisher shall report the fact to the Bureau of General Excises, submitting thereto a sworn statement setting forth the date when loss of the stone was noticed, cost of the stone, and steps taken towards finding it and result of the investigation made. (2) The data on the stone in process of polishing or cutting shall be written down on the polisher's records. (3) The polisher shall at once notify the Bureau of General Excises the finding of any stone reported as lost during the polishing or cutting process, and shall make the pertinent notes on his records. (b) Nor shall the tax be applicable to precious or semi-precious stones lost after finished and ready for sale or exportation, provided the same are found within a period which shall not exceed 60 days from the date the polisher noticed their loss and notified the same to the Bureau of General Excises. (c) The Secretary reserves the right to levy and collect the tax on such articles, if through investigation it is ascertained that the polisher is not excercising due control and care to avoid recurring losses.

§ 4078-271. Articles used in manufacturing processes [Text of Act, see 13 L.P.R.A. § 4046 (b).] § 4078-272. Scope of exemption 

The exemption shall include all equipment, parts and accessories used to obtain and distribute the energy indispensable to run the manufacturing equipment; as well as the equipment, parts and accessories to replace the factory machinery in use. The manufacturer shall however, render to the Secretary an annual inventory of the equipment stocks acquired by him to be used as spare parts. 

§ 4078-273. Articles introduced by manufacturer 

The manufacturer may take possession, without the previous payment of taxes, of that machinery, apparatus, equipment, parts and accessories thereof that he may introduce in Puerto Rico to be installed and used in his manufacturing plant in any of the exempt activities. However, the exemption shall be of a conditional nature until the final use to which the articles so introduced are devoted is determined. The manufacturer shall keep in his files for a period of not less than 4 years or until a final determination has been made as to the exemption, the commercial invoices, bills of lading and any other documents related to the introduction of said articles. § 4078-274. Articles acquired in Puerto Rico by manufacturer (a) The manufacturer shall be entitled to reimbursement of the tax paid by the dealer-importer on those articles acquired in Puerto Rico for use in any exempt activity under Article 46 of the Excise Act [13 L.P.R.A. § 4046], provided that in the sale price has been included said tax and that he establishes the claim. within 4 years from the date of the acquisition of the articles. (b) For the purposes of the reimbursement, the manufacturer shall accompany with his application the following documents: (1) Commercial invoice of purchase; (2) Certificate of seller waiving his right to the reimbursement and assenting that same be made in favor of the manufacturer, stating at the same time the number and date of the internal-revenue invoice in which he paid the tax. 

May 31, 1968 

Vol. 7, No. 5 128.30

Ch. 354

ADMINISTRATIVE PROVISIONS T.13 § 4078-278 

§ 4078-275. Articles acquired by manufacturer from bonded warehouses or from other manufacturers who process them (a) When the manufacturer acquires the articles in Puerto Rico from bonded warehouses or other manufacturers who process them, the acquiring-manufacturer shall require from the owner or lessee of the bonded warehouse or the manufacturer from whom he acquires the articles, as the case may be, a commercial invoice describing clearly and concisely the articles acquired, keeping them in his files for a period of not less than 4 years from the date of acquisition. (b) The seller of the articles shall transmit to the Bureau of General Excise Taxes, not later than 10 days following the month of the sale, a copy of the commercial invoice issued for each sale made. § 4078-276. Duties of manufacturer upon disposing of his machinery

The manufacturer shall be obligated to: (1) Pay immediately the taxes in those cases where the machinery on which exemption was granted is devoted to non-exempt activities; (2) To inform immediately to the Bureau of Excise Taxes as to the machinery transferred for exempt purposes to other manufacturers, stating description of same; (3) Require evidence of the payment of the tax from the nonexempt acquirer before delivering any machinery or equipment sold or transferred to him. § 4078-277. Transfer of tax-exempt articles among manufacturers 

The manufacturers may transfer, sell or otherwise alienate to other manufacturers the articles on which the exemption was previously granted, provided the acquirer previously seeks and obtains the granting of the exemption. 

§ 4078-278. Joint liability 

The manufacturer-purchaser, as well as the manufacturer-seller, or owner or lessee of a bonded warehouse shall be jointly and severally liable for the payment of taxes, plus penalties and administrative fines, in case the exemption on the machinery and equipment sold is finally denied by the Secretary. 

May 31, 1968 

Vol. 7, No. 5 128.31

T.§ 4078-279 

Ch. 354

EXCISE ACT § 4078-279. Equipment unfit for requirements 

In those cases where the manufacturer, after having obtained his equipment, finds that same, for economic, climatic, or analogous reasons, cannot operate efficiently in Puerto Rico, or does not adapt itself to the structure of the manufacturing plant, or becomes useless, the manufacturer shall immediately notify the Secretary, who shall, upon verifying the absence of bad faith or negligence, consider the exemption conclusive and final (as well as the reimbursement, if any), upon occurrence of any of the following alternatives: 

SECTIONS 

(1) If the equipment is reshipped or returned to its point of origin abroad or is returned to the manufacturer-seller; (2) If the equipment is transferred to another manufacturer who has previously sought the exemption from the Secretary of the Treasury; (3) If the equipment is definitively put away and clearly unfit for subsequent use; or (4) If the equipment is dismantled, and converted into units and parts or into used metal or junk and the acquirers of same pay the taxes on the articles that may result taxable under the Act.

§ 4078-295. Bonding of manufacturer 

[Text of Act, see 13 L.P.R.A. § 4073, first and third para graphs.] § 4078-296. Amount of bond required from manufacturer (a) Any person who wishes to engage in the manufacture of any taxable article for sale in Puerto Rico shall give a bond to the 

Secretary in behalf of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico for an initial amount of not less than 1,000 dollars. The Secretary shall review the volume of sales of the manufacturer when he may deem it necessary to determine if the amount of the bond given guarantees the taxes to be paid. (b) The bond shall be given in legal tender, bonds of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico or the Treasury of the United States, mortgage notes, bank deposits "escrow", certified checks, or through an insurance company authorized to do such business in Puerto Rico, and which shall be liable for payment of taxes, as well as for the penalties and administrative fines that may be imposed to the manufacturer for violations of the Act or of this division. 

§ 4078-297. Application for establishing manufacturing plants 

Any person who wishes to engage in Puerto Rico in the manufacture of taxable articles, shall serve a written notice of the 

Secretary stating the following data: (1) address where the manufacturing plant shall be installed (2) type of articles to be manufactured, and (3) raw materials to be used.

§ 6088-3. Definitions 

The terms used in this division shall have the same meaning provided in Act No. 143 of June 30, 1969, as amended [13 L.P.R.A. 

§§ 6001 to 6135] (Alcoholic Beverages Act of Puerto Rico). 

§ 6088-4. Time for the payment of the tax-Partially bonded industrial plants (a) Partially bonded rectifiers shall pay the taxes imposed by sec. 6 of the Alcoholic Beverages Act of Puerto Rico [13 L.P.R.A. 

§ 6006] before the unrectified products are withdrawn from the warehouse or processing room for rectification and bottling. (b) The manufacturers shall pay the taxes before the alcoholic beverages produced by them are withdrawn for bottling from the bonded premises in which they are stored. (c) Bottlers having bonded warehouses shall pay the taxes prior to the withdrawal of the alcoholic beverages from the bonded warehouse for bottling. Bottlers not having a bonded warehouse shall pay the tax at the time the alcoholic beverages are received at his bottling premises. (d) Basis for the payment of the tax. The taxes on distilled spirits shall be paid on the basis of their alcoholic content at the time they are gauged prior to rectification and bottling. If the alcoholic strength is 100° proof or more, the tax shall be paid on the proof gallons determined by the gauging and if the alcoholic strength is below 100° proof, the tax shall be paid on the wine gallons determined by the gauging. 

§ 6088-5. Unit of measurement 

In assessing the taxes provided by the Act the unit of measurement shall be the standard gallon of 231 cubic inches (128 fluid ounces). § 6088-6. Payment of tax by wholly bonded industrial plants (a) The tax on alcoholic beverages produced, rectified and bottled under Government control shall be paid prior to the withdrawal 1972 

Vol. 11, No. 5 128.38

Ch. T.13 § 6088-9 

POWERS OF THE SECRETARY 

thereof from the ad hoc bonded warehouses in which they are stored. In the alternative, such tax may be paid, if the owner so desires, before the products are taken for storage to the ad hoc bonded warehouse. (b) When distilled spirits are rectified and bottled under Government control, the tax shall be levied and paid on the basis of proof gallons if the alcoholic strength at the time of the gauging is 100° proof or more before being taken to the processing plant for rectification and bottling and on the basis of wine gallons if they were below 100° proof. § 6088-7. Procedure for the payment of the tax 

Whenever the owner wishes to pay the tax in any of the cases set forth in sec. 6088-4 of this division, he shall file an application therefor on Form 628.1, in quadruplicate, or on such other form that may be required, and a declaration of alcoholic beverages indicating the alcoholic beverages on which the tax is to be paid. The 

Internal Revenue Agent shall verify the data in both documents and if he should find it correct shall authorize the payment of the tax, but shall not deliver possession of the alcoholic beverages until the tax has been paid. In order to pay the tax, the owner shall send to the Internal Revenue Office the original and the copy of the declaration of alcoholic beverages (Form 635) together with his remittance of the tax in full, either in legal tender of the United States of America or by check payable to the order of the Secretary of the Treasury. 

§ 6088-8. Action by the Collector of Internal Revenue 

Upon receipt of Form 635 with the remittance covering the payment of the tax levied by the Internal Revenue Agent, the Collector of Internal Revenue shall stamp both copies of Form 635 acknowledging the amount of the tax paid and the number of the prenumerated receipt (Form 848) issued to the taxpayer. The 

Collector of Internal Revenue shall return the original and the copy of Form 635 and the original and one copy of Form 848 to the taxpayer. 

§ 6088-9. Action by the owner 

The owner shall deliver to the Internal Revenue Agent the original of Form 635, the copy of the receipt (Form 848) issued by the Collector of Internal Revenue and the original and both copies of Form 628.1 or of any other form which may be required in lieu thereof. 1972 

Vol. 11, No. 5 128.39

ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGE LAW § 6088-10. Action by the Internal Revenue Agent 

Upon receipt of the documents referred to in sec. 6088-9 of this division the agent shall deliver to the owner the distilled spirits and/or alcoholic beverages on which the taxes were paid and shall stamp the pertinent certification in Part III of Form 628.1. He shall retain a copy of Form 628.1 for his files and shall forward to the District Revenue Agent the original and a copy thereof, the original of Form 635 and a copy of Form 848 issued by the Collector of Internal Revenue. The District Revenue Agent shall retain one copy of Form 628.1 for his files and shall forward the original thereof, the original of Form 635 and a copy of Form 848 to the Bureau of Alcoholic Beverages Taxes. § 6088-11. Deferred payment of the tax-Security

All distillers, rectifiers, bottlers or manufacturers who are interested in receiving the benefits of the procedure for the deferred payment of the tax shall give to the Secretary a security which may consist of a bond issued by an insurance company duly authorized to do business in Puerto Rico, or some other security. 

The said security shall comply with the requirements henceforth provided and it must be approved by the Secretary. The said security shall guaranty the payment of the deferred taxes, as well as the payment of such interests, surcharges and administrative fines as may be levied or imposed for any violation of the provisions governing the procedure for the deferred payment of the tax. 

§ 6088-12. Amount of the security 

(a) The total sum of the security shall not exceed $1,000,000 nor shall it be less than $1,000. The security shall in no case be for a lesser amount than the deferred tax. (b) Every person who files a security pursuant to sec. 6088–11 of this division shall keep an account of the security given and shall charge against the same an amount equal to the liability incurred upon by withdrawing spirits or alcoholic beverages when the payment of the corresponding taxes is deferred, and the security shall be credited with an amount equal to the taxes paid at the time he files each return with its corresponding payment. The account shall show the balance available under the security at all times. 1972

(c) When a distiller, rectifier, bottler or manufacturer intends to withdraw spirits or alcoholic beverages and the total amount of his security is insufficient, he shall either increase the total sum of the security or pay the tax before withdrawing said products from the government controlled premises in which they are deposited. 

§ 6088-13. Changes to the security 

Whenever an original security, supplementary security or substitute security is approved, the Secretary or his delegate shall notify the amount of the security or securities to the District Revenue Agent or the Revenue Agent in charge of the distillery, industrial plant or manufacturer concerned. Whenever a bond is cancelled, the said agents shall be so notified. § 6088-14. Application for permit by the operator of the plant- Procedure (a) Prior to withdrawing the spirits or alcoholic beverages from the premises in which they are deposited under Government control, the distiller, rectifier, manufacturer or bottler shall apply for and obtain a permit from the Secretary or his delegate, on the forms that shall be prepared by the Director of the Bureau for computing and deferring the tax, and for the withdrawal of said products. The permits shall be correlatively numbered at the beginning of each natural year. (b) In said permit, the operator shall certify that he is not in default of any payment of tax chargeable against his security and that his security is sufficient to cover the amount of tax on the spirits or alcoholic beverages described on the permit, in addition to other amounts chargeable against his security. 

§ 6088-15. Action by the Internal Revenue Agent 

When the Internal Revenue Agent in charge of the plant receives the said document, he shall verify the computation of the tax entered on the permit and, if the owner has a sufficient balance on his security, the agent shall approve the permit. 

§ 6088-16. Computation of the tax 

Once the permit to compute and defer the tax is approved, the Internal Revenue Agent shall gauge the spirits or measure the alcoholic beverages and make a report on the form prescribed by the Director. He shall fill the release report (Part III of the permit 1972 128.41

The Agent in charge of the plant shall forward daily, through the office of the District Revenue Agent, the original of the permit and the gauging report to the Director of the Bureau; he shall forward a copy of each of said documents to the owner and the agent in charge of the district and shall retain a copy of each of said documents for his files in the plant. § 6088-18. Deferment period (a) The deferred period shall be semimonthly. The periods shall run from the 1st day through the 15th day of each month and from the 16th day through the last day of each month. (b) Taxes deferred during a given semimonthly period shall be paid at the appropriate Internal Revenue Collector's office not later than the last working day of the next succeeding semimonthly period, by means of checks or legal tender, against receipts correlatively prenumbered. Taxes deferred during the month of 

June of each year shall be paid not later than the 30th day of that month. § 6088-19. The owner or operator of the industrial plant shall verify the balance of his bond as of the last day of the semimonthly period. The statement shall include the dates, permit numbers, total number of gallons covered by each permit, the amount of the tax deferred in each withdrawal, the serial number and the total sum of the security and the taxpayer identification number (the same assigned to him by the 

Bureau of Income Tax). (b) The same day that the tax is paid, the taxpayer shall deliver to the Internal Revenue Agent in charge of the plant the original and 2 copies of said statement and a copy of the prenumbered receipt issued by the Tax Collector. (c) The agent shall retain for his files one copy of the statement and he shall, the same day, forward the original and a copy of the statement and a copy of the receipt to the District Revenue Agent. Bureau's registry (a) The Review Division of the Bureau shall keep a registry of the bonds filed by each industrialist (owner) in which the amount of tax deferred daily by the owner shall be recorded. (b) Said registry shall at all times reflect the balance available on each security. (c) The Review Division shall notify the Director of the Bureau at the end of the second semimonthly period of each month the total sum of the security for each plant, the amount of taxes deferred during each semimonthly period and the available balance at the end of each one semimonthly periods corresponding to each month. 

§ 6088-21. Penalties 

(a) Any person who withdraws from an industrial plant any product on which the tax has not been paid in violation of the provisions of this division shall incur a misdemeanor, and if convicted shall be fined in an amount not less than $100 nor more than $500, or imprisoned not more than 30 days.

Explanatory note. In this section the first term of imprisonment in the Spanish text reads “90 días”. (b) Any person engaged in the industry of distilling, rectifying or manufacturing any product taxable under the provisions of the Alcoholic Beverages Act of Puerto Rico who fails to comply with or who violates any of the provisions hereof shall incur a misdemeanor and if convicted shall be fined in an amount not less than $100 nor more than $1,000, or imprisoned not less than 30 days. nor more than one year. 

§ 6088-22. Repeal 

All regulations or parts of any regulations in conflict with the provisions of this division are hereby repealed. § 6088-23. Effective date

This division shall take effect 30 days after the date of its filing at the State Department of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, pursuant to the provisions of the Regulations Act of 1958, as amended [3 L.P.R.A. §§ 1041 to 1059].

Chapter 1. Public Recreation and Parks Administration Subchapter 5. Professional and Amateur Sports DIVISION 1. AMATEUR SPORTS GENERALLY SECTIONS 

5-1. Purpose 

5-2. Definition of amateur 5-3.

§ 5-1. Purpose 

The practice of organized sport in Puerto Rico necessarily requires, for its stability, that the opposing areas of professionalism and amateurism be delineated through the formulation of a clear definition of the term "amateur". This definition should find its origin in the codes already recognized and accepted in the international sport practice. Pursuant to Act No. 4 of June 30, 1947 

[15 L.P.R.A. § 1 note, 2 et seq.], which created the Public Recrea tion and Parks Commission, and to Reorganization Plan No. 2 which took effect on July 1, 1950 [15 L.P.R.A. § 1 note], to determine its organization, powers, faculties and duties and to authorize the promulgation of regulations and impose penalties for violations thereof, and by virtue of the provisions of sec. 7 of said Act which vested the Public Recreation and Parks Commission, now the 

Public Recreation and Parks Administration, and its Administrator, with all such powers and faculties necessary to organize, direct, regulate and control all amateur and professional sports in Puerto Rico, and to this end, the Public Recreation and Parks Administrator has promulgated and approved rules defining the term amateurism, which shall from now on govern the participation of persons in the amateur sport. Such rules shall be interpreted and applied by the Council of Amateur Sports of Puerto Rico which the Parks and Recreation Administrator may appoint pursuant to powers granted thereto by law. Those cases not foreseen by these rules shall be dealt with and resolved upon by the Council of Amateur Sports of Puerto Rico, pursuant to the provisions and practices of the national and international organizations. 

Source. Sections 5-1 to 5-6: Regulation on the Practice of 

Amateur Sports in Puerto Rico, app. by Public Recreation and Parks Administrator June 9, 1966, eff. immediately after

§ 5-2. Definition of amateur 

An amateur is any person who competes only for pleasure and for the physical, mental and social benefits he may derive from the competition, and whose status as amateur has not been affected by the commission of one or more of the following acts: (1) Receiving money, directly or indirectly for participating in a competition or public exhibition. (2) Accepting, directly or indirectly, any payment or compensation for loss of time or salary while attending or training for a competition. (3) Receiving, directly or indirectly, any compensation or reward for preparing and/or training any person or team for a competition, exhibition or exercise in any sport. (4) Training, preparing and directing any person or team for a competition or exhibition in any sport. The following are hereby excluded from this rule: (A) Physical education teachers, because of the educational nature of their work which comprises the teaching of sports in general. Said physical education teachers shall not receive any pay, either directly or indirectly, for training persons or teams for competitions, as a task alien to their work as a teacher in our school system. (B) Any other teacher in our school system, whose work is exclusively academic, if he does not receive any pay, directly or indirectly, for training or directing persons or teams for competitions, as a task incidental to such work as a teacher. (C) Persons holding purely administrative positions preparing physical education or recreation courses; preparing schedules for 

June 30, 1966 136 

Vol. 5, No. 6

Ch. 

AMATEUR SPORTS GENERALLY 

T.15 § 5-2 sport competitions of groups or organizations or supervising sporting activities, if they do not receive any pay when working on activities outside of the school system. (D) Persons working as lifeguards or assistants in resorts or sport fields, if said work is not a consequence of their having capitalized on their athletic fame or ability. (E) Recreational leaders, because of the nature of their work which comprises the direction, administration and/or teaching of recreational programs. These recreational leaders shall not receive any pay for training persons or teams for competitions outside of their duties as recreational leaders. (5) Capitalizing on his sports name by endorsing, for pay, any commercial or athletic articles or equipment. (6) Participating in programs advertising a certain product through the radio, television or press, or sanctioning the use or publication of his photograph in the advertising of articles, for pay or any other material compensation. The announcing of any sporting or civic or educational event by an athlete should not be considered a violation of this rule if previously approved by the Public Recreation and Parks Administration. (7) Allowing the use of his name or his still or motion photograph as a means for advertising or recommending products of a firm, manufacturer, or agent. (8) Knowingly taking part in a competition or public exhibition as an individual or member of a team with or against ineligible persons or professionals in the sport in which said participation may occur, without previous authorization of the Public Recreation and Parks Administration, which is the registration and certification organization. (9) Betting or being interested in bets relating to any sports competition in which he is to participate. (10) Participating for any prize which cannot be duly inscribed with letters or words commemorative of the competition. (11) Issuing a challenge or in any other way evidencing his intention to participate with or against professionals. (12) Personally claiming, directly or indirectly, expenses incurred by trainers, masseurs, friends or relatives of the participant on the occasion of a competition. (13) Accepting, directly or indirectly, any gratuity for becoming or continuing as a member of a team or sporting organization. (14) Signing a contract binding himself to accept a position in

§ 5-3. Special provisions 

(a) Permit may be granted to participate against professionals in activities or competitions for charity, or in those where no entrance fee is charged. (b) Reinstatements: (1) A professional athlete and/or player may apply for his reinstatement as amateur one year after having retired or being discharged as a professional or having ceased acting as such, but his participation shall be limited only to state competitions. He cannot represent Puerto Rico in national or international competitions. The Council of Amateur Sports of Puerto Rico shall have discretion to grant or deny the reinstallation requested. (2) When the professionalization arises from his having incurred in any of the acts previously enumerated, reinstatement may be requested one year after the date of commission of the act on account of which professionalization took place, as determined by the Council. The Council of Amateur Sports of Puerto Rico shall have discretion to grant or deny the reinstallation requested. (c) Second offenders for acts which affect the status of amateur shall not be reinstated. 

§ 5-4. Procedures 

(a) Every person or organization (including the Public Recreation and Parks Administration) who has reason to believe that an amateur has committed an act which affects his status as an amateur, shall file in writing before the Public Recreation and Parks Administration, or before the Council of Amateur Sports of Puerto Rico, a complaint to those effects, stating and pointing out the act allegedly committed. It the complaint is filed before the Administrator, he shall refer it to the Council for its attention. The Council, within the next 15 days after receiving the complaint, will notify 

June 30, 1966 

Vol. 5, No. 6 138.2

Ch. 

AMATEUR SPORTS GENERALLY T.15 § 5-6 

the complained party in writing informing him of the complaint and the nature of the acts or act allegedly committed. Not before the next 15 days after notification, and within 30 days after the same, except for justified cause, the Council shall hold the corresponding administrative hearing and will receive evidence and listen to witnesses. The Council shall have power to carry out any additional investigation. (b) Every person interested in his reinstatement as an amateur, according to clauses (b) (1) and (b) (2) of the Special Provisions of this division, and not before the period of time therein stated, shall file his request in writing with the Council of Amateur Sports of Puerto Rico, accompanying the request with a sworn statement containing the facts of professionalization and the fact that he has not committed any of the acts enumerated in this division during the period of reference. The Council of Amateur Sports, within the next 30 days after the filing of the request, but not before the next 15 days after its filing, shall hold the corresponding hearing and shall receive evidence and listen to testimony. Prior to the hearing the Council shall give notification of the request filed, in writing, to those persons whom the Council believes have an interest in the matter or could be affected by the decision issued, informing them of the date and place of said hearing. (c) The decisions issued by the Council of Amateur Sports of Puerto Rico shall be issued by a majority of the total members of the Council. (d) The decisions issued by the Council of Amateur Sports of Puerto Rico shall be appealable before the Public Recreation and Parks Administrator by the persons who have a direct interest in the matter. The appeal shall be filed in writing within the next 15 days from the date of notification of the decision. 

5-5. Repeal

The Regulations, set out in this division, repeal in all its parts the Regulation of Amateur Sports in Puerto Rico, promulgated on August 5, 1953, in San Juan, Puerto Rico. 

§ 5-6. Date of effectiveness 

In accord with the Executive Order of the Governor of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico the Regulations, set out in this division, shall be effective immediately after their filing at the office of the Secretary of State.

§ 5-32. Application 

Every basketball event taking place on the Island of Puerto Rico shall be subject to the provisions of this division. § 5-33. Franchises for competitions and tournaments

No natural or artificial person may devote himself to organizing or sponsoring competitions or tournaments of amateur basketball in Puerto Rico without first having obtained a franchise issued by the Public Recreation and Parks Administration on his application and according to the requirements specified below. 

§ 5-34. Qualifications of applicants 

Every applicant for a franchise to devote himself to the organization or sponsorship of basketball tournaments shall: (1) Have a good reputation in the community. (2) Be morally and economically solvent. (3) Have amateur status in sports. (4) Submit the regulations governing the activities to which he intends to devote himself. (5) Not have been convicted of a crime involving moral turpitude. (6) Show the teams or players on whom he is counting for the activity and their amateur status, and that they are persons of good "moral standing in the community" and that they have no relation direct or indirect with illicit businesses. (7) Show that the managers of teams have amateur status. 139

T.15 § 5 

Ch. 1 § 5-35. Duties of person obtaining franchise 

Every natural or artificial person who obtains a franchise from the Public Recreation and Parks Administration shall: 

(1) Render an annual report of the sporting activities for which the franchise is issued. (2) If in such activity admission is charged, render a report of each of the activities as well as an annual report of the finances of the natural or artificial person who organizes them. (3) Every participating player shall obtain from the Public Recreation and Parks Administration a credential of his amateur status. (The same shall include a picture of the person.) 

§ 5-36. Effect and duration of franchises 

The franchises issued by the Public Recreation and Parks Administrator shall be understood for all purposes as a privilege and not as a property right, they shall be issued for a period of two years and never for more than said period and they shall not be transferable; and when the period for which the franchise is issued comes to an end, any petition shall be regarded as a new petition for a franchise. 

5-37. Seasons

The Public Recreation and Parks Administrator shall establish the seasons during which the activities for which franchises are requested may be performed. 

§ 5-38. Revocation or suspension of franchises 

The Administrator of Parks may revoke, cancel or suspend for just cause any franchise granted in accordance with this division after the holding of a public hearing. § 5-39. Regulation of conduct; disputes; appeals

The natural or artificial person who possesses a franchise in accordance with this division is vested with the authority to compose his own constitution to regulate the conduct of his teams, players, trainers and scorers, interteam relations, or playermanager relations, and any dispute that may arise among them shall be aired first within the said organization and any person or team affected by the decision who does not agree with the terms of the same may appeal to the Administrator of Parks within a term of not more than 72 hours after notice of such decision. 140

Ch. T.15 § 5-44 

BASKETBALL § 5-40. Credentials of players 

To obtain a credential of participant in amateur basketball the applicant shall comply with the following requirements before the 

Public Recreation and Parks Administration: 

(1) File a certificate of a doctor, authorized to practice the profession in Puerto Rico, certifying that the petitioner is physically capable of participating in strenuous athletic activities. (2) Submit two 3" by 3" portrait photographs. (3) Submit an affidavit in which he declares that he has not participated in athletic competitions for payment or any remuneration. 

§ 5-41. Filing and approval of agreements 

The agreements existing between players and teams, between managers and teams, and between teams and the organization shall be filed in the Office of the Administrator of Parks and shall have no validity whatever until they have been approved by such officer. 

§ 5-42. Organization of tournaments by Administration 

The Public Recreation and Parks Administration may itself develop, sponsor and organize basketball tournaments when in its judgment the best interests of the sport so require. 

5-43. Penalties 

Any person guilty of an act, activity or practice prohibited by this division or who fails to comply with any condition or requirement required by the same, or who in any other manner violates any of its provisions, shall be subject to the penalties provided in sec. 7 of Act No. 4 of June 30, 1947 [15 L.P.R.A. § 6].
