§ 5-72. Equipment 

(a) Ring. The ring shall contain not less than 20 square feet inside the ropes and the floor shall extend not less than 31½ feet outside the ropes. The ring posts shall be not less than 32 feet from the ropes. The floor shall be padded with felt, corrugated paper or any other soft material, not less than 2 inches thick, which material shall extend not less than 1 foot outside the ropes. 

This padding shall be covered with canvas or strong linen, duly smoothed and stretched and firmly attached to the ring platform. 

No padding material which tends to form small mounds or bumps shall be used. (b) Height of the ring. The height of the ring shall be not more than 4 feet above the surface on which it is installed and 147

T.15 § 5 

Ch. 1 it shall be provided with stairs suitable for the use of the contestants. The ring posts shall be of metal not more than 3 inches in diameter, reaching from the floor of the building to a height of 58 inches above the floor of the ring, which shall be properly lighted. (c) Ropes of the ring. There shall be three, not more than 1 inch in diameter. The lower rope should be placed 18 inches from the ring floor, the second 35 inches from the floor and the third 52 inches. All the ropes shall be covered with a soft material. (d) Bell. The bell shall be not less than 10 inches in diameter and shall be solidly attached level with the ring platform. The timekeeper shall use a metal hammer to strike the bell so that it can be clearly heard by the referee and the contestants. (e) Obstructions. The entire ring platform shall be free of obstructions and obstacles, including buckets, stools, etc., when the bell sounds indicating the start of a round, and none of these objects may be placed on the ring platform until the bell ending the round has sounded. No advertisement shall be placed over or around the ring. Nor shall any appear on the posters announcing the rounds. (f) Gloves. New gloves shall be used for all main events, as well as for every fight of 10 or more rounds, and they shall weigh at least 8 ounces each. They shall be supplied by the club administration. (g) Water buckets. The club administration shall provide enough buckets for the contestants' use. The clubs shall also provide fans, rosin for the canvas, three stools for the seconds. in each corner, two seats for the Administration representatives, in each neutral corner and any other articles or equipment which may be needed during the course of the fights. (h) Scales. Scales shall be of a recognized make. They shall be supplied by the club administration and shall be examined and aproved before being used for each program. (i) Programs. All programs shall be submitted to the Administration two days before the date of the fights. 

The corporations shall obtain the consent of the guardians of boxers under 21 years included in a program to be held. 

This consent shall be included in the contract submitted to the Administration and shall be duly subscribed and sworn to before a notary public. 148

Ch. T.15 § 5-73 

BOXING § 5-73. Officials 

(a) Officials in general. Shall consist of a referee, two judges, a timekeeper, a fight director, an announcer and a doctor. (b) Referee and judges. The main official of the fights shall be the referee who shall have charge of supervising all the fights and who shall station himself within the ring. The two judges shall place themselves at opposite sides of the ring. 

The referee, before starting a fight, shall ascertain from each of the contestants the name of his chief second, and shall hold him responsible for the conduct of the assistant seconds during the course of the fight.

Before starting each fight, the referee shall call the contestants together to give final instructions, at which time the boxers shall be accompanied by their chief seconds only. After the instructions, the contestants shall shake hands and retire to their corners. They shall not shake hands again at any time during the fight. 

No person, except the contestants and the referee shall be in or enter the ring during the course of a round. 

The referee shall examine the gloves and make sure that no foreign substance has been applied to them or to the boxers' bodies to the detriment of the adversary. 

The referee shall have authority to: (1) Suspend a fight at any stage and render a decision if he considers the fight one-sided. (2) Suspend a fight if he considers that the contestants are not in earnest. In this case, he can disqualify one or both contestants. (3) Stop a fight at any stage due to the commission of a major foul and disqualify, with the consent of the judges, the contestant guilty of a major foul and concede the decision to his opponent. (4) Penalize either or both contestants with the loss of a round in case of low blows. (5) Penalize either or both contestants with the loss of a round in case they are guilty of a minor foul after having been warned. (6) When either contestant has been penalized, at the end of the round the referee shall go to the places occupied by the judges and indicating the boxer penalized, inform them that it was for having delivered a low blow or having committed a foul after 149

T.15 § 5 Ch. 1 

having been warned. The referee and judges shall make the appropriate notes on their cards. 

The referee shall refrain from touching the contestants except when one or both of them does not obey the order to "break."

The pre-fight meeting in the center of the ring for the purpose. of the referee's giving final instructions shall be limited to the contestants and their chief seconds, that is, a total of four persons. 

The only exception to this rule is in the case of a foreign boxer who requires the services of an interpreter. 

When a contestant has been knocked down, the referee and the timekeeper shall begin at once to count the seconds, indicating the count with a movement of the arm. If a contestant does not get up before the count of 10 seconds, the referee shall declare him the loser.

If a contestant has been knocked down and gets up before 10 seconds have elapsed and returns to the canvas intentionally, without having been struck, the referee and the timekeeper shall renew the count from the number at which it was interrupted. 

If a boxer leaves the ring during the one-minute period between rounds and does not return at the sound of the bell to renew the fight, the referee shall procede to count the 10 regulation seconds as if the boxer had been knocked down.

If a boxer who has been knocked out of the ring is not upright within the same before 10 seconds have elapsed, the referee shall declare him beaten, as if he had been knocked down. A boxer who has been knocked out of or fallen out of the ring, shall return without the help of other persons.

When a contestant has fallen to the canvas, his opponent shall retire to the farthest corner and shall remain there until the count is completed. If he fails to do so, the referee and the timer shall refrain from counting until he complies or shall suspend the count, if they have commenced, until he retires to the corner indicated. 

The referee shall penalize with the loss of the round a boxer who strikes his opponent below the belt. The referee shall notify the judges of his decision at the end of the round since they would otherwise have no knowledge of the penalty to mark their cards properly. The referee is the only one who may penalize the boxers. 

If the referee has given more than three warnings during a fight, he shall submit a special report to the Administration. 

Referees are ordered to stop any fight in which a boxer has 150

Ch. T.15 § 5-73 

BOXING 

been knocked down three times in one round as a result of blows, except for falls caused by the boxer's being off balance. (c) Judges. The two judges shall place themselves at opposite points of the ring.

It shall be the duty of the judges to observe each phase of the fight, and render a decision if the fight goes the agreed number of rounds. 

They shall be prepared at all times, if so requested by the referee, to help in a decision as to whether or not fouls have been committed, and may call the referee's attention to any other point at the end of a round.

The decision of the referee and the judges shall be based on effectiveness, the following points being taken into consideration: (1) Any strong, clean blow landed on any vulnerable part of the body above the belt shall be accredited in proportion to its effect on the one struck. (2) Aggressiveness comes next in importance and credit should be given the fighter who makes the greater number of effective attacks during a round. (3) Defense is of relative importance and credit should be given a boxer for dodging or effectively blocking the blows of his adversary. (4) Credit should also be given for conspicuous strategy demonstrated in the ring. This includes the capacity for taking advantage of any advantage that may present itself; being equal to all situations that may arise, forsee-neutralizing the opponent's method of fighting and forcing an adversary to adopt a boxing style in which he is not particularly dextrous. (5) Special attention should be given to the fact that a boxer who persistently delays the action of a fight by clinching frequently during a round runs the risk of the referee's penalizing him with the loss of the round in question. (6) Credit should be given a boxer for sportsmanship shown in the ring, for the faithful observation of the spirit and the letter of the rules, and for refraining from taking technical advantage of difficult situations prejudicial to his adversary. 

The judges and the referee shall mark their cards at the end of each round, using the letter "W" to signify the winner, "L" to indicate the loser and "T" in case of a tie. The round shall be awarded by the officials to the boxer who, in their judgment, has demonstrated superiority over his opponent. 151

T.15 § 5 

Ch. 1 

At the end of the fight, the boxer who has won the greater number of rounds shall be declared winner. In case both have won the same number of rounds, the decision shall be awarded the one who has accumulated the greater number of points. (See appendix A for the method of scoring points.) In case the boxers have also accumulated an equal number of points, the decision shall be awarded to the boxer who, in the judges' judgment, is in better physical shape at the end of the fight. 

It shall be in the discretion of the judges to award the decision to the fighter who has won fewer rounds than his adversary only in a case where, in the judges' opinion, such fighter has inflicted more damage on his opponent and has demonstrated marked superiority during the fight, having finished in better physical condition. The total number of points accumulated by a fighter who wins under these conditions shall be greater than that of his opponent who won the greater number of rounds. 

At the end of each round, the referee and the judges shall fill the columns of the scorecard and shall indicate the number of points accumulated by the winner of the round. If the winner of the fight has in his favor fewer rounds than his adversary, the reasons for the judges' having awarded him the decision shall be noted.

The referee shall be the one to decide any question, not specifically covered by this division, that may arise during a fight.

IMPORTANT NOTICE: At the end of each fight, the referee and judges shall indicate their decision on the back of their scorecards, in brief, clear and concise form. The announcers should read said declarations to the public, making known the votes of judges and referee in cases where the decision is not unanimous. 

SPECIAL NOTICE: Unless special permission is granted, referees and judges shall not identify themselves with or take part in any boxing program not authorized by the Administration. (d) Club doctor. At weighing-in time and within three hours before the start of a fight, each contestant shall receive a complete medical examination. The doctor shall give the Fight Director a duly signed certificate establishing the fact that the fighters are in good physical condition for the fight. The doctor shall be in attendance during the fight, ready to intervene in any emergency that may arise. 152

Ch. 

BOXING T.15 § 5-73 

The doctors are ordered to inform the boxers during the weighing-in ceremony that they are subject to another physical examination before entering the ring. 

Frequently, boxers eat heavily immediately after the weighingin, and doctors are ordered to instruct the fighters in regard to this practice.

Doctors shall not enter the ring to render emergency aid to a boxer unless requested to do so by the Administration representative. When the doctor wishes to communicate with the referee during the course of a fight, he shall do so only through the 

Administration representative. (e) Timekeeper. The timekeeper shall sit next to the ring near the bell. He shall indicate the beginning and end of each round, striking the bell with a hammer.

He shall be provided with a whistle and a watch which has been duly examined before the fight to determine its accuracy. 

Ten seconds before the start of each round, the timekeeper shall sound his whistle to indicate to the seconds that they should leave the ring.

In case a fight ends before the prearranged number of rounds is up, the timer shall inform the announcer of the exact duration of the fight.

No one shall be permitted to sit near the ring in the part occupied by the judges, except the timekeeper and the doctor, who shall be situated no less than six feet from the judges. 

When a knockdown occurs the timekeeper the timekeeper shall stand up immediately and clearly announce the seconds as they pass. The referee shall first make sure that the fallen fighter's opponent has gone to the most distant corner, and turning to the timekeeper shall count in unison with him the passing seconds. The referee shall begin to count from the number reached by the timekeeper when the boxer in in the most distant corner. If the boxer who is standing up does not remain in such corner, the referee and the timer shall immediately suspend the count until he does. The regulation 10 seconds having passed, unless the round has previously ended, the referee shall raise both hands and shall loudly say “OUT.” If the round ends during a knockdown, the timekeeper shall sound the bell as he normally does and at the same time shall announce the second at which the count ended. (f) Announcer. He shall announce the names of the contestants and their exact weight, the decisions of the umpire and judges, 153

T.15 § 5 

Ch. 1 and any other matters indicated by the Administration's representative, and nothing more. The clubs shall provide adequate facilities for announcing the rounds. The announcer is strictly forbidden to make speeches, jokes or to try to ridicule a boxer with nicknames, etc. 

At the end of each fight, the announcer shall collect the decision cards of the referee and the judges. After examining them, he shall proceed as follows: first he shall announce to the public if any of the participants in the fight has been penalized with the loss of a round, giving the number of the same and the reason he lost it. Then he shall announce the judges' decision.

When a contestant is knocked down and cannot get up before the regulation 10 seconds are up, the decision is that said contestant has been knocked out and the announcer shall give the exact moment of the knockout.

When the referee intervenes to avoid unnecessary additional punishment to a boxer during the course of a fight or during the minute of rest between rounds, the announcer shall say as follows:

THE FIGHT HAS BEEN STOPPED. THE BOXER CANNOT CONTINUE. 

IS THE WINNER. 

(g) Fight director. He shall be responsible for all details of the fight not coming under the jurisdiction of other officials. (1) He shall see that all necessary equipment is at hand, that the contestants are ready on time, that the seconds have been duly instructed as to their duties, that the doctor's report and that of the weighing-in has been delivered to the referee and that, all requirements and rules governing a fight have been complied with. (2) He shall not permit the boxers to put on their gloves until the wrappings have been examined by the Administration representative. 

(3) He shall suspend those boxers who appear for the fight weighing more than the weight agreed on for the fight. (4) The canvass shall not be placed over the padding of the ring until the material used for padding has been examined and approved by the Administration representative. (5) The stadiums or clubs shall have a special room for the use of judges and referees. No one shall be permitted to enter except the Administration representative. (6) Any second who changes his sweater next to the ring shall be suspended. 154

Ch. T.15 § 5-75 

BOXING 

(7) It shall be necessary for each fighter to designate his chief second.

The Fight Director shall submit the names of the chief seconds for the Administration representative's approval. 

5-74. Seconds 

There shall not be more than three.

They shall refrain from directing their fighters by shouts or signals during the course of the fight. 

The seconds shall remain seated and silent during the rounds and shall refrain from throwing water or otherwise helping their boxer during the course of a round. 

A boxer's parents, brothers, and sisters may not serve him as seconds.

The use between rounds of fans to refresh a boxer shall be authorized but the use of towels for this purpose shall be prohibited.

The chief second only shall be permitted to help the boxer in the ring; the assistant seconds shall remain outside the ropes. 

The seconds shall not enter the ring until a round is over and they are forbidden to sprinkle the fighters or throw water at them.

The seconds shall leave the ring at the sound of the timer's whistle 10 seconds before the start of the round. They shall retire from the ring platform and shall remove all obstructions such as buckets, stools, etc., immediately at the sound of the bell to start the round.

The seconds shall not throw a towel into the ring to signify defeat. The referee shall be the only one authorized to determine a boxer's ability to continue fighting.

Any violation of the above rules shall be cause for the culprit's expulsion from the corner in which he is serving and may lead to the referee's disqualifying the boxer. 

§ 5-75. Fighters 

They shall be presented to the fight director at least two hours before entering the ring. They shall box wearing appropriate ring clothing, including protective cups, the type of which shall be approved by the Administration. All clothing and equipment shall be duly adjusted before entering the ring. The contestants shall use regulation trunks which shall reach at least halfway down 155

T.15 § 5 Ch. 1 

the thigh. The use of tight-fitting trunks shall not be permitted. 

The elastic of the trunks shall not be wider than the waist. The shoes shall be of a soft material and shall not have cleats, grooved soles or solid heels. No other article, with the exception of a robe, shall be used by a fighter in the ring. 

The gloves shall be put on in the dressing room under supervision of the Administration representatives, and shall be tied on the reverse side of the wrist. 

The use of grease or any other substance which may place the adversary at a disadvantage shall be prohibited. The contestants shall enter the ring duly well-groomed and shaved. 

Each boxer shall be equipped with two pairs of trunks of the following colors: (1) Purple trunks with blue waist band. (2) Black trunks with red waist band and red two-inch side stripes.

They shall also use a protective cup which shall be approved by the Administration.

Boxers shall be prohibited from indicating to the spectators by gestures or words their belief that they have won or lost a fight. 

Upon the announcement of the decision, the contestants as well as the seconds shall leave the ring immediately and retire to the dressing room, where the boxers' gloves shall be removed. 

Managers and seconds of a boxer shall be forbidden to throw a towel into the ring signifying the defeat of their fighter or to otherwise admit that he has been defeated. The referee shall be the only one authorized to determine the physical condition of a boxer who has received severe punishment and to determine whether or not the fight should continue.

The seconds shall use sweaters or jerseys of solid color. The use of short-sleeved sweaters or jerseys shall not be permitted. 

No boxer, manager, second or helper shall enter the ring wearing a sweater, T-shirt or robe bearing any advertisement apart from the name of the boxer.

Employees of the club or corporation shall be forbidden to direct or encourage the fighters during the course of a fight or exhibition. 

Trunks: The use of racial, political, religious or other type of insignia on the same shall be prohibited. 

Robes: The use of the boxer's name on the back of the robe shall be permitted, but at no time shall the use of commercial 156

Ch. 

BOXING 

T.15 § 5-76 advertisements or racial, religious, or political insignia be permitted on the same. 

Wrappings: Wrappings shall be of soft cloth only, not longer than 10 yards nor wider than 1½ inches and no more than 4 feet of tape on each hand shall be used to keep them in place. This shall apply to all divisions up to middleweight, inclusive. In the remaining divisions - light heavyweight and heavyweight — the wrappings shall be 12 yards in length and 2 inches in width and 8 feet of tape on each hand may be used to keep them in place. 

The use of 6 inches of adhesive tape not wider than 11½ inches on the back of each hand before putting it in the wrappings shall be permitted, provided that said tape is not placed over the knuckles. These wrappings shall be put on in the dressing room in the presence of the Administration representative. Under no circumstances shall the wrappings be placed on the fighters' hands without previous authorization of the Administration representative. 

Shoes: Shall be of a soft material and shall not have cleats, grooved soles, hard soles or hard heels. § 5-76. Knockdowns 

A boxer shall be considered down when: (a) Any part of his body, other than his feet, is in contact with the canvas. (b) He hangs helpless from the ropes. (c) When he is getting up. 

Note (a): A boxer who is hanging from the ropes is not officially down until the referee declares him to be so. The referee may count and declare a boxer knocked out on the ropes as well as on the canvas. 

Note (b): A boxer may fall due to an accident or weakness, but shall get up immediately. If he is knocked down by a blow, he may take a count of nine without being declared knocked out. 

Note (c): The referee and judges of a fight, in rendering their decisions, shall declare any contestant knocked out when he can not stand up after having been knocked down, before 10 seconds have passed.

On intervening to stop a fight and to avoid unnecessary punishment to a helpless boxer, the referee shall render the following decision: THE FIGHT HAS BEEN STOPPED. 

CANNOT CONTINUE. 

IS THE WINNER. 

....... 157

T.15 § 5 Ch. 1 

Major fouls. The referee shall disqualify a boxer for the following reasons: (1) Striking the opponent below the belt. (2) Striking the opponent when he is on the floor or is getting up. (3) Striking the opponent with the knee, or using it to stop an attack. (4) Falling to the canvas purposely without having been struck. (5) Disobeying the referee or performing any physical action, detrimental to the opponent, other than honorable and gentlemanly boxing.

Minor fouls. Referees shall penalize a boxer with the loss of the round in which he commits one of the following violations after a warning: (1) Holding an opponent or deliberately prolonging a clinch. (2) Holding an opponent with one hand and striking with the other. (3) Striking with the head, the palm of the hand, the wrist, or the elbow, including the so-called "reverse blow." (4) Striking with open glove on any part of the adversary's body. (5) Striking deliberately any part of the adversary's body over the kidneys. (6) Using the "pivot blow" or "Rabbit Punch". (7) Striking while coming out of a clinch. (8) Using insulting or profane language.

It shall be the duty of a referee, who penalizes with the loss of a round, for any of the above violations and infractions, to notify clearly each of the judges, and the judges shall note it on their respective cards. The judges shall not penalize a boxer with the loss of a round unless they receive due authorization from the referee.

Number and duration of rounds. No fight shall be for more than 

10 rounds and none of such rounds shall be more than 3 minutes duration. There shall be one minute of rest between rounds. 

§ 5-77. Championships 

Every boxer who holds a championship title, except those who are in the service of the United States Army or Navy, shall defend it within a period of three months after winning it or after defending it in a bona fide fight which ended with a final decision. 158

Ch. 

BOXING 

T.15 § 5-77 

If the boxer does not defend his title, the Administration shall receive and forward to the champion a challenge in the name of another boxer, after three months have passed. The champion shall be obliged to accept such challenge within the next 15 days after receiving it and to take the necessary steps to arrange the fight with the challenger, providing that if he does not do so his license shall be cancelled at the will of the Administration. 

To guarantee the good faith of the challenge, each challenge shall be accompanied by a deposit in the following amounts: $100 $100 $100 $100 $100 

Flyweight, bantamweight and featherweight Lightweight

Welterweight and middleweight 

Light heavyweight Heavyweight

These deposits shall be made by certified check to the order of the Public Recreation and Parks Administration of Puerto Rico. 

The Administration, on receiving and accepting the challenges, reserves the right to consider only those which in its opinion are from outstanding challengers, and if there is no logical contender, reserves the right to return all challenges. 

The Administration shall suspend the license of any boxer who, within the insular limits of Puerto Rico or outside them, participates in a fight against a champion who has been suspended for refusing to accept a challenge in the manner provided above. 

If such boxer has no Puerto Rico license the fight in question shall constitute sufficient reason for denying him one should he petition subsequently.

Apart from the aforesaid disciplinary measures for the champion, if for any reason he cannot qualify, the Administration may declare the title vacant, promote a tournament, and concede the title to the winner of the same.

Every fight that a recognized champion makes in Puerto Rican territory shall be within his weight limit, except when a champion of a division competes as contender in another weight category. 

No club shall hold fights outside the weight categories defined in sec. 5-71 of this title. 

A championship or title may be lost for breach of contract, disobedience, or inability to make weight, but a championship or title may be won only as a result of a fight. 

Contracts for championship fights shall be signed in the Admin- 159

istration offices. On the day the contract is signed, the two contestants as well as the promoter of the fight shall each deposit a $100 bond with the Administration. 

The bonds of the contestants shall be to guarantee their weight and their appearance on the day of the fight. 

If a champion finds himself unable to accept a challenge owing to being in service in the Armed Forces of the United States and inability to obtain leave, he shall be excused from accepting challenges during his service to the nation. 

Failure on the part of either contestant or of the promoter to comply with the provisions of the contract shall occasion the forfeiture of his deposit, which shall be divided among the other contracting parties.

§ 5-151. General provisions 

(a) Weight-lifting includes for the purposes of this division, the practice of the recognized Olympic lifts, to wit: Olympic Press, Two-Arm Snatch, and Two-Arm Clean and Jerk; the practice of physical culture involving bodybuilding and all lifts based thereon and competitions of Physical Culture. 

(b) Any person shall be a bona fide amateur weight-lifter who devotes himself to the practice of weight-lifting according to the amateur rules in effect and who has been recognized as such by the Public Parks and Recreation Administration as provided in this division. (c) Any group shall be a bona fide amateur weight-lifting club the purposes of which are the practice of weight-lifting according to the amateur rules in effect and which has been recognized as such by the Public Recreation and Parks Administration as provided in this division. 160

Ch. T.15 § 5-152 

WEIGHT-LIFTING 

(d) Any tournament shall be official which is organized by the Executive Committee mentioned below or which is recognized by said Committee.

§ 5-152. Executive Committee 

(a) To administer this division the Executive Committee of Amateur Weight-lifting of Puerto Rico (hereinafter called the Committee) is hereby created. (b) The Committee shall consist of three members of equal authority who shall be named by the Public Recreation and Parks 

Administrator and who shall: (1) Be morally solvent. (2) Have shown genuine interest in amateur weight-lifting. (3) Know completely the rules of weight-lifting and those of amateurism. (4) Not actively participate in the sport of weight-lifting. (c) The Committee shall draw up its own Regulations to govern its internal functions. (d) The Committee shall hold at least one regular meeting yearly for drawing up and programing of activities for the year and a regular meeting before each official activity. (e) The functions and duties of the Committee shall be the following: 161

T.15 § 5 

Ch. 1 (1) To organize, develop and promote Amateur weight-lifting in Puerto Rico. (2) To organize and hold weight-lifting tournaments, exhibitions and clinics in Puerto Rico, establishing adequate regulations for the same, and taking all steps necessary for the celebration of these activities. For this purpose, it shall prepare annually an official program which shall be submitted for the consideration of the Public Recreation and Parks Administrator and which, once approved, shall be the official program for weight-lifting. (3) To investigate violations of this division and report the results of such investigations to the Public Parks and Recreation 

Administrator, with pertinent recommendations. (4) To investigate violations of the amateur code by amateur weight-lifters and report the results to the Public Parks and 

Recreation Administrator, with pertinent recommendations. (5) To examine the registration applications made by weightlifters and weight-lifting clubs to the Public Recreation and Parks Administration and to recommend appropriate action to the Public 

Recreation and Parks Administrator. (6) To maintain a register of all amateur weight-lifters and all weight-lifting clubs recognized by the Public Recreation and 

Parks Administration. 

(7) To stimulate weight-lifting club activities, cooperate in the holding of the same and see that they proceed in accordance with the rules of sports and amateurism. (8) To maintain a register of the official records established in the various official tournaments. (9) To organize elimination tournaments in order to select the weight-lifters who shall represent Puerto Rico in extra-insular competitions, establish the rules for selection in said tournaments and recommend to the Public Recreation and Parks Administrator the candidates thus chosen. Register of weight-lifters and clubs (a) The weight-lifters and the weight-lifting clubs of Puerto Rico who are interested in participating as such in official competitions sponsored by the Public Recreation and Parks Administration shall register with such agency. (b) Such registration shall be made by application to that effect by the corresponding weight-lifter or club to the Public Recreation and Parks Administrator, in which application shall be indicated among other things, the name of applicant, address, age and promise of the applicant to respect the provisions of this division and the amateur rules in effect. (d) The public Recreation and Parks Administrator shall give an official card to each weight-lifter and club whose application is accepted. § 5-154. Competitions 

(a) At least five official Commonwealth tournaments shall be held annually in the following order: 

(1) Commonwealth Tournament of Olympic Lifts for Novices. 

(2) Commonwealth Junior Tournament of Olympic Lifts. 

(3) Commonwealth Senior Tournament of Olympic Lifts. 

(4) Commonwealth Tournament of Free Lifts. 

(5) Selection of Mr. Puerto Rico. 

The winners of these annual tournaments shall be recognized as Commonwealth champions in each category and tournament. (b) For the tournaments of olympic lifts the rules of the International Federation of Weight-lifting (Federation Internationale Halterophile et Culturiste) shall govern. 163

T.15 § 5 Ch. 1 

(c) For the tournaments of free lifts the rules published by the Executive Committee shall govern and they shall be similar to those adopted by the A.A.U. or any other recognized association. (d) For the selection of Mr. Puerto Rico or for any other such tournament the rules adopted by the A.A.U. for the selection of 

Mr. America shall govern. (e) For the tournaments of free lifts the following lifts shall be recognized: (1) Olympic Press. (2) Deep Knee Bend. (3) Two Arm Bench Press. 

(4) Two Hand Dead Lift. 

(f) For every selection of weight-lifters who represent Puerto Rico in outside competitions at least two eliminations shall be required. It shall be an indispensable requirement that to figure in the final selection, the athletes participate in all eliminations announced. (g) Only those records established in official tournaments by officially-registered weight-lifters with the right to participate shall be recognized as official. Every new record shall be certified in writing by the judges of the competition to the Executive Committee in order that the latter proceed to recognize it. (h) The judges for the official tournaments shall be named by the Executive Committee prior to the holding of each tournament and shall be persons who know completely the rules applicable in in weight-lifting tournaments. (i) The winners of first, second and third places in each category of the first four official Commonwealth tournaments mentioned above shall receive respectively medals of gold, silver and bronze donated by the Public Recreation and Parks Administration. The outstanding weight-lifter in each of these tournaments shall receive a trophy with appropriate inscription. Similarly, the three finalists in the selection of Mr. Puerto Rico shall receive trophies from the Public Recreation and Parks Administration. 

§ 5-155. Participants in competitions (a) In official tournaments only bona fide amateur weight-lifters as previously defined may participate. (b) In Commonwealth Tournaments of Olympic Lifts for

Novices only weight-lifters who have not won first, second and third place in a previous Commonwealth Tournament for Novices, 164

Ch. 

BASEBALL T.15 § 5-201 

and those who have not participated in other official tournaments, shall participate. 

(c) In the Commonwealth Junior Tournaments of Olympic 

Lifts, only weight-lifters who have not been Commonwealth junior or senior champions shall participate. (d) In the official Commonwealth tournaments, in addition to restrictions already indicated, only lifters native to Puerto Rico may compete for Commonwealth titles. Other American citizens may compete for Commonwealth titles only if they have resided in Puerto Rico at least one year immediately before the competition in which they desire to participate. Foreigners shall not compete for Commonwealth titles. In the selection of Mr. Puerto Rico only athletes native to Puerto Rico and residents thereof may compete for this title. These athletes on whom residence and citizenship requirements have been applied may participate in the tournaments only as extra lifters.

§ 5-202. Application 

Every baseball spectacle for which any admission is charged and, in addition, in which all or some of its participants receive emoluments for their services shall be subject to the provisions of this division. 

§ 5-203. Franchise or provisional permit 

After approval of this division, no natural or artificial person may devote himself to professional baseball competitions as professional baseball is defined in sec. 5-202 of this title, without previously having received a franchise referred to in sec. 5-205 or having obtained a provisional permit from the Public Recreation and Parks Administration of Puerto Rico.

§ 5-205. New Franchises 

No new franchise shall be considered or recognized for any professional baseball team if first: (1) The applicant does not prove that he has a baseball park, either as owner or lessee, in the city he represents, which offers. guarantees of public security. (2) He does not prove that he has under contract at least 

15 players duly qualified to participate in professional baseball competition. (3) He does not prove to the complete satisfaction of the Public 

Recreation and Parks Administration of Puerto Rico that the applicant or applicants are persons of good moral reputation in the community and that they have no relation direct or indirect with illicit businesses. 

§ 5-206. Tournaments and championships 

After franchises have been granted by the Professional Baseball League and recognized by the Public Recreation and Parks 

Administration of Puerto Rico, the teams shall organize among themselves for the holding of tournaments and championships to begin not later than October 15 of each year. 

§ 5-207. Reports, contracts, and licenses 

It shall be the duty of every professional baseball team possessing a franchise to file with the Public Recreation and Parks Administration a report with the names of the players composing. the team as well as a copy of the contract for services between the players and the team; Provided, That no person may par- 167

Administration of Puerto Rico. 

The following are the requirements for obtaining a professional baseball license: (1) Filing a certificate of a doctor, authorized to practice the profession in Puerto Rico, certifying that the petitioner is physically fit for participating in professional baseball. (2) Submitting three portrait photographs two inches in length by two inches in width. (3) Presenting proof to the satisfaction of the Public Recreation and Parks Administration of Puerto Rico that the applicant has competed in two Class Double "A" amateur championships sponsored or organized by institutions or organizations recognized by the Public Recreation and Parks Administration or that he has played professional baseball outside Puerto Rico for at least one complete season. 

No professional baseball player may participate in exhibitions, whether championships or not, without signing a written contract in triplicate, the original and a copy to be sent immediately with his signature to the Public Recreation and Parks Administration for consideration and approval. One of the clauses of the contract shall be that it shall have no effect or validity until it is approved by the Public Parks and Recreation Administration of Puerto 

Rico. No clause or condition of the contract that does not appear specifically in the same shall have any validity whatever. Any verbal agreement between the person, league or institution organizing the championship or exhibition and the ball player which does not appear in the signed contract shall be considered by the Administration as an illicit act of both parties and shall occasion the administrative correction determined by the Public Recreation and Parks Administration through investigation and hearings. 

The players' contracts shall not be transferable in any sense, nor their status altered, unless the Public Recreation and Parks Administration is notified and its previous written authorization is obtained. § 5-208. Schedules

In holding tournaments or championships, the organization or league of professional baseball teams shall approve within itself 168

its schedules, with no requirement other than filing with the Administration a copy of such schedules as definitely approved by the organization or Professional Baseball League 30 days before beginning the same. 

§ 5-209. Reports of ticket sales 

Within 48 hours following the end of any game, professional baseball spectacle, the Public Recreation and Parks Administrator of Puerto Rico shall be informed in writing, authorized by the natural or artificial person or by a legal representative of the organization or Professional Baseball League to which the participating teams belong, of the exact number of tickets sold for each spectacle, without denominations in quantities and the total amount of the gross receipts. 

§ 5-210. Umpires' licenses 

After the approval of this division no one may act as umpire in professional baseball games without first having been issued an umpire's license by the Public Recreation and Parks Administration of Puerto Rico, after having paid for said license the sum of $10. 

§ 5-211. Selection of umpires 

The organization or Professional Baseball League shall have power to select its umpires from among those persons authorized by license of the Administrator to act as such according to the provisions of sec. 5-210 of this title. § 5-212. Sale of tickets

The sale of tickets for the baseball games scheduled by the organization or Professional Baseball League shall be made the same day of the game in the places expressly provided for the purpose in the park in which the game is to be played, except in the form provided in sec. 5-213 of this title. Every ticket shall indicate the game for which it is valid and the place for which it is issued. It shall have correlative numeration corresponding to the number of tickets sold and shall be previously authenticated by the Secretary of the Treasury in the form and manner determined by the latter through regulations to that effect. Provided, That the Administrator may grant permission for a certain number of tickets to be assigned and sold by the visiting team pursuant to regulations to that effect by the Administrator.

§ 5-215. Penalties 

The organizations and professional baseball leagues recognized by the Public Recreation and Parks Administration shall have power to penalize the players and directors of their organization for breaches of discipline and the penalties shall be final insofar as they do not exceed a fine of $50 and a suspension of four weeks; 

Provided, That any penalty exceeding $50 and four weeks' suspension may be appealed to the Public Recreation and Parks Administrator of Puerto Rico. 

§ 5-216. Rules of organization or League 

The organization or Professional Baseball League is vested with the power of editing its own constitution to regulate conduct between teams and players, between teams, or between players and the Baseball League, and any dispute that may arise among them shall first be heard before the President of the organization and every decision with which the person or persons, team or teams, affected by it do not agree may be appealed to the Public Recreation and Parks Administrator of Puerto Rico.

 § 5-255. 

Other persons; fines (a) The promoter shall be responsible that every person working in his programs has been previously granted his corresponding license, if required by law. (b) If one or more of these persons is found acting without a license, the promoter shall be fined in the sum of $25 for each of such persons acting without a license. The total amount of the fine will be deducted from ticket sales or his surety bond. (c) Likewise, in setting up matches, the promoter shall see to it that wrestlers are more or less matched as to weight as well as experience and ability, so as to make the event interesting and attractive. § 5-256. Doctor; examination of wrestlers

It shall be required that wrestling promoters obtain the services of a doctor to examine all contestants before they participate in the program and further, that said doctor be present during the program in case his services are needed. After having examined the wrestlers, the doctor shall not authorize the participation of any contestant if in his judgment he is suffering from any disease or handicap which may in any manner interfere or prevent him from displaying a complete and satisfactory exhibition of his ability, or if his participation may result detrimental to his own health or that of his opponent. The promoter shall call all participants to physical examination with ample time, and no contestant may withhold from the doctor information on any disease or handicap he may be suffering. § 5-257. Behavior of wrestlers (a) Wrestlers are strictly forbidden to intervene in any manner whatsoever with any referee or spectator, and to pull, push or hit a referee or spectator under risk of disqualification. The referee who does not enforce this provision shall be fined or suspended by the Administration, provided that the fine does not exceed $25 and the suspension does not exceed a term of 30 days. (b) The referee shall see to it, according to his powers, that wrestlers do not use tricks or wiles which in any manner may impair the development of the match or be detrimental to his opponent or the sport in general and he may punish or disqualify the contestant who insists in such practices. If this is the case, he

shall render a report to the Parks Administration, setting forth his reasons for punishing or disqualifying the wrestler or wrestlers. 

§ 5-258. Age 

No professional wrestler's license shall be granted to any person under 18 years of age, and every person under 21 shall, together with his application, file the authorization from his father or guardian and birth certificate. 

§ 5-259. Officials 

The officials in every wrestling match shall consist of one referee, one timekeeper and one announcer. § 5-260. Referee's decision

The referee's decision is final and unappealable. 

§ 5-261. Meets 

Falls

Each meet shall end with a fall, or 2 falls out of 3, and contracts shall specify the number of falls to decide each meet and time limit of each. There shall be a 2 minute rest between falls. 

How decided 

All meets shall be decided as follows: (1) In one-fall meets, the wrestlers forcing the fall within the time limit shall be declared the winner. If there is no fall within the prescribed time limit, the referee shall take a decision, in his own judgment declaring the match even or granting the victory to any one of the contestants. (2) In a two-falls-out-of-three match, the contestant or team (when it is by pairs) forcing 2 falls within the specified time limit shall be declared the winner. If there should only occur 1 fall within the time limit, the contestant or team forcing said fall shall be declared the winner. In case no contestant or team is able to force 2 falls within the time limit, or each one has forced 1 fall or no one has forced any fall, the referee shall make a decision based upon his appreciation of the match. § 5-263. Fall, when accredited

A fall shall be accredited against a contestant when, for the referee's count of 3 seconds, his 2 shoulders have remained touching the mat at the same time; or when, because of a painful hold or 

June 30, 1968 172.3 

Vol. 7, No. 6

T.15 § 5 

Ch. 1 legitimately received punishment, a contestant surrenders. In that case the referee shall touch the shoulder of the contestant forcing the fall so that he lets go of his opponent. 

§ 5-264. Contracts 

Contracts shall be personally signed by contestants or managers, if any. In the case of a minor, the contract shall be signed in his behalf by his father or guardian. 

§ 5-265. Antisport behavior 

Any antisport or physically dangerous behavior or tactic at a match on the part of a contestant may be sufficient reason for the referee to consider the match ended, and the decision granted to his opponent. § 5-266. Seconds; behavior 

Seconds shall not touch the contestants during the match; nor shall they advise or instruct them until the rest period has been decreed. 

§ 5-267. Refusal or impossibility to wrestle 

When, despite the referee's order, a contestant refuses to continue wrestling, or when because of physical impossibility he is unable to continue, the match shall be declared ended and the opponent shall be declared the winner. 

§ 5-268. Place for match 

Every match shall necessarily take place within the ring. Any contestant who deliberately throws his opponent out of the ring may be warned or punished by the referee and may even lose the match. 

§ 5-269. Leaving the ring 

No contestant may deliberately leave the ring during the match, and should this action be repeated after being warned by the referee, he may be punished with a fall. 

§ 5-270. Obedience to referee's orders 

Contestants shall immediately obey all referee's orders. If this is not done, the referee shall grant such seconds as he may deem convenient, to a maximum of 5 for the contestant to obey, and if this period elapses and the contestant has not obeyed he shall be disqualified.

T.15 § 5-274 § 5-271. Contestant thrown out of the ring (a) When a contestant leaves the ring to avoid punishment, the referee shall count 10 seconds, and if at the end of such time the contestant has not returned to the ring, he shall be disqualified. (b) When a contestant is involuntary thrown out of the ring, the referee shall count 20 seconds. If at the end of such time he has not returned to the ring, he shall be disqualified. (c) On both occasions the contestant who remained in the ring shall place himself close to the ropes of the side opposite to that through which his opponent is entering the ring. § 5-272. Physical examination

Every wrestler shall be at the place specified for holding the program, at such time as the promoter may fix, for the purpose of submitting to the prescribed physical examination and ready to wrestle as soon as his turn comes up. § 5-273. Wrestler-promoter; prohibition 

No wrestler may be a wrestler's promoter or manager, or vice versa. § 5-274. Team wrestling

If the match is to be held between a pair forming a team against another pair from another team, the time shall be limited to one (1) hour and the meet to 2 falls out of 3. When a member of a team suffers a fall, it shall be counted against the team. There shall never be more than one man by team wrestling in the ring at the same time. The meet shall begin with a man from each team while the respective partners stay in their corresponding corners outside the ring, not taking part in the meet until their partner has been defeated, or after he has touched his teammate's hand to relieve him. 

The partner outside the ropes shall hold himself by grabbing a piece of rope 3 feet long tied to one end of the highest rope at his corner. For a relief to be valid, the man who is relieving shall have both feet on the floor outside the ropes, holding himself to the 3-foot long rope, and then contacting his partner with his hand extended over the highest rope in the ring. The referee shall make sure that the relieved wrestler retires to his corner outside the ropes as soon as his partner has entered the ring. If there is a fall, members of one team may relieve themselves mutually at pleasure. If a member of a team is unable to continue wrestling, June 30, 1968 

Vol. 7, No. 6 172.5

T.15 § 5 

Ch. 1 his partner will continue the meet alone. If a wrestler is injured, the time elapsed while he is taken out of the ring shall not count as wrestling time. If, while awaiting his turn outside the ropes, a wrestler helps his partner or intervenes with his opponent, it shall be construed as a violation of the rules and shall be counted against the respective team. It shall also count against a team if any contestant withdraws from the rope in his corner without duly making the relief contact. If the violator, once the referee has called his attention in any of these situations, persists in his tactics, the referee may proceed to disqualify him. § 5-275. Contracts between manager and wrestler (a) Before the Parks Administration recognizes the validity of this type of contract, it shall be necessary that: (1) The manager file with the Parks Administration copy of the contract, duly notarized by manager and wrestler. If the wrestler is a minor, the contract shall be signed by his legal guardian. 

The contract shall specify the share of benefits between manager and wrestler, and the manager shall not, in any case, receive more than one-third of the wrestler's take. (2) In order for the contract to be recognized, both manager and wrestler shall previously obtain their respective licenses from the Parks Administration. (3) During the time covering the contract, both manager and wrestler shall always hold active licenses from the Parks Administration. If one party, or both, allows his license to expire without renewing it, the contract shall be automatically void until both parties obtain their respective licenses. (b) The manager shall sign the contracts in behalf of the wrestler. (c) Before a contract signed by a wrestler who has a manager recognized by this Agency is approved, the wrestler shall: Submit his manager's written authorization to sign the contract and receive the agreed pay. (d) Noncompliance with the specific terms of this contract with a promoter exposes a wrestler and/or his manager, if any, to the retention of his take and/or the suspension of his license or licenses for such a term as the Parks Administration may determine.

PROFESSIONAL WRESTLING T.15 § 5-281 § 5-276. Breach of contract 

A wrestler who does not show up to comply with a contract shall prove to the satisfaction of the Parks Administration that he was ill or prevented, by force majeure, from such compliance. In the case of illness, he shall present a medical certificate; in all other cases he shall submit an affidavit. 

§ 5-277. Mixed meets 

Mixed meets between wrestlers and boxers or between wrestlers of different sex are strictly forbidden. § 5-278. Grease and foreign substances; mask and half-mask 

The referee shall make sure that the wrestler's body is clean and free of any grease or foreign substance. A wrestler may wear a mask or half-mask covering his face in all or in part, if it is free from any harmful substance or object. Before the start of any match, a Parks Administration representative shall make sure that this safety measure is strictly complied with. 

§ 5-279. Referee's powers 

The referee is fully empowered to direct and control the matches and enforce the rules and regulations of this Administration. His decision shall be final. If there should arise any circumstance not covered by the rules, the referee is hereby authorized to make the final decision. 

§ 5-280. Revocation of license 

Any person who holds a license from the Parks Administration and violates the rules or regulations of this Agency may have his license revoked or may be fined, suspended, or punished in such a manner as the Parks Administration may determine. The Parks 

Administration shall have discretionary power to retain any take or part thereof belonging to any wrestler, or wrestlers, or the part corresponding to any manager, if in its judgment there is reason. to believe that said contestants or manager have committed an act that violates Agency rules or regulations. § 5-281. Withholding of take

In all such cases in which the Parks Administration retains the take or part thereof from wrestlers and/or managers, the amount thus retained shall remain in the custody of the Parks Administration until a public hearing is held at the petition of the aggrieved 1970 

Vol. 9, No. 1 

172.7

T.15 § 5 

Ch. 1 

party or parties. If at said hearing it is proved that in effect a violation was committed, or the aggrieved party or parties do not request the public hearing within 5 days after said retention, the Parks Administration may impose such fine or fines as it may deem convenient and applicable to the violations committed. The fine thus imposed shall in no case exceed the sum of 1,000 dollars. 

§ 5-282. Ring 

It shall not be less than 20 feet X 20 feet inside the ropes, and the floor shall extend not less that 2 feet outside the ropes. The ring posts shall be at a distance not less than 3.5 feet from the ropes. The floor shall be covered with a mat, special matting or any other soft material, not less than 2 inches thick, which material shall extend to a distance not less than one foot outside the ropes. This padding shall be covered with canvas or strong linen, duly smoothed and stretched and firmly attached to the ring platform. No padding material which may tend to form small mounds or bumps shall be used to cover the ring. There shall be 3 ropes in number, each not less than one inch in diameter and covered with a soft material, duly stretched and firmly tied to the ring posts. 

The lower rope shall be placed 2 feet from the ring floor; the second 

3 feet from the floor; and the third 4 feet from the floor.

§ 5-301. Purposes 

This tournament is held for the following purposes: (1) To develop able players that may follow baseball as a career. (2) To use baseball as the means to educate the citizenry, stressing the practice of good sportsmanship.

§ 5-302. Organization The Class "A" Amateur Baseball Tournament shall be organized, directed and supervised by the Public Recreation and Parks Administration in accordance with the regulations set forth hereinbelow. 

§ 5-303. Division by groups and leagues 

(a) The island shall be divided in leagues, and these shall in turn be divided in as many groups as necessary. 1970

(b) The Director of the Public Recreation and Parks Ad ministration Recreation and Sports Bureau shall distribute the groups and the leagues, according to his own judgment and considering the number of teams registered and distance between the towns where the teams are located. 

§ 5-304. Group and league directors The Public Recreation and Parks Administration shall delegate to certain persons, as often as necessary, part of its responsibility in the direction and solution of problems arising in the tournament at the eliminative stage of groups or league teams. 

(1) The Director of the P.R.P.A. Recreation and Sports Bureau shall, whenever he deems it necessary, appoint a director in each league and a representative in each group. In case there is no group or league director, the Director of the P.R.P.A. Recreation and Sports Bureau shall assume every responsibility at the eliminative stage of the tournament. (2) Section directors may, for the solution thereof, bring cases of undiscipline or any other problem before the P.R.P.A. League 

Director to which their groups belong, or directly before the 

Director of the P.R.P.A. Recreation and Sports Bureau. 

(3) Group directors as well as league directors may, for any violation, recommend to the Public Recreation and Parks Administrator the penalties to be imposed on players, coaches, managers and other persons directly related with the teams. The director's official notice shall be needed for the final application of said penalties. (4) Group directors as well as league directors may appoint umpires for their respective groups or leagues, and a representative for each park where a game is to be held. (A) Umpires shall be selected following, as far as possible, the rotary plan established by the Public Recreation and Parks Administration. (B) Park representatives shall have the authority to solve all problems arising therein, including the matter of umpires. § 5-305. League champions

BASEBALL § 5-306. Signing of contract 

(a) Players shall sign the official contract between player and teams; Provided, That the P.R.P.A. shall not accept any other form that does not bear the Agency's official seal and corresponds to the season's year. (b) Players are not committed to play with the team in which they played the year before, and may sign with other teams; 

Provided, That they comply with the provisions hereof.¹ 

§ 5-307. Eligibility and registration 

Each team may register a maximum of 20 players, 2 coaches and one manager, but the latter 3 may not play for said team unless they comply with the eligibility requirements and are counted as part of the 20 players that form the team. Once the coaches and manager are registered, they may only act as players with the authorization from the Director of the P.R.P.A. Recreation and 

Sports Bureau. 

§ 5-308. Closing of registrations 

Registrations shall close when the Director of the P.R.P.A. 

Recreation and Sports Bureau so reports personally or by phone, through the press, letter or any other means. § 5-309. Exchange of registration of players (a) Any changes shall be made within 30 days after the beginning of a tournament, but only as regards new players. Players from other teams may be used only in such cases as are expressed herein. (b) Players released within the first 30 days of the tournament may, up to a maximum number of 3, cover vacancies in another team: Provided, That said new registration is made 10 days after the date on which the player's release was officially registered with the P.R.P.A. (1) If a player's release is to be accepted, he must surrender his identification card. (2) When said player substitutes another player, he shall submit a new contract. His previous physical examination shall be valid.

§ 5-314. Ineligibility 

(a) A player's ineligibility may be proven at any time, giving rise to the corresponding penalty. That is why both player and manager should comply with the rules. Ineligibility cases shall be solved in the manner considered most appropriate by the Puerto Rico Public Recreation and Parks Administrator, and such ineligibility shall be notified to said Administrator within 5 days after the player's participation has been confirmed. (b) The following acts, among others, may be considered reasons for ineligibility: (1) Violation of the amateurism rules. (2) Signing the medical certificate in place of the doctor. (3) Violation of the rules on residence and on Superior Baseball and New York Amateur Spanish Leagues. (4) Disorderly conduct in the field. (5) Disrespect toward officials. (6) Noncompliance with the team. (7) Any break of the rules of discipline and general rules of the game. 

Medical certificates. Regulation File No. 1273, set out in this division, contained under this section the following note: "Note: Every medical certificate shall be carefully checked to assure the doctor's authentic signature. A false medical signature entails administrative penalties by the P.R.P.A. and penal sanctions when initiated by the affected doctor." 

§ 5-315. Nullification 

In case of forfeitures or withdrawal of teams which may affect the position of any other team or teams in deciding the group championship, the Public Recreation and Parks Administrator shall assign a series between said affected teams, if the difference is of 

2 or more accredited games. § 5-316. Complaints (a) Complaints shall be filed in triplicate with the Public

Recreation and Parks Administration, duly signed, within 48 hours after the completion of the game giving rise to the complaint. If 1970 172.8.9 

Vol. 9, No. 1

T.15 § 5 

Ch. 1 submitted in any other manner, the complaints shall be denied and shall not be considered. (Teams do not usually follow this rule, thus facing problems. It is convenient for them to remember it.) (b) No complaints may be considered in any manner if they are based on plays of appreciation. If a complaint remains unanswered, it means that it does not merit a reply. Consequently, it should not be insisted upon. 

§ 5-317. Regulations 

The tournament shall be ruled by the official baseball rules for the year of the season begun, and by this division and any such other additional rules as may be adopted. 

§ 5-318. Uniforms 

All players on a team shall wear identical uniforms, no matter how simple they might be. No variety in uniforms shall be accepted. 

A violation of this rule may give rise to penalties. Managers and coaches may act as such wearing a player's shirt, but it must be equal to the one used by their team. At no time may managers intervene in the playing field wearing civilian clothes. No teams shall be accepted with names of alcoholic beverages, bars or cigarettes. 

5-319. Scorers (a) Each team shall have one scorer and both teams shall, within 24 hours after the game has been completed, forward the scorer's reports to the Public Recreation and Parks Administration. 

Scorers shall have an identification card, for which they shall file the corresponding form and send 2 2 × 2 photographs. (b) Teams shall forward in advance, by telephone, telegram or letter, the results of a game not later than a day after the completion of the game. § 5-320. Order in the playing field

Team managers shall be responsible for the order and discipline among players and the public. (1) Umpires shall not, under any concept, allow arguments in the field, except from coaches and managers who are wearing the uniforms as above indicated. Players, or any person wearing civilian clothes, shall not become involved in arguments, except umpires. The intervention of players in arguments may give rise to 1970 172.8.10

Vol. 9, No. 1

T.15 § 5-323 heavy penalties for them, the umpires making the pertinent recommendations. (2) Considering the value of the advice from professionals, they shall be accepted as team advisors, but they may not leave the dugout to intervene in any matter related with the team, except as relates to the practice before the game. (The violation of this rule shall cause his immediate withdrawal.) These professionals shall receive a letter officially authorizing them to act as such, for which they must submit a 2 × 2 photograph. 

§ 5-321. Cancellation of franchises 

All franchises shall be cancelled at the end of the season. In order to be able to manage a team for the following years, the interested party shall file an application as soon as the P.R.P.A. declares the registrations open, subject to such conditions as may be prescribed. In meritorious cases the P.R.P.A. shall give preference to those who have held franchises for this year, if they request them on time, over those persons who file new applications. 

When filing an application, it shall indicate if the person participated the preceding year, accompanied with a letter of recommendation from a municipal authority or persons of high repute in the community. District supervisors shall investigate new franchises and the results of said investigation shall determine if the franchises. are granted or not. § 5-322. Starting time

Games shall definitely begin at the time appointed by the Public Recreation and Parks Administration. In special cases umpires may wait up to 15 minutes. (1) Visiting teams affected shall submit clear and final proof attesting that some unusual occurrence prevented their appearing in the field before the appointed time. (2) The home team shall practice in the morning until 9:15 a.m. and in the afternoon until 2:15 p.m. Visitors shall begin their practice after those hours until the beginning of the game. § 5-323. Absence and leave (a) In case of unsuitable weather or unfitness of the playing field, the umpire shall decide upon the suspension of the game, for which reason the home team shall have to be present thereat. If it is determined that it is impossible to play and the home team 1970 Vol. 9, No. 1 172.8.11

T.15 § 5 

Ch. 1 is absent, the umpire shall proceed to forfeit the game. He may also determine, according to the weather and playing field conditions, if the suspension of the second game is anticipated, and he shall thus notify all parties. (b) No excuse shall be accepted to justify a team's absence in its own town, when the visiting team is present. (c) Leaving the field of a game entails the penalty provided by official baseball rule, except in special situations to be determined by the Public Recreation and Parks Administrator. § 5-324. Regular and suspended games (a) In case of suspension because of rain or unfitness of the playing, a doubleheader of 7 innings each may be played in the afternoon, depending upon the umpire's judgment and determination. (b) Regular games shall be of 9 innings each, but doubleheaders shall be of 7 innings each. If one of the doubleheaders is suspended, when it is reassigned only 7 innings shall be played. Regular games assigned as doubleheaders shall be of 7 innings. In case only one. of these is played, when the other one is reassigned, 9 innings shall be played. § 5-325. Suspended games (a) The official baseball rule shall apply in the suspension of games for any reason not stated herein. (b) Seven-inning games shall be considered official, after the first half of the fifth inning, or after the second half, as the case may be, according to the official baseball rules, in case of suspension because of rain or any other reason. § 5-326. Discipline on the playing field (a) Teams which provoke incidents through the uncalled-for intervention of players in groups shall not be accepted for the following year's season. (b) Players, coaches and managers may not smoke while wearing uniforms on the playing field, it being understood that this also covers the dugout. Team managers shall see to the compliance with this rule, since umpires, after issuing a warning, may throw out from the game violators of this rule. Any notice from a P.R.P.A. official on this matter, if proven, shall be sufficient reason for applying a suspension to the violator of the rule. 1970

Absence of umpires (a) If no official umpires are appointed, the teams shall agree on said appointment, it being understood that the home team does not have the exclusiveness in this selection. Teams may not reject the umpires after a game has begun. (The team which is not ready to follow this rule should not request a franchise.) (b) Home teams shall provide the balls for the game. In metropolitan parks, and in towns with more than one team when these play against each other, the balls shall be provided in equal shares.

§ 6-4. Title 

This division shall be publicly and legally known as: "Rules and 

Regulations for the Use of Facilities in Bathing Resorts, Swimming Pools and Public Beaches under the Jurisdiction of the Public Recreation and Parks Administration of Puerto Rico". It shall only apply to bathing resorts, swimming pools and public beaches under the jurisdiction of the Public Recreation and Parks Administration of Puerto Rico.

§ 6-5. Definitions 

The following terms appearing in this division shall have the following meaning: (1) "Administrator", the Administrator or Head of the Public

Recreation and Parks Administration created by Reorganization 

Plan No. 2 of 1950 [15 L.P.R.A. §§ 1 to 11]. 

(2) "Parking area", an area reserved and divided in such a way for the parking of motor vehicles.

PUBLIC BEACHES T.15 § 6-6 

(3) "Bathing Place", an area already delimited or to be delimited in the future by the Administration, with buoys around it. (4) "Bathhouse", building for showers, toilet rooms, space to dress and undress, and lockers to keep clothes and other wearing apparel. (5) "Swimming pool", a pool for bathing and swimming, outdoors or indoors, with its annexed buildings and installations. (6) "Public bathing resort", areas for bathing or swimming, located by the seashore, the banks of a river, lake, etc., with buildings and installations for public amusement. § 6-6. Rules for use or enjoyment of facilities 

From the date this division takes effect, the use or enjoyment of the facilities in bathing resorts, swimming pools and beaches operating under the jurisdiction of the Public Recreation and Parks Administration shall be subject to the following rules: (1) Bathing resorts, swimming pools for day use, and beaches shall remain open to the public on all workdays from 10:00 a.m. to 

6:00 p.m., excepting Mondays, when they shall be open from 2:00 p.m. to 6:00 p.m. Saturdays, Sundays and holidays they shall be open to the public from 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. After 6:00 p.m. no person or vehicle shall be allowed within the limits of the bathing resort, swimming pool or beach. (A) The entrance and exit schedule for illuminated swimming pools for night use shall be determined according to the rules established by the Public Recreation and Parks Administrator of Puerto

Rico. Said schedule shall be posted in a visible place in the main structure and swimming pool. 

(B) The Public Recreation and Parks Administration of Puerto 

Rico shall reserve the right to alter the entrance and exit schedules for the existing facilities whenever it deems it necessary, according to the natural seasons of the year and to solve traffic agglomeration or any other problem. (C) Whenever a Monday falls on a holiday, the regular Monday schedule shall be observed on the Tuesday following that holiday Monday. (2) The maximum speed for motor vehicles within the bathingresort area is hereby limited to 10 miles per hour. (3) The traffic of motor vehicles in such areas of the bathing resort wherever it is thus specified through signs and notices is hereby prohibited. 

April 28, 1967 

Vol. 6, No. 4 173

T.15 § 6 

Ch. 1 

(4) The sale of food of any sort within the bathing-resort area, except in such places established for said purpose, is hereby prohibited. (5) The introduction and use of alcoholic beverages, except beer, within the entire bathing-resort area, is strictly prohibited; Provided, that it is hereby forbidden to carry refreshments or beer, in cans or bottles, into such places reserved for bathing or swimming. (6) Throwing rubbish or waste throughout the entire bathingresort area, except in such places established for said purpose, is hereby prohibited. (7) Access to beaches, bathing resorts and swimming pools for motor vehicles shall always be through the entrance gate after payment of the fee prescribed for the area where this division applies (8) All entering vehicles shall park in the area already indicated and to be known as the parking area. (9) The bathhouses shall be used through the payment of a fee as determined for each area where this division applies. (10) Within the bathing-resort area there shall be sanitary facilities and showers for the public not using the bathhouse facilities, and they shall be used as indicated in the signs affixed therein. (11) Introducing or permitting the introduction of animals within the bathing-resort, swimming-pool or beach area is strictly prohibited. (12) The practice of baseball or softball games in the bathingresort area, except in such places provided with facilities for said use, is hereby prohibited. (13) Knocking down coconuts, as well as climbing palm trees, or any other kind of trees, is prohibited. (14) Any person damaging the personal or real property in the bathing resorts, beaches and swimming pools, shall be prosecuted pursuant to provisions of the Penal Code in force [33 L.P.R.A. § 1 

et seq.], or processed for violating this division. (15) Access to all facilities under this division shall always be through the entrance marked as such, and the exit shall be through the places marked "Exit". (16) Lockers shall only be used for keeping wearing apparel and only one locker per person shall be allowed. The Parks Administration shall not be responsible for damages, or losses, or theft of any-

body's property within the area covered by the bathing resorts, beaches or swimming pools. (17) Picnicking shall only be allowed in the area reserved for such use. (18) Bathhouse facilities in swimming pools or beaches described in this division shall be used as indicated in the signs posted on said bathhouse, that is, by men exclusively where it is so indicated, and by women wherever it is so indicated. (19) Any person using the lockers shall be responsible for the return of the key and, if said key is not returned, the person shall be obliged to pay $0.50. (24) The use of floaters that are not adjusted to the body, masks, fins and tanks which menace the bathers' safety is forbidden. (25) Pasting, painting, sticking or fixing any posters, signs, notices, advertisements or leaflets of any kind on buildings, routes of communication, promenades, fences, trees or benches within the bathing-resort, swimming-pool or beach areas is forbidden. (26) Sanitary facilities shall be used only for their appropriate purposes. (27) Damaging or altering in any way whatsoever any of the dependencies, facilities or services of the bathing resort, beach or swimming pool, as well as affixing thereon drawings, paintings or signs of any kind, is forbidden. (28) Standing, sitting or lying on the tables placed in the picnicking area is forbidden. (29) Obscene and/or indecent exposure by any person in any place or structure within the bathing-resort area and/or in automobiles or other vehicles parked within the areas covered by this division is forbidden. (30) The use of the bathing or swimming pool by persons suffering from any contagious or infectious disease or any other disease 

April 28, 1967
