T.15 § 6 

Ch. 1 

included in the Rules and Regulations of the Health Department on the use of pools is forbidden. (31) No food, refreshments, chewing gum or tobacco shall be allowed to be taken to the pool. (32) It is an indispensable requirement that all persons take a shower before entering the pool and step into the wading pool provided at the entrance of the same. Any person who for any reason leaves the pool after using it shall take another shower before going in it again. (33) Swimmers shall not be allowed in the diving area. Divers should wait for the diving area to be free of any persons before initiating the performance and shall obey the order of the lifeguard or lifeguards in charge of the diving boards. (34) Bathing suits for persons using the swimming pool shall be in a material other than wool. (35) Juggling feats, fantasy somersaults or the practice of any game within the swimming-pool area or inside the pool shall not be permitted. [Women and girls must use bathing caps while swimming in the pool.] (36) Spitting or blowing ones nose inside the pool is strictly forbidden. 

§ 6-7. Penalties 

Pursuant to Act No.

4 of June 30, 1947, as subsequently amended, and Reorganization Plan No. 2 of 1950 [15 L.P.R.A. §§ 1 to 11], any violation hereof is considered a misdemeanor and any person found guilty shall be punished by the competent Court with a fine not exceeding $500 or imprisonment not exceeding 3 months, or both penalties, in the discretion of the Court. 

§ 6-8. -Imposed by Administrator 

The Administrator himself may judge administratively any violation hereof, and the violator shall be punished by a fine not exceeding $1,000, the Administrator being hereby empowered to prosecute and punish such violations. 

§ 6-9. Effectiveness 

This division shall become effective immediately after its publication to the public, in a newspaper of general circulation throughout the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico.

§ 6-51. Definition of El Cañuelo Recreation Area 

This division refers to El Cañuelo Recreation Area on so-called "Isla de Cabra," that is the key off Morro Castle at the exit (left) of San Juan Bay and the highway or constructed road which gives access to it from the mainland next to Palo Seco.

T.15 § 6-53 EL CANUELO REC. AREA § 6-53. Rules of conduct 

The use of recreation facilities existing or which may exist in said El Cañuelo recreation area, including cultivated land, roads, playing fields, outdoor huts, tables, ovens, benches, etc. shall be subject to the following provisions: 

(a) Movement of motor vehicles. (1) Maximum Speed. Motor vehicles shall proceed within the perimeter of such island at a maximum speed of 10 miles per hour. (2) Traffic laws. The Commonwealth laws relating to traffic shall govern vehicle traffic within the perimeter of Isla de Cabra. (3) Except in emergencies, the washing, repairing, cleaning, and greasing of motor vehicles are prohibited within the area of such island. (b) Property damage. (1) Writing, painting, marking, drawing lines on or mutilating the tables, benches and/or any other structure for the service of the general public is prohibited. (2) Obstructing, damaging or mutilating the plumbing and mechanical devices for water service already installed or to be placed on such island is prohibited. (3) Altering or replacing signals and signs placed for the better use of the recreation facilities by the authority charged with supervision of the island is prohibited. (4) Pasting, painting, sticking, carving or affixing any poster, sign, advertisement, notice or leaflet, personally or by an intermediary, in the routes of communication and promenades, fences, trees or benches there installed is prohibited. 

(5) Sanitary facilities shall be used only for their appropriate purposes. Damaging or altering them in any form, or affixing drawings, paintings or obscene writings is prohibited. (6) Trees and plants generally. Cutting, damaging, burning, painting or mutilating in any form any tree, plant, grass, flower or any vegetable growth whatever, is prohibited. (7) Removing sand from the recreation area and marine zone thereof is prohibited. (8) Spilling poisonous substances anywhere on the island is prohibited. (9) Removing or transferring the tables and benches from the places where they are located to any different place is prohibited. (10) Standing, sitting or lying on the tables installed for the use of those who come to the island is prohibited. 175

T.15 § 6 Ch. 1 

(c) General safety. (1) The crowding of people or vehicles in the entrances and exits of the recreation places of the island, and in the roads, in such manner as to obstruct or interrupt traffic in the routes of access and roads of the island, is prohibited. (2) Parking such vehicles as bicycles, automobiles, trucks, pick-ups, carts and others in such manner as to obstruct the use of the roads is prohibited. (3) Traffic in and use of alcoholic beverages other than beer within the recreation area are prohibited. (4) The entrance of cattle, horses or other livestock into the recreation area is prohibited. (5) Lighting fires outside the places provided for them and/or throwing lighted objects, such as cigarettes and cigars, where there may be papers, dry leaves, tree roots, etc., and where such action might start a fire are prohibited. (6) The use of fireworks in the recreation area of the island is prohibited. (d) Standards of conduct. (1) Throwing rubbish and waste anywhere except in the containers especially placed for them by the administration is prohibited. (2) Sanitary facilities shall be used in such a way as to maintain cleanliness. (e) Games. (1) The use by adults and young people over 16 years of age of swings and other playground apparatus installed in the recreation area exclusively for children under 16 years of age is prohibited. (2) Playing baseball, softball, or any other sport in places where it may interfere with or cause danger to other persons enjoying the facilities of the recreation area not dedicated to such games is prohibited. (f) Other activities. (1) Persons frequenting the recreation area with the intention of using it permanently as a lodging are prohibited from remaining. (2) Parking automobiles or other vehicles with lowered curtains is prohibited. (3) Begging shall not be permitted. (4) Throwing stones in any part of the recreation area, and throwing breakable objects outside the containers provided for waste and rubbish, are prohibited. (5) Knocking coconuts from the palms and climbing the trees, 176

Ch. 

EL CANUELO REC. AREA T.15 § 6-55 

bathhouses, or other structures in the recreation area and/or any other place on the island are prohibited. (6) Obscene and/or indecent exposure by any person in any place or structure of the recreation area and/or in automobiles or other vehicles within the recreation area and/or in any other place on the island and roads leading thereto is prohibited. (7) In everything anticipated by the penal code, with respect to public order, expression or conduct in such form as to molest or disturb other persons by obscene, injurious, or blasphemous conduct or language is prohibited. (g) Signs and Advertisements. Placing advertisements and signs that obstruct free traffic, impede easy vision of sections of communication routes and walks, and within the cultivated area and parking area of the recreation area, and render impossible the passage of pedestrians and vehicles, is prohibited. (h) Radios and loudspeakers. The use of electro-mechanical sound reproducers, such as radios, television sets, victrolas, at an extremely loud volume which disturbs or deafens the general public, is prohibited. 

§ 6-54. Commercial and industrial activities 

(a) No person, natural or artificial, may carry on any industry, business, or occupation on the island or recreation area, or place counters, boxes and appliances, instruments or implements of any kind, in the streets, promenades, or sidewalks surrounding the same, in order to practice any business, industry or lucrative occupation, without written permission expressly granted by the 

Public Recreation and Parks Administration. 

(b) The sale of food of any sort within the recreation area without express permission of the Administration is prohibited. 

§ 6-55. Authority; penalties 

This division is promulgated under the powers granted this Administration by Reorganization Plan No. 2 of 1950, as amended by Act No. 11 of April 5, 1952 [15 L.P.R.A. §§ 1 and 6] and any violation of the rules herein established shall be punished according to provisions of such Act.

§ 15-3. Countersigning of total issue of tickets 

Every impresario of sports event shall be obliged to present to the Bureau of General Excises of the Treasury Department, at least 10 days before the date of the event, and in strictly 178

Ch. 

ADMISSION TICKETS 

T.15 § 15-6 correlative order, the total issue of the admission tickets for said event. The impresario shall present an invoice in duplicate, typewritten, or written in ink or with indelible pencil, in clearly legible characters, setting forth the following particulars: (1) Terminal numbers of each price denomination of the series (2) Color of each denomination (3) Ticket price, tax included (4) Date of the event (5) Whether the event is in the morning, afternoon, or evening.

The Secretary of the Treasury may waive the requirement of the countersigning when the impresario submits an issue of tickets offering sufficient guaranty that they can not be duplicated or forged. § 15-4. Collating and acknowledging receipt of tickets 

The official to whom the Director of the Bureau of Excises may delegate shall collate the total issue of tickets against the invoice, and if in conformity, shall sign the original of the invoice with the indication "received in conformity," and the date, delivering said original to the impresario, or to his authorized representative, and withholding the duplicate, and, where necessary, shall proceed to countersign the tickets. 

§ 15-5. Deposit and delivery of tickets 

The official responsible for the examination and/or countersigning of the tickets shall keep them locked in steel shelves, the same to remain under his custody and responsibility until their delivery to the impresario upon the corresponding receipts. § 15-6. Distribution of tickets for sale

The tickets shall be taken to the box offices or places expressly designated by the impresario of the event or his authorized representative, with the previous approval of the Public Recreation and Parks Administrator, half an hour before the moment fixed to start the sale of tickets. The ticket seller or the person authorized to sell the tickets shall not sell any tickets if an Internal

Revenue Agent of the Bureau of General Excises is not present. 

It shall be the duty of the impresario or his representative to notify the corresponding District Internal Revenue Office of the Bureau of General Excises, sufficiently in advance, the hour set for starting the sale of tickets. 179

Ch. 1 § 15-7. Access to box offices restricted 

Right from the moment the tickets are delivered to the different box offices or authorized places of sale, entrance to said box offices or places is strictly prohibited for all persons other than the following:

The impresario of the home team. 

The ticket sellers or persons assigned to each box office. 

The Internal Revenue Agent of the Bureau of General Excises. 

The General Manager of the home team. 

A duly accredited representative of the League or Sports 

Association sponsoring the sports event. § 15-8. Hour to begin sale (a) The sale of tickets to the public shall commence at the time the impresarios may deem expedient, with the previous approval of the Public Recreation and Parks Administrator. It shall be understood, however, that the sale shall not begin unless an Internal Revenue Agent of the Bureau of General Excises is present. (b) Once the total number of tickets in each of the box offices has been sold, an Internal Revenue Agent of the Bureau of General Excises shall immediately proceed to make the total liquidation. § 15-9. Ticket sale limit

The ticket seller or person authorized for the sale of tickets shall under no circumstance sell to any one person more than four tickets or one box seat for each game. $ 15-10. Tickets returned

It is hereby absolutely prohibited that an impresario or his representative accept the return of sold tickets. 

§ 15-11. Reservations prohibited 

The reservation of tickets is hereby absolutely prohibited except as prescribed through regulations by the Public Recreation and 

Parks Administration.

No tickets in excess of the authorized capacity of each of the localities of a park shall be approved and/or countersigned to any impresario; the capacity of each park shall be determined by the 180

Ch. T.15 15-14

Public Recreation and Parks Administrator and by the Chief of the

§ 15-13. Supervision by Internal Revenue Agents 

The sale of regular tickets shall always be supervised by Internal Revenue Agents of the Bureau of General Excises, it being at all times their duty: (1) To audit the tickets and ascertain that the total issue has been distributed to each box office or place especially designated for the purpose by the impresario of the event, with the previous approval of the Public Recreation and Parks Administrator. If upon receipt of the tickets in a box office or authorized place, the internal revenue agent discovers that some tickets have not been approved or countersigned, he shall proceed to seize said tickets, thus preventing their sale to the public. (2) To verify that the ticket seller or person authorized to sell the tickets does not charge a price other than the one shown on the face of the tickets, and to denounce any person caught in the act of violating this paragraph. (3) To see to it that the ticket seller or persons authorized to sell the tickets does not deliver or sell to any one person more than four tickets or one box seat for a given game. (4) To see to it that the sale of unnumbered tickets (excepting the box seats) are sold to the public in a strict serial-number order at each box office or place especially designated by the impresario of the event with the previous approval of the Public Recreation and Parks Administrator. (5) In case of suspension of the sale due to difficulties in the work schedule of the employees or to other circumstances, they shall, in the presence of the ticket seller, make an inventory of the tickets remaining unsold at the close of the sale. The Internal 

Revenue Agent shall prepare in ink or with indelible pencil, a certification stating the terminal numbers of each denomination of tickets unsold, which certification shall be signed by both the agent and the ticket seller. Upon reopening the box office for sale again, the Internal Revenue Agent must ascertain that the total of tickets shown in the certification are put on sale. 

§ 15-14. Duties and powers of Internal Revenue Agents and 

Commonwealth Police

It shall be the duty of the Internal Revenue Agents and of the members of the Commonwealth police to arrest and denounce 181

T.§ 15-14 

Ch. 1 before the corresponding court any person who sells, permits or helps anyone to sell, tickets for sports events outside the places expressly designated for the purpose by the impresario of the event with the previous approval of the Public Recreation and

§ 15-15. Penalties 

Any person who fails to observe any of the provisions of this subchapter shall have imposed and collected, through administrative procedure, a fine not exceeding $500 for each violation. The 

Secretary of the Treasury shall denounce before the courts and shall refrain from continuing the administrative procedure in those cases where he may deem it pertinent. Any person violating this subchapter shall, upon conviction by a competent court, be punished by a fine not less than $200, nor more than $500, or by imprisonment in jail for a minimum term of 30 days or a maximum term of 6 months, and for the second and succeeding violations, both penalties, fine and imprisonment, shall be imposed. 182

§ 76-1. Title; application 

This division will be known as "1957 Regulations for the Granting of Franchises for the Operation of Gambling Parlors for Games of Chance in Puerto Rico," and its provisions shall be applicable to every concessionaire of a franchise granted according to the provisions of Act No. 221 of May 15, 1948, as amended [15 L.P.R.A. 

§§ 71 to 79]. 

Any person interested in obtaining a franchise according to the Gambling Law for games of chance, shall file a sworn application with the Secretary of the Treasury of Puerto Rico. Before considering such application the Secretary of the Treasury, shall see that a notice of said application is published in one of the daily newspapers of general circulation in the Island of Puerto Rico, once every week for four weeks. Fifteen days after the publication of the last notice, the Secretary of the Treasury shall, after proper consideration of said application and the endorsement thereof by the Economic Development Administration (which hereinafter shall be referred to as "The Administration"), finally approve or reject the application, pursuant to sec. 76-7 of this title. 183

Codification. In the English of these regulations, “sociedad" was translated "company" in some places and "partnership" in others. In this division all such references have been changed to "partnership" in conformity to 31 L.P.R.A.

§ 76-2. Qualifications 

The applicant for a franchise must meet the following requirements: (1) Shall be a natural or legal person, or a group of persons, or a partnership, that in the Administrator's judgment have the intention and the ability to establish and operate such tourist facilities and those that the Administration may require in accordance with the provisions of this division, as a condition to the granting of the franchise applied for. (2) Shall enjoy a good reputation in Puerto Rico and be free from conviction for a felony or misdemeanor involving moral turpitude. These requirements shall be met, in the case of legal persons or partnerships, by all shareholders or partners. In any case, this requirement shall be met by the true owners, and not merely by the nominal owners of the business or of any participation therein. (3) Shall have the means and the organization to establish a gambling parlor adequate for the guests of the hotel, restaurant or recreation center which he may possess or manage. 184

Ch. 

T.15 § 76-7  § 76-3. Acceptance of conditions and rules 

On accepting the franchise granted, the concessionaire obligates himself to accept the conditions and rules which the Administration may formulate covering the operation of the gambling parlor. 

§ 76-4. Cancellation of franchise 

Any franchise granted for the operation of a gambling parlor shall be subject to cancellation in the event that the concessionaire fails to comply with the conditions stipulated in the franchise or in any complementary document thereof, or with the provisions of the Gambling Law. 

§ 76-5. Sale or transfer of franchise 

A franchise granted under the provisions of the Law is not transferable. The sale or rental of a gambling parlor cannot include the gambling license. The purchaser or lessor of same must file application for a new franchise in order to be able to open the gambling parlor to the public, and his application shall be processed as a new franchise. 

§ 76-6. Location; number 

The Administration will determine the localization of the gambling parlors, as well as the number of franchises that can be issued for each zone, as these have been established according to the Regulations for Games of Chance, approved by the Governor of Puerto Rico December 14, 1951 [§ 76-101 et seq. of this title], Act 221 of May 15, 1948, as amended [15 L.P.R.A. §§ 71 to 79]. 

§ 76-7. Requirements 

Before the Administration may recommend to the Secretary of the Treasury the issuance of a franchise or license for the operation of a gambling parlor in Puerto Rico, the following requirements must be met: (1) That the concessionaire obligates himself to maintain the hotel where the gambling parlor is to be operated on a level of the standards of first-class hotels, in accordance with the Hotel Code in effect in Puerto Rico, approved according to the provisions of the Industrial Incentive Act of 1954 [13 L.P.R.A. §§ 241 to 251]; 

and in compliance with all the provisions of the law. (2) That the concessionaire obligates himself to maintain the restaurant, bona fide amusement center, casino, club or private club which permit the visitors to use their facilities, as well as any 185

T.§ 76-7 Ch. 5 

other attractions for the tourists which the Administration may require, at the level of international standards, and which will best serve to develop tourism. (3) That the concessionaire establish and have in operation one or more tourist attractions that will comply with the minimum requirements stipulated and enumerated further on in this division.

Cross references. Code of Minimum Standards for Tax- Exempt Hotels, see 13 R.&R.P.R. § 225-1 et seq. 

§ 76-8. Notice of ownership change; approval of employees

When the concessionaire of a gambling franchise for games of chance is (a) a corporation or (b) a partnership, said concessionaire must notify the Administrator of the Economic Development

Administration and the Secretary of the Treasury of Puerto Rico in writing, of any transfer or cession of shares of stock or participation in same, within 30 days of the date in which such transfer or cession has taken place. The failure to make such notification, or the concealment in any form or manner of the true owner or owners of a gambling parlor, or of stock or participation of a corporation or partnership that operates a gambling parlor, will be sufficient cause for the Secretary of the Treasury to cancel a gambling license. Before considering the appointment of a manager, assistant manager, supervisor or of any other employee to work in a gambling parlor, the concessionaire must first give the name and personal history of each candidate to the Administration, and no appointment may be made until the latter's authorization to do so has been received. In the event that the Administration rejects any candidate it need not reveal the reason or reasons for such rejection. § 76-9. Minimum standards within zones

The Administration defines the requirements and policies by which it will be governed when considering the applications for a gambling franchise made by the hotels interested in establishing gambling parlors, in the following manner:

The Commonwealth of Puerto Rico is divided into three areas according to their touristic importance and the following minimum requirements are established for each zone: 

(1) Minimum Requirements for Zone No. 1. Zone No. 1 includes an area which, with the city of San Juan as a center, describes a semicircle with the following boundaries on the east, along the 186

Ch. 

 T.15 § 76-9 

road by the sea leading to Loíza Aldea up to Loíza River;

by Road 

No. 1 from Caguas to La Muda; and by Road No. 2 from San Juan to Bayamón, up to the town of Bayamón itself, including the 

Cataño zone.

The concessionaire must possess or own one or more tourist hotels, whose cost, size, complementary attractions and operation shall comply with the following conditions: (A) The hotel or hotels must have a minimum of 300 rooms, and if this requirement is not met, then the total investment should be not less than $5,000,000. (B) The tourist hotel must establish and have in operation the necessary beach attractions, as well as other attractions and/ or a swimming pool with a surface area of not less than 

250 sq. meters, besides its "cabañas," lockers and other complementary facilities. The development of the beach attractions or of the swimming pool should be proportionate to the cost of the hotel, the number of its rooms and the volume of visitors which said hotel can handle. (C) Said tourist hotel shall operate at all times under the strictest policies applicable to tourist hotels located in well known tourist centers. (D) The hotel must be managed at all times by a person of well known good moral standing, competence and experience in the management of tourist hotels. 

(2) Minimum Requirements for Zone No. 2. Zone No. 2 includes the municipalities of Ponce, Mayagüez, Arecibo and the Northeast zone of Puerto Rico, from the municipality of Fajardo to the municipality of Humacao. The concessionaire must possess or own a tourist hotel or beach resort, whose cost, size, complementary attractions and operations are subject to the following conditions: (A) The hotel must have a minimum of 150 rooms, and in the event this condition is not met, the total cost of the hotel and its complementary attractions must be not less than $2,000,000. (B) The beach resort or tourist hotel must include and operate the necessary beach and other attractions, and/or a swimming pool with a surface area of not less than 200 sq. meters, and also have a reasonable number of "cabañas," lockers, and other complementary facilities. The development of the beach attractions or swimming pool must be proportionate to the 187

T.§ 76-9 

Ch. 5 cost of the hotel, the number of its rooms, and the volume of visitors it is able to handle. (C) In these projects not included in Zone No. 1, the complementary attractions may include also a golf course with a minimum of 9 holes, natural springs, and any other facility which by its nature may constitute a real attraction for the guest or visitor, thereby contributing to his relaxation and spiritual wellbeing. (D) Said tourist hotel or resort must operate at all times under the strictest policies applicable to the resorts or tourist hotels. (E) The hotel or resort must be managed, at all times, by a person of well known good moral standing, competence, and experience in tourist hotel administration. (3) Minimum requirements for Zone No. 3. This zone comprises the rest of the Island which is not already included in 

Zones No. 1 and No. 2. 

The concessionaire must possess or own a tourist hotel or resort, whose cost, size, cost of the complementary facilities and operation must comply with the following conditions: (A) The hotel shall have a minimum of 75 rooms, and in the event this requirement is not met, the total cost of the hotel plus its complementary facilities should be not less than $1,000,000. (B) The resort or tourist hotel must also comply with the provisions set forth in paragraphs (B), (C), (D) and (E) of the 

Minimum Requirements for Zone 2 in subd. (2) of this section. 

§ 76-10. Construction to meet requirements 

The construction of tourist attractions required for the concession of a gambling franchise must be made within a reasonable period from the date of the granting of the franchise. 

§ 76-11. Plans and specifications 

The plans and specifications for the construction of a tourist hotel or resort to contain a gambling parlor must have the 

Administration's prior approval. 

§ 76-12. Opening of gambling parlor 

A gambling parlor cannot open its doors to the public until the construction of the hotel is completed and open to the public. 188

Ch. T.15 § 76-18 

 § 76-13. Rules for games, approval 

All applicants shall submit to the Administration jointly with the application for the franchise, a draft of the rules by which they intend to govern the gambling parlor, as well as the various games that will be played, including stipulations as to the maximum bets allowed and the hours of play. The Administration may approve, amend or reject said proposed rules, as provided by the 

Gambling Law and Regulations for Games of Chance in Puerto 

Rico. § 76-14. Approval of rules; inspection of parlors 

No game can be operated in a gambling parlor until the Administration has approved the rules governing same, as well as those governing the gambling parlor itself; and until a physical inspection of the parlor has been made to verify the equipment and paraphernalia authorized for use in same. 

§ 76-15. Posting of rules 

(a) The gambling parlor must have available to the public, at all times, a copy of the standing regulations for the games. (b) The English and Spanish texts of the basic rules, limits and odds established by the parlor for each game which is to be played, as approved by the Administration, shall be posted in a prominent and visible place within the parlor. The English and 

Spanish texts of the parlor's admission rules shall also be posted in a visible place immediately preceding the entrance to the same. 

§ 76-16. Access by inspectors 

The Administration, its employees or inspectors, shall have free access to the gambling parlors, their equipment, books and documents. The concessionaires, gambling parlor managers and their employees are compelled to make available to the Administration and to its inspectors any and all information requested from them in connection with the parlor, its operation, employees, and the true owners and stockholders. 

§ 76-17. Inspectors as agents of Administration 

The gambling inspectors appointed by the Administration shall be its direct representatives in all authorized gambling parlors. § 76-18. Inspector's decision; appeal

The decisions of the gambling inspectors on matters pertaining 189

T.§ 76-18 

Ch. 5 to operation and procedure within a gambling parlor shall be respected by the concessionaire or the manager of said parlor; provided that, in the event the concessionaire or his manager should disagree with the inspector's decision, he is free to appeal in writing to the Economic Development Administration within the next 72 hours after said decision was taken. The Administrator must render his verdict 15 days after the filing of the appeal; and this will be final and unappealable. 

§ 76-19. Approval of equipment 

No equipment or device shall be used in a gambling parlor without the prior approval of the Administration. The Administration or its inspectors may at any time demand the change, or prohibit the use, of any equipment (including roulette wheels, tables, cards, etc.) which in their judgment do not offer the proper guarantee to the public. 

§ 76-20. Bond 

Every concessionaire shall file a bond with the Administration up to the sum of $100,000 to answer for the concessionaire's gambling debts to the public. The prior approval of such bond by the Administration and its maintenance in effect shall be an indispensable requisite for the operation of all gambling parlors. § 76-21. Cash on hand

Every concessionaire must have, each day the gambling parlor is open to the public, a sum not less than $25,000 in cash in its vault. § 76-22. Effectiveness (a) Section 76-9 of this title will not be applied to the applications of a franchise or license to operate a gambling parlor which may have been filed with the Secretary of the Treasury prior to the approval of this division. (b) This division will come into effect immediately upon approval by the Governor of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico and filing an original and two copies in Spanish and English in the 

Office of the Secretary of State of Puerto Rico.

The licensee shall display the license in a conspicuous place in his gambling room, and shall fully and consistently abide by the provisions of the law, and the regulations thereunder, as well as the stipulations printed on the face of the license. 195

T.§ 76-212

 § 76-212. Renewal of license 

A licensee who, after having complied with the law and its regulations, is willing to continue in the operation of a gambling room, shall serve notice of the fact on the Secretary of the Treasury, by again executing Form DL-1 and making an additional payment of $6,000, at least 15 days prior to the expiration of the license. If no changes have taken place as to the shareholders or partners, the renewal of the application shall be approved definitively, subject to cancellation only under the circumstances provided in sec. 76-213 of this title. If changes have occurred and, in the judgment of the Secretary of the Treasury, it appears that the new partners or shareholders do not meet the qualifications prescribed by sec. 76-202 of this title, the application for renewal shall be denied; provided, however, that if the Secretary of the 

Treasury, because of limitation of time or due to complications in the investigation, or for any other reason, is prevented from reaching a decision before expiration of the 90 days authorized by the license, said officer may renew the license tentatively without prejudice to its cancellation if after the investigation it appears that the new partners or shareholders have made false statements in their application, or that they do not meet the conditions prescribed in sec. 76-202 of this title. 

§ 76-213. Cancellation of license 

The following circumstances shall be grounds for the cancellation of a license: (1) Failure to own and manage a hotel, restaurant, or bona fide amusement place suitable for tourists, or casino, club-house or private place that permits the freedom of its facilities to tourists and in which the gambling room would be established, or ceasing to be the owner of the building in which one of said establishments is located. (2) Having been convicted of a felony or a misdemeanor involving moral turpitude and/or losing his good standing in Puerto Rico, in the judgment of the Secretary of the Treasury and the 

Administration. 

(3) Failure to own the means and the organization for the establishment of a gambling room suitable for tourists, in a hotel, restaurant, or recreation place, or casino, club-house or private place. (4) Failure to pay the license fees when due; or evading payment thereof. 196

Ch. T.15 § 76-217 

(5) Violation of any of the provisions of Act No. 221, of May 15, 1948, as subsequently amended [15 L.P.R.A. §§ 71 to 79], and of the regulations implementing same. (6) Nonpayment within the prescribed term of the fines im posed by the Economic Development Administration under sec. 9 of said Act No. 221 [15 L.P.R.A. § 78]. 

§ 76-214. Notice to police authorities 

The granting, renewal, or cancellation of each license shall be immediately notified by the Secretary of the Treasury to the Chief of Police of Puerto Rico. 

§ 76-215. Fines imposed by the Administration If under sec. 9 of Act No. 221 [15 L.P.R.A. § 78] the Administra tion imposes administrative fines on the licensee and the latter does not pay same within 30 days after the date of notice thereof, the Secretary of the Treasury shall then proceed to collect said fines through the procedure prescribed by sec. 105 of the 

Internal Revenue Law, or he may in his discretion cancel the license of said licensee.

§ 76-216. Clandestine gambling room 

Any officer in charge of the enforcement and execution of the law and its regulations who in the discharge of his duties shall unexpectedly catch a gambling room established against the law, or operating before a license is issued to it, shall serve notice simultaneously on the police authorities and the Secretary of the Treasury. 

§ 76-217. Notice of transfer or assignment 

Any transfer or assignment of any shares or interest in a gambling room whose operation has been authorized through a license issued by the Secretary of the Treasury, shall be notified to said officer, as well as to the Administration, within a period of 30 days from the date of said transfer or assignment, regardless of the date the transfer is registered on the stock book. Failure to notify the transfer or assignment, or the concealment in any form of the actual owner or owners of the gambling room, or of any share or participation in the artificial person, or assignee of a 197

license, shall entail the cancelling of the license. (Sec. 6 of Act 

No. 221, approved May 15, 1948 [15 L.P.R.A. § 75].) § 76-218. Publicity of authorized gambling room prohibited; minors

No gambling room shall be permitted to advertise itself or in anywise offer its facilities to the public of Puerto Rico, nor shall any such gambling room admit persons under 18 years of age.

Subchapter 76a. Regulations for Games of Chance DIVISION 1. GENERAL RULES SECTIONS 

76a-1. 

76a-2. Employees 76a-3. Inspectors

76a-6. Rules for games 

76a-7. Rules applicable to all games of chance Concessionaires $ 76a-1.

Upon application to the Economic Development Administration for a gambling license granting the concessionaire the right to operate a gambling casino in accordance with the provisions of Act 221, approved May 15, 1948, as amended by Acts 21 and 24 of June 7, 1948 and Act 343 approved May 14, 1949 [15 L.P.R.A. §§ 71 to 79], and upon the granting of said license by the Secretary of the Treasury, the concessionaires shall comply with the provisions in the law and also with the following requirements: (1) The concessionaires, in applying for a license to operate a gambling casino, will submit to the Economic Development

Administration the rules and regulations for the different games of chance that they intend to operate. If and when the Administrator approves the submitted proposed rules and regulations, no other games can be played that are not included in said regulations. 

Notwithstanding the aforementioned, the Administrator can consider applications to include other games of chance and will approve or disapprove the corresponding petitions. (2) When the concessionaire does not personally operate the 198

Ch. 5

T.15 § 76a-1  

gambling casino, he shall designate an administrator or manager that will represent him and will be responsible for fulfilment of all of the latter's obligations. (3) In case there should be any discrepancy between the concessionaire, his representative or employee, and an inspector authorized to act for the Administrator, the concessionaire or his representative will abide by the decision of the inspector, reserving the right to appeal to the Economic Development Administration for a revision of his decision. (4) To guarantee complete settlement of all claims against his bank at any given time during play, the concessionaire of a gambling license shall have at all times, in his establishment, not less than $15,000 in cash. If during the gaming hours this amount should be alarmingly depleted to the extent that there is an imminent possibility that the house will not be able to meet the claims against his bank, the concessionaire will be required, and is hereby required, to replenish his bank adequately to meet all impending claims. All monies collected at the time on the gaming tables may be used at any time by the concessionaire to replenish his bank. 

Under no circumstances shall the inspector allow the game to continue if, after due investigation, he finds out that the players are in danger of not being able to collect their claims. (5) In those cases when the inspector has had to order the discontinuance of the games because the concessionaire has not been able to offer the public sufficient guarantee that he will redeem the winning chips, the Administrator will, within the next 48 hours, order the cancellation of the franchise, unless the concessionaire, within 24 hours, makes a written request to the Administrator for a hearing. In such event the Administrator shall set the date for the hearing as promptly as possible, at which time the concessionaire shall offer sufficient evidence to prove that the incident was of such unforeseen nature that it was impossible for him to satisfy the bettors or the Government inspector at the time. (6) The concessionaire and/or the casino employees shall be required to submit to the Administrator all data required relative to the gambling casino, its operation, its employees, its owners, and stockholders. (7) No concessionaire, nor his agent or employee is authorized to advertise the gambling parlors to the public in Puerto Rico. 1972

Without the previous authorization by the Company, no one shall be allowed to photograph or film movies within the gambling parlors.

§ 76a-2. Employees 

(a) The following requirements must be met before approval can be given to an employee to work at the tables: (1) He must be over 21 years of age. (2) He must be a citizen of the United States of America. 1972 

Vol. 11, No. 3 200

Ch. 

T.15 § 76a-2 (3) He must not have been convicted of a felony or misdemeanor involving moral depravity, and he must enjoy a good reputation; it is ruled that in cases where an applicant for a position in a gambling parlor has been convicted of a misdemeanor not involving moral depravity, the Administrator has the power to approve or deny such application. (4) He must not have suffered a nervous breakdown or possess a physical defect that will prevent the employee from adequately discharging his duties. (5) Every employee will be required to obtain a license issued by the Economic Development Administration which will be granted without cost. The application for this license should be accompanied by a "good conduct letter" from the Chief of Police and accompanied by two photographs of the applicant. No one may be employed by a gambling casino without possessing the abovedescribed license and each employee granted said license should always have it in his possession while performing his duties. (6) Croupiers and other employees of the gambling casino must wear a dinner jacket. (b) All employees in the gambling casino shall comply with the 

1972 

Vol. 11, No. 3 200.1

200.2

Ch. T.15 § 76a-3 

(1) Treat the customers with courtesy. (2) The employees shall abstain from making suggestions to the players as to the manner in which they should bet but the employees of chemin de fer can advise the banker as described in the portion of this subchapter relative to that game. (3) Employees will abstain from soliciting tips from the players or in any way suggest that they be given tips. (4) No employee of a gambling casino shall be permitted to play even though he is not on duty. (5) All employees must show absolute honesty in their work as provided in this subchapter.

§ 76a-3. Inspectors 

(a) Inspectors are the direct representatives of the Administrator, in and outside the gambling parlors, and will see that the law and regulations are complied with. (b) Inspectors will inspect the devices, such as dice, card boxes and cards, as well as furniture and all equipment to make sure they meet the specifications called for by the regulations for each game. The inspection of equipment will be made just prior to the opening of the parlor to the public and as many times as the inspector may deem it necessary. The inspection of the furniture shall be made periodically, but never less than once a month, making sure that it offers the public sufficient guarantees. 

If in the judgment of the inspector, the furniture, equipment, or any part thereof, should not meet the provisions of these regulations, he shall order same changed or prohibit its use. This provision includes roulette wheels, cards, dice or any equipment in use. (c) The inspector will render to the Chief Inspector a daily written report covering the development of the games in the gambling parlor assigned to him, giving details of any incidents which may have occured. The concessionaire may request from the 

Department of Tourism a copy of any report rendered by the inspector when he may deem it convenient, but the department is empowered to comply or deny such request. (d) In the event that concessionaires, their agents or employees should commit acts contrary to the law or regulations in the operation or administration of a gambling parlor, it will be the 201

T.§ 76a-3  

Ch. 5 duty of the inspector to intervene to restrain such violation and he shall render in the succeeding 24 hours a detailed written report to his immediate superior. The decision of the inspector will prevail until the concessionaire has appealed to the Administrator or its successor within the next 72 hours following the inspector's decision and until the Administrator makes a decision on such appeal. The Administrator's ruling will be final and unappealable. (e) If the violation is committed by an employee, the inspector should communicate such violation to his immediate superior in order that such violation will not recur. (f) The inspectors will render detailed reports to their immediate chief of any incident which they have noted and said chief will report the matter to the Administrator if he deems it of sufficient importance. 

§ 76a-4. Rules for players 

(a) No person under 18 years of age will be permitted in the gambling room. (b) The players at each table should, at all times, conduct themselves properly. It is required that no person will raise his or her voice unnecessarily or conduct himself in such a manner as to irritate the other players congregated in the gambling casino. (c) All players are subject to the provisions of this subchapter which apply to them. (d) No intoxicated or disorderly person will be allowed in the casino. No alcoholic beverages may be served or consumed in the gambling casino. (e) No person in "shirt sleeves" will be permitted in the gambling rooms. It will be required that persons wear a suit or coat or jacket, and no person will be permitted to remove it after entrance into the establishment. 

§ 76a-5. Hours of play 

(a) No gambling parlor shall open to commence games before 8 p.m. and the specific closing time will be 4 a.m. The Administrator may change the hours of play but the gambling parlor will not remain open beyond 4 a.m. regardless of circumstances. (b) In cases where gambling parlors may wish to establish a different time table to that already authorized, a written request should be filed with the Administrator and same will not go into effect until written authorization has been received from the 202

Ch. 

T.15 § 76a-7  

Administrator, and prominently displayed to the public in the parlor. (c) The specific closing time shall not be changed without first conspicuously displaying an announcement to that effect to the public on each gaming table before the beginning of play. Once the announcement is made the time shall not be changed. 

§76a-6. Rules for games 

(a) All prescribed rules and regulations approved by the Administrator for the various games of chance shall be prominently displayed in Spanish or in English on the wall of the gambling casino. (b) Notices of odds quoted for bets in the different games will also be visibly and prominently displayed to the public on the walls as close as possible to the tables corresponding to each game. (c) Crowding at the gaming tables and parlors is strictly prohibited. (d) The Administrator in each instance can specify the maximum number of persons that shall be allowed to congregate at each gaming parlor. (e) The concessionaire or his authorized employees shall be allowed to specify the maximum and minimum bets for each different type of game not exceeding the maximum allowed by the Administrator for each individual type of game. § 76a-7. Rules applicable to all games of chance (a) The games allowed to be played by each individual casino should be, at all times, conducted under the specific rules and regulations specified by the Administrator for the particular game. (b) The Administrator shall specify the maximum number of players that shall be allowed at each individual gaming table. (c) No player shall be allowed to place a bet after the employee of the concessionaire, assigned to a specific table, indicates that no more bets are allowed. (d) The concessionaire will install in the gambling room a cashier who will redeem the chips, to all effects securities payable to bearer, that will be presented to him at the window, in legal tender of the United States of America, and at the same price quoted at the gaming table. (e) The players shall limit their bets to the maximum amounts specified by the concessionaire for each game. Said maximum 203

T.§ 76a-7 

Ch. 5

specified by the concessionaire shall at no time exceed the maximum specified by the Administrator. In case a player has made a bet that exceeds said maximum, the bet shall be considered valid only to the maximum amount specified, but the amount over and above said maximum shall be returned to the player as though such an amount had never been paid. (f) The concessionaire may set the minimums and maximums of bets in his parlor provided they do not exceed those authorized by the Administrator. However, the limits which the concessionaire or his agent proposes to set, within the limits authorized by the Administrator, should be submitted to the Administrator at least 10 days in advance and must have his approval before they can be put into effect. These minimums and maximums should be in proportion to and in agreement with the tables which form part of the rules applicable to all games and which form part of this subchapter. (g) The concessionaire and his employees will not accept bets from the public unless the sums are placed on the playing table in the form of chips, which may be purchased at each gambling table. (h) The extension of credit shall be at the sole discretion of the management of the individual casino. (i) Odds quoted and paid to winning players shall be in accordance with the Administrator's regulations. (j) Not less than $5 worth of chips will be sold to any one person. (k) The concessionaire shall assign all necessary employees for the operation of the gaming tables. 

SECTIONS (1) All officials and employees of the Economic Development 

Administration, having administrative or executive functions, directly or indirectly in the application, interpretation, inspection, supervision or fiscalization of the law and regulations for the operation of the games of chance are hereby forbidden to directly or indirectly engage in betting, or to participate or have any interest in such gambling enterprises.

Limit § 76a-31. Roulette

Equipment (a) The authorized roulette wheels are the ones known as American roulette with 36 numbers, and the signs 0 and 00. The roulette known as the French or European roulette with 36 numbers and only one 0 shall not be installed or operated in any gambling parlor, without the written approval of the Administrator. These roulette wheels similar in construction consist of one wooden concave bowl with a diameter of approximately 32 inches in its interior. The center of this bowl has a revolving disc, also made of wood, and rests and rotates in its center on a steel axle crowned by a ball bearing so that its action will be smooth and uninterrupted. The disc or plate in its superior part shows a smooth surface slightly convex. On the edge of this plate or disc are marked between metal partitions the numbers from 1 to 36 in black and red, alternately, as well as the signs 0 and 00, in green colors. This disc is the only revolving part of the roulette and shall 205

T.15 76a 

Ch. 5

be operated only by human power. It is permitted to use roulettes with one or two layouts. (b) The balls to be used may be of ivory or synthetic composition and of various sizes. (c) The layouts shall have clearly marked the numbers 1 to 36 and the signs 0 and 00 in their respective colors, as well as the bets of simple and double chances. (d) Each roulette table of one layout shall have a chip set in five different colors, one for each player, besides one or two more different colors for paying higher denominations. 

§ 76a-32. Number of players 

Not more than five players shall be allowed at a roulette table of one layout and not more than ten at a roulette table of two layouts. 

§ 76a-33. 

Personnel (a) Each roulette table of one layout shall have one dealer who will be in charge of the conduct of the game. He shall see that the rules are observed by the players and enlighten them in this respect. This employee will be the only person authorized to operate the roulette wheel and to collect and pay the losing and winning bets. There shall be another employee to assist the dealer in his work, but his duty shall be exclusively the stacking of the chips. (b) The concessionaire reserves the right to assign the dealers at the roulette tables. (c) A player has the privilege to ask the concessionaire or manager to substitute the dealer, providing there is no opposition from one or more players at the table, and, not before the dealer has thrown the ball five times. Players shall not abuse this privilege.

§ 76a-36. Bank craps-Equipment 

(a) An oval or rectangular table of approximately 4 or 5 feet wide by 11 or 12 feet long, with a wooden rail of 8 to 10 inches high around the edge of its surface and covered with rubber in its interior. The surface of the table must be covered with a layout on which the following bets must be marked: win or pass line; lose line or don't pass with one of the following combinations bar, aces (1-1) or sixes (6-6) at the election of the concessionaire; the field with the following numbers: 2-3-5-9-10-11-12; all craps; craps separately; seven; eleven; big 8 and 6; come; don't come with aces (1-1) or sixes (6-6) bar. All these bets must appear on the layout besides other bets that the concessionaire wishes to offer to the players. (b) Dice shall be transparent, high tempered celluloid and shall caliper perfect between facets with a tolerance of not less than 

1/1000 of an inch. Size of dice from 1/2 to 3/4 of an inch, razor edge and flush spots. No dice with beveled edge, round corners or deep flush spots shall be permitted. Six or more dice shall be used; 

2 for the conduct of the game and the rest shall be kept in a conspicuous place on the table to be used during the game. (c) Stick to be used by the stickman to pass the dice to the player. (d) Set of chips. § 76a-37.

Personnel There will be three employees in charge of the table; two dealers and one stickman. The dealers will be in charge of paying the winning bets and collecting the losing bets. They will also be in charge of selling the chips to the players unless the house or concessionaire wishes to use a boxman to perform this duty. The stickman will pass the dice with the stick to the players, will announce the different combinations made by the dice at every throw and will call the winning bets. He shall be the only judge at the table to make all decisions pertaining to the game. § 76a-38.

 § 76a-39. -Procedure 

(a) The players around the table shall place the amount of chips they desire to bet on the different bets marked on the layout. The stickman will pass the dice with the stick to the player to whom the turn to roll the dice corresponds, who is the first person to the right of the dealer. This player, as any player whose turn is to throw the dice must make a bet on the win or lose line, besides any other bets marked on the layout that he wishes to make. 

Immediately the player receives the dice he shall throw them across the table according to the rule posted by the concessionaire on the wall near the crap table, which, must be according to the section 76a-36(a) of this title relative to this game. When the dice stop rolling and settle on the layout they will make a combination. If this combination is 7 or 11 all bets against the house win (Pass Line) and the bets in favor of the house lose (Don't Pass). 

The player has already made a "Natural" pass. In the next new roll if the dice make one of the following combinations known as "Craps"; two (2), three (3) or twelve (12) all bets against the house lose and the bets in favor of the house win, with the exception that the combinations made by the dice, is bar in the "Don't Pass". In this case there is no action in the bets in favor of the house (Don't Pass), the bets don't win or lose. New bets are made on the win line and the dice are rolled again by the same player. If in this new roll the dice don't make any of the combinations already mentioned above and makes any of the following combinations 4-5-6-8-9-10, the combination formed will become automatically the point of the player and of all who are playing that he wins. The player shall throw the dice until he repeats the number which constitutes his point. If before he makes his point he makes the combination of seven (7) all the bets on the "Win Line” will lose and the bets on the "Loss Line" will win. The player loses the opportunity of throwing the dice again and it shall be the turn of the player to his right to throw the dice, who shall continue the same procedure as the previous player. § 76a-43. Number of players 

Not more than the number of betting squares on the layout are permitted to sit at the table. S76a-44. -Shuffle and cut 

Dealer shuffles the two packs together and gives to any player to cut. The blank card is placed at the bottom of the cards and all cards are placed into the dealing box face down. The first card is drawn, shown to the players and not used in that deal. After this procedure the cards are ready to deal. § 76a-45. -Betting

Before the deal begins each player places a bet in front of him on the table in chips. Players can bet the amount they desire providing they don't go over the maximum nor under the minimum posted by the house. $76a-46. Deal

When all players have placed their bets, dealer gives one card face up to each other player in rotation starting by the left; then one card face down to himself; then another card face up to each player including himself. Thus each player except the dealer receives two cards face up and dealer receives one card face up and one card face down. 

§ 76a-47. -Object of game 

Counting any ace as 1 or 11, as he wishes, any face card as 10, and any other card at its pip value, each player attempts to get a count of 21, or as near to 21 as possible, without going over 21. 

§ 76a-48. Naturals 

If a player's first two cards are an ace and a face card or ten, giving him a count of 21 in two cards, he has a natural or black jack. If any player has a natural and the dealer does not have a natural, dealer immediately pays that player one and one-half times 1972 

Vol. 11, No. 3 212.1

T.§ 76a-48 

Ch. 5 

the amount of his bet. If dealer has a natural, he immediately collects the bets of all the players who do not have naturals, but no player need pay any more than he bet originally. If dealer and any other player both have naturals, the bet of that player is a stand off (he takes back his chips, and neither pays nor collects). 

If dealer's face-up card is ten, face card or ace, he may look at 1972 

Vol. 11, No. 3 

212.2

Ch. T.1576a-51 

his face-down card to see if he has a natural; if his face-up card is anything else he will not look at his face-down card until his turn comes to draw. 

§ 76a-49. Drawing 

If dealer did not have a natural, when he has settled all bets including naturals he turns to the player nearest his left. That player may stand on the two cards originally dealt him, or may require the dealer to give him additional cards, one at a time, until after receiving any such card he stands on the total already dealt to him if it is 21 or under; or busts (goes over 21) in which case he immediately pays the amount of his bet to the dealer. Dealer then turns to his next player in turn to his left and serves in the same manner. 

When dealer has thus served every player, he turns up his own face-down card. If his total is 17 or more, he must stand; if his total is 16 or under, he must take a card and must continue to take cards until his total is 17 or more, at which point he must stand.

If the dealer has an ace, and counting it as 11 would bring his total to 17 or more (but not over 21) he must count the ace as 

11 and stand. § 76a-50.

Settlement 

A bet once paid and collected is never returned. If dealer goes over 21 he pays to each player who has stood the amount of the player's bet. If dealer stands at 21 or less, he pays the bet of any player having a higher total; collects the bet of any player having a lower total; and is at a stand off with any player having the same total. § 76a-51. Reshuffling

As each player's bet is settled, dealer gathers in that player's cards and places them in the discard box face up. 

Dealer continues to use the originally shuffled pack until he comes to the face-up blank card, which signifies the end of the shuffled cards. At this point he interrupts the deal, shuffles all cards not in play, has them cut by any player or players, again places the blank card face-up on the bottom, and continues the deal. Before any deal, if the dealer does not think there are enough cards to go around in the next deal, he may gather up all cards for a new shuffle and cut. 213

T.§ 76a-52 Ch. 5 

 § 76a-52. 

Splitting pairs

If the player's two first cards are of the same denomination, as two jacks, or two sixes, he may choose to treat them as two separate hands. The amount of his original bet then go as on one of the cards, and he must place an equal amount as a bet on the other card. When this player's turn to draw comes, dealer first gives him one card face-up to each. The player may then require dealer to give an additional card or cards to either hand, in whatever order he wishes, until he has gone over or stood on both hands. The two hands are treated separately, dealer settling with each on its own merits. 

§ 76a-53. Other bets 

There are other bets, like "down for double", "insurance" and an additional hand to a player, that can be made, but which the house has the privilege to accept or deny. 

If the player has eleven in his first two cards, he may double the amount of his bet and draw only one more card, which will be dealt him face down. He must not look at this card until the dealer turns his card face up. This play is known as "down for double". "Insurance" may be bet, at dealer's choice, when a player draws an ace as his first card. Player places an outside bet that he draws a face card or ten in the next card. If he does, banker will pay him two to one on the outside bet; if he doesn't he loses the outside bet, but his original hand stands until there is a decision in the usual manner.

The dealer may or may not consent to allow a player to play more than one hand, except in case of splitting pairs when the dealer must abide by the rule governing such a play. 

The last card of the pack is never dealt. If given to any player by mistake it shall be taken back.

Codification. The last paragraph of this section was not in the original Spanish text. 

§ 76a-54. Irregularities

Since all player's cards are dealt face up, there is no penalty for any irregularity, but an irregularity must be corrected if discovered before the bet has been settled; after the bet has been settled, there can be no correction. If dealer has a natural, but fails to announce it before dealing an additional card to any player, his hand constitutes a count of 21 but can be tied by the hand of any player whose total is 21 in three or more cards. 214

Ch. 5

§ 76a-56. Chemin de Fer-Equipment 

(a) The standard Chemin de Fer Table is approximately 8 feet long by 412 feet wide. The playing surface is heavily padded and covered with the standard Chemin de Fer layout. This table may have 9, 10, 11, 12, or 13 numbered sections, one for each player besides, a place for the dealer. The table is provided with a slit and a discarded card receiver under it. (b) Palette for handling chips and cards (not compulsory). 1972 215 

Vol. 11, No. 3

T.§ 76a-56 

Ch. 5 (c) Chemin de Fer dealing box, called shoe, which releases one card at a time face down. (d) Six 52-card packs of American playing cards shuffled together; plus two blank cards. (e) Set of chips. 

§ 76a-57. -Number of players 

Not less than four players and no more than the number specified by the numbered sections on the layout are permitted to sit at the table. Persons gathered around the table are permitted to bet against the bank when those sitting have not covered the total amount with their bets. They do not have the privilege to hold the bank since the game develops on the strict numerical order of the sections on the layout, and only receive cards when one of them calls "Banco" and gets the option, or is the highest bettor against the bank. 

§ 76a-58. 

Shuffle Portions of the packs are given to different players to shuffle and given back to the dealer who will shuffle the cards together and offers the pack to one player to cut. The cutting is usually done by introducing a blank card between the cards and placing one portion divided by the blank card behind the other. The blank card will stay in that position as a cover to the last card of the pack. 

The dealer places another blank card, six to nine cards from the end of the pack to warn the banker of the ending of the cards. No deal shall be started after this blank card comes out. The cards so shuffled and cut are placed in the shoe. Then the dealer draws the first card face up to determine by its numerical value the number of cards to be taken out of that deal (burned). In other words, if the first card drawn is a five the dealer shall burn five additional cards besides the first card drawn, but never more than six cards shall be burned. 

§ 76a-59. -Deal 

(a) The dealer does not participate in the game, except to shuffle cards, assist the players in making and setting their bets, to advise them on the proper procedure for the game, and to quote to them the mathematical advisability of alternate plays. He also collects the percentage fixed by the concessionaire from the banker of the profit of the second pass made and after each and every successive pass. This percentage should not exceed 5%. Banker 1972 216 

Vol. 11, No. 3

Ch. 5

T.15 § 76a-59  

surrendering the bank after the first pass must pay the house the percentage based on the value of his bank. Player at number one section will be the first banker and the amount of his bank is announced and placed on the table in chips. After the turn of the first banker is consumed the player to his right will be the next banker. The rest of the players will proceed to bet against this bank until the full amount is covered. All bets must be made before dealing. The banker will not be responsible for the payment of bets exceeding the amount of his bank. Bets in excess of the total of the bank do not win or lose. The player who makes the highest bet receives the cards dealt by the banker and plays his bet together with the other player's bets against the banker. In case of two or more players betting the same highest amount, the player nearest to the banker's right receives and plays the cards. (b) A banker while holding the bank cannot withdraw any portion of the bank, but he can withdraw the amount not covered by players. Nevertheless, he has the privilege of retiring the whole amount after making any number of complete passes. In this case he has to give up the bank which goes to the highest bidder. In case of tie among two or more players bidding for the bank, the player nearest to the right of the outgoing banker, has the option. After this new banker loses the bank, the player to 1972

216.2

Ch. 

T.15 § 76a-61 the right of the previous banker will be the next banker. If a player calls "Banco" it means that he accepts the banker's entire bank as a wager, and all smaller bets must be withdrawn. If two or more players call "Banco", the nearest to the banker's right has the option to the bank. However, a player who has "Bancoed" the previous hand and lost it, has preference to the bank a second and third time, but no more than three consecutive times. (c) After all bets are made the dealer will instruct the banker to deal the cards. The banker deals one card face down to the players, then one card face down to himself; then another card face down to the players; then another card face down to himself, so that there are two cards face down for players at the center of the table and two cards also face down in front of him. The dealer will pass the cards for players to the player who has made the highest bet against the bank. 

§ 76a-60.

Object of game (a) To form in two or three cards, a combination counting as near to 9, 19 or 29 as possible. Only the final digit counts. Face cards and tens count nothing, aces count for one, other cards for their numerical value. In other words, the picture card King and a five count five (5), and will beat a ten and four which count 14.

If either player has a count of 8 or 9 in his first two cards, he has a natural and shows his cards immediately. If a banker alone has a natural, banker wins all bets, if the opponent alone has a natural, banker pays all bets. A natural 9 beats a natural 8; two naturals of the same number are a stand off, cards are tossed in, all bets are withdrawn, and players place their bets for the next deal. (b) If neither banker nor his opponent has a natural, the opponent may draw one card, following the rules of drawing for players. This card is dealt to player face up. The banker will decide to draw or not, following the rules of drawing for the banker. In case the banker draws, the card will be dealt face up. No more than one card can be drawn by either player or banker. When both players have stood or drawn, all cards are shown and whoever is closer to 9, wins the bets; if they have the same total all bets are a stand off, there is no action and deal continues.

(a) Rules for players. Player against banker must draw to four

Chapter 7. Puerto Rico Lottery Subchapter 126. Administration and Operation of Lottery DIVISION 1. BUREAU OF LOTTERY SECTIONS 126-1. General powers and duties 126-2. Powers and duties of the Director of the Bureau 

126-3. Powers and duties of the Assistant Director 

§ 126-1. General powers and duties 

The Bureau of the Lottery of the Department of the Treasury shall have charge of everything concerning the direction and administration of the Puerto Rico Lottery, subject to the provisions of the Act and of this subchapter. The Director of the 

Bureau of the Lottery shall be vested with the necessary powers to direct, either directly or by express delegation thereof to his assistants and other subordinate personnel, everything concerning the administration of the Puerto Rico Lottery, pursuant to the provisions of the Act and of this subchapter. 

Source. §§ 126-1 to 126-214: Regulation for Administra tion and Operation of the Puerto Rico Lottery, promulgated by Secretary of the Treasury, app. by Governor Jan. 17, 1957, eff. day following 5th day of publication (March 1, 1957). 

Filed with Secretary of State Sept. 26, 1957; File No. 180. 

Authority. Act May 15, 1947, No. 465, p. 1022, § 16, 15 L.P.R.A. § 126. 

§ 126-2. Powers and duties of the Director of the Bureau 

The director of the Bureau shall, in addition to the powers and duties prescribed by law and other provisions of this subchapter, have the following: (1) He shall annually prepare and submit to the Secretary of the Treasury, on the date determined by him, a draft of the budget of expenses for the Bureau of the Lottery; (2) Shall prepare, with the approval of the Secretary of the

Treasury, the prospectuses for the drawings to be held, which prospectuses shall be printed and distributed to the public and the agents. In said prospectuses shall be set forth the number, series and class of drawings; the price, total number of tickets to be issued, the prizes to be awarded, the date on which the drawings will be held, and the cost of the ticket to the agent and to the peddlers; (3) Shall sell for cash to the agents the lottery tickets with 221

T.§ 126-2 

Ch. 7 the discount stipulated in the discount schedule prepared by him with the approval of the Secretary of the Treasury; (4) Shall submit to the Secretary of the Treasury a report on the result of each drawing; (5) Shall certify the general accounts, settlement vouchers and other documents to be issued, in the form and manner prescribed by official regulation of the Secretary of the Treasury; (6) Shall recommend to the Secretary of the Treasury the amount of the bonds to be given by the officials and employees of the Bureau; (7) Shall see to the enforcement of the Act and this subchapter; (8) Shall prepare, for the approval of the Secretary of the

Treasury, the bylaws for the proper operation of the Bureau; (9) Shall keep a register of the expiration of all agency contracts and shall notify the Secretary of the Treasury, with at least 45 days in advance of the expiration of each contract, the grounds for which said contract should or should not be extended; (10) Shall keep a register of all the appointments of peddlers made by each agent, their exact addresses, identification number of each peddler, and number of tickets which the agent has committed himself to deliver to each; (11) Shall be responsible to the Secretary of the Treasury for the issuance and distribution of the lottery tickets; (12) Shall be in charge of all the investigations carried out by the Bureau, including the investigation of lottery agents, peddlers and applicants for lottery agencies; (13) Shall coordinate and direct the work of all the Bureau's inspectors; and (14) In addition, the Director of the Bureau shall have such additional powers and duties as are from time to time conferred or imposed on him by the Secretary of the Treasury. 

§ 126-3. Powers and duties of the Assistant Director 

The Assistant Director of the Bureau shall have such powers and duties as may be entrusted to him by the Director of the Bureau, and shall also perform such functions as from time to time the Secretary of the Treasury may assign to him. 222

DIVISION 2. TICKETS

Fraction of ticket Ownership

Sale of whole tickets or fractions Distribution § 126-21. Issue of tickets 

The issue of lottery tickets shall unfailingly be in whole tickets, divided into not less than 20 fractions. § 126-22. Number of tickets, drawings

The number of tickets of each drawing, the value of each ticket, the prizes of each drawing, and the number of drawings to be held in any one month, shall be determined, and the dates on which said drawings are to be held shall be fixed, by the Secretary of the Treasury, but not less than two drawings shall be held each month; provided, that one or more special drawings shall be held annually on such dates as may be approved by the Secretary of the Treasury on recommendation of the Director. § 126-23. Fraction of ticket

Each fraction of lottery ticket shall have a value proportionate to that of the whole ticket, and in each drawing there shall be as many winning tickets as there are prizes authorized and advertised on the back of said tickets. The amount to be distributed in prizes shall not be less than 60 percent of the total value to be paid by the public for the tickets corresponding to each drawing. § 126-24. Ownership 

The lottery tickets shall be considered as securities payable to bearer, and therefore, no person other than the one possessing and presenting the ticket for collection shall be considered as the owner thereof. 

§ 126-25. Description of tickets 

The lottery tickets shall have the lithographed seal of Puerto Rico on each of their fractions and there shall also appear on the same, the value of the fraction, the date on which the drawing will be held, the series number of the drawing, the amount of tickets 223

T.15 126 Ch. 7 

to be issued, their price, the number of prizes, the date of their prescription, a facsimile of the Secretary of the Treasury's signature, and any other information that the Secretary may think proper.

Codification. The English translation of this section has been supplied by the editors. § 126-26. Sale of tickets; agents and peddlers

The lottery ticket shall be sold by the Director of the Bureau of the Lottery and by the agents and peddlers appointed according to the Act and this subchapter. The Director of the Bureau shall sell the tickets to the duly appointed agents who have qualified to act as such, unless the Secretary of the Treasury for good reason, orders otherwise.

Codification. The English translation of this section has been supplied by the editors. § 126-27. Discounts to agents

The lottery agents shall buy the tickets cash from the Director of the Bureau of the Lottery, who shall make them a discount in accordance with a schedule of discounts prepared by him, from time to time, with the approval of the Secretary of the Treasury, such discounts never to exceed 20% of the official price of the tickets; Provided, that whenever the official price of a ticket is $6 or more, the discount will not be less than $1 per ticket. 

Codification. The English translation of this section has been supplied by the editors. § 126-28. Sale of whole tickets or fractions

The Director of the Bureau shall, with the approval of the 

Secretary of the Treasury, sell the tickets, either in whole tickets, or in fractions thereof, or in both ways, at his discretion. 

SECTIONS § 126-29. Distribution 

The tickets issued in each drawing shall be distributed by the Director of the Bureau, with the approval of the Secretary of the Treasury, among the authorized agencies, in accordance with the existing contracts with said agencies.
