126-70. Determination of number for each agency § 126-41. Selection of lottery agents

Every person who, in accordance with the Act and this subchapter, qualifies to become an agent of the Puerto Rico Lottery, may apply for an agency by using the printed application form provided for such purposes by the Bureau. 

As it becomes necessary, the Bureau of the Lottery shall investigate the applications for agencies to determine the merits and qualifications of each applicant. § 126-42. Government officials

No person shall be eligible for appointment or be appointed lottery agent who holds any position in the Federal, State or Municipal Government, including mayors and legislators. 

§ 126-43. Property qualifications 

Nor shall any person be appointed as agent who possesses property assessed at more than $10,000 for purposes of taxation. 

No person who is a lottery agent and who has satisfactorily been such prior to January 1, 1951, shall be deprived of his agency for the reason that his property is assessed at more than $10,000 as a result of the scientific assessment of property in Puerto Rico carried out under the provisions of the Act for the cadastre, 225

T.§ 126-43 

Ch. 7

classification, and assessment of property, of May 9, 1947, as amended [13 L.P.R.A. §§ 431 to 438]. 

§ 126-44. Personal qualifications 

Lottery agents shall be of legal age, residents of Puerto Rico, of recognized integrity and morality, and physically and mentally capable for the adequate fulfillment of the duties and obligations imposed on them by the operation of a lottery agency. 

Except in those cases of widowed mothers, or of a person partially disabled to obtain employment in other occupations, agents of the lottery shall be over 45 years of age. 

126-45. Income qualifications

On and after the effectiveness of this subchapter, no person shall be appointed as agent who has a monthly income which, added to the monthly income of the family living under the same roof, exceeds $300, taking into account the proceeds deriving or that may be derived from the lottery agency. 

§ 126-46. Conjugal partnerships 

In the case of spouses under the existing conjugal partnership system in Puerto Rico, the agency contract shall, for all purposes of the Act and this subchapter, be executed with the conjugal partnership, and all the limitations stipulated in this subchapter shall be made specifically extensive to both spouses. 

The contract shall be signed by both spouses, and the administration and representation shall be assumed by the husband as the legal representative of the conjugal partnership, except in those cases in which, by mutual agreement of the parties the Bureau of the Lottery and the conjugal partnership and for good cause, in the interest of both, such administration and representation is partially or fully delegated to the wife, or any other person. 

§ 126-47. Recommendations for agency

When it shall become necessary to choose agents, the Director shall submit to the Secretary of the Treasury his recommendations for each agency, together with a copy of the investigation report carried out in the case, and stating the grounds on which he bases his recommendation. 

§ 126-48. Order of preference 

After verifying that the applicants qualify within the limitations 226

Ch. T.15 § 126-52 

stipulated by this subchapter, upon preparing his recommendation, the Director shall observe, as far as possible, the following order of preference: (1) widows with children in their custody; (2) married couples with dependents of school age; (3) persons with minors under their patria potestas; (4) persons handicapped by partial physical disability to perform other works or occupations; (5) persons with other handicapped dependents under their guardianship; (6) persons who by reason of age are precluded from obtaining remunerative work in other trades or occupations. § 126-49. Recommendations, number of tickets; bond

The Director shall likewise make his recommendation as to the number of tickets that should be assigned to the agency, and the bond that in his judgment should be required as security for the agency contract. 

§ 126-50. Action on recommendations 

The Secretary may approve or reject the recommendations of the Director, both with respect to appointment and as regards quota and bond, and in case of rejection, the Director shall submit new recommendations. 

§ 126-51. Execution of contract 

When the Secretary approves a recommendation, the Director shall execute the corresponding lottery agency contract with the recommended person approved by the Secretary, which person shall, upon executing said contract, be bound to comply with all the other requirements prescribed by this subchapter to qualify as an agent. 

§ 126-52. Duration of contract 

The said contract shall have an original effectiveness of one year from the date it is signed; provided, however, that said contract shall contain a clause reserving to the Bureau the right to cancel same, as provided in this subchapter; and provided, further, that said contract shall be understood to be extended from year to year, unless 30 days in advance of the date of its expiration either of the parties shall notify the other of its intent not to extend it. 227

T.§ 126-53 

Ch. 7 

§ 126-53. Bond 

Said contract shall require the furnishing by the agent of a sufficient bond conditioned upon his faithful performance of all his obligations under said contract and this subchapter. 

§ 126-54. Removal of agency 

The agencies may not move from the municipal jurisdiction for which they were originally granted without the previous investigation and favorable recommendation of the Director of the Lottery and the official approval of the Secretary of the Treasury. 

§ 126-55. Effect of appointment 

The appointment of an agent is tantamount to the granting of a permit or franchise to: (1) purchase, under certain conditions and limitations, with a fixed discount, a certain number of tickets of the Lottery of Puerto Rico; (2) sell said tickets, either directly or through peddlers, at the price stipulated by the Bureau of the Lottery. 

§ 126-56. Relationship of parties 

Therefore, the granting of an agency does not entail the existence of management-labor relations between the Bureau of the Lottery or the Government of Puerto Rico on the one hand and the agencies on the other. 

§ 126-57. Status of agents 

The agents of the lottery, are therefore, grantees, contractors, or commission agents, to whom no salary is fixed or paid; no fixed hours of work are imposed, and whose work is not disciplined beyond the provisions of this subchapter. The profit or income. received by the agents as such are derived exclusively from the commission they receive from the sale of tickets. § 126-58. Quotas

On and after the effective date of this subchapter, no lottery. agency shall be assigned a quota in excess of 60 tickets per drawing; provided, that if it should become necessary to authorize an increase of this number of tickets, the maximum quota assigned to an agency for each drawing shall not exceed an amount of $900 of the total price at which the tickets shall be sold to the public, and it is further provided that these limitations shall apply only to regular drawings. 228

Ch. 7

T.15 126-64 

§ 126-59. Responsibility of Bureau 

The Bureau of the Lottery assumes no responsibility for the acts done by lottery agents in the course of their transactions with the public, or with private firms, enterprises, or entities. § 126-60. Collection and payment

The agents shall collect and pay in cash or by checks or bank drafts drawn to the Secretary of the Treasury, in the Bureau of the Lottery or at any other place designated by the Secretary of the Treasury, on the days set by the Director, the number of tickets assigned to them in accordance with the contract in force. 

§ 126-61. Collection agent 

When the agent is unable to collect his tickets in person, he may delegate this function to any natural person who meets with the approval of the Director of the Bureau. 

§ 126-62. Seal 

The tickets received by each agent shall be clearly stamped by him on the back of each fraction, before their sale, with his seal, in whose inscription he shall indicate his name, town where his residence is located, and the number assigned to his agency. § 126-63. Collection of tickets; forfeiture

If for any reason or cause the agent should fail to collect the tickets on the dates previously fixed, said agent shall forfeit his right to the tickets, but the forfeiture of such right shall not affect in anywise the responsibilities and obligations contracted by the agent, the Bureau reserving the right to cancel the contract, or to claim against the bond given. § 126-64. Peddlers, use by agents

The agent shall be bound to utilize peddlers to dispose of part of his tickets according to the following scale: Agencies of 21 to 35 tickets, not less than 30 percent to peddlers; agencies of 36 to 46 tickets, not less than 40 percent to peddlers.

If evidence is obtained that the agent has overcharged any of his peddlers, or the public, it may be sufficient ground for the cancellation of the contract with the agent, as well as for the termination or annulment of the appointment of said agent. § 126-67. Monthly report

Every agent shall submit, not later than the 10th day of each month, a monthly report, on the printed form supplied for such purpose by the Bureau of the Lottery, showing his ticket transactions, including an exact list of the number sold to each one of his authorized peddlers during the month preceding the rendering of said report. Should the agent render a totally or partially false report, it may be sufficient cause for the cancellation of his appointment as lottery agent. § 126-68. Public services 

The agents shall render the following public services: (1) to pay prize-winning tickets, strictly at par, as far as their resources will go; (2) to post to the public the prospectuses of drawings during the effectiveness thereof, as well as the official lists of the prizes corresponding to the last two drawings held; (3) to post in a conspicuous place to the public all the propaganda material that the Bureau of the Lottery may send them; (4) to stamp and distribute the tickets to their registered peddlers; (5) to hear all complaints and claims of the public, and of their peddlers; (6) to keep a register of their peddlers in which shall appear; (A) name of each peddler, (B) address, (C) number of tickets the agent sells to him, price, and conditions of the sale; 1969

§ 126-70. Determination of number for each agency

The number of tickets assigned to each agency shall reflect, among other factors, the economic necessity of the agent. The

§ 126-91. Causes for termination 

The agency contract shall terminate for any of the following causes: (1) by the death of the agent; (2) by expiration of the term of the contract or of any extension granted; (3) when the contract has been entered into with a conjugal partnership, by the dissolution of such conjugal partnership for any of the causes determined by the Civil Code of Puerto Rico; provided, however, that the bond furnished by the agent in accordance to sec. 126-49 of this title shall continue in force until 30 days after the surety or any of the spouses notify the Bureau of the Lottery of the fact of the dissolution of such conjugal partnership, unless before expiration of such term the Bureau of the Lottery stops selling and delivering tickets to the agent because of the termination of the contract. And provided, further, that in case of the dissolution of the conjugal partnership by the death of one of the spouses, the surviving spouse shall be under obligation to notify the fact of the death to the Director of the Bureau of the Lottery, and in case of the dissolution of the conjugal partnership by divorce or through declaration of nullity of the marriage, the person who, according to the record of the Bureau of the Lottery, has in his charge the administration of the agency, shall be under obligation to notify the Bureau of the Lottery of the dissolution of the conjugal partnership; (4) by the rescission of his contract as hereinafter provided. 231

Ch. 7

§ 126-92. Violations; notice of rescission; reconsideration 

If it is found that an agent has violated the provisions of the Act of this subchapter, or of the contract for the purchase and sale of tickets, it may be grounds for the rescission by the Bureau of the contract for the purchase and sale of lottery tickets.

The rescission of the contract shall be by letter or telegram sent to the agent at the address appearing in his record in the Bureau of the Lottery. In said letter or telegram shall be stated briefly the grounds for the rescission of the contract. The rescission of the contract shall be effective on the 30th day after the delivery of such letter to the agent or of the deposit of the telegram in the offices of the Communications Authority. 

During the 10 days immediately following the date of the delivery of such letter or of the deposit of the telegram, the agent may petition the Secretary of the Treasury for reconsideration of his contract, giving the reasons on which he bases his petition. 

If the Secretary of the Treasury denies reconsideration of the case; or if the agent does not apply for reconsideration within the term fixed, the cancellation shall be final and unappealable. § 126-93. Additional causes for rescission

The following shall be additional causes for the rescission of the agency contract: (1) that the agent loses his qualifications to act as such, during the effectiveness of his contract;

§ 126-111. Appointment 

The peddlers shall be appointed by the agents, who shall submit their selections to the approval of the Director of the Bureau. 232

Ch. T.15 § 126-115 

The Director may provisionally approve the designations of the peddlers made by the agents, but approval shall not be formally imparted until an investigation of the candidates recommended has been carried out, for the purpose of ascertaining their financial responsibility and moral solvency, no person being eligible for appointment as peddler who has been convicted of a felony, or of an offense involving moral turpitude. 

§ 126-112. Number of tickets 

No peddler whatsoever shall be permitted to contract for more than 60 tickets per drawing, but if it is necessary to authorize an increase in this number of tickets, the maximum quota assigned to a peddler shall not exceed an amount of $900 of the price at which the tickets shall be sold to the public; provided, that these limitations shall only apply to the regular drawings. § 126-113. Price

The price at which the tickets are to be sold to the peddlers by the agents shall be that fixed by the Bureau of the Lottery for these transactions.

The price at which the tickets are to be sold to the public shall be that fixed by the Bureau of the Lottery, and if evidence is obtained that a peddler has overcharged in the sale of tickets, either in the sale of whole tickets or of a fraction or fractions thereof, it shall be ground for the immediate revocation of his appointment as peddler of lottery tickets. 

§ 126-114. Records 

Once the appointments of peddlers are officially approved, the Bureau shall prepare a record for each peddler, and in that record shall be set forth, among other particulars, the number assigned to the peddler by the Bureau of the Lottery, full name, home and postal address, a health certificate issued by the Department of 

Health, and two recent photographs 2 X 2, as well as the number of tickets contracted for by the peddler with one or more agencies. § 126-115. Personal qualifications 

The peddlers of lottery tickets shall be over 21 years of age, residents of Puerto Rico, of recognized integrity and morality, and physically and mentally capable for the adequate performance of their duties. 233

T.§ 126-115 

Ch. 7

To accredit his trade as authorized seller of tickets, each peddler shall visibly carry the official distinction mark issued for the purpose by the Bureau of the Lottery. 

§ 126-116. Minors 

(a) The Bureau of the Lottery shall reject the appointment of minors for the sale of tickets, and lottery agents and authorized peddlers are strictly enjoined from using minors for the sale of lottery tickets. (b) When it is proven that a peddler has made use of the services of a minor for the sale of tickets, it may be sufficient cause for the immediate revocation of his permit to sell lottery tickets by the Director of the Bureau. 

§ 126-117. Termination of contract 

When an agent may wish to discontinue his business relations with any of his peddlers, or to modify the terms of the obligations contracted with said peddler, he shall so notify the Bureau before taking any action, giving the reasons for so doing. § 126-118. Revocation of appointment

The following may be reasons for requesting the revocation of the appointment of a peddler by the agent: (1) that the peddler defaults in his official obligations contracted with the agent; (2) when the peddler observes a reproachable behavior in his relations with the Bureau of the Lottery, with the agents, or with the public; (3) when his conduct is in conflict with the administrative norms of the Bureau of the Lottery. § 126-119. Appeal; hearing (a) If a peddler is not satisfied with the determination notified to him by the agent, he may appeal from said decision to the 

Director of the Bureau. (b) After hearing both parties, the Director shall decide on the action to be taken, and both parties shall abide by his decision; provided, that if any of the parties does not agree with the decision, the same may be appealed from to the Assistant Secretary in charge of Public Revenues, and the decision of said official shall be final and unappealable for both parties. 234

126-135. Suspension of provisions 

§ 126-131. Quotas of tickets 

The quotas of tickets for the agents shall be as determined in the appointments. In order that any change in said quotas may be of a permanent character, the same must have been approved by the Secretary of the Treasury; provided, however, that the quotas of lottery tickets of agents over 72 years old shall be adjusted so that the income to be received, counting the pension to which the agent and/or his wife may be entitled, in cases of conjugal partnerships, pursuant to federal social security legislation in force in Puerto Rico, be equal to the income he was receiving from the operation of his agency before receiving, or being entitled to, the federal pension aforementioned. 

§ 126-132. Administration of agency 

The agent engages and binds himself to continuously, daily, and personally administer his agency in the city or town for which the permit has been granted, and not to transfer or delegate to another person his administration of the agency or the supervision of his peddlers. § 126-133. Distribution of surplus tickets

When for any reason there is a surplus in the Bureau in the distribution of tickets, said surplus shall be proportionally distributed among the agencies having the lowest quotas, and always in rotation, if compatible with the best interests of the organization. 

§ 126-134. Cornering tickets 

Any agent, peddler, or any other person who, by any means or manner, and through agreement, contract, or other transaction, corners or tries to corner lottery tickets in violation to this subchapter, shall be guilty of a misdemeanor, and upon conviction thereof shall be punished as provided in section 19 of the Lottery Act [15 L.P.R.A. § 127], and, likewise, the Director of the Bureau 235

T.15 126 

Ch. 7 shall be under obligation to immediately cancel the agency or revoke the peddler's permit, as the case may be. 

§ 126-135. Suspension of provisions 

Authority and discretion are hereby conferred on the Secretary of the Treasury to suspend any of the provisions of this subchapter in force, if in his judgment such suspension is necessary to authorize any acts compatible with the provisions of the Lottery Act.

§ 126-151. Board of drawing 

Each drawing shall be organized, directed and inspected by a Board of Drawing composed of three persons of good repute and qualified for the performance of their duties, who shall be appointed by the Director of the Bureau, at least three days prior to the day on which the drawing is to be held. The Director of the 

Bureau shall likewise appoint at least two alternates to substitute for the regular members as hereinafter provided. The Board shall elect a chairman. The duties of the Board shall be: (1) authorize the act with their presence. 236

Ch. 7

T.15 126-156 

(2) pass upon any incident relative to the holding of the drawing. (3) suspend the drawing when any act may occur whose seriousness calls for such measure, in which case the Board shall immediately notify the Secretary of the Treasury for the proper action. (4) overcome any difficulty that may arise in the holding of a drawing, and see that the drawings are held in strict compliance with the law and with this subchapter. 

§ 126-152. Assistance to Board 

The Board of Drawing shall be assisted in its functions by the Director of the Bureau and by the employees he may designate. 

The Director of the Bureau shall act as Secretary of the Board of Drawing. 

§ 126-153. Attendance at drawing 

The attendance of three members of the Board of Drawing shall be required for the holding of a drawing. In case any of the regular members is unable to attend, or absents himself, the Director of the Bureau shall designate in his place one of the alternates previously chosen. 

§ 126-154. Minutes of the Board 

Minutes shall be kept of the decisions of the Board of Drawing by the Secretary thereof, who shall keep a journal ad hoc. The minutes shall be signed by all the members of the Board of Drawing present and attested to by the Secretary. 

§ 126-155. Chairman of Board 

The chairman of the Board of Drawing shall be in charge of all the operations of the drawings and the employees designated by the Director of the Bureau shall be under his orders. 

§ 126-156. Public view 

The verifications and other necessary acts shall be performed in such manner that the public attending the drawings shall constantly have in sight the prize-winning balls, which, once the drawing is terminated, shall be exposed to the public's view during the time and at the site designated by the Director of the Bureau of the Lottery, in order that any one who so wishes may examine them. 237

T.§ 126-157 

Ch. 7

 § 126-157. Repairs to equipment 

If any globe or other device employed in the drawing should be broken or damaged, the chairman shall direct that it be immediately repaired, if possible; and if not, and the drawing is hindered thereby, the drawing shall be suspended, and the occurrence and the resolution of the Board shall be entered in the minutes. A copy of such minutes shall be immediately transmitted to the Secretary of the Treasury for his information. As soon as the necessary repairs have been carried out, the drawing shall be proceeded with on the same day or on the next working day. 

§ 126-158. Remarks by public 

The attending public shall have the right to make to the Board of Drawing any remarks they may deem pertinent, and the Board shall, by a majority of its members, decide thereon. 

§ 126-159. Examination and recount of balls 

On the eve of each drawing, unless it be a holiday, and if it is, two days before each drawing, there shall be publicly made the examination and recount of the balls corresponding to the tickets and prizes to be used therefor. The examination and recount of the balls shall be carried out by a member of the Board of Drawing, the Director of the Bureau of the Lottery, the employee in charge of the mechanical operations, and the employee in charge of the balls, the latter performing the duties of secretary in such act. 

§ 126-160. Arrangement of balls 

The balls corresponding to the numbers of the tickets shall be strung in cords in numerical order, beginning from the lowest numbers up, conveniently sealed and united in one cluster of a thousand balls. The same procedure shall be followed with the balls corresponding to the prizes, except that these shall be arranged in the order of their value, from the highest down, so that they may be easily examined by the parties concerned. § 126-161. Placing in bag 

The employee in charge of the balls with the numbers shall present them as above stated and shall facilitate the examination and verification thereof by the public attending the act. Upon completion of this task, each thousand balls shall be placed in a 238

Ch. T.15 § 126-166 

burlap or other transparent-cloth bag sufficiently strong to insure that it will not disintegrate. Said bags shall be conveniently fastened and strapped and sealed, and on the outside of each bag a card shall be fixed, within the strapping, duly marked and indicating the number of balls contained in the bag, and all the balls shall be placed and closed in the bags through the use of a patent padlock with two different and independent keys and a safety padlock of only one key. § 126-162. Balls corresponding to prizes

The same procedure established in sec. 126-161 of this title shall be followed for the balls corresponding to the prizes, except as to the total that shall be placed in each bag. § 126-163. Closing of bags after recount

Upon conclusion of the examination and recount of the balls, the person in charge thereof shall close the bags and deliver a key of each one of the bags to the member of the Board of Drawing present, to the Director of the Bureau, and the other one to the employee in charge of the mechanical operations. The 

Secretary shall draw up the proper minutes, which shall be countersigned by the member of the Board of Drawing present. 

§ 126-164. Safekeeping of bag 

The person in charge of the balls, together with the Director of the Bureau and the member of the Board present, shall safekeep said bags in the vault of the Bureau, from where he shall transport same, accompanied by the Director of the Bureau, on the day of the drawing, to the premises specifically designated for the holding of the drawing. Said bags shall remain in the premises of the drawing, under his vigilance, until delivered to the Board of Drawing. § 126-165. Opening bags; inspection

Once the Board of Drawing is constituted on the day, hour and place designated, the drawing shall be started by publicly opening said bags and inviting the public to examine the balls. 

§ 126-166. Receptacles for balls 

A series of balls shall bear the corresponding numbers of the quantity of the tickets of the drawing; another series of balls shall indicate, also in figures, the amount of each one of the prizes 239

T.§ 126-166 

Ch. 7

making up the total number of prizes of the drawing. The first series of balls, showing the numbers of the tickets, shall be placed in a receptable, and the second series, showing the amounts of the prizes, shall be placed in another receptacle. Both receptacles shall be covered with a wire-mesh. Once all the balls corresponding to each thousand of the numbers and then those of the prizes have been gathered in their respective receptacles, at a given signal of the chairman, the balls shall be mixed in each receptacle by means of an adequate device until the chairman directs that each thousand balls be introduced in the globes ready to receive them, which shall be done by means of a mechanical device and so that no one will touch them. The globes shall be covered by a wiremesh and shall have a device at the lower parts thereof to make an opening which will allow the passage of only one ball which shall always be in view of the persons attending the drawing. 

Upon finishing this operation, the chairman shall close the globes, placing the keys thereof in sight of the public, on the tip or top end of a rod which shall be placed vertically on the tables of the Board. 

§ 126-167. Drawing 

The chairman shall direct that the globe containing the numbers and the globe containing the prizes be simultaneously whirled so that they revolve at least ten times before starting the drawing. 

After stopping the whirling of the globes, and at a signal of the chairman, the drawing shall be started by making each globe revolve at least once on its axle from time to time, as directed by the chairman of the Board. The person in charge of the mechanical device which allows passage of the balls shall have the forearm bare, up to the elbow, and on receiving the numbered ball in a transparent receptacle, a child from the charitable institution designated beforehand shall withdraw the ball from said receptacle and loudly announce the number shown on it. The child shall forthwith insert the ball in a rod of the corresponding exhibition board, and after thus inserted, the employee of the Bureau appointed for the purpose shall verify if the number has been correctly called out. In case said employee discovers that the number called out by the child does not correspond to the number indicated on the ball, the child shall again loudly announce the correct number. Simultaneously the same procedure shall be followed with respect to each ball corresponding to the prizes. 240

Ch. 7

T.15 § 126-172 

 § 126-168. Disposition of ball 

Inasmuch as the balls evince the result of the drawing, they shall be withdrawn from the globes one at a time. These balls shall be placed in the rods of the exhibition board intended for such purpose, in the order in which they have been withdrawn from the receptacles, in such a way that each number ball shall have beside it the prize won thereby, and in such fashion as to avoid the least variation among them. 

§ 126-169. Determination of prizes 

The ball withdrawn from the globe corresponding to the prizes shall determine the prize won by the ball simultaneously extracted from the globe corresponding to the numbers. 

§ 126-170. Reading of prizes 

Major prizes shall be read aloud thrice by the institutional inmates acting in the drawing, who shall hand over the balls to the chairman of the Board, who shall verify them before placing them in the exhibition boards, and shall note them in ink on the list prepared for the purpose. Thus shall continue the balls in both globes to be withdrawn until those corresponding to the prizes are exhausted. § 126-171. Placing balls on rods

The placing of these balls in the exhibition boards as herein provided shall be done by the inmates from the charitable institution serving in the drawing, supervised by the employees, who, being near them, may, without touching the balls, notice any mistake or error on their part. Said employees shall see to it that any error be immediately corrected, and shall, furthermore, inform the chairman of the Board whenever two balls are missing to complete a rod in the exhibition board. § 126-172. Closing of exhibition boards

After the balls corresponding to the numbers and those corresponding to the prizes have been placed on each exhibition board, said boards shall be closed with manifold double patent padlocks fastening the top ends of the rods so that no ball can be withdrawn, one of the keys to be kept by the chairman of the Board and another by the Director of the Bureau. This operation shall be performed by the employee designated for such purpose by the Director. 241

T.15 126 Ch. 7 

 § 126-173. Lists of numbers 

As the numbers and the prizes are announced out loud, two employees designated by the Director of the Bureau shall prepare lists of the numbers, under his immediate inspection, sending a copy of said lists to the printery to prepare proof lists, after verifying them with the numbers in the exhibition boards. There shall be as many lists as there are exhibition boards, and the latter shall contain the numbers in the same order as the balls have been placed on said board. Said lists shall only be considered as auxiliary for the printery and of a private character, for which reason no person outside the Bureau shall have a right to inspect them. § 126-174. Correcting of lists; number

Once the proof lists are printed, two employees designated by the Director of the Bureau shall compare them with the balls placed on the exhibition boards and shall correct any mistakes. that may be found, until the lists are correct. Of these lists, the 

Secretary shall sign four copies, countersigned by the chairman of the Board, of which the first copy shall go together with the minutes of the drawing, the second shall be posted to the public, the third shall be sent to the printery, and the fourth shall be transmitted to the Secretary of the Treasury. 

§ 126-175. Public view of board 

The boards containing the balls, after so compared for a second time, shall be placed in sight of the public at the premises wherein the drawing was held, during work hours on the days directed by the Director of the Bureau, an employee designated by the Director of the Bureau having the custody of said boards. 

§ 126-176. General list of prizes 

After conclusion of the said second comparison, the lists signed by the secretary and countersigned by the chairman of the Board, shall be replaced by a general list of prizes approved by the Board, as soon as it is received from the printery and verified through a last collation. 

§ 126-177. Records 

For each drawing a record shall be formed including all pertinent information concerning same, the minutes and the lists signed by the Director of the Bureau, the list of the major 242

Ch. T.15 126-193 

2 prizes, the general list and the lists which have served for its verification, and said record shall be sealed and filed for such effects as may be pertinent.

§ 126-191. Payment of prizes 

The prizes corresponding to each lottery ticket shall be paid at the Bureau of the Lottery, at the offices of the Collectors of Internal Revenue of the municipalities of the Island and by the agents appointed in accordance with the Act and this subchapter. 

The major prizes shall be paid in the Bureau of the Lottery. The payment of the prize-winning tickets shall start on the working day following the holding of each drawing, and without any further delay than is necessary for the proper organization. The payment of prizes in the Bureau of the Lottery may be made in cash up to the sum of $200 per person for special drawings, or by checks made out to the bearer or in the name of the person designated thereby. 

§ 126-192. Cash 

The payment of prizes in the offices of the Collectors of Internal Revenue of the municipalities of the Island shall be made out in cash up to the sum of $200 per person and as far as the funds allotted by the Official Paymaster of the Lottery may go. The payment of prizes by the agents shall be in cash up to the amount permitted by their funds. 

§ 126-193. Official lists 

For the payment of prizes in the Bureau of the Lottery and in the offices of the Collectors of Internal Revenue of the municipalities of the Island and in the office of the agents, there shall only be accepted the authentic lists of prize-winning numbers as 243

T.15 126 

Ch. 7

are printed and distributed by the Director of the Bureau, with the approval of the Secretary of the Treasury, and any other document or notice shall be considered a private notice and without official character. 

§ 126-194. Payment period 

No prize-winning ticket may be paid in the offices of the Collectors of Internal Revenue after the lapse of 150 days from the date of the drawing to which said prize-winning ticket appertains. 

§ 126-195. Presentation of ticket 

No prize-winning ticket shall be paid without the previous presentation of such ticket and the ascertainment of its legitimacy. § 126-196. Payment of mutilated tickets

No ticket shall be paid that has been perforated as proof of annulment or that has been cancelled or paid by the Bureau of the Lottery. In relation to any torn or mutilated ticket giving rise to doubt, it shall be the Director of the Bureau who shall determine if payment of the corresponding prize is in order. From the decision of the Director of the Bureau appeal may be taken to the Secretary of the Treasury within a term of fifteen days counting from the day notice of the decision of the Director of the Bureau was served on the party concerned. § 126-197. Expiration of right to collect prizes 

The right to collect prizes shall expire at the end of six months counting from the day following that on which the drawing to which they correspond was held. At the expiration of this term the Government of Puerto Rico shall be free from all liability. 

§ 126-198. Tax exemption 

The prizes of the Puerto Rico Lottery shall be exempt from all kinds of taxes. § 126-199. Possession as ownership

The Bureau of the Lottery, the Collectors of Internal Revenue of the municipalities of the Island and the agents shall not recognize as rightful owner of a ticket any person other than the one who possesses and presents it for collection.

Any person who presents for its payment any prize-winning ticket of any drawing, shall verify the payment made to him in front of the window of the teller and in his presence, and if he does not agree with said payment, he must right there and then, present the pertinent claim.

§ 126-211. Penalties 

Any agent, peddler, or person who violates the provisions of the Act or of this subchapter shall be guilty of a misdemeanor, and shall, upon conviction thereof, be punished by a fine of not less than $10 nor more than $100, or by imprisonment in jail for one day for each dollar of the fine he fails to pay, or by both penalties, in the discretion of the court. Recidivists shall be punished by imprisonment in jail for a term of from three to six months, in the discretion of the court. § 126-212. Lottery offenses

Except as provided by law, the establishment, maintenance and operation of lotteries in Puerto Rico, is hereby prohibited. The persons convicted of lottery offense as prescribed in chapter VIII of the Penal Code [33 L.P.R.A. §§ 1211 to 1218], shall be punished as provided in said code. § 126-213. Forgery, counterfeiting

The tickets of the Puerto Rico Lottery shall be considered as securities of the Government of Puerto Rico, and any person who, with intent to defraud another, or The People of Puerto Rico, falsely makes, alters, forges, or counterfeits any lottery tickets of the Puerto Rico Lottery, or fraction thereof, or circulates, publishes, passes, or attempts to pass, as true and genuine, any ticket of the Puerto Rico Lottery or fraction thereof, knowing the same to be false, altered, forged, or counterfeited, with the intent to defraud any person or The People of Puerto Rico, shall be 245

T.§ 126-213 

Ch. 7 guilty of forgery, as prescribed by sec. 413 of the Penal Code [33 

L.P.R.A. § 1641], and upon conviction thereof, shall be punished by the penalty prescribed for said offense. § 126-214. "Act" defined

For the purposes of this subchapter, the word "Act" shall mean 

Act No. 465, approved May 15, 1947, entitled, "An Act to create an official lottery to be known as the 'Puerto Rico Lottery'.. 

[15 L.P.R.A. §§ 111-128]. 

Publication. Official notice was published in the daily press on Feb. 23, 25, 26, 27 and 28, 1957. ... 

§ 126-215. Effectiveness 

This subchapter shall be promulgated by the Secretary through administrative order directed to the officials and subordinate employees in charge of the administration of the Act, as well as to the lottery agents, and official notice to the general public of its final approval and that said subchapter is available to all those who may wish to get acquainted with it in the Office of the Lottery of Puerto Rico and in the offices of the Collectors of 

Internal Revenue of the Island. 

This notice shall be published at least for five consecutive days in two newspapers of general circulation in the Island of Puerto Rico, and the subchapter shall be effective and shall have the force of law from the day following the last publication of said notice. 246

Subchapter 186. Powers of Board; Regulation DIVISION 1. HORSE RACING REGULATIONS SUBDIVISION 1. DEFINITIONS 186-1. Definitions § 186-1. Definitions 

The following words and phrases shall have the meaning stated opposite them. The use of the masculine gender includes the feminine and the neuter and the singular includes the plural and the plural includes the singular unless the contrary be clearly indicated by the context. 

(1) "Administration". Racing Sport Administration. 

(2) "Administrator". Administrator of Racing. (3) "Horse racing agent". A person designated by the Association to receive pool, daily double (dupleta), and exacta bets. (4) "Year". Natural calendar year. (5) "Equipment". Riding gear used on race horses and by their jockeys including, but not limited to the bridle (the horse's check rein and the gear to support the animal's head), blinders or blinkers, saddle, cinch strap, sweat cloth, whip, boots, spurs, bandages, nose band, bands, tongue strap, etc. (6) "Attorney in fact". Authorized representative of an owner. (7) "Association". A natural or artificial person authorized to operate a race track in Puerto Rico. (8) "Mutuel". Place designated for betting on each individual race and the betting system known by that name. 1972 

Vol. 11, No. 3 

247

T.§ 186-1 

Ch. 11

(9) "Licensee". Holder of a license. (10) "Race". A contest between horses for a prize in the presence of duly appointed officials. (11) "Claiming race". A race in which any horse entered therein may be claimed for a previously fixed sum. (12) "Classic". A race with an additional prize in which a special fee may be required for the registration of horses. (13) "Shed". A stall or group of stalls for the keeping of an owner's horses. (14) "Multiple combination pool ticket". Printed form on which two or more combinations of play in the pool are noted. (15) "Depressant". Any product or substance that depresses or affects the natural condition of a horse. (16) “Day”. Period comprised between two consecutive midnights. (17) "Race day". Period comprised between 6 o'clock in the forenoon and 12 o'clock of the night of the day on which races are held. (18) "Drug”. Any product or substance that stimulates, depresses or affects the natural condition of a horse. (19) "Owner". Any natural or artificial person with a license issued by the Administrator and who is a bona fide owner of one or more horses. (20) "Daily double". A bet to determine the winner of two races specifically designated for such a bet. (21) "Horse". A race horse or colt. (22) "Paddock". Place designated for saddling the horses. (23) "Entry". Two horses taking part in the same race and considered as a single horse for betting purposes. (24) "Stable". The structure where one or more sheds are located. (25) "Stimulant". Any product or substance that stimulates or affects the natural condition of a horse. (26) "Horse racing nuisance". A person declared to be such by the Board according to law for obstructing the development of the horse racing sport. (27) "Field". Horses grouped and considered as an individual for the purposes of the bets in one race. 1972

§ 186-201. Race tracks; licenses - Prior requirement 

No race tracks shall be opened to the public or operated in Puerto Rico for the holding of horse races without a license granted by the Board. § 186-202. 

Filing of petition

Every natural or artificial person desiring to operate a race track must file a petition to that effect before the Board and furnish all the information and documents required of him. § 186-203. 

Hearings, announcements and notices

Before granting a license to operate a race track, the Board shall hold hearings and shall give an opportunity to be heard to all interested persons and the government agencies and instrumentalities concerned. The applicant shall publish such announcements and notices as the Board may order in connection with said hearing. 1962 

Vol. 1, No. 8 251

T.§ 186-204 

Ch. 11

§ 186-204. 

Minimum requirements

Before granting any race track license the Board shall inform the applicant of the minimum conditions and requirements under which he may operate the race track and the same shall form a part of the license if it be granted. 

§ 186-205. - Rules, regulations and orders 

The rules, regulations and orders periodically issued by the Board shall insofar as pertinent form an integral part of the license originally issued. 

§ 186-206. List of personnel 

The Association shall inform the Administrator in writing of all personnel designated or that it may from time to time designate to intervene directly in the betting or in the holding of the races stating the complete name, address and office of each person and the duties he performs. The list of the said personnel shall be submitted within the 30 days following the approval of this Division. 

In subsequent years, such list shall be submitted within the first 15 days of the month of January. All changes or additions to said personnel effected during the course of the year shall be notified in the same manner, within 10 days after designation. 

§ 186-207. - Removal of personnel 

The personnel referred to in the preceding section shall be designated and shall perform their duties subject to the condition that the Administration may, at any time, for just cause and after hearing, order their removal. § 186-208. Reasons for not granting licenses

No race track license shall be granted to or renewed to any person who: 

(1) Has any interest in race horses. (2) Is a member, employee or official of the Racing Sport Administration. (3) Has a doubtful reputation in the community in respect to his moral conditions. (4) Has ever been convicted of a felony. (5) Has been associated with or has any common interest in any business or activity with any person of bad repute or who has been 1962 

Vol. 1, No. 8 252

Ch. T.15 § 186-215 

RACING ACT 

convicted of the use of or traffic in narcotic drugs. (6) Who has ever been held to be guilty of illicit practice or practices prejudicial to the horse racing sport in any local or foreign race track. (7) Refuses to comply with or obstructs compliance with the act, the rules, regulations, decisions and orders of the Board. § 186-209.

Transfers A race track license granted by the Board is not transferable wholly or partially; Provided that when a license is granted to a corporation or partnership and the control of either of these changes hands without the approval of the Board, this shall be sufficient cause for cancellation thereof. § 186-210. Holding assigned races

The Association is under the obligation to hold all races assigned to it by the Board. 

§ 186-211. Designation of personnel 

The Association shall designate and maintain the personnel required of it by this Division or by any resolution of the Board. 

Cross references. Specific penalty for violation of this section, see § 186-1401 of this title. - · 

§ 186-212. Responsibility for acts of personnel 

The Association shall be responsible for the conduct and actions of its employees in the performance of their duties. § 186-213.- Suspension or cancellation

The Board may temporarily suspend or cancel the license of a race track for just cause, provided, that in order to cancel the same the Board must give the licensee an opportunity to be heard in his defense, in proper person or with assistance of counsel.

§ 186-214. Other licenses - When required 

No person may, in the race tracks of Puerto Rico, register horses for participation in races, train them, care for them or ride them without having a license granted by the Administrator.

§ 186-216. 

Provisional, conditional and special The Administrator may grant provisional or conditional licenses which shall not exceed a period of 60 days.

He may likewise grant special licenses for a period not exceeding 30 days waiving the requirements for licenses fixed by this Division. § 186-217. Fees; type; transmission

Before the granting of any license by the Administrator, including provisional or conditional licenses, the applicant shall pay the fees fixed by law within 10 days after demand therefor. Licenses shall be personal and nontransferable. 

§ 186-218. Expiration 

All licenses granted by the Administrator shall expire on the 31st of December of the year in which issued, except such special, conditional or provisional licenses granted with a specific expiration date prior to the above date. § 186-219. Renewal

Every application for a renewal of a license must be filed in writing on the form furnished by the Administrator on or before the thirtieth of November each year. 

§ 186-220. · Renouncement 

The license shall be understood to have been renounced whenever there is a failure to apply for its renewal within the period provided and also in the event that the holder thereof fails to pay the corresponding legal fee. § 186-221. 

Suspension or cancellation 

Every license granted by the Administrator may be temporarily suspended or cancelled by him for just cause; Provided, That to cancel a license, he must proceed by a complaint and afford the licensee an opportunity to be heard in his defense, in proper person or with assistance of counsel. 

§ 186-222. -Effectiveness and suspension

The effective term of a license shall not alter any period of suspension ordered against the licensee. 1962

RACING ACT 

§ 186-223. 

Rules and regulations The horse racing rules and regulations as well as any orders periodically issued by the Board shall be understood to form an integral part, insofar as pertinent, of the license as originally granted. § 186-224. 

Reasons for denial

The Administrator may deny the application for a license as owner, trainer, groom, groom's helper and jockey if, in his judgment and opinion the temperament, reputation, experience and ability of the applicant do not deserve the granting of said license or if the granting thereof might be detrimental to the horse racing sport for the public interest. In the case of an owner the financial solvency of the applicant shall have special consideration. 

§ 186-225. Other reasons for denial of the granting or renewal

No license as owner, trainer, groom, groom's helper or jockey shall be renewed or granted to any person who: (1) Is an officer or employee of the Racing Sport Administration, or owner, stockholder, official or employee of a race track in operation in Puerto Rico. (2) Is not a resident of Puerto Rico and does not have a resident legal representative in Puerto Rico duly authorized and approved by the Administrator. (3) Has an unfavorable reputation in the community in connection with his moral conditions. (4) Has been convicted of a felony implying moral turpitude. (5) Has been convicted for traffic in, possession, or use of narcotic drugs. (6) Is associated with or has any common interest in any business or activity with any person of bad reputation or who has been convicted of the use of or traffic in narcotic drugs or of any other offense involving moral turpitude. (7) Has incurred in illicit practices or practices prejudicial to the horse racing sport in any local or foreign race track. (8) Who knowingly gives false or incorrect information to the officials, officers, and employees of the Administration. (9) Is unable to prove that he made or will make effective use of the license after it is granted. (10) Whose responsibility and financial obligation are such that his active participation in the horse racing sport could or would be

obstructive of or detrimental to the best interests of the horse racing sport. 

§ 186-226. Natural or artificial persons 

Owner's licenses shall be issued only to natural persons who are of lawful age or to artificial persons. In the case of an artificial person, it shall designate, with the approval of the Administrator, a natural person as its attorney in fact. Any order or penalty imposed upon the attorney in fact shall be understood to be imposed upon the artificial person and it shall be responsible for compliance therewith. Although an application for an owner's license made by a natural or artificial person may be considered before the applicant possesses a horse, said license shall not be issued until the applicant shall have shown that he in fact possesses one or more horses. Every transfer of shares or interest must be notified to the Administrator within thirty (30) days after it is made.

The transfer of control of the artificial person without the approval of the Administrator shall be sufficient cause for the cancellation of the license.

§ 186-227. 

Married women

No owner's license shall be issued to any married woman unless her husband be legally incompetent to administer the community property, or who is married under an exception to the community property system.

§ 186-228. Attorney

The owner may be represented by an attorney in fact whose appointment must receive the approval of the Administrator who may withdraw it for just cause. 

§ 186-229. Instrument for appointment of attorney

The appointment of an attorney in fact must be made by public deed, and said instrument shall state the terms for which said appointment is made. 

§ 186-230. Moral requirements of attorney (a) The attorney in fact must comply with all of the moral requirements required of an owner. (b) An owner cannot act as the attorney in fact for another owner. An attorney in fact shall not act in said capacity for more than one owner.

Amendments- 1964. Subsec. (b) was added to this section by amendment File No. 929 cited in 1964 amendment note under § 186-226 of this title.

Revocation of power

Revocation of a power of attorney in fact must be made by public deed with notice to the Administrator by service upon him of a certified copy of the same. 

§ 186-233. -Approval of attorney by Administrator 

When the Administrator withdraws his approval of the designation of an attorney in fact he must give written notice to the owner 10 days in advance of the effective date of the order. § 186-234. 

Examination for trainer's license

Every person applying for a trainer's license shall be obliged, if so required by the Administrator, to take an examination before one or more examiners designated by the Administrator. The examination shall cover subject matters connected with the care, feeding, and training of and elementary knowledge of the anatomy and diseases of horses. דיר. § 186-235. -Minimum age for trainer's or groom's license

No trainer's license or groom's license shall be issued to any person under 21 years of age. § 186-236. Requirement of good health for trainer, groom and others 

The Administrator shall not grant any license as trainer, groom, groom's helper or jockey to any person who does not prove by medical certificate obtained in a Public Health Unit that he is in good health. § 186-237. 

Minimum age for jockey or groom's helper

No license as jockey or groom's helper shall be granted to any person under the age of 18 years; Provided that a license as groom's helper may be granted without the above age requirement when this is authorized by the Department of Labor of Puerto Rico. § 186-238. Suspension in other jurisdiction

Every license granted by the Administrator shall be suspended when the licensee is penalized in any other jurisdiction for violation relating to the horse racing sport. The suspension shall last for the same period as the suspension imposed in the other jurisdiction. 1969

§ 186-239. Strike

No person holding a license granted by the Administrator or the Board shall call a strike or stop his activities related to the horse racing sport without giving prior notice to the Administrator; Provided that upon receiving notice of said decision, the Administrator must within a period of 72 hours notify the parties in dispute if he has decided to mediate the matter; Provided further that if the 

Administrator decides to mediate the dispute, the parties involved in the same shall be obliged to continue performing their commitments under the same condition existing as of that time for a period of 30 days, at the end of which, if the controversy has not been satisfactorily resolved, the parties shall be at liberty to act according to their best interests.

The Administrator may employ such technical and mediation services as he believes necessary to aid in the resolution of the controversy.

§ 186-240. Conflict of interests 

Persons owning or having any interest in race horses are disqualified from obtaining a jockey's license.

§ 186-241. Effect of false information 

No license obtained through false or incorrect information shall have any effect nor shall it acknowledge any privileges or rights whatsoever.

By order or resolution the Board shall draft a plan of races which it may clarify, alter or amend from time to time as it may find necessary. 

§ 186-504. Secretary of races-Designation 

The Administrator shall designate a secretary of races who will prepare the conditions under which the races in the race tracks of Puerto Rico shall be held following the standards laid out in the races plan prepared by the Board. § 186-505. Assistants

The Administrator may appoint or employ assistants or helpers for the secretary of races. 

§ 186-506. -Decisions 

The decision or order of the secretary of races to exclude the entry of a horse in any determined race shall be final. 1972

RACING ACT § 186-507. Registration in races-Prior requirement 

No horse shall qualify to be entered in a race unless it has been duly registered for that race. § 186-508. 

Date, time and place

Registrations shall be made on the date, at the time and place fixed by the Administrator. § 186-509. —When they shall be made

Registrations must be made not less than 2 days prior to the date set for the races except in cases where the Administrator authorized registrations in a shorter period of time. 

§ 186-510. Official form 

The request for registration must be made on the official form prepared for this purpose by the Administrator. § 186-511. Signatures

The registration form must be signed by the owner, attorney in fact or trainer and by the jockey who is to ride. No jockey shall sign more than one form for each race. § 186-512. Who may be present

At the act of the registrations only the owner, attorneys in fact, trainers, jockeys, the officials in charge of the registration and any other persons authorized by the Board or by the Administration may be present. § 186-513. Closed box for requests

The request for registration will be deposited in a closed box in charge of the Racing Secretary or the Entry Judge, which box shall not be opened before the time set for commencement of the act of registration.

After the application for registration has been deposited it cannot be withdrawn under any circumstances. The application for registration may only be cancelled by depositing a counter order duly signed before the box is opened. 

Amendments-1964. The closed box for requests will be in charge of the Racing Secretary or the Entry Judge before it was in charge of the secretary of races, also changes in phraseology were made in this section by amendment File

Opening of box; selection of horses

Racing Secretary or the Entry Judge shall proceed to open the box, he will organize the registration sheets for each race and will determine which horses are qualified and entitled to take part in each of the races according to the conditions set for the same. 

The applicant may withdraw his horse after the other participants are known but this must be done before the race is organized and it can only be done if such an action will not cause a race to be declared abandoned.

§ 186-515. 

Void requests

Every request for registration that fails to conform with the requirements of this Division and the registration sheets shall be void. - · § 186-516. 

Post positions by lot

After the determination of what horses are to run in each race notice of this will be given to the interested persons present and the post positions will immediately be drawn by lot. 

§ 186-517. Maximum number of participants

Not more than 14 horses can take part in one race; Provided, however, That the Board may fix a smaller number. 

§ 186-518. Order for eliminations 

In the event more horses are registered than the number permitted to run eliminations shall be made in the following order: (1) Horses constituting an entry of the same owner. (2) Inferior horses. (3) Horses who ran on the most recent date. (4) By lot; Provided that in the cases of an entry the owner may select the horse to be withdrawn. (5) In races assigned to imported horses they shall have preference over native horses except in classics. 

§ 186-519. Abandoned or voided race (a) Any race for which less than four horses belonging to different owners none of which constitute an entry are registered shall be declared abandoned. Classic races shall be held with whatever number of horses are registered. (b) Any race in which less than three horses compete shall be declared void for the pool. 

Amendments- 1964. Subsec. (b) was added by amendment File No. 929 cited in 1964 amendment note under 

§ 186-226 of this title.

No horse which has been sold or transferred from one owner to another may enter in the same race in which a horse belonging to the seller has been registered during the 15 days following the date of the registration of the transfer in the registry.

§ 186-521. 

Inspection of horses

No horse shall be registered that has not raced for a period of 90 days without being first inspected by the veterinary. 

Amendments 

- 1964. The requirement that the veterinarian inspection shall be 15 days prior to the registration was omitted by amendment File No. 929 cited in 1964 amendment note under § 186-226 of this title. 

§ 186-522. Bad manners or unruliness of horses 

No horse that has been suspended for bad manners or unruliness in a race shall be registered unless the starter gives a certificate showing that the bad manners or unruliness has been corrected. 

§ 186-523. Fines in arrears

No horse shall be registered whose owner or trainer is in arrears for a period greater than 10 days for any fine imposed upon him. 

Amendments-1964. The words "or trainer" following "owner" were added by amendment File No. 929 cited in 

1964 amendment note under § 186-226 of this title. 

§ 186-524. Races for native horses

No imported horses shall be registered for races assigned to native horses. 

§ 186-525. Races for imported horses; exception

The registration of native horses in races assigned to imported horses shall not be permitted except where the native horse, in the opinion of the secretary of races, can compete under equal opportunities. The determination of the secretary of races in this respect shall be final. § 186-526. Participation on consecutive days 

The registration of a horse to run on 2 consecutive race days shall not be permitted; Provided That when this occurs the request for registration for the second race day shall be void. 

Participation in more than one race on the same day When the registration of a horse for more than one race on the same day is requested the horse shall be declared ineligible for registration in said races.

§ 186-529. - Horses or licenses suspended

§ 186-530. Entry 

Requirements 

The following shall be considered an "entry": (1) Horses kept in the same shed. (2) Horses trained or cared for by the same person. 

(3) Horses with the same owner. (4) Horses whose owners, trainers or jockeys are within the second degree of consanguinity. The word owner as used herein includes the members of an artificial person.

§ 186-531. Rules

The race rules applicable to a horse which is an entry affect all of the horses in the entry as if it were a single horse.

§ 186-541. Change of jockey 

In making a change of jockey his substitution by another jockey who is to take part in the same race shall not be permitted, except that when a horse is withdrawn from the race at the official hour his jockey may be permitted to ride another horse in that same race. 

§ 186-542. Official program 

After the withdrawal, alterations or corrections have been made, the Association will publish and circulate the official program in conformity with the information and requirements of the Administrator or the secretary of races; Provided that all of the races to be held on the race day shall appear on the official program.

 § 186-601. System of wagers 

The Association shall be under the obligation to maintain at its racetrack systems of wagers for playing the pool, mutuels, daily double (dupleta), and exacta and shall not suspend said systems of wagers without prior authorization of the Board; Provided, That to give said authorization it shall be the duty of the Board to hold a public hearing. 

Amendments-1971. Reference to exacta betting was added and the word "Board" was changed to "Racing Board" by amendments, File No. 1465, cited in 1971 amendment note, under § 186-1 of this title.

 1 § 186-602. Horse racing agents for bets

The Association shall designate horse racing agents to receive pool, daily double (dupleta) and exacta bets. The agent must be a natural person and his designation, suspension or retirement shall be subject to approval by the Administrator. Agencies shall be transferable with the approval of the Association and the Administrator. The Administrator shall not approve the concession of an agency to a person who has been convicted of the use, possession or traffic in narcotic drugs or of any other felony that implies moral turpitude. 

Amendments-1971. Reference to exacta betting was added and "Administrator" was changed to "Racing Administrator" by amendments File No. 1465, cited in 1971 amendment note under § 186-1 of this title. § 186-603. Furnishing of material for betting

The Association shall furnish to the agent all of the material necessary for betting, such as multiple combination tickets, single combination tickets, registration sheets and official programs; Provided, That in case of conflict, the Administrator after a hearing shall determine the needs of the agency. § 186-604. Commission of agents

The Board shall fix the commission to be received by the agents for the bets made through them, and said commission shall be a share of the total value of the combinations played in the agency. 

The Association shall not be entitled to receive any commission on the bets on the pool made on the premises of the race tracks. 

Cross references. Specific penalty for violation of this section, see § 186-1401 of this title. 1972

RACING ACT § 186-605. How pool bets shall be made 

Pool bets shall be made only through the agents and within the premises of the race track directly with the Association at a place previously designated by the latter and approved by the Administrator.

§ 186-606. Hour of closing bets 

The Administrator may fix the hour of closing bets in the agencies. The closing hour for pool wagers on the premises of the race track shall not be later than the last closing time fixed for the agency. 1972

RACING ACT § 186-607. Location of agencies 

The operation of an agency located at a distance of less than 25 meters from any scholastic or religious institution shall not be permitted, nor shall the operation of an agency be permitted without previous authorization from the Planning Board. § 186-608. Minors; pinball machines and other machines

The presence of persons under the age of 18 years of age in the premises of racing track agencies shall not be permitted. Neither shall the devices or machines known as pinball machines be permitted in the premises, nor bingo, pool tables, etc. § 186-609. Charges for materials and use of equipment by agents 

The charges and amounts that the Association charges the agents for the materials and the use of the equipment for betting shall be filed in the office of the Administrator 30 days in advance of their effective date; Provided that the charges in effect at the time of the approval of this Division shall be filed within the 30 days subsequent to said approval. The Board may revise said charges and amounts at the request of the Administrator or of any party directly interested.

§ 186-610. Bond of agent 

The Association may require the horse racing agents to post a bond in a reasonable amount which shall be submitted to the approval of the Administrator. 

§ 186-611. Pool Definition 

A pool wager for the purposes of the act and of this Division is understood to be a system of betting consisting of selecting the greatest number of winning horses and the greatest number of winning horses minus one on a race day, and which appear in the single combination pool tickets and in multiple combination pool tickets duly received, stamped and registered by the Association.

Only the 6 races of each program designated by the Association as such shall be valid for betting on the pool. 

§ 186-612. - Value of combinations 

In playing the pool each combination shall be of a value of 25 cents. 1962 

Vol. 1, No. 8 

273

T.15 186 

Ch. 11

 § 186-613. 

Winning combinations; distribution of total amount 

The total amount of the pool corresponding to the winning combinations shall be distributed in the following manner: (1) Sixty percent to the combinations that determine the greatest number of winning horses, which shall be referred to as the first winners, and (2) Forty percent for the combinations determining the greatest number of winning horses minus 1, minus 2, minus 3, minus 4, minus 5, as the case may be, who shall be referred to as second winners. § 186-614. Combinations selecting greatest number of winners 

Whenever the combination or combinations selecting the greatest number of winners appears only on single combination tickets and no combination or combinations selecting the greatest number of winning horses minus one appears, forty percent of the pool shall be distributed amongst all of those combinations which have selected the greatest number of winning horses minus 2 or minus 3, or minus 

4 or minus 5 as the case may be. 

§ 186-615. First and second winners; distribution

Whenever in the distribution of the pool the second winners are entitled to less than twenty-five cents per winning combination, one hundred percent of the pool shall be totally distributed amongst the first winners. 

§ 186-616. - Second winners; rights 

The second winners shall be entitled to collect as many parts as the horses played by them in the race in which they failed to select the winner in addition to the multiplicity resulting from horses played in void races. § 186-617. Races not run

Whenever, after one or more races are run, the remaining races for any reason cannot be run on that race day, those races not held shall be considered void for the purposes of all bets. 

§ 186-618. Void races 

Whenever a race is declared void for the effects of the pool, all horses registered for that race shall be deemed winners and the bettor who shall have played more than one and has picked the

Bond in the amount bet

The Association shall be responsible for the total amount bet on the pool, daily double (dupleta), mutuels, and exacta each race day and that the share corresponding to winners is distributed in the manner provided in this division, for which purpose it shall put a bond in favor of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, the amount of which shall be fixed by the Administrator.

§ 186-620. Expiration of time for prizes

The right to collect prizes shall be barred after the expiration of 6 months from the day they were won, and any such unclaimed monies shall be immediately remitted by the Association to the Secretary of Finance with a copy of the settlement to the Administrator.

§ 186-621. Presumption of ownership 

The holder of a multiple combination ticket or a single combination ticket is presumed to be the owner thereof.

File No. 929 cited in 1964 amendment note under § 186-226 of this title. § 186-624. -Manual system for emergencies

The Board, the Administrator or the stewards may in an emergency or for just cause authorize a manual system for the operation and determination of the pool. § 186-625. Forms for multiple combination pool tickets

Forms for the multiple combination pool tickets shall consist of two cards exactly alike, bearing the same serial number, separated from each other by perforations and identified by the name of the race track; one card shall be marked "Bettor's Receipt" and the other "Official Form" and the word "Cuadro" (Multiple Combination Pool Ticket) shall appear on each card.

The cards shall be divided by perpendicular lines in spaces conforming to the order on the official program of each one of the races designated for wagering on the pool. Each space for each race shall contain 12 numbers corresponding, fully or partially, to the number of each horse on the official program. 

Selection of horses shall be by numbers, both cards being simultaneously punched in the space corresponding to the horse picked. 

After being punched the cards will be separated, and the "Bettor's Receipt" will be handed to the bettor. The card marked "Official Receipt" will be retained by the agent or the Association's employee, who will deliver it to the person authorized to receive it in the official premises of the pool at the time set for delivery, which in all cases must be before the time fixed for closing the pool. § 186-626. —Forms for single combination pool tickets

Single combination pool tickets shall comply with all the requirements provided for multiple combination pool tickets, except that they must be of a different color and only one combination can be played on them. If more than one combination is played on a single combination ticket, the ticket will be void. The word "Papeleta" (Single Combination Pool Ticket) must appear on the forms for single combination tickets. 1972

Any claim in connection with any multiple or single combination pool ticket respecting the numbers of the horses selected by him for each race valid for the pool must be made by the bettor when the "Bettor's Receipt" is handed to him. No consideration shall be given any claim made subsequently. 

§ 186-628. Information of agents on cards (a) Horse racing agents must account for all forms delivered to them. Any form on which a mistake was made or which is spoiled or mutilated in any manner shall be marked "void" on both cards and must be returned to the Association. (b) The Association shall keep a record of the serial number of all "void" forms and of unreturned forms and a copy of said record will be delivered to the stewards before running of the first race valid for the pool. 

§ 186-629. Check sheets 

After all forms played have been registered in the pool, the Association will prepare check sheets. These shall contain the serial number of each form registered, the number of the agency, the number of the horses selected by the bettor for each race, the total number of combinations played on each form and the total amount of multiple or single pool combination tickets registered. Check sheets will be in triplicate. The original will be delivered to the agents, who are obliged to place them on visible places in their agencies.

The duplicate will be delivered to the Chief Inspector of Bets before the start for the first race valid for the pool or at any time fixed by the Administrator, and said Chief Inspector of Bets will keep it in his possession until the day after the races are run when he will deliver it to the Administrator. The Association will retain the triplicate copy.

Amendments 1964. The check sheets shall contain the number of the agency instead of the name, address and number of the agent and also changes in phraseology were made by amendment File No. 929 cited in 1964 amendment note under § 186-226 of this title. 

§ 186-630. Steel case

§ 186-631. Multiple or single combination pool ticket unreturned

Any multiple or single combination pool ticket which appears to be unreturned according to the check sheet shall not be deemed valid for determining the pool, nor can it share in the distribution of the pool. Whenever there is any discrepancy between the "Official Form" and the "Bettor's Receipt", the information in the check sheet will govern for all purposes of the determination of the pool and the participation in the distribution of the pool. 

§ 186-632. Delivery and registry of tickets for validity

No multiple or single combination ticket will be valid, nor will it confer any action or rights whatsoever against the Association until and unless the same be delivered and registered in the pool; 

Provided, nevertheless, That the Association shall be liable for the amount of the prize the said multiple or single combination ticket may be entitled to, unless the Association shall have notified the stewards before the running of the first race valid for the pool with a record of the "void" forms and the forms unreturned by the agents. § 186-633. - Sales price of multiple combination pool ticket

The sales price of a multiple combination pool ticket to the public shall not be in excess of 10 cents each; Provided, That any tax imposed by law shall be added thereto.

The Association will see to it that on race days only officials of the Administration of the Horse Racing Sport and the employees of the Association in charge of these operations of the pool, and mechanics and technicians in charge of the maintenance and repair of the electronic equipment enter the premises where the pool operates. 

 § 186-638. 

Information during determination of pool No information shall be given out respecting determination of the pool until it has terminated and been declared official. § 186-639. 

Announcement of total amount The Association shall announce to the public the total amount of the pool before the first race valid for the same. The stewards may excuse the Association from this requirement. § 186-640. Distribution of gross total

The gross total of the pool shall consist of the bets made in the agencies and at the race track after deducting the agents' commissions. The Association will deduct 30 percent of the gross total of the pool retaining 95 percent of the amount deducted for itself and shall remit 5 percent to the Secretary of Finance with a copy of the settlement to the Administrator. § 186-641. 

Suspension of payment of tickets in controversy

In the event of any controversy between the inspectors of bets and employees of the Association respecting the payment or allotment of a prize to a multiple or single combination ticket, the Association shall immediately notify the Administrator in writing. 

The Administrator shall investigate the case, hearing the parties. 

Until the Administrator shall have rendered his award, payment of the part of the pool in dispute, will be suspended. 1972
