Responsibility for determinations without objection Whenever officials of the Administration make a determination of the pool without any objection thereto being made and in the absence of the procedure for settlement of the controversy by the Administrator, the Association shall be deemed to have assumed the full responsibility for the determination. § 186-643. —Stewards; official declaration of winners

For purposes of betting on the pool, mutuels, daily double (dupleta), and exacta the winning horses shall be those declared "official" winners by the Stewards independently and without any consideration of the fact that said horse may subsequently be penalized or even deprived of the prize for one or more violations of this division. § 186-644.

Bettor, wagering, registration sheet, official program, and this division

A bettor in wagering on the basis of the registration sheet or the official program does so subject to the provisions of this division and agreeing that the same may be the subject to changes or alterations and it is understood that he assumes said risks in placing his bet. § 186-645. -Dead heat for first place

In the case of a dead heat of two or more horses for first, each of the horses that dead heats shall be deemed winner for the purposes of the bets; Provided, That a multiple combination ticket including all or some of the horses that dead heat will collect as many parts as the horses it played in the dead heat race.

§ 186-648. Mutuels-Bets when 5 or more horses run

The Association shall be obliged to accept bets for first and second mutuels on all of the horses in all of the races in which 5 or more horses run.

Each ticket shall bear the number of the horse bet on, as it appears in the official program. These tickets, after issuance, cannot be returned.

RACING ACT § 186-651. -Winning tickets 

Winning mutuel tickets shall be paid on their presentation and delivery at the windows designated for that purpose. 

 § 186-652. Minimum mutuel

The minimum mutuel bet shall be $2 and the Association shall be under the obligation to pay in every case a minimum profit of 5 cents on each dollar bet. In those cases in which these provisions result in a loss, the loss shall be for the account of the Association operating the race track and the government will receive its corresponding share in full, including any residue. 

Cross references. Specific penalty for violation of this section, see § 186-1401 of this title. § 186-653. Tickets, opportunity for claim 

Every claim respecting a ticket mistakenly delivered to a bettor must be made before the bettor leaves the window where the bet was placed. No claim made subsequently will be considered, nor any claim for lost or destroyed tickets or tickets mutilated in such a way as to be unidentifiable. 

S 186-654. -Minors

No person under the age of 21 years may place bets at the mutuel windows. § 186-655. Hours for sale and payment 

Mutuel ticket sellers will open sales not less than 30 minutes prior to the hour set for the running of the first race. The paymasters will open their windows as quickly as possible after the official result of each race is known. 1972

§ 186-656. 

Locking of machines by electrical control

All mutuel machines shall be locked by electrical control at the time fixed for the start of each race by the stewards. 

Uncompleted sales

The Association shall not be liable for the sale of tickets that cannot be completed before the locking of the mutuel machines. § 186-658. Closing of pay-off windows 

The pay-off windows shall remain open for a period of 30 minutes after the last race has been declared official. 

§ 186-659. —System additional to totalizator

On such race days on which, in addition to the totalizator, any other additional system is used for making the calculations, that fact must be reported to the Administrator in detail. § 186-660. Return of bets - Retirement of horse; effect on pool

Whenever a horse is retired after the betting has started, all money bet on that horse shall be deducted from the total amount bet and returned to the bettors. The race shall be void for the purposes of the pool. § 186-661. Withdrawal of horse of an entry; effect on pool

Whenever one of the horses forming part of an entry is withdrawn after the betting has started the entry shall be eliminated from the betting and the money bet on the same shall be deducted from the total amount bet and returned to the bettors on the entry. 

The race shall be void for the purposes of the pool. 

Cross references. Daily double, withdrawal of horses or prevention from running, see § 186-712 of this title. § 186-662. Withdrawal of one of two horses from one field; effect on pool 

When the field is constituted by only two horses and one of them is withdrawn after the betting has started the field shall be eliminated from the bets and all the money bet on the field shall be deducted from the total amount bet and returned to the bettors on the field. The race shall be void for the purposes of the pool. 

Cross references. Daily double, withdrawal of horses or prevention from running, see § 186-712 of this title. 1962 

Vol. 1, No. 8 283

T.§ 186-663 

Ch. 11

§ 186-663. 

Retirement of two or more horses from one field; effect on pool

When the field is constituted by more than two horses, if one of the horses constituting the field is withdrawn after the betting has commenced, no return shall be made to the bettors on the field, provided, nevertheless, that the money shall be returned if two or more horses of that particular field are withdrawn. The race shall be void for the purposes of the pool. 

Cross references. Daily double, withdrawal of horses or prevention from running, see § 186-712 of this title. 

§ 186-664. Defect of starting gate

If the starter decides that a horse has been prevented from running because the door of the cage he occupied in the starting gate failed to open, the money bet on that horse shall be returned. If this occurs to a horse forming part of an entry or part of a field of two horses, or to two or more horses of a field of more than two horses the money bet on the entry or the field, as the case may be, shall be deducted from the total amount bet and returned to the corresponding bettor. The race shall be void for purposes of the pool. 

Cross references. Daily double, withdrawal of horses or prevention from running, see § 186-712 of this title. 

§ 186-665. Mutuel - Presumption of ownership 

The holder of a mutuel ticket is presumed to be its owner. 

Cross references. Presumption of ownership of daily double ticket, see § 186-725 of this title. 

Presumption of ownership of pool ticket, see § 186-621 of this title. 

§ 186-666. 

Expiration of winning tickets

The right to collect on a winning mutuel ticket expires after 6 months counted from the day on which it won and the unclaimed monies on the same shall immediately be remitted to the Secretary of Finance with a copy of the settlement for the Administrator. 

Cross references. Daily double, expiration of time for dividend, see § 186-724 of this title.

Pool, expiration of time for prizes, see § 186-620 of this title. § 186-667. Announcing of pay-offs on board 

The Association must announce on the Board not less than four times in each race the estimated pay-offs on each horse in the betting. 1962 

Vol. 1, No. 8 284

RACING ACT 

§ 186-668. Delivery of document containing pay-offs 

At the end of each race the Association must deliver immediately to a person designated by the Administrator, a document containing the approximate pay-offs announced to the public together with the amounts wagered on each horse at the time the announcement was made and also the final pay-offs. 

§ 186-669. Mutuel Amount of pay-offs 

The mutuel pay-offs announced to the public shall comprise the winnings plus the $2 bet. 

§ 186-670. Responsibility for accuracy of pay-offs 

The Association shall be responsible for the accuracy of the payoffs announced to the public. The Mutuel Administrator shall cause each calculation sheet to be verified before announcing the pay-off on any given race. Said verification will include the pay-off, the residue, the commission for the Association and the taxes, which added up must give a total equal to the total lost. All pay-off sheets must be verified with the calculation sheet with respect to the winners and pay-offs before being delivered to the paymasters. All pay-offs that are to appear on the Board showing the results must be verified a second time before being given to the public. 

§ 186-671. Closing of sale of tickets

No ticket will be sold after the totalizator is locked or the betting terminates. The stewards shall fix the time of closing mutuel bets. 

§ 186-672. Deficiency of this Division 

Whenever an emergency arises in connection with the operation of the mutuel system and the emergency is not covered by this Division and an immediate decision is required the same shall be decided by the Administrator of the mutuels together with the Inspector of Betting present, who will render a detailed report to the Administrator. 

§ 186-673. Notification of horses to run

Before the wagers begin on each race the stewards will notify the mutuels administrator of the horses to run in the race. 1962 

Vol. 1, No. 8 285

T.§ 186-674 

Ch. 11

Failure of mutuel machines 

If for any reason the mutuel machines lock or fail to operate before the time set for starting a race, the same shall remain locked until after the race and the betting on that race will cease and the pay-off will be calculated according to the sums bet, unless the machines can be restored to operation before starting time. 

§ 186-675. Payment of tickets; official result

No payments shall be made by the mutuels until the order of finishing has been declared official by the stewards. § 186-676. Calculation of payments when mechanical failure 

occurs

Whenever because of mechanical failure the totals of the wagers do not agree with the tote board, pay-offs shall be calculated by the sums wagered as shown by the recapitulation of the sales of each of the mutuel machines. This will be authorized and verified by the Betting Inspectors. 

§ 186-677. Correction of errors in payments

In case an error is made in announcing the pay-offs to the public on the board, the error will be corrected quickly and only the correct pay-off will be made without taking the error into consideration. If because of some mechanical failure it is impossible to correct the error on the board, the correction will be announced to the public by the public address system. § 186-678. When money wagered is returned 

If none of the horses in a race finishes the race, the money wagered shall be returned to the bettors. § 186-679. Races called off

Whenever a race is called off by the stewards, the money bet on that race shall be returned to the bettors. § 186-680. When no money bet on winner

If a horse wins and there is no money wagered on him to win, all the money wagered in that race to win shall be apportioned among the holders of the place tickets on that horse. § 186-681. When no money bet on first or second winner

If no money has been wagered to place on a horse which is placed first or second in a race, all the money wagered to place for 1962 

Vol. 1, No. 8 

286

Ch. 11

RACING ACT 

T.15 § 186-687 that race shall be apportioned among the holders of tickets on the other horse which was placed first or second. § 186-682. Place tickets; when one horse finishes

If only one horse finishes in a race, the money wagered to place for that race shall be apportioned among the holders of place tickets on that horse. § 186-683. Mutuel, daily double, pool and "exacta"; separate calculations

In every race the mutuel wagers to win and to place, the daily double (dupleta) wagers, pool wagers, and exacta wagers shall be handled separately and the calculations on the same shall be made independently from each other.

Amendments-1971. Exacta betting was added by amendment File No. 1465, cited in 1971 amendment note under 

§ 186-1 of this title. 

§ 186-684. Fractions of cent in payments

In the paying of the pool, mutuels, daily double (dupleta), and exacta 1, 2, 3, and 4 cents or fractions of a cent shall not be included. These cents and fractions shall be retained by the Association and remitted weekly to the Administrator by check to order of the Secretary of Finance. 

Amendments-1971. Exacta betting was added by amendment File No. 1465, cited in 1971 amendment note under 

§ 186-1 of this title. 

§ 186-685. Tickets of doubtful validity or mutilated tickets

Mutilated mutuel tickets, or tickets of doubtful validity, shall be submitted to an official of the Association designated for the purpose of deciding each claim. § 186-686. Approved tickets

Only tickets approved by the Administrator may be used for mutuel wagers. 

§ 186-687. Deduction and excise-Win mutuel 

Of the total amount wagered in the win mutuel the money bet on the winning horse shall be deducted; the 25 percent authorized by the act for the Association shall be deducted from the remainder; the 10 percent fixed by the act as excise will be deducted from the 1972 

Vol. 11, No. 3 287

T.15 186 

Ch. 11 balance. The remainder shall be the net amount to be distributed and it shall be divided by the amount bet on the winner. 

§ 186-688. Place mutuel 

From the total wagered in the place mutuel the amount bet on horses placing first and second shall be deducted; the 25 percent authorized by the act for the Association shall be deducted from the balance; from the remaining balance the 10 percent excise provided by the act shall be deducted. The remainder shall be the net amount to be distributed, which will be divided into two halves and each half shall be divided by the amount bet on the horses that placed first and second. § 186-689. Dead heat-To win

In case two or more horses are in dead heat to win, the money wagered to win shall be distributed in the same way as a place wager. § 186-690. For second

In the case of a dead heat for second, one half of the net amount to be distributed shall be applied to the tickets on the winner and the other half shall be applied equally among the amounts bet on each of the horses that were in a dead heat for second.

§ 186-691. Places for mutuel wagers 

Mutuel wagers can only be made at the places designated for that purpose within the premises of the race track.

§ 186-701. Place for wagers 

Daily double wagers can only be placed at the agencies and at the place designated for that purpose at the race track. § 186-702. Number of daily doubles per day

The Board shall determine by Resolution the number of daily doubles that may be held on a given race day.

The Association shall designate which races constitute the daily double. 

Amendments 1964. This section was amended generally by amendment File No. 929 cited in 1964 amendment note under § 186-226 of this title. 

§ 186-703. Closing of wagers 

The stewards will designate a time for closing daily double wagers which time must be not less than 5 minutes prior to the start of the first of the races which constitute said wager. The total of the daily double must be announced to the public by the Association before the start of the two races constituting the daily double. § 186-704. System of wagering

The daily double system of wagering will operate in the same manner as the single combination pool wagers, that is, that only one combination can be made on a single ticket on which the horses selected by the bettor will be designated by the number they have on the official program. 

§ 186-705. Tickets 

Only tickets approved by the Administrator may be used for wagering on the daily double.

 § 186-706. Value of combinations

The value of each combination on the daily double wager shall be $2. § 186-707. Maximum price for bettors

The price to the bettor for each daily double form shall not exceed 10 cents when obtained from a race track agent.

The price the Association may charge an agent for each form for daily double wagers shall be determined by the Administrator. 

§ 186-709. Forms with serial numbers 

The forms used to receive daily double wagers through the pool agents will bear printed serial numbers. Pool agents will have to account for all forms delivered to them and shall return all void forms to the Association. The Association shall deliver to the 

Inspector of Betting present, before the time set for starting the first race designated for the daily double, a list containing the serial number of all returned and void forms. § 186-710. Who may distribute forms

Only the Association may print and distribute forms for daily double wagers. 

§ 186-711. Deficiencies of this Division 

Whenever an emergency arises in connection with the operation of the daily double that is not covered by this Division and the same needs an immediate decision, it shall be decided jointly by the director of mutuels and the betting inspector present, and they will render a complete report to the Administrator with a copy to the Association. § 186-712. Withdrawal of horses; or prevention from starting

If a horse is withdrawn before the start of the first race of the daily double or if in said race the starter decides that a horse was prevented from starting because of a locked starting gate, there will be deducted from the total of the daily double the amount of the tickets which included said horse and the bettors on said horse will be reimbursed; Provided, That if the horse withdrawn or prevented from running forms one of an entry or field the provisions of secs. 186-661, 186-662, 186-663 and 186-664 of this title will apply. § 186-713. Net amount to be distributed Winner of first or second race 

If no ticket including the winners of both races of the daily double have been sold, the net amount to be distributed shall be distributed in equal shares among the holders of tickets including 

Sept. 30, 1964 290 

Vol. 3, No. 7

Ch. 11

RACING ACT 

T.15 § 186-718 the horse that placed first in the first race or first in the second race of the daily double. § 186-714. - Placing second

If no daily double ticket containing the horse that placed first in either one of the two races of the daily double has been sold, the net amount to be distributed shall be paid to the holders of tickets containing the horses that placed second in the two daily double races. § 186-715. Dead heat in first or second races

In cases of a dead heat in the first or second races of the daily double the winning tickets shall be those having as many combinations as horses in dead heat. The amounts bet on the winning combinations shall be deducted from the net amount to be distributed and the balance shall be divided by the number of winning combinations and each portion resulting from this operation will be distributed among the holders of tickets including the corresponding winning combination. 

§ 186-716. Dead heat in both races 

In case of dead heat in both races of the daily double the winners shall be as many combinations as result from a multiplication of the number of horses that are in dead heat in the first and second races. 

The amounts bet on the winning combinations shall be deducted from the net amount to be distributed and the balance will be divided by the number of winning combinations and each portion resulting from this operation will be distributed among the holders of the tickets including the corresponding winning combination. 

§ 186-717. Refund of amount wagered

If no ticket is sold that would require distribution, the Association shall make a full refund of the complete amount wagered to the bettors. § 186-718. If first race called off

If for any reason the first race of the daily double is not run or the Stewards void it for all bets, the net amount to be distributed shall be distributed among the tickets having the winner of the second race of the daily double.

If for any reason the second race of the daily double is not run or the stewards void it for all bets, the net amount to be distributed shall be distributed among the tickets having the winner of the first race of the daily double.

§ 186-720. If both races called off 

If for any reason the two races constituting the daily double are not run or the stewards void them for all bets, the Association shall return the total amount wagered to the bettors. § 186-721. Withdrawal of horse in second half

In the event a horse is withdrawn in the second half of the daily double after the first race has been run, or if the starter determines that the horse was prevented from running by failure of the starting gate to open, all the money wagered in combinations including said horse shall be deducted from the total amount wagered on the daily double, and all those daily double tickets including that horse in combination with the horse winning the first race of the daily double will share in a consolation prize which will be formed by deducting from the total amount wagered on the daily double the total of all the combinations including said horse. 

§ 186-722. Computation of dividend 

The pay-off on the daily double shall be computed and paid as follows: The total amount of the daily double shall consist of the bets made at the agencies and at the race track after deducting the agent's commission. From the gross total wagered the deductions fixed by law shall be made; the excise taxes imposed by law shall be deducted from the balance; the remaining balance shall be divided among the winning tickets to determine the pay-off for each ticket.

§ 186-751. Place for "exacta" wagers

Exacta wagers can only be placed at the agencies and at the places designated for that purpose at the race track. 

Amendments-1971. This subdivision was added by Resolu tion of the Racing Board July 1, 1971, File No. 1465, cited in 1971 amendment note under § 186-1 of this title. 

§ 186-752. Number of "exacta" wagering per day

The Board shall determine by Resolution the number of races on which exacta wagering shall be conducted on a given race day. § 186-753. Designation of races with "exacta" wagering

The Association shall designate the races on which exacta wagering shall be conducted and such races shall be clearly indicated on the Official Program. 

§ 186-754. Closing of wagers 

The stewards shall designate the time for closing exacta wagers at the track which time must not be less than 5 minutes prior to the start of the exacta race. § 186-755. "Exacta" pool announced daily

The exacta pool on any particular race must be announced to the public present at the track by the Association before the start of the exacta race. The Chief Inspector of Betting may excuse the Association from this requirement. 1972

RACING ACT § 186-756. System of wagering 

Horses selected by the bettor in exacta races will be designated on exacta tickets by numbers corresponding to the numbers assigned to said horses in the Official Program. 

§ 186-757. Selection of order of horses 

The numbers of only 2 horses may be selected on each exacta ticket, that is, the number of the horse the bettor has selected to finish first followed by the number of the horse selected by the bettor to finish second. § 186-758. "Exacta" tickets 

Only tickets approved by the Administrator may be used for exacta wagering. Said tickets should be easily distinguishable from tickets used for other types of wagers. § 186-759. Price of tickets

The price to the bettor for each combination of 2 numbers on an exacta ticket shall be $2, exclusive of the cost of the ticket when purchased at a horse racing agency. § 186-760. 

Maximum price for bettor 

The price to the bettor for each exacta ticket shall be 10 cents when obtained from a horse racing agency. § 186-761. Price for agents 

The price the Association may charge the horse racing agents for each exacta ticket sold by said agents shall be 8 cents. 

§ 186-762. -Printing and distribution 

Only the Association may print and distribute exacta tickets to the horse racing agents. 

§ 186-763. -Sale 

Horse racing agents shall not sell any exacta tickets except those printed and distributed by the Association. $ 186-764. -Mutilated or doubtful 

Mutilated exacta tickets, or tickets of doubtful validity shall be submitted to an official of the Association designated for the purpose of deciding such claims. 1972 

Vol. 11, No. 3 292.3

Ch. 11

 § 186-765.-Cards 

Exacta tickets issued by the Association to the horse racing agents shall consist of 2 serially numbered cards joined together by perforations and imprinted with the name of the race track. 

The cards shall be identical except that one shall be imprinted "Bettor's Exacta Ticket" and the other "Official Exacta Form".

The cards shall contain 2 vertical columns. They shall each contain 10 spaces numbered from 1 to 10 from the top down to correspond with the numbers assigned to the horses in exacta races on the Official Program. 

The first column shall be used to designate the number of the horse selected by the bettor to finish first and the second column shall be used to designate the number of the horse selected by the bettor to finish second. 

Designation of horse selections on exacta tickets shall be by punches in the areas of the numbers corresponding to the numbers assigned to the horses in exacta races on the Official Program and both cards shall be punched simultaneously in the appropriate spaces.

After being punched the cards shall be separated and the bettor's exacta ticket shall be handed to the bettor by the agent. 

The card imprinted Official Exacta Form shall be retained by the agent who shall deliver it to the person designated by the Association to receive it at the race track at the time set for delivery which in all cases must be at or before the time fixed by the Association. 

§ 186-766. Ticket records 

After the Official Exacta Form portion of all exacta tickets sold at the agencies have been delivered to the race track the Association shall prepare a check list in triplicate for each agency. Said list shall contain the date, the serial number of each exacta ticket sold, the number of the agency, the number of the exacta race, the numbers representing the 2 horses selected by the bettor on each ticket and the total number of tickets sold by the agency. The original shall be delivered to the agent who shall be required to post it in a prominent place in his agency. 

The duplicate shall be delivered to the Chief Inspector of Betting before the start of the exacta race or at any other time set by the Administrator. The Chief Inspector of Betting shall keep it in his possession until the day after the race is run when he will deliver 1972 

Vol. 11, No. 3 292.4

Ch. 11

RACING ACT 

T.15 § 186-769 it to the Administrator. The Association will retain the triplicate.

The Association shall also prepare 2 summary lists. The first shall be prepared in duplicate and shall contain the date, the number of the exacta race, the numbers of the agencies at which exacta tickets were sold for that race, the number of tickets sold by each and the total number sold by all agencies. The original shall be delivered to the Chief Inspector of Betting before the start of the exacta race and the duplicate shall be retained by the Association. 

The second summary list shall show the number of tickets sold on each of the various combinations of horses selected, for example, 1 and 2, 1 and 3, etc. This list shall be prepared in triplicate. The original shall be delivered to the Director of Mutuels to facilitate the consolidation of the tickets sold by the agencies with those sold at the race track. The duplicate shall be delivered to the Chief 

Inspector of Betting and the triplicate shall be retained by the Association. 

§ 186-767. -Voided 

Horse racing agents must account for all exacta tickets issued to them by the Association. Any ticket on which a mistake is made or which is spoiled or mutilated in any manner shall be marked "void" on both parts and same must be returned to the Association.

The Association shall keep a record of all void and of all unreturned tickets and a copy of said record shall be delivered to the 

Chief Inspector of Betting before the start of an exacta race. 

§ 186-768. 

Discrepancy

Any exacta ticket not appearing as having been sold on the checklist required by sec. 186-766 above shall not be deemed valid for determining the exacta pool, nor can it share in the distribution of the net exacta pool. Whenever there is any discrepancy between the Official Exacta Form and the bettor's exacta ticket, the information in the checklist shall govern for all purposes. § 186-769. Validity

No exacta ticket sold by an agent shall be valid nor will it confer any rights or rights of action whatsoever against the Association until and unless it is delivered to the race track and listed on the checklist; Provided, nevertheless, That the Association shall be liable for the amount of the prize the said exacta (quiniela) ticket 1972

For the purposes of exacta wagers the "field" shall be the same as the "field" for mutuel wagers. § 186-771. Wager on two horses

Whenever 2 horses are grouped as an entry an exacta wager on either of the 2 shall be deemed a wager on both. § 186-772. Suspension of payment

In the event of a controversy between the Chief Inspector of Betting and employees of the Association regarding the payment or allotment of a prize to an exacta ticket, the Association shall immediately notify the Administrator in writing. The Administrator shall investigate the case, hearing the parties. Until the 

Administrator shall have rendered his decision, payment of the part of the net exacta pool in dispute shall be suspended. § 186-773. Settlement of controversy 

Whenever officials of the Administration make a determination regarding the exacta in the absence of a procedure for settlement of the controversy by the Administrator, the Association shall be deemed to have assumed the full responsibility for the determination, provided the Association was notified of said determination and did not object to same. § 186-774. Questions not covered by this division 

Whenever an emergency arises in connection with the operation of the exacta that is not covered by this division and the same needs an immediate decision, it shall be decided by the Director of Mutuels and the Chief Inspector of Betting present and they will render a complete report to the Administrator with a copy to the Association. If the Director of Mutuels and the Chief 

Inspector of Betting cannot agree on a decision the matter shall be referred to the stewards for resolution. § 186-775. Withdrawal of horses; or prevention from starting

§ 186-776. Net amount to be distributed-First place winner 

If no ticket combines the numbers of the winner and the secondplace horse in order in an exacta race the net exacta pool shall be distributed to holders of tickets designating the winner to win. 

If no ticket has been sold designating the winner to win, the net exacta pool shall be distributed to the holders of tickets designating the second-place horse to finish either first or second. 

§ 186-778. Official winner 

If only one horse finishes in an exacta race and is declared 'the "official" winner by the stewards, the net exacta pool shall be distributed to holders of tickets designating the winner to win. 

§ 186-779. Dead heat-First place 

In the event of a dead heat for win in an exacta race the net exacta pool shall be distributed equally among tickets combining the numbers of the horses involved in the dead heat, in either order. 

§ 186-780.-Second place 

In the event of a dead heat for second in an exacta race the net exacta pool shall be distributed equally among tickets combining the number of the winner with the number of any of the horses involved in the dead heat for second. § 186-781. Refund of amount wagered

If no horses finish in an exacta race or if no exacta ticket is sold that would require a distribution of the net exacta pool, the Association shall make a full refund of the total amount wagered to the bettors. § 186-782. Called off or voided "exacta” race

If for any reason an exacta race is not run or is voided for all bets by the stewards, the Association shall make a full refund of the total amount wagered to the bettors. 1972

§ 186-783. Computation of dividend 

The payoff on the exacta shall be computed and paid as follows: 

The total amount of the exacta pool shall consist of the bets made at the agencies and at the race track after deducting the agents' commission. From the total amount of the exacta pool the deductions fixed by law shall be made; the excise taxes imposed by law shall be deducted from the balance; the remaining balance shall be divided among the winning tickets to determine the payoff for each ticket. 

§ 186-784. Announcing the dividend 

The exacta payoff shall be announced to the public present at the race track as soon as possible following the finish of the exacta race. 

§ 186-785.-Claims 

If any mistake is made by an agent in punching an exacta ticket the bettor shall be given a new ticket free of charge. Any claim in connection with the designation of the horses selected on any exacta ticket purchased at an agency must be made by the bettor when the bettor's exacta ticket is handed to him. No consideration shall be given any claim made subsequently and the bettor shall be required to pay for a new ticket in order to correct an error. § 186-786. When Official "Exacta" Form is punched too many times

If more than one punch appears in any one or more columns on an Official Exacta Form the same shall be considered void and the holder of the corresponding bettor's exacta ticket shall be entitled to a refund of the amount of his wager upon presentation of said ticket. § 186-787. 

When not punched

If no punch appears in any one column on an Official Exacta Form the same shall be considered void and the holder of the corresponding bettor's exacta ticket shall be entitled to a refund of the amount of his wager upon presentation of said ticket. § 186-788. Expiration of right to cash dividend

Conflict of interests on claim cases § 186-801. Rules and conditions

The Board will prescribe the rules and conditions under which horse races are to be held on the race tracks of Puerto Rico. § 186-802. Dates and places

The Board shall determine the days and places for the holding of races and may change the place and date set for them. § 186-803. Examination of registered horses

The veterinary, prior to the time for withdrawing horses, must examine all horses registered for the competition in the races to be held the next day and he shall certify to the secretary of races the physical condition of each horse; Provided that in case in his opinion any horse is unsound to race he must notify the secretary of races who will excuse the horse. 

§ 186-804. Jurisdiction of Administrator 

After the time for withdrawals and changes the horses that are still registered will be under the jurisdiction of the Administrator; 

Provided, That the above does not relieve its owners, trainers, grooms and groom helpers of the obligations and responsibilities imposed upon them by this Division. 1962

T.15 § 186-811 § 186-805. Withdrawal for physical unsoundness;

diagnosis of veterinary If after the time for withdrawals it becomes necessary to withdraw a horse for physical unsoundness, the owner will inform the Administrator, veterinary or the secretary of races of this fact. The official veterinary will immediately be ordered to examine the horse and certify whether said horse is or is not in condition to compete in the race; Provided, That the opinion of the veterinary shall be final; Provided, furthermore, That if the withdrawal of the horse is ordered, the race shall be void for the pool. The Administrator, veterinary or the secretary of races must notify the withdrawal to the stewards and to the Association so that the latter may immediately announce it to the public.

 § 186-806. Jockeys, hour of arrival

The Administrator will determine the hour when the jockeys who are to take part in the races must be present in the jockey room. 

§ 186-807. Shoes 

Every horse shall enter competition with shoes on its four feet, unless the steward authorizes some other condition. 

Cross references. Specific penalty for violation of this section, see § 186-1401 of this title. § 186-808. Assembling of stewards

The stewards must assemble at least one-half hour before the start of the first race. 

§ 186-809. Paddock Time 

The paddock judge will give notice of the time when the horses must be brought to the paddock. § 186-810. Conduct and discipline

The paddock shall be under the charge and supervision of the paddock judge, who shall be responsible for the conduct and discipline in that area. 

§ 186-811. Place of inspection 

The veterinary shall inspect the horses in the paddock and it is his duty to notify the steward if all of the horses are in condition. for competition.

§ 186-812. Identification of horses

The paddock judge and the veterinary will identify the horses that are to take part in each race and give the stewards notice of this. 

§ 186-813.

Persons authorized to enter Only the trainers, grooms and groom helpers attendant upon the horse may enter the paddock. Each horse shall be attended by three persons. 

§ 186-814. 

Persons who may attend horses

The horses may only be touched and attended by the three persons who conduct them to the paddock and by the officials of the Administration. § 186-815. Who will announce schedule

The stewards will notify the paddock judge of the post time and the starting time. § 186-816. When horses shall be saddled

The horses shall be saddled when ordered by the paddock judge. 

 § 186-817. Paddock Warming up in such area

The horses by authorization of the paddock judge may be warmed up in the paddock area. 

Cross references. Specific penalty for violation of this section, see § 186-1401 of this title. 

§ 186-818. Authorization of jockeys to enter 

The paddock judge shall order the entrance of the jockeys to the paddock. 

§ 186-819. Inspection of equipment 

The paddock judge shall inspect the equipment of each horse and shall see that it is in conformity with the equipment announced in the official program. § 186-820. Information of paddock judge 

The paddock judge shall inform the stewards when all of the horses are ready for the race. 1962

RACING ACT 

§ 186-821. Leaving paddock

The paddock judge when ordered by the stewards, shall order the jockeys to mount their horses and to leave the paddock in an ascending numerical order. § 186-822. Parade

When the horses arrive at the track they shall parade or move in any other manner determined by the steward. The parade shall be presided over and closed by ushers. The jockeys shall salute the stewards when passing in front of their room. They will repeat this salute upon returning to the weighing scales. The jockeys during this parade shall not communicate with the public in any form whatsoever.

 § 186-823. Starting line

After the parade the jockeys will take their horses to the starting line where they will remain under the jurisdiction of the starter. 

§ 186-824. Use of pony 

Owners of horses requiring the services of a pony to lead their horses to the starting line must request the corresponding permission from the stewards. § 186-825. Search of jockeys, ushers and hostlers 

The starter or the stewards may order a search of the jockeys, ushers and hostlers as well as the horses and equipment. § 186-826. Uniform start

The starter shall take all necessary measures to ensure a uniform start. He will see to it that the rules referring to start are obeyed. § 186-827. Notification of closing of mutuel

The stewards shall notify the starter the post time for each race. Amendments 1964. This section was amended generally by amendment File No. 929 cited in 1964 amendment note under § 186-226 of this title. 

§ 186-828. Leave to dismount

No jockey may dismount from his horse without leave from the starter.

Cross references. Specific penalty for violation of this section, see § 186-1401 of this title. 

Sept. 30, 1964 

Vol. 3, No. 7 297

T.§ 186-829 

Ch. 11

§ 186-829. Accident at starting line; effects

If a horse suffers an accident at the starting line or before arriving at it, the starter or the steward shall order the veterinary to examine the horse and that official will determine whether the horse can or cannot compete in the race. If the veterinary determines that the horse is not in condition to compete in the race, the race shall be void for the pool. The stewards will notify the Association and the latter will in turn announce to the public the name of the horse scratched and the money wagered in the mutuels on the scratched horse will be returned to the bettors; Provided that if it be the case of the withdrawal of a horse competing in a field or entry or which is part of a daily double the rules provided herein for those cases shall be applied. 

§ 186-830. How races shall start 

The races shall start from a starting gate; Provided that in the event the starting gate fails to operate the stewards may authorize the start by any other means. 

§ 186-831. Period of start 

Except in the case of classic races the starter shall have 10 minutes to start the race after post time, which shall be signaled by hoisting a flag. 

Amendments 1964. The words "Except in the case of classic races" were added at the beginning of this section and the words "raising of flag" were changed to "hoisting a flag", by amendment File No. 929 cited in 1964 amendment note under § 186-226 of this title. 

§ 186-832. Withdrawal of horses causing delays

At the flag signal the stewards shall commence to count the time and upon the expiration of 10 minutes will advise the starter, who shall withdraw the horse causing the delay. The race shall be declared void for the pool. The stewards will announce the name and number of the withdrawn horse to the public and the Association. 

In connection with the wagers on the scratched horse procedure will be in conformity with the provisions of this Division. § 186-833. Starting positions

The starter shall place the horses in their corresponding cages according to their starting position in the official program.

§ 186-834. Bad manners 

Suspensions

Any horse three or more years old which because of its unruliness is withdrawn by the starter at the post, or which when the order to start is given remains within the starting gate, or which upon breaking turns or interferes with any other horse without any fault of its jockey may be suspended by the stewards for a period of 15 natural days. If said horse incurs in the same fault 

3 times within a period of 12 months it shall be declared unfit to race in the race tracks of Puerto Rico, and shall be striken from the corresponding register. 

Amendments 

1964. This section was amended generally by amendment File No. 929 cited in 1964 amendment note under § 186-226 of this title. 

§ 186-835. Proof of correction of such fault

Any two year old horse which because of its unruliness is withdrawn by the starter at the post, or which when the order to start is given remains within the starting gate, or which upon breaking turns or interferes with any other horse without any fault of its jockey may be suspended by the stewards for a period of 10 natural days, to attend in said period the training school and upon the expiration of said suspension, it must be brought before the starter, to show, with the corresponding rehearsal that it is no longer unruly, and if that be the case the starter shall authorize it to take part in competition again. 

Amendments 1964. This section was amended generally by amendment File No. 929 cited in 1964 amendment note under § 186-226 of this title. 

§ 186-836. Effect of start 

Once the race has started all of the horses who were present at the starting line shall be deemed to have taken part in the race. 

§ 186-837. Voiding of start 

After the race has been started by the starter it cannot be voided. 

186-838. Defects of starting gate

In the event that, because of improper operation of the starting gate a uniform start is not accomplished, the starter shall immediately notify the stewards and he shall cause the signal flag to be waved continually indicating said fact. The stewards shall void the race for all wagers and the same shall be considered as not having been run.

§ 186-839. Method of conducting; use of whip

After the race has started the jockeys will conduct their horses in a straight line and without using the whip during the first 100 meters of the race. Any horse that is ridden in violation of this provision may be disqualified and its jockey punished by the stewards.

Whip, see § 186-841 of this title. § 186-840. Prohibitions in course of race

No jockey shall in the course of the race cross his horse in the line of another horse without being at least two lengths ahead of the same. Neither may he push, squeeze or in any way touch another jockey or horse. Any horse ridden in violation of this provision may be disqualified and his jockey punished by the stewards. 

Cross references. Behavior during the running of races, see 

SS 186-839, 186-841 and 186-842 of this title.

Specific penalty for violation of this section, see § 186-1401 of this title. § 186-841. Whip, its use, size and weight

Each jockey shall whip his horse in such a manner that his whip does not touch or frighten any other jockey or horse. The jockey's whip shall not be longer than 30 inches nor shall it weigh more than one and one-half pounds.

Each jockey must maintain his horse in the respective line in which he initiates his entrance into the straightaway leading to the finish, unless he has a horse in the same line, in which case if he is going to pass him, he must do so taking care not to invade the

 § 186-844. Authorization for dismounting after finishing race

All jockeys after finishing a race shall return to a position in front of the stewards and shall not dismount until ordered to do so by the stewards.

Cross references. Specific penalty for violation of this section, see § 186-1401 of this title. § 186-845. Who shall unsaddle horses

Horses shall be unsaddled exclusively by the jockey who rode him and the helper shall limit himself to holding the horse by the bridle except when, because of the existence of extraordinary circumstances, the stewards determine otherwise. 

Amendments 1964. The words "except when, because of the existence of extraordinary circumstances, the stewards determine otherwise" were added at the end of this section by amendment File No. 929 cited in 1964 amendment note under § 186-226 of this title.

Cross references. Specific penalty for violation of this section, see § 186-1401 of this title. § 186-846. Weighing in of jockey 

The jockey shall go before the clerk of scales for weighing in inmediately after unsaddling his horse except when the stewards determine otherwise.

§ 186-847. Changes of weight 

Any horse that has run with 2 or more pounds less weight than the weight stated in the official program shall be disqualified. § 186-848. Punishment to jockey for his weight 

Any jockey carrying less than the weight stated in the official program shall be punished by the stewards. 

Cross references. Specific penalty for violation of this section, see § 186-1401 of this title. 

§ 186-849. Overweight 

No horse shall be run with more than 5 pounds overweight and no jockey may exceed the weight announced in the official program by more than 2 pounds. The stewards will punish their jockeys and if the overweight exceeds 5 pounds another jockey shall be assigned to the horse.

Cross references. Specific penalty for violation of this section, see § 186-1401 of this title. § 186-850. Objects that shall be included in weight 

For the purposes of weighing in and out the saddle, saddle cloths, cinch strap, surcingle and weights shall be included. § 186-851. Result of weighing in

The clerk of scales upon termination of weighing in shall report the result to the stewards. 

§ 186-852. Report on irregularities, etc. 

The starter at the termination of each race shall report in writing to the stewards any irregularity occuring in the start and such fines and suspensions as he may have imposed in the race, setting forth the reason for the same. 

§ 186-853. Observations 

The track judges, at the end of each race, shall give the stewards a written report on their observations of the same.

§ 186-854. Protests of jockey 

Any jockey having any protest to make concerning the developments of the race must notify the stewards immediately after the weighing out; Provided that any jockey making frivolous and unbased protest shall be punished by the stewards. 

 § 186-855. Time clocked

After the end of each race the timer shall notify the placing judges of the time clocked by the winning horse, and said judges will in turn announce this to the public. 

§ 186-856. Announcing of order of finishing 

After the end of each race the placing judges will announce to the public the order of finishing of the horses. § 186-857. Case of dead heat

Whenever the placing judges determine that two or more horses have finished in a dead heat for first place, these horses shall be considered winners for the purposes of the wagers; Provided that for the purposes of the purse the corresponding prizes shall be added and divided by the number of horses in dead heat; Provided, furthermore, That this last method shall be applied in all other cases of dead heat. 

§ 186-858. Official results 

The stewards shall declare the official results of the races and their decision cannot be altered under any circumstance and the same shall be binding and final. § 186-859. Which horse may be claimed

Every horse participating in a claiming race may be claimed for the price for which it was registered by any person who on the date of the claiming has an owner's license. 

§ 186-860. Method of claiming 

Every person qualifying to claim a horse may do so through his authorized agent; Provided, nevertheless, That no person shall directly or indirectly claim his own horse.

Cross references. Specific penalty for violation of this section, see § 186-1401 of this title.

§ 186-861. Relationship 

No owner or representative may claim the horse of another owner to whom he is related by affinity or consanguinity within the third degree. 

§ 186-862. Restrictions on claims 

Owners of horses having the same stable or the same trainer or groom may not claim horses which are in the custody of said trainer or groom, nor shall any of said horses be claimed by any other person directly or indirectly for the benefit of said owners. This restriction is also applicable to owners-trainers. § 186-863. Term and other limitations

No horse that has been claimed may be registered in the name of the immediately preceding owner within the 30 days following the date of the claim; it shall not run with the same colors nor remain in the same stable of its immediate former owner; nor may it be trained by the same trainer who trained it before it was claimed, nor shall it remain under the administration, management and care of the person to whom it belonged, unless it be newly obtained by its immediate former owner as the result of another claim.

 § 186-864. Claiming tickets; number

No person may deposit more than one claiming ticket for the same horse.

Cross references. Specific penalty for violation of this section, see § 186-1401 of this title. 

§ 186-865. Form for claims 

Claim shall be made on the form furnished by the Association to the owners or their representatives. § 186-866. Receipt of deposit in cash

The claiming petition shall not be accompanied by any money except any sum covering the fees fixed by law. Every person wishing to make a claim must first deposit in cash with the Association the complete amount of the claim for which he will be issued a receipt which must be attached to the claiming petition. 1962 

Vol. 1, No. 8 303

T.15 186 

Ch. 11

§ 186-867. Necessary equipment and system of making award 

The Association shall provide the judge of claims the boxes, clocks and any other equipment necessary. These boxes shall be furnished with a patent lock for each box and the judge of claims, when the horses go out to the track, shall open the box and shall report to the stewards before the announcement of the official result of the race, the number of requests deposited and the name of each one of the petitioners and the horses that they wish to claim. As soon as the stewards receive the report they will announce it to the public over the public address system so that the interested person may appear for the purposes of making the award. § 186-868. Withdrawal of claim petitions 

A claim petition may not be withdrawn from the box and the claimed horse shall remain in the charge of the claimant from the moment in which the jockey mounts and goes forth to the track. § 186-869. Award by lot among claimants 

If there is more than one claiming petition for the same horse the award shall be made by the judge of claims by lot in the presence of the claimant and the owner of the claimed horse within 10 minutes after the running of the race. If they fail to appear within said period, the judge of claims shall draw lots in their absence. 

The person winning the draw shall be the owner of the horse whatever may be the condition of said horse. § 186-870. Return of deposit

Immediately after the drawing the judge of claims shall return to the losing claimants the deposit receipts which they had attached to their claiming petition and said receipts may again be used for the purpose of claiming in other races; Provided that the owner of the claimed horse may use the receipt with which his horse was claimed to make a claim in another race. § 186-871. Pick up of claimed horses

Claimed horses must be picked up by the claimants or by persons designated by them within one-half hour after the claim; Provided that upon the expiration of this period of time, if they have not been picked up by the interested person, they shall be deposited in a neutral stable for the account and risk of the claimants. 

 1962 

Vol. 1, No. 8 304

Ch. T.15 S 186-876 

RACING ACT § 186-872. Delivery order 

The judge of claims shall issue a delivery order for each horse claimed and no person may refuse said delivery. Any owner or representative refusing to deliver the claimed horse shall have his license suspended for not less than 6 months and said suspension shall affect all of the horses appearing in his name. 

§ 186-873. Interference with claims 

Any owner or representative who in any form whatsoever interferes with the claim of a horse shall be punished in the manner prescribed by this Division. 

§ 186-874. Reasons for voiding petitions 

The following petitions to claim shall be declared void: (1) Those not signed by an authorized person. (2) When an owner or representative files more than one claim for the same horse. (3) The claiming petition does not comply with the requirements of this Division. (4) All petitions which have not been filed in the corresponding box at least 15 minutes before the start of the race. § 186-875. Claiming fees; voiding

Claiming fees shall be in force even when the claim is declared void. 

§ 186-876. Appeal by voiding or rejection 

When the judge of claims voids or rejects any claiming petition, the person or persons prejudiced thereby may appeal to the stewards immediately after such action is taken, before any award is made or any lots are drawn, and the decision of the stewards shall be final and conclusive. The stewards shall have the obligation of rendering a decision as stated above within the next 48 hours and in the meanwhile the horse in controversy must be deposited in a neutral stable, designated by the stewards, for the account and risk of the person who was the cause of the declaration that the claiming petition was void and in the opposite case for the account of the person to whom the horse was finally awarded. 1962 

Vol. 1, No. 8 305

T.§ 186-877 

Ch. 11

§ 186-877. Transfer

A claimed horse can not be registered to compete in races, before the corresponding transfer in the name of the claimant has been made and the corresponding transfer fee is paid. If a request for registration is made before the transfer is effected, said request shall be void and the secretary of racing will withdraw the same. § 186-878. Consideration of claiming petitions in case of withdrawal from race

After a claiming petition for a horse has been filed, the same shall be considered for the drawing if the horse to which said. petition refers has not been scratched before going out on the track to compete in the race, even though the horse be later withdrawn by the veterinary at the starting line or the race is voided or called off by the stewards. § 186-879. Former owner; term

No claimed horse may be acquired by its immediate former owner by private treaty or by claiming for a period of 30 days after it was claimed.

 § 186-880. Claiming price; official program 

The claiming price for each horse in a claiming race must be printed on the official program of the corresponding races and every claiming petition for any of said horses must be for the amount stated on said program. § 186-881. Prohibition of giving out information on deposits

No official or employee of the Administration or Association may give out any information whatsoever respecting any deposit in connection with a claim or a claiming petition to any other person. § 186-882. Processing of claim questions 

Any allegation made by an interested person, either as owner of the horse which is the subject of claiming or as a claimant of the same, which raises any question relating to the same, including the actual drawing of lots, shall be processed according to the provisions of this Division. § 186-883. To whom purse shall belong

A purse won by a claimed horse shall belong to the person who registers it and in whose name it appears in the official program. 1962 

Vol. 1, No. 8 306

Ch. T.15 § 186-886 

RACING ACT 

§ 186-884. Races for account of claimant 

Whenever a claimed horse has been registered by the immediate former owner before the claim, to compete in races, it will run on those race days in the name of and for the account of the claimant, who shall be entitled to the purse won by the horse. § 186-885. Use of drugs on claimed horses

When saliva and urine specimens have been taken from the claimed horse, the money which is the proceeds of the claim shall be deposited in the offices of the Secretary of the Association until the results of the chemical analysis of the specimen taken from such horse be known to the Administrator. In the event a positive result for stimulants or depressants be reported, the claim shall be declared void and the money paid for the claim shall be returned to the claimant unless the claimant be the person responsible for the administration of drugs or stimulants to the claimed horse, in which case the claim shall be valid; Provided that none of the above provisions shall be construed as limiting the provisions of this Division respecting the administration of drugs, stimulants or depressants. § 186-886. Conflict of interests on claim cases

When a horse changes owner by claiming and it is registered to compete in a race for which the acquiring person has registered some other horse, the secretary of races must scratch, at the option of the owner, one of the horses; Provided that if the horses originally entered formed part of an entry, he will scratch the entry or the claimed horse.

RACING ACT 

§ 186-902. Persons interested in results 

No person interested in the results of a race may act as a racing official on any race day. 

§ 186-903. Substitutes 

When any official is absent on a race day and a substitute is not present, a substitute may be appointed by the Administrator and in his absence by the head steward. § 186-904. Duties in case of emergency

Any duty delegated or specifically assigned to an official may, in case of necessity or emergency, be reassigned or merged with the duties of any other official subject to the limitations established by the act and by this division. 

§ 186-905. Identification of personnel 

Every official, employee or person designated by the Administrator or by the Association intervening in the organization and development of the races and the wagering must be adequately identified. 

§ 186-906. Organization and supervision of races 

The Administrator shall designate the necessary officials for the organization and supervision of the races subject to the limitations established by the act and by this division. § 186-907. Absences

In case one of the stewards is absent, the Administrator or, in his absence, the other members of the stewards, shall designate a substitute. § 186-908. Power of stewards

After the stewards are organized they shall have the power to: (1) Call off, for just cause, the running of the races announced in the official program. (2) Alter the order of the races for just cause. (3) Carry out investigations and require the presence of any person when they consider it necessary. (4) Make provision through orders to this effect for the use of the track and its accessory facilities during race days. 1972 

Vol. 11, No. 3 309

T.§ 186-908 

Ch. 11 (5) Make provision by orders to this effect for the conduct to be observed on the track and its accessory facilities by the persons having access to it. (6) Order the examination of any horse registered in the official program. (7) Determine the starting time of all races. (8) Prevent the starting of the first race valid for the pool until the chief inspector of betting informs them that he has in his possession the calculation sheets of the wagers on the pool. (9) Administer oaths and take statements. (10) Impose penalties. (11) Declare races official. (12) Void races for just cause. (13) Disqualify and suspend horses. (14) Make decisions and give orders in cases of urgency or extreme necessity or in situations not provided for by the act or this division, following for this purpose the uses and customs of the horse racing sport. (15) Require from the Association all facilities that are necessary for the best performance of their duties. (16) Order the search of the premises of the race tracks, the persons and horses competing in the races. (17) Assign places to the track judges. (18) Order the closing of the mutuels, daily double (dupleta), and exacta. (19) Order when and where the total of the bets on the pool, daily double (dupleta) and exacta are to be announced. 

Amendments-1971. "Exacta" wagering was added to powers (18) and (19) and phraseology was changed in general in (19) by amendments, File No. 1465, cited in 1971 

amendment note under § 186-1 of this title. 

§ 186-909. Decisions; majority

Decisions of the stewards shall be by a majority of their members. 

§ 186-910. Voiding of start 

The stewards cannot void a start given by the starter.

RACING ACT § 186-911. Complaints 

The stewards are the only judges of the races. All complaints must be presented to them through the head steward immediately after the happening of the event giving rise to the complaint. § 186-912. Report on actions of stewards 

The stewards shall prepare a report of all of the agreements, decisions, orders, sanctions and punishments, and in general of all action taken by them on each race day, and must transmit the same to the Administrator. 1972

Ch. T.15 § 186-920 

RACING ACT § 186-913. Final decisions 

The decisions of the stewards based on facts of their personal observation or appreciation shall be final. § 186-914. Opportunity to be heard

When the stewards decide to undertake an investigation which will possibly result in the imposition of the punishment or penalty, they must give the person complained of the opportunity to be heard in his defense. 

§ 186-915. Reconsiderations 

The stewards may reconsider at the request of any party or on their own motion, any punishment, provided that when this is done they must render a written report to the Administrator setting forth the reasons and grounds which caused the reconsideration. 

§ 186-916. Notices 

The secretary of stewards will give notice in writing to any person affected of any fines or punishment imposed upon him by the steward or the starter. After each race day the secretary will publish on the bulletin board, to be installed for that purpose in the jockey room, a notice containing a statement of all punishments imposed by the stewards and the starter and all jockeys shall be charged with notice of said announcements. § 186-917. Substitution of jockey 

The stewards for just cause may change any horse's jockey. The substitute designated must be in the same condition and of the same category as the suspended jockey and insofar as possible the owner, representative or trainer will be consulted for this purpose. 

§ 186-918. Placing judges 

Working hours

The placing judges must be at the point to which they have been designated one-half hour before the start of the races, and must inform the stewards of their presence. 

§ 186-919. Announcement of order of arrival 

At the end of each race the placing judges shall announce the correct order of arrival. 

§ 186-920. Mechanical or electronic devices 

In the performance of their duties the placing judges may make use of any mechanical or electronic device in aid of the accuracy of their determination. 1962 

Vol. 1, No. 8 

311

Ch. 11

Decisions

The decision of the placing judges shall be by majority. 

§ 186-922. Starter-Working hours 

The starter must be at the starting line one-half hour before the races commence, and must notify the stewards of his presence. He shall obtain from the secretary of stewards an official program of the races to be run. § 186-923. Helpers and hostlers

The starter must procure and require the presence of his helpers and hostlers before the races begin. 

§ 186-924. Operation of starting gate 

The starter must be accompanied by the employee of the Association in charge of the starting gate and make sure that it is in good operating order before the commencement of the races. 

§ 186-925.

Imposing of punishments The starter at the end of each race will report to the stewards respecting all punishments or suspensions imposed by him, as well as any other information he may think necessary or that may be required of him by the stewards. 

§ 186-926. Assistant

The assistant starter will perform all of the duties assigned to him and, in case of absence or disability of the starter, he will substitute for him, if ordered to do so by the Administrator or by the stewards. 

§ 186-927. Track judges - Working hours 

The track judges must appear before the stewards one-half hour prior to the commencement of the races. § 186-928. Positions

The track judges will take up the position assigned to them by the stewards. 

§ 186-929.

The track judges will observe the conduct of the jockeys during the course of each race, informing the stewards in writing of any irregularities or violations of this Division observed by them, stat-

§ 186-930. - Additional work 

Track judges shall also perform any other work ordered by the stewards. § 186-931. Timer - Working hours

The timer must appear before the stewards one-half hour before the commencement of the races. 

§ 186-932. Duties 

The timer in addition to the duties assigned him by the stewards shall take note of the time clocked by each winning horse, and shall make the same public immediately after the finish of the race. 

The timer shall send the administrator a report of the records made by winning horses. 

§ 186-933. Paddock judge — Working hours

The paddock judge must be in the paddock at least one hour before the start of the first race and must appear before the stewards as soon as they are organized. 

§ 186-934. Charge of registry book 

The paddock judge shall on each race day keep a registry of the time of arrival of the horses at the paddock, name of the persons in whose charge the horses arrive and shall include notes and observations relating to the persons and horses having access to the paddock, and shall deliver said registry to the stewards at the end of the races. 

§ 186-935. Access to paddock

The paddock judge shall have the responsibility of preventing unauthorized persons from having access to the paddock. 

§ 186-936.

Orders The paddock judge shall give any orders that may be necessary for the best organization, conduct and discipline in the paddock. 

§ 186-937. Lack of discipline 

The paddock judge is hereby given power to expel from the paddock any persons committing acts of indiscipline, breaches of the 1962 313 Vol. 1, No. 8

peace, interference with the organization of the races or who assumes an ungovernable, disrespectful attitude or an attitude detrimental to the best interest of the horse racing sport. § 186-938. Withdrawal of horses

It is the responsibility of the paddock judge to prevent the withdrawal of a horse from the paddock without prior authorization of the stewards. 

§ 186-939. Clerk of scales 

Working hours

The clerk of the scales must be at the place where the jockeys are to be weighed in at least 2 hours prior to the commencement of the first race. 

§ 186-940. Jockeys' weight

The clerk of the scales shall weigh the jockeys with their equipment before each race. 

§ 186-941. Charge of registry book 

The clerk of the scales shall keep a registry with the names of the jockeys who are weighed in, the weight of each one and other relevant facts and information. This registry must be delivered to the stewards at the end of the races. 

§ 186-942. Weighing out of jockeys

The clerk of the scales shall weigh out each jockey after each. race taking care that in said weighing the corresponding equipment is included. 

§ 186-943. Jockeys' attire

It is the duty of the clerk of the scales to make sure that each jockey is properly and adequately dressed and that each jockey bears his corresponding number on his right arm, as well as the colors of the owner for whom he rides, and he must also be sure that these colors correspond to those announced in the official program. 

§ 186-944. Overweight

The clerk of the scales shall not permit any jockey to carry more than 5 pounds over the weight stated in the official program; Provided that whenever the overweight exceeds 2 pounds he must report this to the stewards after the races. 1962

RACING ACT § 186-945. Examination of platform scales 

Before proceeding to weigh in the jockeys the clerk of the scales will examine the platform scales in the race track to see whether they are operating correctly, and shall report to the stewards any deficiencies he may find. 

§ 186-946. Veterinary Designation

The Administrator shall designate the veterinaries who are to act in the race tracks and the one designated by the Association shall be subject to his approval. § 186-947. Examination of horses; reports and certificates

The veterinary shall examine all horses registered in order to determine their physical condition. The examination shall be carried out the day before the races before the withdrawal time and time for changes; Provided that he shall make a report to the secretary of races respecting the condition of the horses; Provided further that in case it is determined that a registered horse is not in condition to compete in a race, the veterinary shall issue a certificate stating that circumstance. 

§ 186-948. Examinations in paddock 

On each race day the veterinary shall carefully and minutely examine each horse when it enters the paddock and will notify the stewards of the result of the examination. 

§ 186-949. Withdrawal of horses 

The veterinary will order the withdrawal of a registered horse if after examining it he is of the opinion that said horse is not in a condition to compete in races. 

§ 186-950. Use of drugs and substances prohibited 

The veterinary will order the withdrawal of a registered horse if he determines that said horse has been given, spread with, or applied any drug or substance prohibited by this Division, or has been intervened with parenterally after scratch time, or if the horse is suffering from wounds or contusion, symptoms of jealousy, nasal conditions, digestive upsets or any other condition affecting its sound physical condition. 

§ 186-951. Reports to stewards

The veterinary shall inform the stewards of any decision or order issued by him on race day. 1962

Ch. 11

§ 186-952. Right of access to stables 

The veterinary may enter any stable or place where racing horses are kept to look them over or examine them and neither the Association, owner, his representative, trainer, groom or groom's helper may object to this without incurring in responsibility.

§ 186-953. 

Emergency cases

It shall be the duty of the veterinary to attend to emergency cases involving the horses in any place in the premises of the race track during the running of races. 

§ 186-954. Observation of horses after races 

The veterinary shall observe the condition of the horses after running a race and proceed to suspend any horse showing an unsound physical condition from future competition. Said horse cannot be registered without previously obtaining a certificate from the veterinary stating that it is physically in condition for competition.

Cross references. Specific penalty for violation of this section, see § 186-1401 of this title. § 186-955. Physical fitness of horse; determination

The veterinary shall have the power to determine whether a horse is physically fit to compete in races and his determination to that effect shall be final. 

§ 186-956. Specimens for analysis after each race

After each race the veterinary shall obtain from each winning horse and from any other horses ordered by the stewards, or from any horses that the veterinary himself determines, specimens of saliva, urine, and blood and he may use for these purposes the equipment and technique generally accepted for the same. § 186-957. -Professional relations for compensation

The veterinary shall not have professional relations for compensation nor business relations with the Association, owners, trainers, and breeders.
