SUBDIVISION 10. UNDESIRABLE PRACTICES 

186-1001. Enumeration of undesirable practices § 186-1001. Enumeration of undesirable practices 

The following are declared to be undesirable practices in the horse racing sport: (1) The possession in the premises of the race track, without prior authorization of the Administrator or veterinary, of drugs or substances whether in natural or synthetic form, which upon administration to a horse are capable of stimulating, depressing it, or in any manner affecting his normal physical condition. (2) The possession in the premises of the race track, without the prior authorization of the Administrator or veterinary, of syringes, hypodermic needles or any other object or device capable of being used for the injection or administration of any depressing drug or stimulant into a horse. (3) The submission of a horse to a vitamin treatment, or to treatment with a tonic or preparation which may affect the horse 1972 

Vol. 11, No. 3 318

Ch. T.15 § 186-1001 

RACING ACT 

adversely or beneficially, without prior notice to the veterinary or the Administrator. (4) The submission of a horse after withdrawal and changes time to rubbing with liniment, medicine, or substance or any parenteral treatment. (5) To submit a horse after the time set for withdrawals and changes, to any treatment whatsoever on its extremities excepting treatment with ice. (6) The placing of sponges or any object whatsoever on the nostrils of horses on the day they are to compete in races. (7) The placing or applying of any substance whatsoever on any genital of a horse on race day. (8) The running of a horse with its tongue strapped without having notified the secretary of races when the horse was registered. (9) The permitting by any owner or trainer of a horse to compete in races without being in the proper physical condition. (10) The permitting by an owner or trainer of a horse to compete in a race knowing that the horse is liable to develop nasal hemorrhage (epistaxis and hemoptysis). (11) The registration or causing of a horse to run which has been denerved or hamstrung or which by means of any treatment has been deprived of or had blocked the nerves of one or more of its extremities, or which by any method whatsoever has been deprived of sensitivity in one or more of its extremities. (12) To carry, transport, handle, give or receive, apply or induce the use of electric batteries, or any similar device or thing or anything which imitates the action of an electric battery in the premises of the race track. (13) To pay, satisfy, or contribute to the payment of a fine imposed upon another person. (14) To promise, offer or give prizes, payments or gifts in any form with the intention of influencing the result of a race. (15) For any owner to have in his stable, in his care, administration or handling, horses belonging to another owner. (16) Betting by a jockey on any horse other than the horse he has registered to ride or which he in fact rides; Provided, That a jockey may only wager through the owner or trainer. 1972 

Vol. 11, No. 3 319

T.186-1001 

Ch. 11 (17) Permitting the entrance into the race track of any person who has been declared a race track nuisance. (18) To fight, breach the peace, be disorderly and to conduct oneself in any improper or undesirable manner in the premises of the race track. (19) To be in the premises of the race track while drunk or apparently drunk. (20) To act toward or address in a vulgar or coarse way or to be disrespectful to any official or employee of the Administration. (21) To make statements which are false and detrimental to the horse racing sport and the making of such statements about persons connected with the same. (22) To destroy, damage, deteriorate or in any form whatsoever to make improper use of the property of the Association and the facilities which it offers. (23) Disobedience of orders given by the guards of the Association respecting order, discipline, access to or use of facilities, parking and cleanliness, as well as any order given in the discharge of their responsibility. (24) To prevent by fraudulent, illegal or illicit means the normal development of the races. (25) Failure to use the maximum effort or the proper care in the preparation of a horse or failure to require of the horse the greatest possible effort in a race. (26) Obtaining or attempting to obtain the registration in any of the registers or registries of the Administration by false information. (27) The alteration in any form whatsoever of any official document or certificate issued by the Board or by the office of the Administrator. (28) Advertising or offering to sell, the selling, donating, trafficking, exchanging, transportation or the carrying on the person, the purchasing, taking, receiving or accepting, the printing, causing or ordering the printing, writing, distributing or transferring of any ticket, card or paper which is pretended to be, constitute or represent a means of participation, wagering, or share in any form whatsoever in any wager or bet authorized by law or by this division, operated or conducted in infringement or in violation of the act and this division. 1972 

Vol. 11, No. 3 320

Ch. 11

RACING ACT 

T.15 § 186-1001 (29) To operate or cause the operation of mutuels, daily doubles (dupletas), exactas or pools other than those specifically permitted to the Association. (30) To pay, receive, deliver or distribute any money or other object as a prize, award, or earning of any wagering system not authorized by this division. (31) To cooperate, aid and abet or participate in any of the practices enumerated in the preceding sections. (32) To alter, mutilate in any form whatsoever any single combination pool ticket (papeleta), multiple combination pool ticket (cuadro), mutuel, daily double (dupleta), or exacta ticket with the fraudulent intent to circulate the same as genuine. (33) Improperly to collect or improperly or illegally benefit from the wagers or the proceeds of the pool, mutuel, daily double (dupleta), or exacta. (34) Association by persons connected with the horse racing sport or the maintenance of them of friendship with persons having a recognized bad reputation in the community, with persons who have been declared race track nuisances or with persons convicted of the use of or traffic in narcotics. (35) The interference, obstruction or prevention of the attempt to interfere with the processing and procedure for registration and the organization and development of the races, claims, wagers, weighing in and weighing out of jockeys, the obtaining of blood, saliva or urine specimens. (36) To announce or communicate during the holding of races (except to the public present) the total or approximate amount of the pool, of the daily double, and the real or approximate payoffs of the mutuels and daily double. (37) The consumption of liquor by a jockey on the day prior to or the same day he is going to take part in races; staying up all night the day before he is to take part in races or frequenting gambling rooms.

Every owner who registers a horse in a race shall be understood to have given his consent to the taking or extracting of samples of urine, saliva, blood, nasal secretion or perspiration. The blood sample can only be withdrawn by the veterinary. In the case of the extraction of samples of saliva, urine, blood, nasal secretion or perspiration the veterinary may be assisted by his helpers.

§ 186-1102.-Method for obtaining 

Whenever a horse for three hours after the end of a race has failed to urinate or in the event he has urinated but in the event the quantity he has urinated is insufficient for an analysis, the veterinary may use a catheter to obtain the necessary amount of specimen or he may withdraw a specimen of blood. 1972

§ 186-1103.-Who may order extraction

The Administration, the stewards or the veterinary may order the taking of the samples of urine, saliva, blood, nasal secretion or perspiration from any horse that is registered for competition or which has run in a race. The withdrawal of the sample may be done prior to the same, immediately after the same is disputed or during the 3 days following the running of the race.

Amendments-1964. This section was amended generally by amendment File No. 929, cited in 1964 amendment note under § 186-226 of this title. § 186-1104. Responsibility for physical condition of horses 

The owner, trainer, groom and groom's helper are responsible to the Administration for the physical condition of their horses and it shall be their absolute responsibility to see to it that none of their horses is stimulated or depressed and that it is not administered any drug or substance whatsoever that might affect the natural condition of the same. § 186-1105. Specimens-Who must be present at taking

The owner, in person or represented by the trainer, foreman or groom of the horse from which a sample of urine, saliva, blood, nasal secretion or perspiration is being taken may be present while said samples are being taken or withdrawn. If he is not present he shall be presumed to have accepted the correctness of the procedure carried out for the taking of the sample and placing the same in a container.

§ 186-1109. - Deposit in steel boxes

Once the specimens are placed in the container, stoppered, stamped and sealed, and their identification card is attached, they shall be placed in a steel box. After taking the last specimen of the day, the veterinary shall proceed to close said metal box and lock it or padlock it and only the veterinary and the chemist shall have possession of the key to said box. 

§ 186-1110. - Analysis by chemist 

The specimen box shall be delivered to the chemist who will proceed to make the necessary analyses. The analyses shall be made in the Administration laboratory or in any other laboratory determined by the Administrator according to the circumstances. § 186-1111. Identification cards of specimens

The veterinary shall proceed to transmit to the office of the Administrator in a wax-sealed envelope the parts of the card that were not attached to the containers enclosing a list of the names of the horses corresponding to the card, the time and date when the specimen was taken and any other pertinent and necessary information. § 186-1112. Report from chemist

After the chemist has terminated his analysis of the specimens, he must transmit to the office of the Administrator a report certifying the results of the analysis of each specimen returning together with said report the card which was adhered to each container. 1962

 § 186-1113. Presumptions 

The procedure used in the taking of specimens and the finding of the chemist respecting the analysis of the same shall be presumed correct in the absence of proof to the contrary. § 186-1114. Private chemist

Any owner whose horse has specimens taken from it may designate a private chemist with an authorized license to be present during the analysis of the specimen. When a private chemist is thus designated, the owner shall notify the Administrator or the official chemist immediately after the races of his intention to designate a private chemist. The official chemist shall notify the owner or the private chemist of the place and the time where the analysis is to be made and shall wait upon said private chemist for one-half hour after the time previously set. If the private chemist fails to appear the chemist shall proceed to open the containers and to perform. the work of the analysis. § 186-1115. Containers; supply and requirements

For each race day the chemist shall furnish the veterinary a sufficient number of containers duly sterilized, stamped and sealed, in a locked metal box and shall certify that said containers have been duly sterilized and that their stoppers have never been used. § 186-1116. Mechanical system for placing, sealing and numbering

The Administrator may establish a mechanical system or procedure for placing the specimen in the container, and the sealing and numbering thereof; Provided, That whenever this is done, he must issue a written order notifying the owners, trainers and grooms of the method, system or procedure to be used. § 186-1117. Positive result; suspension of persons responsible

Upon receiving a report from the chemist certifying that a specimen is positive for any drug or substance that stimulates, depresses or alters the natural condition of the horse, the Administrator shall suspend the affected horse and may suspend the owner, trainer, groom or groom's helper connected with said horse as well as all of the horses belonging to said owner. § 186-1118. Period

When the Administrator orders a summary suspension, he shall take whatever action the case justifies within a period of 10 days. 1962 

Vol. 1, No. 8 324

Ch. 

T.15 prec. § 186-1201

RACING ACT 

§ 186-1119. Repeated violations

The Administrator in cases of repeated violation of the provisions respecting drugs, stimulants or depressants, or of electric batteries or similar devices, shall request the Board to declare the person repeating the violation a race track nuisance. 

§ 186-1120. Retention of purse 

The Association shall retain payment of any purse corresponding to a horse from whom specimens of urine, saliva or blood have been taken until the Administrator authorizes payment; Provided that it is the duty of the Administrator to issue the pertinent order for this purpose as soon as he receives the chemist's report. § 186-1121. Forfeiture of purse; effect on wagers 

When a horse, whose sample of urine, saliva, blood, nasal secretion or perspiration has a positive reaction showing that it contains a stimulant, depressant or any other substance which alters the natural condition of the horse, the owner's purse shall be forfeited and the same shall be distributed as in the case of a disqualification. The forfeiture of the purse and the punishment or penalties to be imposed on the horse or its owner shall in no way affect the official result declared by the stewards for the purposes of wagers.

Amendments 1964. This section was amended generally by amendment File No. 929 cited in 1964 amendment note under § 186-226 of this title. 

SECTIONS 

186-1122. Penalties

Any person who prevents, attempts to prevent, embarrasses, delays or interferes unnecessarily with the procedure for the taking of specimens of urine, saliva, blood, nasal secretion or perspiration from the horses, or who disobeys the rules governing said procedure, may be suspended or his license be cancelled, or he may be fined the sum of not more than $500 at the discretion of the Administrator or he may be declared a race track nuisance by the Board. 186-1201. 186-1202. 

Amendments 1964. The specimens may be taken of nasal secretion or perspiration by amendment File No. 929 cited in 1964 amendment note under § 186-226 of this title.

186-1243. Services; license § 186-1201. Authorized licenses; ignorance of law and regulations 

Only the licenses expressly authorized by the act or by this Division shall be granted. Every person who in any capacity shall have obtained or obtains a license, or participates in any manner in horse racing, shall be presumed to have done so with a full understanding and knowledge of the horse racing act [15 L.P.R.A § 181 et seq.], this Division, resolutions and orders proclaimed or that may be proclaimed and is under the obligation to comply with the same.

Ch. T.15 § 186-1203 

RACING ACT § 186-1202. Expelled persons 

No person or horse that has ever been expelled by any recognized racing authority shall be permitted within the premises of the Association. § 186-1203. Indispensable requirements for race tracks

The following shall be indispensable requirements for any race track in Puerto Rico: (1) Have a track not less than 1 mile in length. (2) Have available not less than two starting gates. (3) (A) Have available a mechanized or electronic system for the wagers. (B) It shall be indispensable requirement to have available equipment to take mechanically or electronically the fractional time and the total time of each race. (4) Have available equipment to photograph on film the running of the races. (5) Have available equipment to photograph finishes. (6) Have available an adequate public address system. (7) Have available a daily ambulance service. (8) To keep open daily an emergency room in the charge of an authorized male nurse. (9) To maintain at all times a properly uniformed guard system. (10) Have a stable area of not less than 900 stalls. (11) Have sufficient parking area for the convenience of the public. (12) Have an area and facilities for the taking of specimens of saliva, urine and blood. (13) Have premises adequately equipped for the registrations for races. (14) Maintain stands, first class bars and a first class restaurant. (15) To maintain and preserve the surroundings and premises of the race track in an attractive way. (16) Designate by common agreement with the Board and the Administrator a comfortable area for the exclusive use of these persons and their guests during race day. (17) To designate and have available at its cost a physician who must be present at the race tracks subject to the orders of the stewards during race days at the time fixed by the Administrator. (18) To designate and keep at its cost a veterinary whose designation must be approved by the Administrator, and who shall be 

Sept. 30, 1964 

Vol. 3, No. 7 327

T.§ 186-1203 

Ch. 11

under the orders and supervision of the official veterinary. (19) Prepare such premises, provide facilities and equipment that the Board may determine are necessary or convenient for facilitating the work to be performed on the premises of the race track by any official or employee of the Administration. (20) Maintain the services of not less than two ushers properly and adequately uniformed. 

Amendments 1964. Paragraph (B) was added to this section by amendment File No. 929 cited in 1964 amendment note under § 186–226 of this title.

 § 186-1204. Behavior on race tracks

The Association shall order the departure from the premises of the race track of any spectator or visitor who does not observe good conduct or who disturbs the peace or who uses vulgar language or talks in a disrespectful manner to any person connected with the horse racing sport or who violates the act, this Division, and the orders and resolutions of the Board or the Administrator. § 186-1205. Discrimination

The Association cannot prohibit the entrance of any person to the race track for reasons of race, religion, color, or political beliefs. 

§ 186-1206. Stable personnel - Report; license 

Every owner shall inform the office of the Administrator of the persons working in his stable; Provided that no owner shall employ any person who does not hold the corresponding license issued by the Administrator.

Cross references. Specific penalty for violation of this section, see § 186-1401 of this title. 

§ 186-1207. Substitution; reasons

Every owner shall inform the office of the Administrator when he substitutes his stable personnel and the reasons or causes for the change or substitution.

Cross references. Specific penalty for violation of this section, see § 186-1401 of this title. § 186-1208. Registration of distinctive colors of stable 

Every owner shall register the distinctive colors of his stable and the same shall be subject to the approval of the Administrator. No 

Sept. 30, 1964 328 

Vol. 3, No. 7

Ch. 11

RACING ACT 

T.15 186-1212 change in colors shall be permitted for a period of one year from the date of their approval. The owner shall only use the registered colors. At the time of the race and for just cause the stewards may authorize a change of colors. 

§ 186-1209. Equipment - Registration and change 

Each owner shall register in the office of the Administrator the equipment with which his horses will run. Any change of equipment must be previously approved by the Administrator; Provided, That the change shall be requested the day before the registrations. 

§ 186-1210. Official program 

Horses shall run with the equipment with which they appear on the official program independently of the colors which they have registered with the Administration.

 § 186-1211. Owner's representative

When an owner leaves Puerto Rico or when by reason of physical disability, illness or for any other reason he is unable to attend to or supervise his horses, he must designate a representative, according to the provisions of this Division, and said representative will assume all of the responsibilities, rights and privileges of the said owner. § 186-1212. Purses - Participation of jockey; deduction (a) The compensation of the jockeys who ride in a race shall be a sum equivalent to 15 percent of the purse fixed for the same after deducting the excises imposed by law. No other deduction shall be made before computing said 15 percent. Of that amount jockeys whose mounts finish out of the first five paid positions shall be paid the following sums: (1) $5 to each jockey riding a horse finishing out of the first five paid positions in races with purses up to $2,500. (2) $10 to each jockey riding a horse finishing out of the first five paid positions in races having a purse from $2,500 up. (3) $15 to each jockey riding a horse finishing out of the five paid positions in races having a purse from $10,000 up. (b) The remaining sum shall be distributed as follows: (1) 50 percent for the jockey riding the winning horse. (2) 25 percent for the jockey riding the horse finishing in 

Sept. 30, 1964 

Vol. 3, No. 7 329

T.§ 186-1212 

Ch. 11

second place. (3) 13 percent for the jockey riding the horse finishing in third place. (4) 7 percent for the jockey riding the horse finishing in fourth place. (5) 5 percent for the jockey riding the horse finishing in fifth place. (c) In races in which five or fewer horses participate the owner must pay his jockey an amount equivalent to 15 percent of the purse won by his horse after deducting the excises fixed by law and he shall not make any other deduction prior to computing said 15 percent.

Amendments 1964. This section was amended generally by amendment File No. 929 cited in 1964 amendment note under § 186-226 of this title. 

§ 186-1213. Compensation in case of withdrawal

Every jockey who has been assigned a horse which is withdrawn at the last minute in the paddock or at the post shall be entitled to the compensation assigned to one of the non-paying positions. 

In the event that the scratched horse would have competed in a race of five or fewer horses said compensation shall be paid before determining the compensation corresponding to the other jockeys. 

Amendments 1964. This section was amended generally by amendment File No. 929 cited in 1964 amendment note under § 186-226 of this title.

Cross references. Specific penalty for violation of this section, see § 186-1401 of this title. § 186-1214. Persons subject to suspension; limitations

No person subject to a suspension of license shall have access to the stable, paddock or track areas while the suspension is in force except in cases authorized by the Administrator or a duly authorized official of his office. 

§ 186-1215. Classification of jockeys Jockeys shall be classified as follows: 

Class A. Every jockey who has won 40 races after obtaining his first license.

Class B. Every jockey who has won 20 races after obtaining his first license.

Every jockey shall have for his use in the practice of his profession the following minimum equipment belonging to him: (1) Two riding breeches. (2) One pair of riding boots. 

(3) A whip. (4) A pair of blunt riding spurs. (5) A safety helmet.

§ 186-1217. Official uniform 

Jockeys shall use the following official uniform when mounted: (1) Cap and shirt with the official registered colors of the owner to whom belongs the horse he rides in the race. (2) White or cream colored riding breeches and on rainy days they may use dark breeches. (3) Riding boots. (4) A safety helmet.

 § 186-1219. Excuse; substitution

When a jockey is physically incapable of mounting the horse, by determination of the race track physician, he may be excused and substituted according to the provisions of this Division. 

§ 186-1220. - Questions and testimonies 

Any jockey taking part in a race has the obligation to appear before the stewards to answer questions and give testimony whenever required to do so.

Obligation to substitute

Every jockey under the rules of the stewards on a race day is obliged to comply with a requirement by the stewards that he substitute for another jockey.

Jockeys shall only use spurs with blunt or dull points.

Cross references. Specific penalty for violation of this section, see § 186-1401 of this title. 

§ 186-1223. Training - Facilities; schedule 

The Association must provide facilities to the owners for the training of horses and shall fix a schedule for this which shall be submitted to the approval of the Administrator. 

Cross references. Specific penalty for violation of this section, see § 186-1401 of this title. § 186-1224. In charge of track

The Association shall have a person in charge of the track during the training and schooling hours, who shall organize and supervise the use of the tracks according to the approved schedules; Provided that any person disobeying the rules for the use of the track may be punished.

Horse blankets

At the end of an exercise the horses shall return blanketed to the outer fence. 1962

 § 186-1226. Jockey 

Implied consent

Jockeys are presumed to have knowledge of the contents of the official program and to have given their consent to ride the horses to which they appear assigned in it. 

§ 186-1227. Punishments; when they shall be effective 

Punishments of a jockey during a race day shall be effective at the termination of the races of that day, unless the stewards order otherwise. § 186-1228. Dependencies of race track; inspection; experts

The Administrator may inspect all of the dependencies of the race track and for this he may use the services of experts to determine whether the same offer the necessary security and comfort to the public and to all persons intervening in the horse racing sport; 

Provided that in case of any deficiency he may order that the same be corrected within a determined period or may suspend the running of races until said deficiency be corrected. § 186-1229. Participation in races; ineligible horses 

Horses shall be ineligible to be registered for competition in races under the following circumstances: (1) When they belong to or are managed, cared for or trained by disqualified or suspended persons. (2) When they are in unsound physical condition. 

§ 186-1230. Eligibility pursuant to race plan 

The Association shall not accommodate in its stables, nor shall the secretary of racing admit to registration for races, nor shall the Administrator permit the registration in the registry, of any horse that is ineligible to compete pursuant to the provisions of the race plan, and he shall order the elimination of any such horse that is already registered. § 186-1231. Striking from registry; hearing

After hearing the Administrator may declare a horse ineligible for competition in Puerto Rico and strike it from the registry because of its unsound physical condition or bad manners. 1962 

Vol. 1, No. 8 332

Ch. T.15 186-1238 

RACING ACT 

§ 186-1232. Effect of suspension of license 

The suspension or cancellation of an owner's license covers his horses in the manner provided by the act and this Division. § 186-1233. Consent to be searched 

It is presumed that every person having anything to do with the handling or care of horses or their equipment on race days has given his consent and is subject to be searched at any time while he is present on the premises of the race tracks on race days. 

§ 186-1234. Officials with free access to dependencies 

Members of the Board, the Administrator and officials designated by them shall have free access to all of the race tracks of Puerto Rico and all of their facilities and dependencies by the mere presentation of credentials issued by the Administrator. § 186-1235. Free access to clubhouse and grandstand 

Every person who has ever been a member of the Board or of the former Racing Commission, as well as every person who has held the position of Horse Racing Administrator or Director, shall have free access to the clubhouse and grandstand of the race tracks of 

Puerto Rico on race days by mere presentation of credentials issued by the Administrator. § 186-1236. Public hearings; cost

Any person or entity who institutes before the Board any matter which requires or which in the judgment of the Board calls for a public hearing has the obligation of paying the costs of publishing notices, as well as any other expense directly connected with said hearing. The Board may at its discretion relieve any person or entity of this provision. § 186-1237. Persons prohibited from wagering

No member of the Board nor the Administrator nor any other official or employee of the Administration or the Association may make wagers relating to the races. § 186-1238. Activities other than horse racing sport

The Association shall inform the Board of any activity it proposes to hold in the race track area which is not connected with the horse racing sport. The Board may forbid the holding of any activity 

Sept. 30, 1964 

Vol. 3, No. 7 333

T.§ 186-1238 

Ch. 11

which in its opinion could be prejudicial to or incompatible with the horse racing sport. § 186-1239. Special prize; unauthorized races

No race shall be held for a special prize or trophy without the previous authorization of the Board. The holding of races not appearing on the official program without previous authorization from the Board is also prohibited. 

§ 186-1240. Modifications to this Division 

The Board on its own initiative, by recommendation of the Administrator or any interested person, may amend this Division, repeal the same, or adopt others, in each case holding a public hearing. 

§ 186-1241. Vacating of provisions 

The Board in the proper cases may vacate any provision of this Division setting forth the reasons for this action. 

§ 186-1242. Conflict between act and regulatory provisions 

Nothing contained in this Division shall be understood to be a limitation, modification or waiver of the duties, prerogatives, authority and powers conferred upon the Board by the act. 

SECTIONS 

§ 186-1243. Services; license

No person shall render services in the race track area as a veterinarian, agent selling veterinary or chemical products, blacksmith, exercise boy or watchman unless he first obtains a license which shall be issued by the Administrator. The Administrator shall submit to the Board for its approval, the standards and requirements for each one of said activities which should be established for the granting of said licenses. This section shall not become effective until 30 days after approval of the standards by this Board.

SUBDIVISION 2. DEFINITIONS 

186-2201. Definitions 

§ 186-2201. Definitions 

The following words and phrases shall have the indicated meaning. The use of the masculine gender shall include the feminine and neuter genders, the singular shall include the plural, the plural shall include the singular unless otherwise clearly indicated in the text. 

(1) Administration: Racing Sport Administration. 

(2) Administrator: Racing Sport Administrator. 

(3) Year: Calendar year. 

(4) Agent: Person authorized by legal instrument to represent a breeder or owner. (5) Breeder: Natural or artificial person who is the registered owner of the dam at the time the foal is dropped. (6) Day: Period of time between two consecutive midnights. 1969 

Vol. 8, No. 2 341

T.§ 186-2201 

Ch. 11 (7) Owner: Proprietor of a thoroughbred horse of breeding establishment. (8) Horse: Horse, mare, colt or filly (racing or breeding stock). (9) Native horse: Horse foaled within the territorial limits of 

Puerto Rico. (10) Registration: Notation made in a register to the intent and purposes of this division. 

(11) Board: Racing Board. 

(12) Law: Racing Law of Puerto Rico. 

(13) Month: Calendar month. 

(14) Establishment: Farm, acreage of land or place devoted to breeding, rearing and care of thoroughbred horses. (15) Stud farm: Establishment customarily devoted to the breeding and rearing of thoroughbred horses equipped with the necessary facilities for the purpose. (16) Register: Official book wherein all notations required by these rules are entered. (17) Reproducer: Stud-horse or brood mare. 

(18) Stud Book: Genealogical Register of thoroughbred horses of Puerto Rico. 

(19) Veterinarian: Veterinarian appointed by the Racing Administrator and who works for the Racing Sport Administration. 

(20) Private veterinarian: Veterinarian in the private practice of the profession duly licensed by competent authority. 

SUBDIVISION 3. DIRECTION, ADMINISTRATION AND POWERS SECTIONS 

186-2301. Stud Book; organization, direction and administration 

186-2302. Powers of the Administrator § 186-2301. Stud Book; organization, direction and administration 

The organization, direction and administration of the Stud Book shall be exercised by the Administration under the immediate supervision of its executive officer and administrative head; the Administrator. § 186-2302. Powers of the Administrator

The Administrator shall be the Director of the Stud Book and shall have, without being limited to the provisions herein mentioned, the powers to: 1969 

Vol. 8, No. 2 342

Ch. 11

RACING ACT 

T.15 § 186-2401 (1) Establish the regime for the organization and operation of the Stud Book, issuing to that purpose the pertinent orders and resolutions, and amending them as may be fitting. (2) To establish and adopt the techniques that will permit the best operation. (3) To consider and decide all matters submitted to him. (4) Select the technical and administrative personnel in charge of its operation. (5) To recognize the Stud Books of other countries. (6) To represent the Stud Book of Puerto Rico, in the local and international levels, with powers to make all presentations, take administrative or judicial steps in the defense of its interests. (7) Adopt all necessary measures to insure its best organization and operation and to achieve its purposes. (8) Impose penalties for violations to this division.

At the request of owners, breeders or stud farms the Administrator shall issue certified copies of the registered facts concerning the horses in their establishment. Said documents shall establish the pedigree, description, identification and property rights of the horse.

Notation shall be made of the issuance of said documents in the register concerned and certified copies of the documents shall only be issued by order of the Administrator. 

§ 186-2405. Registration in Stud Book-Thoroughbred horses 

Only thoroughbred horses shall be registered in the Stud Book. 

Only the following horses shall be considered thoroughbreds: (1) Duly identified foals whose sires and dams have been registered in the Stud Book. (2) Thoroughbred horses registered and recognized as such by the American Stud Book and those registered in Stud Books recognized by this or in any other Stud Book recognized by the Administrator, and those horses whose pedigree, description, identification and ownership have been proved. § 186-2406. REQUIREMENTS FOR REGISTRATION; AGENTS 

186-2501. Owners; requirements 

186-2502. Breeder or owner of stud farm-Sworn statement

186-2510. -Absence from Puerto Rico; provisional designation § 186-2501. Owners; requirements

Every individual or corporation devoted to breeding and rearing thoroughbred horses may be recognized as owner. For the approval and registration of the name of his stud farm an owner must have the necessary facilities and own an establishment with breeding stock registered in the Stud Book. § 186-2502. Breeder or owner of stud farm-Sworn statement

For the recognition and registration of a breeder of stud farm, the breeder or owner of the stud farm must submit to the Administrator a sworn statement containing the following information: (1) Name of the person or corporation under which the business is operated. (2) Name of the establishment where his breeding stock is being kept stating the name of its owner. (3) Size of the farm and detailed information of the facilities of the breeding establishment. (4) Location of the stud farm. (5) Detailed list of the breeding stock available in the establishment including: 1969 

Vol. 8, No. 2 345

T.§ 186-2502 

Ch. 11 (A) Original name of each horse and the name by which it is known in Puerto Rico. (B) Age and sex. (C) Color. (D) Markings. (E) Tattoo number. (F) Name of sire, dam and sire of the dam of each horse and country of origin. 

§ 186-2503. Registration 

Once the application is approved by the Administrator, the breeder or stud farm shall be entered in the appropriate register listing all the information prescribed in the preceding section and all other complementary information that may be required. § 186-2504.

Recognition Only natural persons of legal age and corporations shall be recognized as breeders and owners. In the case of a corporation a natural person must be designated to act as its agent. The designation of agent requires the previous approval of the Administrator. § 186-2505. Representation by agent-Breeder or owner

The breeder or owner may be represented by an agent whose designation must have the previous approval of the Administrator. 

The designation of an agent must be made by means of a legal document wherein the rights and privileges granted shall be stated as well as the duration of the designation. 

§ 186-2506. Corporations; documents 

In the case of a corporation the following documents must be filed in the office of the Administrator: (1) Certified copy of the certificate of incorporation. (2) Certified copy of the minutes or resolution designating the agent. (3) Personal information about the agent, using the form which for the purpose shall be supplied by the Administrator. (4) Certified copy of the bylaws of the corporation. § 186-2507. Failure to comply; designation of new agent

Should the agent fail to comply with the provisions of this division or when his official and personal behavior be detrimental . 1969 346 

Vol. 8, No. 2

Ch. 11

RACING ACT 

T.15 § 186-2601 to the racing sport, the Administrator shall request from the breeder or owner the designation of a new agent and shall withdraw the approval granted to the previous agent. 

§ 186-2508. -Exercise of rights and privileges 

When an agent is designated, only the agent can exercise the rights and privileges granted to him as such. Only in the absence of the agent will the breeder or owner be able to act. § 186-2509. -Annulment of power

The annulment of the power granted to an agent shall be made by legal document serving notice to the Administrator by presentation of a certified copy of said document. In the case of a corporation the annulment shall be notified by the presentation of a certified copy of the proceedings, minutes or resolution to that effect. § 186-2510. -Absence from Puerto Rico; provisional designation

The breeder or owner who has not designated an agent on leaving the island must notify the Administrator the name of the person who will represent him during his absence. Upon his return he shall so notify the Administrator and the notification will annul the designation of his representative.

§ 186-2602. Register of Breeding Stock; information In the Register of Breeding Stock the following shall be entered: 

(1) Names of the horses in the establishment or farm and of their owners. (2) Date of entry of each horse to the establishment for breeding purposes. (3) Date of removal from the establishment. (4) Pedigree of each horse. (5) Written and graphic description of each horse and his tattoo number. (6) Number of mares served by each stallion, dates of services, number of leaps and the results obtained. (7) Name of stallion that covered each mare and date of birth of the foal. § 186-2603. In the Register of Stallion Services the following shall be entered: (1) Services to each mare and name of the stallion performing the services. (2) Date of each service. § 186-2604. Register of Births; information

In the Register of Births the following shall be entered: (1) Date of birth of each foal and his pedigree. (2) Observable markings of each foal at foaling time and all changes in these which may occur and the dates on which the changes were observed. (3) Proposed names for the foals. (4) Any other information concerning the foal. 

§ 186-2605. Stud horses-Report to the Administrator 

Of all horses entering the stud, the pedigree, description and proof of ownership shall be sent to the Administrator. The Administrator shall verify the pedigree, description and ownership 1969 348 

Vol. 8, No. 2

Ch. 11

RACING ACT T.15 § 186-2608 

and shall provide the breeder or the stud farm notice thereof. 

The necessary control shall be exercised and the notice issued shall be kept at the establishments to be presented to the authorities on request. § 186-2606. -Transfer; notice (a) When a horse be transferred from a farm or establishment to another or to any other place notice shall be given to the Administrator during the 15 days following the date of such a transfer. The notification shall be made in the form, which for the purpose shall be furnished by the Administrator. In case of broodmares transferred to be bred, the stud farm or owner of the breeding establishment where the mare was bred shall so inform the Administrator. For the validity and acceptance of the services it shall be necessary that the stud farm whose stallions performed the services enter these in the appropriate register noting the date of transfer and the place to which the transfer was made. (b) Failure to comply with the provisions of this section may be cause to refuse the registration of the foal born from these services. § 186-2607. Owners, breeders and/or stud farms; information to the Administrator

The owners, breeders and/or stud farms shall be bound to inform the Administrator of abortions of one or twin foals; births of twins, death of any one of them; castrations of horses; horses that may be retired from breeding, or dropped because of sale, or other reasons; deaths of horses; horses entering or leaving the stud farm or establishment indicating their place of origin or destination; and foals reared artificially because of death or permanent disability of the dam. 

§ 186-2608. Stud farms-Exhibition of mares 

The stud farms shall exibit the mares in the most favorable conditions for their easy identification and inspection. They shall be bound, likewise, to have all broodmares and stallions properly tattooed. When not previously tattooed they must so request immediately from the Administrator who will order the veterinarian to proceed to tattoo them within a period that shall not exceed 

30 days after the receipt of the request. 1969 349

 § 186-2609. -Facilities 

All stud farms must have the facilities and personnel necessary to assist the officials of the Administration in the discharge of their duties. They must, likewise, have stocks for the restraint of foals to be tattooed, built according to the specifications furnished by the Administrator.

§ 186-2701. Stallions-Reports to Administrator 

(a) The owner of the stallion shall inform the Administrator the names of the mares that were served during the year by each one of his stallions making a separate report for each stallion.

The report shall be made in the form that will be supplied by the Administrator. (b) The names of all mares bred (in foal or barren) and the dates of all services shall likewise be informed. Said reports shall be made at the end of the breeding season but never after the 

1st of September of each year. (c) The owner of the stallion shall provide the owner of the mare a certificate showing the dates of all services. (d) No registration certificate shall be issued unless the report of stallion services and the report of dates of services to the mares have been filed in the office of the Administrator. The dates and signatures in both documents must coincide. Should there be any discrepancies the Administrator shall investigate the reasons for them and shall take such action as may be fit. 1969 

Vol. 8, No. 2 350

Ch. 11

T.15 & 186-2707 

RACING ACT § 186-2702. -Death or disability 

(a) In case of death or verified disability of the stallion, the Administrator may authorize the use of another stallion to serve those mares bred for the last time not less than 30 days before.

The veterinarian must certify the barrenness of the mare. (b) On applying for said authorization the report of services of the dead or disabled stallion must be enclosed. 

Every stallion will have to be identified at the time it enters the Stud for reproduction and each time a change of owners occurs. 

The new owner will identify each stallion offering all the information requested on the back of the formulary to inform the mares served. § 186-2704. 

Rejection of registration

Beginning the year 1969, if a broodmare is covered by more than one stallion in the same heat period, the Administrator shall reject the registration of the foal and this determination shall be final and without appeal. § 186-2705. -Mare pasture bred to stallion

Should a mare be pasture bred to a stallion, the owner of the stallion shall take all necessary measures to protect the mare from being covered by any other horse that there may be in the vicinity. 

The owner of the stallion shall keep a record of the dates on which the mare was placed in the pasture with the stallion as well as the date on which they were separated. 

When breeding stock is leased a copy of the lease should be filed in the Office of the Administrator. The contract shall be notarized. The Administrator shall likewise be informed of the name and address of the person responsible for signing the reports required by this division. § 186-2707. Artificial insemination

No foal begotten by artificial insemination shall be eligible for registration in the Stud Book. 1969 

Vol. 8, No. 2 351.

T.§ 186-2708 

Ch. 11

§ 186-2708. Normal gestation 

A period of 310 to 365 days shall be considered a normal gestation period. In case of abnormal gestation the Report of Birth must be filed within 10 days after date of birth. The Administrator, after investigation, may refuse the registration of such a foal. § 186-2709. Report of Birth; term for filing

The Report of Birth of a foal must be filed within 15 days after the date of birth. The report shall be made in duplicate and in the form supplied by the Administrator. The Administrator shall return a copy of the report to the stud farm to be made part of the Register of Births of the establishment. § 186-2710. Native bred foals-Inspection and tattooing; application (a) The inspection and tattooing of native bred foals shall be applied for before the foals are weaned. (b) The application of Inspection and Tattooing of Native Bred 

Foals shall be accompanied by the following: (1) Fees. (2) Certificate by a private veterinarian stating that the foal has been protected against tetanus. (3) Four 5″ x 7″ pictures of the foal in four different positions: front, both sides and rear. The pictures must show all visible markings of the foal including the heels. 

§ 186-2711. -Inspection and tattooing by veterinarian 

The veterinarian, by order of the Administrator, shall inspect and tattoo the foals before they are weaned. The inspection and tattooing shall be made after the application has been filed. Once the foal has been inspected and tattooed and after the Report of Inspection and Tattooing is submitted by the veterinarian, the Administrator shall approve and order the registration of the foal in the appropriate register. 

§ 186-2712. Registration-Weaned or orphaned foals 

No foal shall be tattooed or registered after it has been weaned. 

In case of orphaned foals or those whose dams are unable to 1969 352 

Vol. 8, No. 2

Ch. 

RACING ACT 

T.15 § 186-2802 nurse them, the foals may be tattooed and registered in those cases in which the Administrator has been notified of the death or disability of the dam within 72 hours of such occurrence. The name of the nursing mare or the method to be used to rear the foal shall also be notified. 

§ 186-2713. -Report to Administrator 

After registration any change in markings that appear in the Report of Birth shall be reported to the Administrator by sworn statement. The Administrator considering the time elapsed and any other circumstances of the case may accept the modification or void the registration of which facts due note shall be made in the register. 

§ 186-2714. Computation of age 

The age of all thoroughbred horses shall be reckened as beginning on the 1st of January of the year in which he is foaled.

Not acceptable The following names shall not be approved by the Administrator: (1) Names currently in use. 200 1969 Vol. 8, No. 2 353

T.§ 186-2802 

Ch. 11 (2) Names consisting of more than 18 letters or more than 3 words (space and punctuation marks will count as letters). (3) Names or nicknames of living persons, unless a written permission from the person whose name or nickname is to be used is submitted. (4) Initials such as C.O.D., F.O.B., C.P.A., etc. (5) Names consisting entirely of numbers such as: One, Six, Two Four Eight, etc. (6) Names registered as stable names or names of breeding establishments. (7) Names of racetracks or classic races. (8) Names of sires of broodmares in stud. (9) Names of horses known for their exceptional performance on the track or in the stud. (10) Names whose pronunciation is similar to names currently in use or names difficult to pronounce or understand. (11) Names of famous or notorious persons. (12) Names considered or which may be considered as advertisements. (13) Names of horses retired from racing or stud until 5 years after their retirement. (14) Registered names of books, theatrical works, moving pictures, popular songs, magazines, newspapers, etc. (15) Names having or suggesting an obscene meaning. (16) II and III as part of a name even though spelled out. (17) Prefixes and suffixes as part of a name. 

Names may be claimed or changed up to 30 days before they are to be entered for racing. Once a horse has started his name cannot be changed except when there are valid reasons for the change or at the request of the Administrator. 

§ 186-2804. Change prohibited 

Names of horses retired for breeding purposes cannot be changed. 

Horses imported from the United States will retain their registered names in the American Stud Book. The names of the horses imported from other countries may be changed provided they have 1969 354 

Vol. 8, No. 2

Ch. 11

RACING ACT 

T.15 $186-2808 not been previously registered in the American Stud Book, when they have not been winners in the country of origin, or when there is valid reason for the change. 

§ 186-2805. Color 

(a) The color of the coat of a foal shall be established as accurately as possible in the report of birth. For that purpose the following shall be used as a guide to colors: 

Bay: Varies from yellowish tan to dark rich auburn. A bay always has a black mane and tail and some black in the legs. 

Dark bay or brown: Borderline color as well as those which are brown inclining to black.

Black: Uniformly black in the body, hand, muzzle, flanks and legs. 

Chestnut: Varies from light yellow to dark liver color. Never has black mane, tail or legs. May have flaxen mane and tail. 

Gray: A mixture of black and white hairs. 

Roan: A mixture of white and red hairs. (b) In case of borderline colors the predominant color shall be used. (c) Any change in the color of the coat of a foal shall be informed to the Administrator immediately. 

§ 186-2806. Description-Information 

The description of the horses to be entered in the register shall be made with clear indication of the basic elements to facilitate their identification. Besides the sex, color of the coat, all marks, cowlicks, scars or any other characteristic that will help and assure the identification must be noted. § 186-2807. -Modification

At the request of interested party and after investigation and approval by the Administrator modification to the description of a horse may be made. If approved by the Administrator, evidence of this approval shall be entered in the register as well as of the resolution granting its approval. § 186-2808. Castration; notice to Administrator

In cases of castration, notice shall be given to the Administrator during the 15 days following the operation by filing a certificate issued by the private veterinarian who performed the operation. 1969 355 

Vol. 8, No. 2

 SECTIONS SUBDIVISION 9. IMPORTED HORSES; REQUIREMENTS; 

CONTROL; INSPECTION 186-2901. Registration of imported horses-Requirements 

186-2902. -Procedure; term 

186-2903. -Additional period 

186-2904. -Order of registration 

186-2905. -Registration without presentation of all documents

§ 186-2901. Registration of imported horses-Requirements 

The thoroughbred horses that may be imported shall be registered in the Register of Imported Horses once the requirements set forth in this division have been complied with. § 186-2902. 

Procedure; term (a) For the registration of a horse in the Register of Imported Horses, an application shall be filed in the Office of the Administrator within the 30 days following the arrival of the horse to Puerto Rico. Evidence of the date of importation must be offered. 

Documents that establish the description, identity and ownership of the horse shall accompany the application as well as a certificate of the horse's past performances and money won in purses.

These documents must be issued by the Stud Book of the country of origin or by competent authority in that jurisdiction and duly legalized and attested. (b) A set of four 5" x 7" pictures taken in four different positions: front, both sides, and from behind, must be enclosed. In the pictures, all markings including the heels must be visible. 

Pictures taken in the country of origin will not be accepted. 

§ 186-2903. Additional period 

If for valid reasons any of the required documents, except the Registration Certificate, cannot be presented within the specified time, the Administrator may approve the registration and shall grant an additional 30 day period for the presentation of said documents. 

§ 186-2904. Order of registration 

Once the description is verified and the identification of the horse made by the veterinarian, the Administrator shall approve the application of registration and order the registration in the Regis- 1969 

Vol. 8, No. 2 356

Ch. 

RACING ACT 

T.15 § 186-3003 ter of Imported Horses. If the horse has not been tattooed at the time of the inspection the veterinarian shall proceed to do so. 

Registration without presentation of all documents § 186-2905. 

The registration of an imported horse in the Register of Imported Horses and for which all documents required have not been presented within the term granted shall not grant the horse the right to race. Such a registration may be cancelled by order of the Administrator. § 186-2906. 

Delivery of certificate to owner 

Once the horse has been registered, the Administrator shall issue and deliver to the owner a certificate of registration.

The natural or artificial person in whose name a horse has been entered in the register shall be recognized as the owner of the horse. 

§ 186-3002. -Transfer 

The transfer of ownership of a horse shall be made by means of a written, notarized document. Said document shall contain the name of the parties to the transfer, the name of the horse, place of the transaction and the selling price. If the horse is bought for breeding purposes, this fact shall be stated in the document. § 186-3003. -Application for transfer; term

The application for transfer shall be filed by the buyer in the Office of the Administrator within the 30 days following the 1969 

Vol. 8, No. 2 357

T.§ 186-3003 

Ch. 11

transaction. The transfer shall be considered made when the buyer obtains the custody and possession of the horse. 

§ 186-3004. -Disapproval of transfer 

The Administrator, for valid reasons, may disapprove an application for transfer. On doing so, he shall notify the parties to the transaction. § 186-3005. Transactions affecting ownership

Every transaction or condition that may affect the ownership of a horse, shall be noted on the appropriate register. Evidence of the reasons affecting the ownership and of the attesting documents must appear in the register. 

§ 186-3006. —Limitations 

The limitations to ownership rights shall only be invalidated by resolution of the Administrator. The Administrator shall issue such resolution after application and supporting documents for the nullification of said limitation have been filed. 

§ 186-3007. Register of Horses of Racing Age-Application 

To be able to start a horse, the breeder or owner must apply for the registration of the horse in the Register of Horses of Racing Age. The registration shall be applied for in the forms supplied by the Administrator for that purpose. § 186-3008. -Death or retirement; notice to Administrator

The breeder, stud farm or owner must notify the Administrator the name of every horse that dies, is retired from racing, is retired from breeding purposes or dropped from the stud, is sold to be exported or is otherwise disposed of. The notification must be made within 30 days of the occurrence of any of the aforementioned events. On receipt and verification of the notification the Administrator shall order the horse to be dropped from the appropriate register. § 186-3009.

Reinstallation No horse retired from racing shall be reinstated. The Administrator may nevertheless, order the reinstallation of a horse when in his judgment said reinstallation would be of benefit to the 1969 

Vol. 8, No. 2 358

Ch. T.15 § 186-3101 

RACING ACT 

racing sport. In every such case, he shall require a certificate from the veterinarian to the effect that such horse is in good condition for racing. § 186-3010. Suspended horse

No transfer of a horse shall be authorized during the term of a suspension from racing. In case of horses whose owners have had their licenses cancelled or have been declared racing nuisances, the transfer may only be made after 90 days have elapsed from the date of the cancellation of the license or the declaration as racing nuisance, provided the authenticity of such transaction is attested with supporting evidence and with the previous approval of the Administrator. § 186-3011. Sale without pedigree; report to Administrator

The sale of a horse without pedigree shall be informed immediately to the Administrator and the certificate of registration shall be returned to the Office of the Administrator for cancellation. 

The horse thus transferred whose registration has been cancelled may not be reinstated and shall not be considered a thoroughbred for any purpose whatsoever. All applications for annotation of a sale without pedigree must be signed by the owner of the horse at the time of making the application indicating the date on which the horse was transferred. Such application may not be made retroactive.

Before the horse is shipped its description and identification must be verified. When so required the certificate of exportation may be complemented with pictures of the horse.

If a horse is not exported after the certificate of exportation has been applied for and issued said certificate must be returned to the Office of the Administrator within the 30 days following the date of issue, proper notation being made in the appropriate register.

Issuance of copies

Copies of the certificate of exportation shall only be issued when at the discretion of the Administrator it is deemed proper. In such case proper notations shall be made in the register. § 186-3105. Return of exported horse

When an exported horse is returned to Puerto Rico he shall be examined by the veterinarian who will identify him and report to the Administrator certifying if the horse is fit for racing. The certificate of registration and a certificate by competent authorities as to past performances and money won in the purses in foreign countries must be also filed in the Office of the Administrator. § 186-3106. Horse exported to be operated on or for treatment

When a horse is exported to be operated on or for treatment, on returning, he shall be examined by the veterinarian who shall identify him and report to the Administrator certifying if he is fit for racing. Likewise, a certificate by the private veterinarian who operated on or treated the horse must be filed. For the reinstalation of the horse for racing or breeding the corresponding fees must be paid. § 186-3107. Export of brood mare

§ 186-3201. Officials-Designation 

(a) The Administrator shall designate the officials for the supervision of the breeding establishments. Said officials shall be authorized to: (1) Inspect the breeding establishments as to organization. (2) Verify the description and identity of the horses registered in the establishments. (3) Inspect the broodmares and foals. (4) Ratify or rectify markings and special characteristics that may be observed on the inspected horses. (5) Make any investigation on matters of technical or sanitary interest. (6) Make the investigation and inspections they might consider necessary to verify the observance of this division. (b) The officials shall leave evidence of their inspections in the appropriate registers showing the date of the inspection and signing the notations. § 186-3202. 

Reports to Administrator 

The designated officials shall make written reports of their visits to the establishments. They must inform immediately to the Administrator any events that might affect the rearing of the horses as well as any violation to these rules. 

§ 186-3203. -Preferent attention 

The officials shall pay preferent attention to the description and identification of the horses. § 186-3204. -Advice to breeders and owners

The officials and employees of the Office of the Administrator shall advise the breeders and owners to facilitate the compliance with this division. 1969

SUBDIVISION 15. REPEALING CLAUSE DIVISION 3. SWEEPSTAKES SUBDIVISION 1. DEFINITIONS 

186-4001. Definitions 

§ 186-4001. Definitions 

The following words and definitions shall have the following meaning. The use of the masculine gender includes the feminine and neuter and the singular includes the plural, and the plural includes the singular, unless otherwise clearly indicated in the text. (1) "Administrator": Racing Administrator. (2) "Sales agent": Person designated by the Association subject to the approval of the Racing Administrator to sell sweepstake tickets. (3) "Association": An individual or corporation authorized to operate a racetrack in Puerto Rico and appointed by the Racing Board to operate and control sweepstake gambling. (4) "Ticket": Printed form consisting of two parts numbered by serial numbers and which gives its owner the right to participate in the sweepstake drawings. (5) "Option ticket": Ticket drawn from the drums entitled to a prize and to participate in the final drawing for the distribution of the post positions in the sweepstake race. (6) "Official sweepstake ticket": That portion of a sweepstake ticket which is retained by the authorized seller and which afterwards is used to determine the winners of the sweepstake prizes. (7) "Drawing committee": Committee composed of the Racing

Administrator or his representative, one representative from the Association and one person appointed by the Racing Board to fulfill the functions specified in this division or by order of the Racing Board. 1972 

Vol. 11, No. 4 363

T.§ 186-4001 

Ch. 11

(8) "Sweepstake fund": The gross income from the sale of sweepstake tickets before making any deduction, but without taking into consideration the commission which corresponds to the agents for the sale of same. 

(9) "Educational Fund": Fund created by Act No. 64, approved on June 24, 1969 [18 L.P.R.A. §§ 841 to 844], at the First Ordinary Session of the Sixth Legislative Assembly. 

(10) "Net sweepstake fund": Income which is left from the sale of sweepstake tickets after deducting the commission for the agents who sell the sweepstakes and all operating expenses and disbursements connected with or related to the sweepstake operation. 

(11) "Board": Puerto Rico Horse Racing Board. 

(12) "Judges": Judges of the horse races. (13) "Official sweepstake office": The place designated as the site to which the agents must present, deliver and register the sold, unsold and void tickets and the income from the sale of same. (14) "Post position": Position assigned to a horse at the starting gate for the beginning of a race. (15) "Ticket receipt": The part or portion of a sweepstake ticket which is handed to the buyer of same by the authorized seller when sale of same is effected. (16) "Drawing": Sweepstake drawing: process to determine the tickets eligible to participate in the distribution of prizes. (17) "Sweepstakes”: A drawing or a distribution of prizes or a series of drawings or a series of prize distributions which refer to the results of a horse race designated for that purpose according to this division.

SUBDIVISION 2. AUTHORIZATION 186-4021. Authorization by Board 

186-4022. Requirements 

§ 186-4021. Authorization by Board 

No sweepstake gambling may be carried out in Puerto Rico without the authorization of the Horse Racing Board. The Board, through an Order to this effect, shall not authorize more than 2 sweepstakes per year and shall determine the date and place where said sweepstakes will be held and the Association which will conduct and control said sweepstakes. The Board's determination will be made taking into consideration primarily where the greatest success can be expected for the purposes sought by authorizing this gambling, which are set forth in the preamble.

§ 186-4031. Ticket-Value

The printing of the tickets shall be the responsibility of the 

Association which must comply with the following requirements: (1) The format of the tickets must be approved by the Administrator. (2) The amount of tickets to be printed for each drawing must be approved by the Administrator. (3) The printing company which is given the job of printing the tickets must post a bond in the name of the Association, the 

Horse Racing Administration and the Puerto Rico Government guaranteeing faithful compliance with the printing order, exactness in the numbering, and the safety and fidelity of the issue. (4) Once the tickets are printed they must be delivered to the Administrator who will check them for exactness. The delivery of the tickets must be accompanied by a statement from the printer certifying the amount and numbers of the ticket issued and stating that all the printed tickets and even the damaged tickets have been delivered. (5) The Administrator shall hand over to the Association periodically and upon written request of the latter, groups of tickets to be placed on sale, and shall keep the corresponding records. 

§ 186-4033. Responsibility of the Association 

The Association shall be responsible to the public treasury for all the tickets which are delivered to it by the Administrator. 

§ 186-4034. Description 

Each sweepstake ticket shall consist of 2 parts and shall be numbered by a serial number. Both parts of each ticket shall have the same serial number and shall be identical in all aspects, with the exception of one part which shall be marked "Sweepstake Ticket Receipt". The part identified as "Sweepstake Ticket Receipt" shall not be transferable, saleable and does not need to be retained nor to be presented in order to collect the prize. The part marked as "Official Sweepstake Ticket" shall be retained by the authorized seller of same, who shall deliver it together with the money from the sale of same (less the commission for the sweepstake selling agent) to the cashier designated by the Association to receive same at the official sweepstake office, at the hour set for delivery, which in all cases shall be prior to the hour set for closing the sweepstakes. 1972

Space shall be provided on both parts of the tickets for the name and address of the owner and the buyer shall indicate same. 

§ 186-4036. -Void 

No ticket will be considered void unless both parts are returned to the sweepstake office. Every sweepstake selling agent must pay $1 for each ticket he damages, mutilates or voids, unless both parts of same are returned to the sweepstake office. Money received from this source shall be included in the sweepstakes fund. § 186-4037. -Sale to minors

No tickets will be sold to persons who are or who seem to be under 18 years of age, but this shall not be considered as a prohibition to purchase a ticket by anyone of 18 years or over to be given by this person and for said ticket to be issued in the name of and for the benefit of a person under 18 years of age. § 186-4038. -Sale by authorized agents

The sale of sweepstake tickets shall only be made by authorized agents. Sale of tickets outside the territory of Puerto Rico and using the mail services for the sale of same is prohibited. § 186-4039. -Sale by machine 

Sweepstake tickets may be sold manually or through machines. § 186-4040. Reasons for denial

No ticket shall be sold to and no prize shall be paid to any of the following persons: (1) Any member of the Horse Racing Board, the Horse Racing 

Administrator, or any officer or employee of the Horse Racing

Administration. 

(2) Any officer, director or employee of the Association. (3) The spouse, child, brother, sister or father or mother of any of the above-mentioned persons who live in the same home. 

§ 186-4041. -Validity 

No sweepstake ticket shall be valid and the owner of same shall not be eligible to receive a sweepstake prize until and unless the official sweepstake ticket and the money which represents the purchase price of same (less the commission corresponding to the 1972 366.1

SUBDIVISION 4. SALES AGENTS SECTIONS 

186-4061. Sales agent-Commission 186-4062. 186-4063. -Bond 186-4064. 186-4065. -Designation -Responsibility -Definition 

§ 186-4061. Sales agent-Commission 

A commission is herein established of 10 percent for the sweepstake sales agents of all the sweepstake tickets sold by them.

Every sweepstake sales agent may deduct on the spot said commission from the money of all the sweepstake tickets sold by him. 

§ 186-4062. Designation 

Horse racing agents may be designated by the Association as sweepstake selling agents. § 186-4063. -Bond 

The Association may require that the sweepstake sales agents post a bond for a reasonable amount. § 186-4064.

Responsibility The sweepstake sales agents shall be responsible for the material and/or equipment delivered to them by the Association and must guarantee same. The Association will be authorized to require periodic reports from the agents regarding tickets sold, retained and damaged. The agents will remit the amount of the tickets sold and shall deliver all official unsold tickets and void tickets to the official sweepstake office within the periods which the Association sets forth for this purpose. 

§ 186-4065. -Definition

A sweepstake sales agent shall be considered as an agent of the purchaser of a sweepstake ticket and shall not be considered as an agent or employee of the Association, or the Administration, or the Government of Puerto Rico for any purpose, or shall the Association, the Horse Racing Administration or the Government of Puerto Rico be obliged or responsible for any act committed by said agent. 1972 

Vol. 11, No. 4 366.2

Ch. 11

RACING ACT 

T.15 186-4081 

The Association shall be obliged and shall be responsible for any sweepstake ticket sold or the money collected by any sweepstake sales agent, only when the official sweepstake ticket and the money which represents the respective sales of the sweepstake tickets corresponding (less the commission corresponding to the sweepstake sales agents) have been simultaneously handed over to the cashier designated by the Association to receive same at the official sweepstake office prior to the hour set to close the sweepstakes.

 § 186-4082. Net amount, distribution 

The net amount of the sweepstake fund, which shall be the amount remaining in the sweepstake fund after the authorized deductions, shall be distributed in the following way: (1) 70 percent in prizes to the public (2) 30 percent to be deposited and credited to the Educational 

Fund. 

§ 186-4083. -Special race 

For the purposes of implementing the grand drawing, the holding of a special race is authorized; Provided, That the cash prize for this race will be charged as a legitimate operation expense of the sweepstake fund. This race shall not be considered valid for the pool betting and the procedure to determine positions at the starting gate shall not be subject to the general provisions of the Horse 

Racing Regulations [§§ 186-1 to 186-1501 of this title] but will be subject to the Drawing Rules. The organization and development of the race and the conduct of the personnel taking part in same, except as above provided, shall be ruled by the Horse Racing Regulation in the usual and present manner. § 186-4084. -Distribution of costs and expenses

It is hereby authorized that any expense or susceptible amortization cost, according to the best accounting practices, may be so made for the purposes of making a more reasonable distribution of said costs and expenses and not affect the fund in a determined year. 

§ 186-4085. -Equipment for functioning and operation 

All equipment which is acquired for the functioning and operation of the sweepstake fund and which is paid from this shall be considered property of the People of Puerto Rico and the Administrator shall be obliged to establish the accounting of same in the usual and present manner which the Regulations on Property belonging to the People of Puerto Rico establish. § 186-4086.

§ 186-4101. Prizes 

An amount equal to 70 percent of the net sweepstake fund shall be distributed to the public as prizes in the manner which is hereinafter indicated. 

§ 186-4102. Classification of prizes 

The following 4 kinds of prizes will be distributed to the public in relation to each sweepstake: (1) Grand drawing grand prize (2) Grand drawing consolation prize (3) Monthly special prize (4) Monthly consolation prizes. 

§ 186-4103. -Distribution 

The prizes to be distributed to the public shall be assigned as follows: 

(1) "Grand drawing grand prize". 70 percent of the remaining amount of the total prize money after deducting the amounts as- 1972 366.5 

Vol. 11, No. 4

T.§ 186-4103 

Ch. 11

Seka.c signed for the special monthly prize and the monthly consolation prizes. (2) "Grand drawing consolation prize". 30 percent of the remaining amount of the total prize money after deducting the amounts assigned for the special monthly prize and the monthly consolation prizes. (3) "Monthly special prizes". $6,750 for each calendar month during which tickets are sold for the sweepstakes to which the respective prizes pertain, except for the calendar month immediately preceding the month and the month during which a drawing is scheduled, to determine the winners of the grand and grand consolation prizes. (4) "Monthly consolation prizes". $1,875 for each calendar month during which tickets are sold for the sweepstakes to which the respective prizes pertain, except for the calendar month immediately preceding the month and the month during which a drawing is scheduled, to determine the winners of the grand and grand consolation prizes.
