§ 186-4104. Drawing Committee 

In order to carry out the drawings, a Drawing Committee is hereby created composed of the persons indicated in sec. 1864101 (7) of this title. Its members will appoint a chairman and a secretary from their number. The secretary will record the minutes of all Committee proceedings and will keep the books, records and documents of the committee. 

§ 186-4105. Public drawings 

All drawings shall be open to the public and to the press and shall be supervised by the Drawing Committee. 

§ 186-4106. Drawing rules 

The rules for the drawings shall be submitted by the Association to the Horse Racing Board for its approval and once approved they shall be published at least twice during a period of 15 days in 2 newspapers of general circulation in Puerto Rico, with at least 

15 days prior notice to the first drawing. 1972 

Vol. 11, No. 4 366.6

Ch. 

RACING ACT 

T.15 § 186-4110 § 186-4107. Selection of person drawing tickets

The Drawing Committee shall appoint the persons who will intervene in the drawing of the tickets with prize options; it shall make the corresponding determinations with regard to the tickets and its decisions on these points shall be final and unappealable. 

§ 186-4108. Void tickets 

The following tickets shall be considered void: (1) Any ticket, card paper or any other thing which is not a genuine sweepstake ticket printed and issued by the Association, including any falsification, facsimile or copy of a genuine ticket. (2) Any sweepstake ticket receipt. (3) Any ticket which is not included in the drawing. (4) Any ticket which does not show the name or the address of the owner thereof. (5) Any ticket which only indicates the name of the owner thereof and not the address. (6) Any ticket which only indicates the address of the owner thereof, but does not show the name of the owner. (7) Any ticket issued to an ineligible person to take part in the sweepstakes and to receive any prizes under the provisions of this division. (8) Any ticket which has been marked "VOID" on the face of same. (9) Any ticket which the Association has reported to the Horse Racing Administrator as void, which has been lost or which has not been returned in accordance with this division. § 186-4109. Prize fund increased due to void tickets

If a ticket is void, but this fact is not discovered when it is. first examined, any prize which may correspond to said ticket shall increase the prize fund of the next drawing. § 186-4110. Payment of mutilated ticket

If on a winning ticket the name and/or address of the owner does not appear clearly legible, or if any portion of a ticket is mutilated or where only part of the name and address of the owner appears, such ticket or portion of ticket shall be placed in the winners drum as though it were legible or as though it were a whole ticket. If the owner can be identified by the Drawing Committee within a period of 60 days after the date of the drawing, 1972 

Vol. 11, No. 4 366.7

T.15 186 

Ch. 11 he shall be entitled to receive any prize which corresponds thereto. 

If the owner cannot be identified within that period of time, the ticket shall be declared void by the Drawing Committee and the prize which corresponds to said ticket will increase the prize fund of the drawing following the date of said void declaration. 

§ 186-4111. Eligibility for grand prize drawing 

All the tickets included in a drawing for the special monthly prize and monthly consolation prizes, including all the tickets which won prizes in one or more monthly prize drawings shall remain eligible for and shall be included in the next scheduled drawing for a grand drawing prize and grand drawing consolation prizes. 

§ 186-4112. -Reimbursement of amount 

The owner of a valid ticket which for some reason has not been included in the drawing for which it was sold shall only be entitled to reimbursement of the amount of same. 

§ 186-4113. Option for post position 

For the purpose of the drawing, option tickets shall be assigned for each post position at the starting gate from number 1 to number 14 regardless of the number of horses entered, of the number of horses who take or took part in the race and, regardless of whether there may be horses grouped as one or more entries or as a field in the race used to determine the prize winners. 

§ 186-4114. Entry or field 

For the purpose of the sweepstake prizes, horses grouped as one entry or as a field shall be considered individually as they finish in the officially announced finishing order. § 186-4115. (b) Copies of such lists shall be delivered to the Horse Racing Administrator and sent to each sweepstake sales agent who will be obliged to display same in their respective places of business where they sell the tickets. The prizes shall be paid by checks payable to the persons whose name or names appear on the winning tickets. § 186-4173. Claim, expiration

The right to claim prizes will expire 6 months from the day the prize is won, and the unclaimed money for this concept will be sent immediately by the Association to the Secretary of the Treasury of Puerto Rico to be credited to the Educational Fund, with a copy of same to the Horse Racing Administrator. § 186-4174. (b) Inasmuch as the Association shall earn no monetary benefit from the Sweepstake Program, the cost of said bond shall be considered as an operating expense of the Sweepstake Program and shall be paid from the sweepstake fund. § 186-4175. § 186-4201. Auditing 

(a) Thirty days after effecting the drawing of the prizes, the horse racing Administrator shall have all the accounts of all receipts and disbursements of money and charges related to the sweepstake audited by personnel of the Horse Racing Administration or by an independent qualified person or company contracted by him for this purpose, in which case the fees of said independent auditor shall be considered as an operating expense of the Sweepstake Program and shall be payable from the sweepstake fund. (b) A certified copy of the auditor's report shall be supplied to the Association and to the Board by the Horse Racing Administrator within 10 days after having received it. § 186-4202. The Association shall submit a report to the Horse Racing Administrator and to the Horse Racing Board on or before the 28th day of February of each year, including therein a complete breakdown of all the sweepstakes effected during the previous calendar year and any recommendation for amendments to the regulations and/or legislation which the Association considers advisable.

§ 186-4231. Declared official winners 

For the purposes of the sweepstakes, the winning horses shall be those who are declared official winners by the judges immediately after the race and without any consideration of the fact that said horse or horses may be or will be subsequently penalized or even deprived of the prize because of some violation. § 186-4232. Provisions of this division

The provisions of this division and the drawing rules shall govern the manner to carry out the sweepstakes and all matters which are related to same. The buyers of sweepstake tickets and all persons whose names appear on same shall be bound by the provisions of this division and the drawing rules. 

§ 186-4233. Decision by Horse Racing Board 

In case of any dispute or controversy which might arise between the Association and any buyer of a sweepstake ticket, the person whose name appears on same and/or who holds same, or in the case of any claim of any kind on the part of said person against the Association which arises from or in connection with the sale, purchase, ownership or possession of any sweepstake ticket, the way to effect any sweepstake or the payment or distribution of any prize, such claim, dispute or controversy shall be submitted for determination to the Horse Racing Board by written petition by any of the parties, within 10 days after such dispute, controversy or claim arises. 

§ 186-4234. Advertising the sale of tickets 

It is hereby authorized to announce the sale of tickets and to announce the drawings to be made at the place of sale and at any other place by any means which may be considered appropriate. 

The cost of such announcements shall be considered as an operating expense of the Sweepstake Program. 1972

294-1. Requirements for issuance of licenses

For the issuance or renewal of a cockpit license it shall be an indispensable requirement that the person or entity applying have complied with the indicated requirements and corrected the de ficiencies noted by the Public Recreation and Parks Administration representatives in their inspection visit to the cockpit. In addition, such person or entity shall furnish the Public Recreation and Parks Administration with the following documents, which shall remain on file as part of his license papers: (1) A copy of the deed or agreement, duly certified, which proves that the cockpit is the property of the applicant or that he has it under contract of lease, if there is no copy of the deed or agreement filed with the Parks Administration. 

(2) A certificate of the Department of Public Health proving that the establishment and its dependencies fulfill all health conditions and requirements. (3) Certificate of the Fire Department showing that the cockpits and dependencies fulfill all safety conditions and requirements. 367

T.§ 294-1 Ch. 17 

(4) Application blank for license or renewal duly filled out and signed by the applicant, accompanied by the amount of money fixed by law for the class of his cockpit. (5) License application blanks of the three judges prescribed by law, duly filled out and signed by them, and accompanied by two 2" x 2" photographs of each and the amount of their license fee. (6) In case of renewal, return of the previous license of the cockpit.

§ 294-2. Rights and duties of cockpits according to class (a) First-Class Cockpit: The cockpit so classified shall have one barrier and may hold as many competitions weekly as desired. 

It is authorized to accept fights with unlimited stakes and to charge a maximum price of $8 for a ringside seat. 

(b) Second-Class Cockpit: The cockpit so classified shall have one barrier and may hold three competitions weekly, on days specified by the Public Recreation and Parks Administration. It is authorized to accept fights with stakes up to $1000 and to charge a maximum price of $6 for a ringside seat. 

(c) Third-Class Cockpit: The cockpit so classified shall have one barrier and may hold two competitions weekly on days specified by the Public Recreation and Parks Administration. It is authorized to accept fights with stakes up to $500 and to charge a maximum price of $4 for a ringside seat. 368

Ch. 

COCKFIGHTING 

T.15 § 294-3 

(d) Fourth-Class Cockpit: The cockpit so classified shall have one barrier and may hold two competitions weekly on days specified by the Public Recreation and Parks Administration. It is authorized to accept fights with stakes up to $200 and to charge a maximum price of $2 for a ringside seat. 

(e) Fifth-Class Cockpit: The cockpit so classified shall have one barrier and shall hold one competition weekly on a day specified by the Public Recreation and Parks Administration. It is authorized to accept fights with stakes up to $100 and charge a maximum price of $1 for a ringside seat. 

(f) Sixth-Class Cockpit: The cockpit so classified shall have one barrier and may hold competitions only on Sundays of each week during the time authorized by its license. It is authorized to accept fights with stakes up to $50 and may charge a maximum price of $.50 for a ringside seat.

Provided, That the cockpit which charges a higher price for a ringside seat than the maximum price fixed for its class or which holds competition on a day not assigned, shall be punished with a fine of not less than $25 nor more than $100, its license being suspended until the fine is paid. § 294-3. Requirements for acting as judges in the cockpits

Any person, in order to act as barrier judge, deputy barrier judge or registration judge, shall know how to read and write. The former two shall approve a written and oral examination before they are authorized as such by the Public Recreation and Parks Administration of Puerto Rico, through a license or official receipt of payment. 

Furthermore, before a judge renews his license it shall be an indispensable requirement that he attend at least one of the clinics offered throughout the Island, notice of which will appear in the press. Such clinics will be offered to judges by an official of the 

Public Recreation and Parks Administration, and shall consist of an explanation of the law and regulations in force for cockfighting. A record of attendance shall be carried, wherein the judges shall affix their signatures as evidence of their attendance at said clinics.

§ 294-4. Reports by cockpit owners

It shall be the duty of each cockpit owner to keep a complete register of all fights held at each competition and to send in writing to the Administration, within two working days following the holding of the competition and on the blanks furnished for the purpose to each cockpit by the Administration, the following information: (1) Name of the barrier judge officiating and his license number. (2) Number of fights held. (3) Stake of each fight. (4) Name of the owner of each cock. (5) Winner of each fight. (6) Kind of spurs used. (7) Weight of each cock. (8) Approximate attendance at the competition. (9) Approximate amount of money bet. (10) Cocks killed or disabled during competition. (11) Cocks which fled during competition.

Noncompliance with this obligation on the part of the cockpit owner shall be sufficient cause for suspension of his cockpit license for the time determined by the Public Recreation and Parks Administration. § 294-5. Failure to renew license 

Any cockpit authorized by the Public Recreation and Parks

Administration which does not renew its license during a season shall lose its rights to the renewal of the same. § 294-6. Clocks; bells

All cockpits with licenses from the Public Recreation and Parks Administration shall be required to have, placed in view of the public, a clock, electric or ordinary, to keep the prescribed time of duration of the fights and such clock shall be equipped with buzzer or bell which sounds to announce the end of the time set for the fights. If this clock is electric, the cockpit shall also have an ordinary clock with a bell, which shall be synchronized with the electric clock in every fight. In case, due to any accident, the current is interrupted or the electric clock stops, the time shall continue to be measured by the ordinary clock. The time of the fight shall end officially when the clock sounds. Each cockpit shall also have a special clock (approved by the Public Recreation and

Parks Administration) for the use of the barrier judge pursuant to the regulations of cockfights [division 2 of this subchapter]. 

Failure to comply with these requirements shall be cause for suspending a cockpit's license until it does comply. 

§ 294-7. Ringside seat for Administration 

Every cockpit shall have, marked with the letters "A.P.R.P.", a ringside seat at the side of the barrier judge's seat, available for the official use of the Administration. § 294-8. Notice of resignation by barrier judge

In case a barrier judge decides to resign his position he shall notify the cockpit owner and the Public Recreation and Parks Administration in writing 15 days prior to the date on which he is to retire from his position; Provided, That if he leaves his position without complying with this requirement his license shall definitely be suspended. § 294-9. Interference by cockpit owner; charges against barrier judge

No cockpit owner shall interfere in any form with the direction and decision of the cockfights, but if in his judgment, the barrier judge acts incorrectly or inefficiently, such action being a reflection on his cockpit, he may bring charges before the Public Recreation and Parks Administration. § 294-10. Tournament, classic, and joust defined (a) "Tournament" means a competition where a number of stables bring a specific number of cocks, each at a certain weight. (b) "Classic" means a competition in which prizes and/or trophies honoring the memory of a person are offered to the owner of the cock which finishes the fight in the shortest time or which fights the best in the competition. Provided, that not more than one classic a year shall be held to the memory of any one person. (c) "Joust" means a struggle of one stable or of a group of stables against equal force in a certain number of fights in which prizes or trophies are offered to the stable or group of stables which wins the greater number of fights. There are three kinds of jousts: local, commonwealth and international. "Local joust" means one in which cocks and sportsmen of the locality are competing; "commonwealth", one in which cocks from various districts of the 

June 30, 1966 

Vol. 5, No. 6 371

T.15 294 

Ch. 17

island are competing; and "international", one in which cocks and sportsmen from foreign countries are competing. § 294-11. Time of beginning weighing-in for scheduling fights

The time of beginning weighing-in for the scheduling of fights is left to the discretion of the owner or administrator of each cockpit, the only requirement for commencing the weighing-in being the presence of the registration judge, who shall keep a register of the fights scheduled, noting the conditions established for each fight. The registration judge shall not register any fight unless the persons matching the cocks are authorized to, and have the stake to put on the fight when their turn comes. This register of fights. scheduled in each competition held shall be preserved by the cockpit owner and shown to the representatives of the Public Recreation and Parks Administration at any time on request. 

Before the start of the competition, there shall be copied for the information of the public, on the blackboard which each cockpit shall have for this purpose, the scheduled fights in order, indicating the owner, weight, and spurs, and also the stake. § 294-12. Exhibition cages

Every cockpit shall have, in public view, but out of reach, as many pairs of cages as it wishes, for placing the cocks for the scheduled fights. Only as many fights may be scheduled as the cockpit has exhibition cages. § 294-13. Night competitions 

Before holding night competitions, every cockpit must first secure an authorization from the Public Recreation and Parks Administration, which authorization may be suspended if it is deemed contrary to the peace and quiet of the neighbors. These competitions shall be subject to the following conditions: (1) Not more than one gate ticket shall be charged. (2) No fight may begin after the clock strikes 11 p.m. (3) Every permit for night competition shall be subject to the condition that the zone commander commit himself to appoint an officer for the maintenance of order during the program.

COCKFIGHTING 

§ 294-14. Season for practice of the sport in the cockpits

The season for the practice of the sport in the authorized cockpits shall commence the first day of November and shall end the thirty-first of August and all licenses issued to cockpits by the 

Public Recreation and Parks Administration shall expire the thirty first of August of each year.

No cockpit shall hold any cockfight during the period between the first of September and the thirty-first of October, both dates inclusive. A cockpit discovered to be holding any cockfight during the period expressly prohibited shall be considered a clandestine cockpit. § 294-15. Appeals from decisions of barrier judge

Only the person recognized by the barrier judge as owner of a cock may appeal to the Public Recreation and Parks Administration from the decision of a barrier judge. The cock owner who wishes to appeal a decision shall personally inform the barrier judge in the act of making the decision of his intention to protest it, and within the two working days following the day of the competition shall file with the Public Recreation and Parks Administration his appeal under oath before a notary. The Public Recreation and Parks Administration shall not consider protests or appeals arising from decisions of appreciation of the barrier judge or that do not fulfill the requirements mentioned above. § 294-16. Cages for fighting cocks in turn

Every cockpit shall have in an adequate place next to the ring entrance, two cages of three compartments each, screened and mosquito-proof, where there shall be placed under lock, duly armed and prepared, the pairs of cocks whose turns follow that of the pair that are fighting. The cocks which are to wear artificial spurs may have them so placed without their being tied on, the tying to be done just before they are taken to the ring. Provided, that for purposes of determining the number of fights each cockpit may schedule, these cages shall be considered as exhibition cages. § 294-17. Identification of foreign cocks

The Public Recreation and Parks Administration shall mark every foreign chicken or fighting cock introduced or imported into Puerto Rico with a tattoo under one of its wings which tattoo shall 

June 30, 1968 

Vol. 7, No. 6 373

T.§ 294-17 

Ch. 17 consist of the letters X.Y.Z. Provided, that no breeder of cocks of Puerto Rico shall use the same tattoo to identify his breed. § 294-18. Expiration of permits for construction or moving 

Every cockpit authorized, through permission of the Parks Administration, to be built or moved, shall be completed and ready for inspection within one year of granting the authorization. § 294-19. Police charged with supervision of order in cockpits (a) It is strictly forbidden to set up billiards, slot machines or any other game-of-chance equipment in cockpits or dependencies thereof. (b) Any natural or artificial person who violates the provisions of these Regulations shall be punished with a fine of not less than $25 nor more than $500 and/or the suspension of his cockpit or judging license for a period of not more than one year. Provided, that any punishment infringing on this section is hereby repealed. (c) The Police of Puerto Rico shall be responsible for the preservation of order in the public cockpits of Puerto Rico and for compliance with the law of this division.

§§ 294-71 to 294-86. Repealed. Regulation app. May 7, 1968; File

Sections 294-71 to 294-86 of this title, which were from the 

New Administrative Regulation for the Sport of Cockfighting in Puerto Rico, app. by Public Recreation and Parks Administrator July 23, 1956, File No. 64, were tacitly repealed in 

1968. See note under 294-87 of this title. § 294-87. Cocks not acceptable for fighting

All barrier judges are strictly prohibited from accepting any cock to fight: (1) With unclipped comb or wattles, except on such occasions as the Administrator may provide to the contrary. (2) If it is not plucked or trimmed as follows: the cut of the feathers shall begin 2 inches from the posterior base of the comb, and in such a way that the trunk of each feather measures, down to the shoulder, not less than ¾4 of an inch in length. (3) If its cravat or neck plate is plucked or cleaned. (The cravat is the part of a cock's neck between the lower part of the bill and upper part of the breast). (4) If it is piropo or Japanese (a cock whose neck does not grow any feathers). (5) If its head, neck and spurs have not been previously washed with cotton dipped in pure ether or any other solution medically proven as more efficient. This washing shall be done before the fight begins, inside the ring, in the presence of the cock's owners after they have refreshed the cocks. If, after washing, the cock is still not free from grease, the judge shall, in his judgment, cancel the fight. 

After the cocks are washed, the judge shall not allow their head or neck to be touched by hand, handkerchief, or in any other manner. (6) If it is not completely ready for the fight; that is, it shall not be armed, sharpened, cut or tied inside the ring. The adhesive tape, ribbon or any other material used to attach the spurs shall cover a continuous area not exceeding one (1) inch around and from the lower part of the cock's legs upwards, and 1/2 an inch downwards. 

June 30, 1968 

Vol. 7, No. 6 375

T.§ 294-87 

Ch. 17 (7) If its body, including legs, back, underside of the pelvis, and under the wings, is not duly cut, except in the case of a bolus cock, when not more than 3 inches shall be left uncut from tail bone to neck. (8) If it acts strange or tense on being confronted with its adversary before being released for starting the fight. (9) If it has been wounded in a previous fight and shows that its wounds have not healed completely. (10) With ringworm or showing that it has had it, and still showing crust of medicine and dry skin or scurf adhering to the neck or head. (11) If it does not fulfill the conditions agreed upon when the fight was concerted, according to the registry of the registration judge. In this case the judge shall retain the stake of the party preventing the fight from being held. (12) If it is not reweighed within the ring, in view of the public, and on a duly verified sable and sacks scale. (13) If the public is not advised, through an announcement, of any advantage of weight or spurs of one cock over another, provided that said advantage exceeds one (1) ounce in weight and one line in natural spurs.

Unmatching of cocks prohibited (a) Once matched and placed in exhibition cages, the cocks shall remain under the power and jurisdiction of the barrier judge, who shall not allow any person to unmatch a cock, without just cause, before 6 p.m. Should anyone act to the contrary, his stake shall be 

June 30, 1968 376

COCKFIGHTING 

retained and delivered to the adversary owner, and a fine equivalent to the stake shall be imposed and sent to the Public Recreation and Parks Administration. After the cock has been armed, carried into the ring, and reweighed, the barrier judge shall accept no reason for unmatching it (except when the cock is not ready for the fight), proceeding to retain the stake of anyone who does so. (b) The barrier judge shall not allow any cock placed in the exhibition cage to be given food or water or attended to in any manner, and he shall, within the following 48 working hours, report any such violation to the Public Recreation and Parks Administration. The Administrator shall determine whether a suspension is in order or what kind of punishment is to be imposed. 

§ 294-89. Use of artificial spurs 

The barrier judge shall admit to the fight cocks armed with every type of artificial spurs, the selection of which shall be left to the discretion of the cock's owner; Provided, That said cock owners shall, before the registration judge who shall take note, agree as to the kind and length of spurs to be used. If no agreement has been reached on the kind of spurs to be used, the barrier judge shall admit natural and artificial cock spurs only. The barrier judge shall gather information on the conditions of each fight from the registry prepared by the registration judge. In case one party refuses to comply with the agreement when his turn to fight arrives, the barrier judge shall retain his stake, as provided by section 294-88 of this title; Provided, That no claim as to kind of spurs used shall be considered after the fight has ended. § 294-90. Flight by cock during first minute of combat (a) A fight shall be invalid when a sound cock flees during the first minute of fight; (section 294–102 of this title) shall apply. (b) The barrier judge shall declare invalid any fight in which one of the cocks abandons the combat within the first minute after the start of the fight, fleeing without returning to fight; Provided, That the barrier judge shall, at the beginning of each fight, adjust the special clock to sound at the end of the first minute of fighting. § 294-91. Fixed fights

The barrier judge shall declare invalid for all purposes any fight which in his judgment has been fixed or tampered with.

§ 294-92. Picking up cocks (a) No cock owner or trainer, or any other person, may seize or pick up a cock during a fight, conceding it to have lost, without the barrier judge's authorization; Provided, That the barrier judge may, without awaiting the regulation count, authorize a cock to be picked up, declaring it to have lost, when, because of having received punishment rendering it defenseless, or its spurs having been broken or becoming lose, said cock remains, in the judge's opinion, at the mercy of its adversary. (b) When a cock owner, trainer or any other person seizes or picks up a cock without authorization, the barrier judge shall impose a fine of 25 dollars, reporting his action to the Public Recreation and Parks Administration, and having the cock enter the fight again. § 294-93. Duration of day fights 

No fight may begin after the clock strikes 6 p.m., except night tournaments. § 294-94. Fight turns

After all fights have been matched, their turn shall be obtained through a drawing held in view of the public, using numbered balls. This drawing shall not be held before 8 a.m.; Provided, That if the turn of the fight arrives and one or both cock owners are absent, the barrier judge shall proceed to assign the last turn to said fight; Provided, further, That in case only one adversary is absent, the owner of the opposing cock may demand that his cock. be given to him and the fight annulled. 

§ 294-95. Draws by agreement prohibited 

Draws by agreement are hereby specifically prohibited. The barrier judge shall only declare a fight drawn pursuant to the provisions of this division. 

§ 294-96. Cowardice test 

The barrier judge shall apply the cowardice test in the case prescribed by section 294-97 of this title, and also whenever it may be necessary for the fight decision. He shall submit both cocks to the cowardice test before declaring a draw because of separation for one minute, and when the turn of the fight arrives and the cocks

COCKFIGHTING 

are not fighting at the sound of the bell. The cockpit owner shall at all times have at the barrier judge's disposal, for making this test, a brave cock, plucked and with spurs bandaged, of a weight up to 3 pounds. The judge shall take this testing cock and present him facing the other cock, for which he may move the fighting cock, and will then release the testing cock at a distance of approximately one foot, so that there is an opportunity of immediate contact, until he determines if the cock is fleeing or not; It being understood, That the judge shall not allow the testing cock to punish the fighting cock more than 5 times. The judge shall ascertain the correct weight of the testing cock before the start of the tournament. 

§ 294-97. Duration of fights 

Every fight in which one or more artificial spurs are used shall be considered a fight with artificial spurs. The fights with artificial spurs shall last 20 minutes; the fights with natural ones shall last 

35 minutes, except in case that at the end of the designated fight time the cocks are not fighting, both cocks then being submitted to the cowardice test, in which case the duration of the fight shall be extended to include the time taken by the judge in carrying out said cowardice test. § 294-98. Decision of fights (a) Losses: (1) The barrier judge shall declare a cock to have lost at any moment during the time designated for the fight: (A) When one of the cocks, standing up, is helpless and at the mercy of its adversary, without striking with its feet for one minute, and the opponent has been punishing it during that time. (To punish is to strike with the feet.) (B) When for any reason whatsoever, it is down for one minute, and the opponent is standing. Any cock resting on its knees or body shall be considered as being down. The standing cock, if not pecking at its opponent, shall be submitted to the cowardice test. (C) When it crows in proof of cowardice, providing the adversary is standing. (D) When it jumps over or outside the wall or barrier 3 consecutive times without fighting the 2 times that the barrier judge confronts it with its opponent. The barrier judge shall place both cocks facing each other in the middle of the ring, June 30, 379 1968 

Vol. 7, No. 6

T.§ 294-98 

Ch. 17 holding them by the base of the tail, and releasing them at the greatest distance allowed by the length of his arms, it being understood that the opponent is standing; in case it is lying down, the regulation time provided by par. (1) of subsec. (b) of this section, shall be counted. Provided, That if the cock remains down during the regulation count, while its opponent jumps 3 consecutive times over or outside the wall, the fight shall be a draw. If, on the contrary, it gets up before the regulation count, it shall be submitted to the cowardice test, and the barrier judge shall decide the fight according to the outcome of said test. 

Likewise, the cock who has remained standing inside the ring while its opponent has jumped over or outside the wall for 3 consecutive times without fighting the 2 times that it is confronted with his adversary, shall also be submitted to the test. (2) The barrier judge shall declare a cock to have lost when it flees on being submitted to the cowardice test, (A) during the minute that both cocks stop fighting, (B) at the expiration of the regulation time fixed for the duration of the fight and the cocks are not fighting. (b) The barrier judge shall declare a fight drawn: (1) When at the end of the regular time fixed for the duration of the fight neither of the 2 cocks has been declared to have lost, pursuant to the provisions under subsec. (a) of this same section. (2) When in the course of the same both cocks are down for a minute or both have fled. (3) When both cocks do not flee, on being submitted to the cowardice test: (A) at the expiration of the minute that both cocks stop fighting, (B) at the expiration of the time fixed for the duration of the fight and the cocks are not fighting. (4) When a cock flees on being submitted to the cowardice test, if its opponent has been down for one minute. (5) When, at the expiration of the regulation time fixed for the fight, both cocks, without fighting, are submitted to the cowardice test and neither flees, or both flee. (6) When, during the fight, they stop fighting for one minute and on being submitted to the cowardice test, neither flees or both flee. § 294-99. Appeal from decisions of barrier judge

The direction and decision of every fight rests exclusively with the barrier judge, and only the cock's owner may protest that de-

If at the moment of his decision the barrier judge is advised by the cock's owner that he will appeal said decision to the Public Recreation and Parks Administration, the barrier judge shall retain both stakes. Before the start of the fight, the cock's owner shall identify himself as such to the barrier judge. If he fails to do so, the barrier judge shall recognize as owner only such person who delivered to him the amount of the stake. § 294-100. Fines to be sent by barrier judge to Administration 

Barrier judges shall remit to the Public Recreation and Parks Administration all fines imposed pursuant to the provisions of this division, except stakes forfeited, accompanied with a detailed and precise report specifying the reason for his decision, not later than 

2 working days following the fight. § 294-101. Decision of cases not foreseen in regulations 

Barrier judges are hereby empowered to resolve upon any case occurring in a fight, by accident or any other reason, not foreseen in this division; Provided, That in each of these cases, the barrier judge shall, within the 2 following workings days, render a report to the Public Recreation and Parks Administration, describing the attendant circumstances of the fight and his reasons for his decision. § 294-102. Fleeing cocks

The barrier judge shall cut the feathers on both wings and tail, close to the skin, of any cock that flees. § 294-103. Caught or entangled cocks

When a cock gets caught or entangled in foreign matters inside the ring, the barrier judge may stop the fight and disengage or unhook it and let it fight again. 

§ 294-104. Penalties 

Any violation to this division shall be punished by the Public Recreation and Parks Administration with a fine of not less than 25 dollars nor more than 500 dollars and/or the suspension of the license for a term of not less than one month.

§ 373-2. Definitions 

For the purposes of this subchapter and unless the context of the same clearly indicates otherwise, the following definitions shall be accepted. "Chief of Police" means the Chief of Police of Puerto Rico; "Administrator" means the Public Recreation and Parks Administrator of Puerto Rico; 381

را می کنه . "Marksman" means anyone who devotes himself to or is authorized to participate in the sport of target shooting; "Target shooting" means sport for practicing the use of firearms; "Shot" means discharge of a firearm; "Rifle range" means a place where target shooting is practiced; “Firearm,” means any arm, regardless of the name by which it is known, capable of hurling a missile or missiles by the action of expanding gases; "Person" includes any individual, firm, partnership, association or corporation; "Ammunition" means any bullet, cartridge, projectile, buckshot or any charge that is put or may be put in a firearm to be shot; "Crimes of violence" applies to and includes any of the following crimes, or the attempt to commit any of them: murder in any degree, manslaughter, kidnapping, rape, mayhem, aggravated assault and battery, robbery, burglary, housebreaking, larceny and extortion. 

§ 373-3. Arms defined 

For the purposes of this subchapter, arms to be used in authorized practice of target shooting are defined as follows. (1) Revolver and pistol. 

(A) SEMI-AUTOMATIC, .45 CALIBER PISTOL Any semi-automatic, .45 caliber pistol with a trigger pull of not less than four pounds, the sights may be adjustable but must be open and not more than seven inches apart. 

All the safety features of the arm should work properly. 

Barrel extensions are not permitted. 

(B) CENTRAL-FIRE PISTOL OR REVOLVER — Any cen tral-fire pistol or revolver, .32 caliber or greater; the length of the barrel, including the cylinder, shall not be more than ten inches. The trigger pull shall not be less than two and one-half pounds. The sights may be adjustable but they must be open and not more than ten inches apart. 

(C) .22 CALIBER PISTOL OR REVOLVER Any pistol 

(single-shot or semi-automatic) or revolver using a rim fire .22 caliber cartridge not longer than 1.1 inches and 382

Ch. 23

T.15 § 373-3 

TARGET SHOOTING 

lead or lead alloy bullet not weighing more than 40 grams; the length of the barrel, including the cylinder, shall not be greater than ten inches; the sights may be adjustable, but must be open and not less than ten inches apart. The trigger pull shall not be less than two pounds. (D) FREE PISTOL Pistol of any caliber, any barrel length, without restriction as to trigger pull, with any kind of handle except that no support shall be extended to the forearm. Non-metallic sights are prohibited. (2) Small-caliber rifle. 

(A) .22 CALIBER RIFLE The rifle authorized for small caliber competitions is the .22 caliber rim fire rifle with breech for cartridges commercially designated as the ".22 short," "22 long" or the ".22 long rifle." There are no restrictions as to barrel length or weight of the rifle including accessories. The trigger pull shall not be less than three pounds and it shall not be capable of functioning with set trigger. 

(B) FREE RIFLE 

Any small-caliber rifle without restrictions as to barrel length, set trigger, or any kind of accessories. 

(3) Large-caliber rifle. 

(A) ARMY RIFLE 

Any rifle being used or having been used as a regular service arm of the armed forces of any nation. It must be used without alterations. The trigger pull shall not be less than three pounds. (B) NRA MATCH RIFLE A rifle weighing no more than ten pounds excluding the strap; the trigger pull shall not be less than three pounds, with breech for the .30-06 cartridge and with metallic sights. 

(C) NRA SPORTING RIFLE - Central-fire rifle not weigh ing more than ten pounds excluding the strap, with not less than three pounds trigger pull; the barrel length shall not be greater than 26 inches and the sights shall be metallic. (D) SPECIAL TARGET RIFLE - A central-fire rifle of any caliber or weight; it shall not be equipped with a support for the palm of the hand or with a Schuetzen stock or a set trigger. 383

Licenses for target shooting organizations (a) No license shall be granted to clubs or organizations dedicated to the sport of target shooting which are not constituted as required by law for these groups. The application for a license shall be made by the president and secretary of the club or organization dedicated to the sport of target shooting and the license issued shall permit the practice of the sport only in the place or places authorized by the administrator. Every club or organization dedicated or wishing to be dedicated to the sport of target shooting, shall supply in its license application the following information: (1) Name of the club or organization, (2) Location of the practice ground, (3) Facilities available at the time of application for the practice of the sport, (4) A list in duplicate of all directors and members, including residential and mailing addresses, age, nationality and occupation, and (5) Registration certificate from the Secretary of State of 

Puerto Rico. (b) The Administrator may deny the license applied for by any club or organization: (1) If it does not have 10 or more members; (2) If it has not been favorably recommended by the Chief of Police; 384

Ch. TARGET SHOOTING T.15 § 373-6 

(3) If it does not offer, in his judgment, the necessary facilities for the practice of the sport of target shooting; (4) If it does not offer the minimum public safety requirements; or (5) If it fails to pay a $15 annual license fee. (c) The shooting clubs or organizations shall hold such commonwealth competitions as the Administrator may assign to them unless by force majeure they are prevented from doing so. They shall also be required to hold a minimum of three annual competitions, one of them public, in order for the Administrator to be able to renew their licenses. The secretaries or presidents of shooting clubs or organizations shall inform the Administrator within 10 days of any member who withdraws. In addition to the commonwealth championship competitions that the Administrator may assign them, the shooting clubs or organizations may hold such competitions for the public and for members as they wish. The shooting club or organization shall notify the administrator 10 days in advance of its intention to hold any competition in the club or the organization and shall send a copy of the shooting program. After the contest or competition is held, it shall send in duplicate the complete results of the same to the Administrator, who shall keep a complete file of all the competitions held in all the clubs and shall keep an individual record of each marksman. The Administrator shall attend or shall name a delegate to attend and represent him in these competitions. 

§ 373-5. Commonwealth championships 

Generally

The Administrator shall annually organize and announce the holding of the championships of pistol and revolver shooting, .22 caliber; .38 or more; championships in shooting of army rifles; of .22 caliber rifle; a "skeet" championship and another in "trapshooting" and a special championship in regulation pistol or revolver shooting for officers and classes of the Commonwealth

Police exclusively. These championships shall be held according to the rules of the NRA - National Rifle Association; UIT — "Unión

Internacional de Tiro"; NSSA - National Skeet Shooting Associa tion; ATA - Amateur Trapshooting Association," as the case may be.

§ 373-16. Advisory board 

The Administrator shall designate a board of nine persons of recognized competence in the sport of target shooting, who shall act in the capacity of technical advisers and consultants of the Administrator in all problems that may arise as to the public 

Commonwealth target shooting championships and in the selection of delegations from Puerto Rico to participate in international competitions. 387

$ 373-17. Places and dates

The Administrator shall designate places (clubs) and dates for the holding of the Commonwealth championships sponsored by the Public Recreation and Parks Administration and shall send the program for such championships to the shooting clubs and organizations. The clubs must hold the championships assigned them. 

§ 373-18. Commonwealth champions 

The Commonwealth championships shall be selected on the basis of the best score achieved in the holding of the various Commonwealth championships. The title of champion shall be held by the winner for the period ending with the holding of the next championship. $ 373-19. Forms

The Administrator shall provide the target shooting clubs with forms for applications for licenses to operate, forms to report the results of competitions, and any other forms necessary to carry out the purposes of this subchapter or the Target Shooting Act. 

§ 373-20. Classification of marksmen 

The Administrator shall classify the pistol, revolver, rifle and shotgun marksmen according to the system used by the National Rifle Association, the skeet marksmen according to the rules of the National Skeet Shooting Association and the trap marksmen according to the rules of the Amateur Trapshooting Association. 

The Commonwealth records shall be recognized only when established in official competitions. 

§ 373-21. Intoxicating liquors 

The use, possession, distribution or sale of intoxicating liquors at the range or shooting place, or in the halls or other buildings of the club during the holding of competitions and official championships is prohibited. 

§ 373-22. Storage of firearms 

Keeping or storing firearms and ammunition in the club building or firing places is prohibited. 

§ 373-23. Penalties 

Any violation of the provisions of this subchapter shall constitute a misdemeanor and the person convicted shall be punished 388

§ 505-3. Definitions 

The following terms, whenever used or referred to in these bylaws, set out in this Division, shall have the following meanings, except where the context clearly indicates otherwise: (1) The term "Company" means the Recreational Development 

Company of Puerto Rico. (2) The term "Board" means the Board of Directors of the Company. (3) Words importing the singular number shall include the plural and vice versa, and words importing persons shall include firms, partnerships of all kinds, and corporations. (4) The term "bonds" means bonds, notes, or other evidences of indebtedness or obligations. § 505-5. Seal § 505-4. General powers of the Company 

The Company shall have the general powers enumerated in art. 5 et seq. of the Act [15 L.P.R.A. § 505 et seq.], and such others as may be incidental or inherent to the fulfillment thereof.

505-7. Board of Directors (a) Creation of the Board. The Board shall be composed of 5 1962

members, and the Public Recreation and Park Administrator shall be a member ex officio and Chairman thereof. Of the 4 remaining members, who shall be appointed by the Governor of Puerto Rico, 2 shall be appointed for the term of 2 years and the others for the term of 3 years. Thereafter, as the terms of office of the directors expire, the Governor shall appoint their successors for terms of 4 years, except in cases of death, resignation, or dismissal because of absences, in which case the Governor shall appoint the successors for the duration of the term for which each withdrawn member was appointed. (b) General powers. The Board shall be in charge of the administration and general management of the Company, and it shall specifically exercise the general powers granted thereto by the Act creating the same [15 L.P.R.A. § 501 et seq.]. 

(c) Salary. The members of the Board of Directors shall not receive any salary for their services. Notwithstanding the preceding provision, the Board may, through resolution to that effect, determine and assign a fixed sum for the payment of per diems to its members, when they attend regular and special meetings of the said Board or of the committees as it may create, and it shall authorize the reimbursement of all travel expenses incurred thereby. (d) Absence from meeting. If a director fails, without justifiable reason, to attend three consecutive Board meetings, the Governor may declare his office vacant, and shall fill it as provided by subsec. (a) of this section. (e) Regular meetings. The Board shall hold regular meetings at such place and time and on such date as it may have previously fixed. The Secretary shall call a regular meeting at the request of the Chairman, not less than 5 days before the date of the proposed meeting. (f) Special meetings. The Board shall hold special meetings after the Secretary has issued a call at the request of the Chairman or any 3 directors, not less than 2 days before the date of the said meeting. The call shall specify the purpose of the meeting, as well as the place, time and date and all matters to be considered thereat, and only those matters stated in the call shall be considered at the meeting. (g) Waiving of formalities. Whenever urgent matters require that the Board meet immediately, the requisite of formal call shall be waived and the attendance of directors at the meeting shall 1962 390.3 

Vol. 1, No. 7

T.§ 505-7 

Ch. 25

signify that all formalities of a call as prescribed herein have been waived, and the members attending may then pass upon all matters brought before them. (h) Quorum. Three directors shall constitute quorum to pass upon all matters brought before the consideration of the Board. If less than 3 directors attend the meeting, they may then decide to meet at a subsequent date to pass upon those matters which could not be solved thereat because there was no quorum. However, the directors making such a decision shall invite all members who were absent to attend the said new meeting, and if they in turn do not attend, the directors present may pass upon all matters pending. (i) Agreements of the Board. All agreements of the Board of 

Directors shall be approved by a majority vote of the directors present. In case of a tie vote upon any matter being considered, the same shall be considered and voted upon at the next Board meeting. (j) Minutes. The Secretary of the Board shall keep minutes of all the meetings, which shall be signed by the Chairman and the Secretary after having been duly entered in the minutes book. (k) Committees. The Board may designate, from among its number, such committees as may be necessary to formulate, study, investigate and recommend any action to be taken upon any matter as the Board may consider necessary to the better operation of the Company. 

§ 505-8. Executive officers 

(a) Persons designated. The executive officers of the Company shall be the General Manager, the Assistant Manager, the Secretary, the Treasurer, the Comptroller and those other officers as the Public Recreation and Park Administrator may, with the approval of the Board of Directors, designate as necessary to the Company's management. 

(b) Nominating authority. All executive officers of the Com pany, including the General Manager, shall be appointed by the Public Recreation and Park Administrator, and shall hold office in his discretion. The appointment of the General Manager shall be the only one subject to the Governor's approval. All other officers and employees of the Company shall be appointed by the General Manager according to the norms and procedures as the Public 

Recreation and Park Administrator may approve thereon. 1962 

Vol. 1, No. 7 

390.4

Ch. 25

T.15 § 505-9 

(c) Salary. The salary of the executive officers of the Company, excluding the General Manager, shall be fixed by the Board of Directors through resolution to that effect. The General Manager's salary shall be fixed by the Public Recreation and Park Administrator. (d) Leaves. All such provisions on leave accumulation and enjoyment as the Public Recreation and Park Administrator may promulgate through Bylaws for all the other officials and employees of the Company shall also apply to the executive officers. (e) Absences or disability of executive officers. In case an executive officer is absent or unable to carry out his duties, the Public Recreation and Park Administrator shall appoint a person to hold such office, and, to that effect, the new person shall have all the faculties, duties and responsibilities of the substituted officer. 

§ 505-9. Duties of executive officers 

(a) General Manager. The General Manager shall be the highestranking officer among the Company's executive officers, and, subject to control by the Public Recreation and Park Administrator, he shall have the following duties: (1) To administer, direct, supervise and control all the activities of the Company; also to take care of and keep all properties owned by or under the control of the organization. (2) To plan and recommend to the Board of Directors the 

Company's organization. (3) To create, consolidate or eliminate administrative operating units whenever in his judgment the interests of the Company so require. When it is necessary to create additional units, he shall submit his recommendations to the Public Recreation and Park Administrator for their consideration before the Board. (4) To define, revise and alter, whenever it may be necessary, the functions to be carried out by each operating unit. (5) To determine, create, classify or eliminate all administrative charges as may be necessary for the adequate operation of the organization, all of which he shall do within the framework of the political policy established by the Board, and, in every case, subject to budgetary limitations. (6) To appoint, suspend or remove, according to such norms as the Public Recreation and Park Administrator may establish to that effect, any Company officer or employee, excluding the executive officers. 1962 

Vol. 1, No. 7 390.5

T.§ 505-9 

Ch. 25

(7) To assign all duties and responsibilities to each office he may create. (8) To fix the salary to be paid to any office or offices, all of which shall be done according to the resources available and within a grade of austerity convenient to the interests thereof. (9) Pursuant to determinations passed by the Board, to construct, purchase, sell, lease, maintain, and in any manner dispose of properties of the Company or for the Company, and, in every case, within the limitations of the Organic Act and of this Division. (10) Subject to budgetary limitations and the norms established by this Division, to purchase, sell or lease by contract or any other means, in the name of the Company, all kinds of materials, accessories, tools, machinery and equipment as may be necessary to develop the Company's programs and activities, and to contract for the services necessary and convenient to the organization's operation, maintenance and management. (11) According to the policy established by the Board, to negotiate and enter into agreements in the name of the Company, for the better establishment of workers-employers relations. (12) To modify the terms, conditions or clauses of any contract entered into in the name of the Company, whenever such action is convenient and necessary to facilitate the activities thereof, or whenever the party or parties to such contracts, agreements or transactions have difficulties in the production, delivery or rendering of services that bring or may bring about substantial losses to the parties and/or Company. To that effect, he may, with the authorization of the Public Recreation and Park Administrator, extend the performance of the obligations incurred by the Company, provided that extension does not render useless, as to the aims of the objective being sought, the properties to be delivered or the services to be rendered. (13) To solve, rescind or in any other manner end any lease or contract whenever such action is necessary or convenient in order to protect the interests of the organization, and, in every case, he shall proceed according to law. (14) To delegate those responsibilities as he may soundly deem advisable for the organization's management. (15) To sign, make, or deliver, in the name of the Company and in the manner determined by the Board, every check, voucher, deed, contract, agreement, obligation, commitment and instrument necessary to the discharge of his duties. 1962 

Vol. 1, No. 7 390.6

Ch. 25

T.15 § 505-9 

(16) To select the bank or banks which are to be the depositaries of the Company's moneys, pursuant to the provisions of art. 10 of the Act [15 L.P.R.A. § 510]. 

(17) As may be provided by the Public Recreation and Park Administrator, to have the responsibility of informing the Board on the progress and conditions of all activities of the organization, and to prepare all such reports as the Public Recreation and Park Administrator may, from time to time, request from him. (b) Assistant Manager. The Assistant Manager shall, subject to control by the Public Recreation and Park Administrator, help the General Manager in the discharge of the latter's duties. He shall also exercise all the duties of the General Manager, when the said officer so delegates, or in his absence, or at the Board's orders. 

(c) Secretary. The Secretary shall have the following duties: 

(1) To prepare and keep all minutes of every Board meeting. (2) To call all Board meetings prescribed herein, or have them called. (3) To be custodian of the seal and all documents of the Company, and to see to it that the seal is affixed on every document issued and drawn in the name of the Company. (4) To maintain a register of the names and addresses of all members of the Board, the date on which each member started in office and the expiration date of his term, in order to inform the Chairman 60 days before the expiration of the director's term, so that the Chairman may notify the Governor and the latter may appoint the respective successor. (5) To carry out any other duties as may be assigned to him by the Board or the General Manager, provided the said duties are not in conflict with the Act or this Division. (d) Treasurer. The Treasurer shall be the custodian of the funds, values and accounts of the Company, and shall have the following duties and responsibilities: (1) To maintain and keep an accounting system for the Company. (2) To maintain and control a register of all revenues and expenditures, assets and liabilities of the organization. (3) To sign, together with the General Manager, all checks and fund disbursement vouchers. (4) To maintain such account or accounts as may be necessary for the organization's operation. 1962 

Vol. 1, No. 7 390.7

T.15505 

Ch. 25

(5) To maintain a separate account of every project under construction, development and operation, so as to determine the utility and public convenience thereof. (6) To prepare financial reports for the Board as it may require, and also for the General Manager and the Public Recreation and Park Administrator at their request. (7) In general, to take all such action and to carry out all such duties and responsibilities pertinent to the office of Treasurer. (8) Shall give a bond to warrant his full compliance with his obligations, the amount of which shall be determined by the Board. (9) To carry out any other duty as may be assigned to him by the Board or the General Manager. (e) Comptroller. The Comptroller shall be the auditing officer of all the transactions of the Company. To that effect he shall have the 

(1) To examine, from time to time and as the Board of Directors may determine or request, all the financial transactions of the Company, including, but not limiting himself to, the auditing of accounts, revenues, disbursements, the use of all property and conservation thereof. (2) To examine the legality and origin of the obligations incurred under the provisions of the Act, this Division, or of any other resolution of the Board of Directors. (3) If he finds any irregularity, to inform immediately the General Manager and the Public Recreation and Park Administrator so that they may act accordingly. (4) To render written reports on the outcome of his auditing directly to the Board of Directors. (5) To make recommendations as to how to improve the methods and procedures utilized in the registry and maintenance of all financial transactions. (6) To carry out all duties incidental or inherent to his office, or any other duty as may be assigned to him by the Board. § 505-10. Bonds of officers and employees; generally

The Board of Directors shall, through resolution to that effect, determine which officers and employees in addition to the Treasurer, shall have to give bond, and the amount thereof, to warrant the full compliance with their duties; Provided, That the Company shall pay the premiums on such bonds. 1962 

Vol. 1, No. 7 390.8

§ 505-11. Annual budget

Beginning with fiscal year 1961–1962, a budget of the Company shall be prepared and submitted to the approval of the Board of Directors. The said document shall specify all personal service expenditures, and all general expenditures for operation, as well as the costs of construction, enlargement, conservation and development of the organization's physical facilities, including personal services, materials, equipment and other related expenses. The amount necessary for the payment of the principal of and interest on the debentures issued by the Company shall also be included. 

The said budgets shall be in force for a term of one fiscal year, but may be amended at any moment, whenever the needs of the organization so require, by the Board of Directors. § 505-12. Financing of the Company (a) Financing plans. The financing plans of the Company shall be prepared by the General Manager and shall be submitted, together with detailed reports, to the Board of Directors for study and approval. (b) Bond issues. The Board may, through resolution approved by a majority of the members thereof, issue bonds to finance the Company's operations, under the provisions of art. 10 of the Act 

[15 L.P.R.A. § 510]. 

(c) Execution. All the bonds shall be signed by the General 

Manager and the Treasurer of the Company, or by any other officer as the Board may, by resolution, determine. (d) Order for payment of debts. If the resources available for a fiscal year are not sufficient to cover the appropriations approved for that period, the interest and amortization of the debt incurred by the Company in the issuance of bonds and other obligations thereof shall be paid first, and the other disbursements shall be effected then in accordance with such priorities as the Board of Directors may establish. § 505-13. Sale or lease of physical facilities and/or equipment (a) Generally. The Board of Directors may authorize the sale or lease of properties and/or equipment thereof, with or without need of a public call for bids, and that determination shall rest on the sound judgment of the members of the Board of Directors, but in every case there shall be considered the costs and maintenance of 1962 

Vol. 1, No. 7 390.9

T.§ 505-13 

Ch. 25

the properties and the benefits that the community will receive from such sales or leases. (b) Limitations. Nothing contained in the preceding section shall be construed as authorizing the gratuitous assignment of properties owned by the Company. However, an offer from an interested party to construct or operate facilities in lands or buildings belonging to the Company may be considered as the set price required by our Contracts Act in order to determine the considera tion for contract. [See 31 L.P.R.A. § 3431 et seq.] 

(c) Construction and improvements. Any work on or improvement of the physical facilities controlled by the Company for a total cost exceeding the sum of $5,000 shall be made by contract and public call for bids. To that effect, the Board of Directors shall appoint the members to compose the Board of Awards; Provided, That the adjudications shall be granted to the lowest bidder. Nevertheless, the Board may grant the award to a bidder who is not the lowest bidder, whenever in its judgment one of such bidders offers better conditions, materials, equipment and gives guarantees that will result more convenient to the Company's purposes. 

When a call for bids is announced and the bids are, in the judgment of the Board of Awards, unacceptable, the said Board may reject all such bids and the Board of Directors may then order the construction of said works by administration. 

The award shall be announced at least 10 days before the date on which it shall be held, in a newspaper of general circulation. 

All other improvements for a sum lower than the one established herein may be carried out by administration or in the manner as the General Manager may, with the approval of the Public 

Recreation and Park Administrator, determine. (d) Purchase of materials, equipment and appliances of all kinds. 

All transactions involving the purchase of materials, equipment and appliances to be used in sports as well as in the office, which exceed the sum of $500, shall be made through a public call for bids. All other purchase transactions for a lower sum shall be made as the 

General Manager may provide; Provided, That any purchase made in violation of the provisions of this section shall not be considered valid and the General Manager shall be responsible for the payment of any such transaction. Provided, further, that in cases of emergency the General Manager may, with the approval of the Public Recreation and Park Administrator, effect such purchases as are 1962 390.10

§ 505-14. Disbursements 

(a) In general. All disbursements of the Company shall be made after the expense has been certified by the General Manager, or the officer or employee to whom he may delegate, and only through a payment voucher duly authorized by the Treasurer and the General Manager or the officer to whom he may delegate. (b) Forms. To the effects of making any disbursement, the forms or documents which have been adopted within the accounting system recommended by the Secretary of the Treasury and approved by the Public Recreation and Park Administrator shall be used. § 505-15. Travel expenses and per diems; generally

All officers and employees of the Company shall be entitled to receive travel expenses and per diems when travelling on official business. Accordingly, the Public Recreation and Park Administrator shall determine and approve, through regulations to that effect, the amounts to be paid therefor to the Company's officers and employees, but such amounts so fixed shall not necessarily correspond to the salary earned by the employees, but to the expenses truly incurred, under present economic conditions, in providing themselves with subsistence, board and transportation. § 505-16. Norms for the appointment, suspension, etcetera of Company officers and employees (a) In general. The norms for appointing, removing, promoting, transferring, suspending, reinstating, leaves granted, and changes made in the rank, salary and title of the Company officers and employees shall be made according to the rules and norms as the Public Recreation and Park Administrator may prescribe. 

(b) Amendments. Such rules as the Public Recreation and Park 

Administrator may to this effect prescribe may be amended as they are deemed convenient to the improvement, convenience or efficiency of all the Company's activities and employees. 1962

Chapter 1. General Provisions 

Subchapter 13. Supervision of Elections DIVISION 1. RULES FOR THE VICINITY OF POLLING PLACES SECTIONS 

13-1. Political propaganda prohibited 

13-2. Election day 

13-3. Loudspeakers 13-4. 

Penalties 

13-5. Closing of propaganda places 

§ 13-1. Political propaganda prohibited 

(a) It is hereby prohibited to engage in political propaganda within a radius of 100 meters from any place where there is established a polling place. By place shall be understood, for purposes of this provision, every and any part of the building, or the lot on which said building is located, where one or more polling places are established. The distance shall be measured between the polling place and any part of the place where the political propaganda is being engaged in. (b) It shall be understood that the preceding prohibition would be violated by the existence, within the indicated radius, of any place open to the public for purposes of propaganda allusive or relative to the elections; any person with posters allusive or relative to the elections; any person who distributes, or any vehicle from which are distributed, pamphlets, handbills, or material of any kind allusive or relative to the elections; any loudspeaker for the broadcasting of messages allusive or relative to the elections; or any person who addresses another with a request for the latter's vote in favor of a political candidate or party, or for that person's abstention from voting. (c) This prohibition does not include the home or residence of any person, be it adorned or not with emblems, flags or colors that show the political affiliation of the resident, except where said homes or residences are being used on election day as a political club, or as center for the concentration of persons for purposes of political propaganda, or for circulating political propaganda by any means, in which case said prohibition extends to said homes and residences.

§ 13-2. Election day 

By "election day" shall be understood the period of time from twelve o'clock midnight of the Monday immediately preceding the day on which the elections are to be held until twelve o'clock midnight of election day. 

§ 13-3. Loudspeakers 

The use of loudspeakers is strictly prohibited in any part of 

Puerto Rico on election day. 

§ 13-4. Penalties 

Pursuant to the provisions of sec. 97a of the Election Law [16 L.P.R.A. § 285] concerning the regulations to be adopted by the Commonwealth Board of Elections, any person violating any provisions hereof shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and punished in accordance with the provisions of said sec. 97a of the Election Law. 

§ 13-5. Closing of propaganda places 

The Commonwealth Police is hereby authorized to shut down any place which on election day, as herein defined, is used for political propaganda, provided it is located within a radius of 100 meters from a place where there are polling places. Moreover, the Commonwealth Police is hereby authorized to take possession of any vehicle, Dec. 30, 1964

Chapter 61. Plebiscite on Political Status of Puerto Rico Subchapter 846. Provisions Governing the Plebiscite DIVISION 1. RULES FOR POLITICAL PROPAGANDA ON PLEBISCITE DAY SECTIONS

§ 846-1. Political propaganda prohibited 

To prohibit the propagation of any political propaganda on Plebiscite day, July 23, 1967, within a radius of 100 meters from any premise where there is a polling place. To the ends of this provision, a premise shall be any and every point of the building, or the lot whereon said building is located, where there are one or more polling places. The measurement shall be taken from the building to any point of the place where political propaganda is being spread.

§ 846-2. Definitions 

(a) The existence within said radius of any place open to the public for purposes of propaganda allusive or relating to the plebiscitary consultation shall be deemed as violating the preceding prohibition. (b) Any person who distributes, or any vehicle from which are distributed, pamphlets, leaflets, or material of any kind, allusive or

Ch. 61 relating to the Plebiscite; any loudspeaker for transmitting messages allusive or relating to the Plebiscite; or any person who addresses another requesting his vote for any of the three status formulas, "Commonwealth", "Statehood", and "Independence", or who requests that person's abstention from voting at the Plebiscite. (c) This prohibition does not include a person's home or residence, whether adorned or not with emblems, colors or flags showing the resident's political affiliation; except when said homes and residences are, on July 23, 1967, being used as political club or center or place for the gathering of persons with political propaganda purposes, or for the diffusion of political propaganda, through any means, in which case such prohibition shall include said homes and residences. (d) Plebiscite day shall be understood to mean the period between 12 o'clock midnight of the Saturday immediately preceding the day on which the Plebiscite will be held, until 12 o'clock midnight of July 23, 1967. § 846-3. Loudspeakers

The use of loudspeakers is strictly forbidden on Plebiscite day, that is, July 23, 1967, in any part of Puerto Rico. 

§ 846-4. Penalties; closing of propaganda places 

(a) Pursuant to the provisions of section 97a of the Election 

Law [16 L.P.R.A. § 285] and section 49 of the "1967 Plebiscite 

Act" [16 L.P.R.A. § 892] regarding the rules to be adopted by the 

Plebiscite Commonwealth Board, any person who violates any provision of this division shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and punishable according to the provisions of said section 97a of the Election 

Law [16 L.P.R.A. § 285] and section 49 of the 1967 Plebiscite Act. 

(b) The Police of Puerto Rico is hereby authorized to close any premises which, on Plebiscite day as herein defined, is dedicated to political propaganda, whenever it is located within a radius of 100 meters from a place or building where there are polling places. 

Likewise, the Police of Puerto Rico is further authorized to take possession of any vehicle, device, material or apparatus which is or has been used for political propaganda within a radius of 100 meters as mentioned above; and it is further authorized to take possession of any loudspeaker used in Puerto Rico on Plebiscite day (July 23, 1967) as herein defined; and further, to arrest any person who violates any provision of this division.
